t: THE MIRROR IS SEEDED ONLY WHEN THE BOOK MOVES
n: AN UNCHANGED BOOK IS NOT SEEDED AGAIN. Every deploy re-seeded the D1 mirror, because its hash carried the moment the book was extracted. The hash is now the book itself, so a push that moves no rows leaves the mirror answering throughout.
NO SNAPSHOT MEANS A SEED IN PROGRESS. The seed takes the snapshot row out first and puts it back last.

NOTHING DRAFTS DURING A SEED. While the mirror has no snapshot the drafter drafts and refuses nothing, and the next pass drafts those entries against the whole book. An Accept preview asked for then answers try again in a minute.
A DAMAGED MIRROR IS SEEDED BY HAND. node tools/d1.mjs --seed --force seeds regardless, for a mirror damaged while its book stayed the same.

t: A REJECTION ON ONE DEVICE LEAVES THE OTHERS
n: A REJECTED ROW LEAVES EVERY DEVICE. A row rejected on one device stayed in every other device's queue and figures. The Worker already names each entry it dropped in its answer to a post, and the desk now takes them out of its queue and stored copy, then redraws.
ON THAT DEVICE'S NEXT POST. Another device clears the entry the next time it posts to the cloud, not before.

NOTHING IS QUEUED AGAIN. The drop is written straight to storage, since the cloud already holds the queue without it, so the marks of what the cloud has taken stay the answer's. A failed redraw cannot turn a delivered post into a failed one.

t: THE TICK POSTS ONLY WHAT THE CLOUD HAS NOT TAKEN
n: NO REPOST EVERY TEN SECONDS. The tick posted the whole queue whenever it held anything. It now posts only an entry newer than the acknowledged mark, or a change the mark cannot see, so an acknowledged, refused or stuck entry is not posted again.
UNDO STILL REACHES THE CLOUD. Undo, Clear queued and a withdrawal mark the queue as owed, and only the answer to the post that carried the change clears it.

A STUCK ENTRY GOES TO APPROVE. The notice no longer says to re-record the sale, which would make a twin. The drafter still drafts the entry: decide it under Approve, then Undo the copy held here once its row is in the book.

t: THE BULLETIN EDITOR READS BACK WHAT HE JUST SET
n: THE BULLETIN IS NEVER CACHED. The desk's service worker passes /bulletin to the network, so the editor shows the notice as it stands after his own Set, and a change made on another device shows too.
ONLY HIS EDITOR WAS STALE. Customers read the bulletin on the Counter, which caches nothing, and were unaffected.

t: A REOPENED DESK REVALIDATES INSTEAD OF DOWNLOADING AGAIN
n: AN UNCHANGED DESK IS NOT SENT AGAIN. /desk and / pass the browser's If-None-Match and HEAD through to the store, so reopening an unchanged desk answers 304 with no body instead of the whole page.
ONE HOP TO THE STORE. The store is asked for /desk, where it serves desk.html. It redirects /desk.html there, and a request arriving at the Worker does not follow redirects.
ONLY GET AND HEAD ARE THE DESK. Any other method on / or /desk answers not found.

t: A ROW ANOTHER PASS MADE FIRST NO LONGER WAKES HIM
n: THE DRAFTER COUNTS ONLY WHAT IT MADE. A row is drafted only when this pass's own insert made it. A row another pass made a moment earlier, the tap against the quarter-hour net or the minute cron reading a stale queue at another location, is counted as raced, and the log shows it.
ONE WAKE A ROW. The quarter-hour net no longer sends 1 row waiting for a row his own tap has just drafted. A row the net did make still wakes him once.

t: A CORRECTION THAT SENDS GOODS OUT AND LEAVES THE RM130 STANDING
n: FOLDED: ONE CORRECTION ON s202, CR3-DAM. The patch sets deliveredQty from 0 to 1.5, deliveredOn from unset to 26 Sep 2026 and handover from unset to collected, preapproved by phone. No cash moves, so the order of 1.5 unit for RM130 dated 25 Sep goes from acknowledged and pending to fully handed over and fully unpaid. The rate of RM86.67 a unit sits above their median of RM80 and inside their range of RM80 to RM92.50.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID AND WHAT IS UNUSUAL. The shelf rolls out 1.5 unit to CR3-DAM, the difference the correction states, leaving 27 against a reorder mark of 28.2. The drafter flagged RM48 a unit as a blend across more than one lot rate, and these figures do not settle it; replacement stands at RM51. The drafter also flagged the advance: with RM155 outstanding before, no cap figure is on file to check it against.

t: ONE UNIT OUT AT FULL RATE, THE BLEND STILL UNANSWERED
n: FOLDED: one salt sale to CM6-PJ, 1 unit for RM100 dated 25 Sep 2026, collected on the day with RM100 cash in, so nothing is owed and nothing is left to move. At RM100 a unit the row clears the RM58.40 floor for 1 unit and sits under the RM140 ask, ceiling RM160. Costed at RM48 a unit from the desk's own inventory cost, RM52 on the goods at 52%.

UNUSUAL: the party's median rate is RM100 over two prior orders, range RM90 to RM100, so this row sits at the top of their own habit rather than above it. Nothing outstanding before, none defaulted, 0 unit on credit against a cap of 1, not an associate, on the roster. The drafter flagged RM48 as the inventory average across more than one lot rate; the figures here do not settle it, and the cost basis is unchanged.

t: A FULL PURSE AND NOTHING OFF THE FLOOR
n: FOLDED: one salt sell to CA2-SEN, 12.5 unit at RM750, the whole RM750 in cash on 25 Sep 2026 and none of the 12.5 unit moved. The rate holds at RM60 a unit, the same figure as their only prior order, and the total clears the RM729.98 floor for that size while sitting well under the RM1,090 ask. Paid in full, so nothing is outstanding against them.

UNUSUAL: the size is the largest this party has taken and the goods stay with the desk, so the book carries a delivery obligation rather than a debt. The drafter flagged RM48 a unit as a blended inventory average across more than one lot rate rather than the lot this row draws; the figures on hand do not settle that blend, and it stays open for the next fold.

t: ONE WHOLE LOT AT HIS OWN TIER RATE
n: FOLDED: a single salt purchase from SA5-BTR dated 25 Sep, 12.5 unit for RM700 at RM56 a unit with RM20 freight beside it, collected, RM700 cash out and all 12.5 unit received on the day. Nothing on the row stays open: no balance, no part receipt, no credit taken. The total matches the 23 Sep quote tier exactly, which on his word sells only in multiples of 12.5 unit at RM700 each.

UNUSUAL: the rate sits at the party's median of RM56 and well inside their RM44 to RM64 range, yet RM8 above the RM48 the book carries as inventory cost. The drafter flagged that RM48 is a blend across more than one lot rate, and this row does not settle the blend. The inventory took the 12.5 unit in on 25 Sep and left the stated cost basis untouched pending that check.

t: NINE UNIT WALK AND S195 CLOSES
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A FULFILMENT AND NOTHING MORE. The desk booked 9 unit of rice out to CM4-TO on 25 Sep against order s195 of 23 Sep, 10 unit for RM50 at RM5 a unit, already paid in full on the day. No cash moves with this hand over. The row is not recomputed in the fold: the master applies the amendment, so a fulfilment has one definition and one only.

WHAT IT LEAVES AND WHAT IT DID NOT TOUCH. The drafter flagged that this settles the order in full, and the figures answer it: RM0 and 0 unit outstanding after, against RM0 and 9 unit outstanding before. CM4-TO stands at 5 orders, median RM52, range RM5 to RM65, nothing outstanding, nothing on credit and nothing defaulted, on the roster. The salt position is untouched at 15.5 unit and the cost basis holds at RM48 a unit.

t: AN ORDER ACKNOWLEDGED, NOTHING MOVED AND NOTHING IN
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A PENDING SALT SELL TO CR3-DAM. Taken from the statements site as order 20260925115016-gqlz1q, 1.5 unit for RM130 dated 25 Sep 2026, acknowledged and to collect, preapproved by phone. No cash in and no stock out, so the row draws nothing and books nothing until something moves. The total clears the RM85.07 floor for 1.5 unit and sits well under the RM210 ask.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID: NOTHING. Stock stays at 15.5 unit, cost basis unchanged at RM48 a unit against replacement of RM49.43, and the reorder mark of 31.2 is untouched by a row that has not drawn. The drafter's flag that RM48 is a blend across more than one lot rate is carried forward unanswered, and the collection itself stays outstanding.

t: AN ADVANCE THAT PUTS A THIRD UNIT ON A CAP OF ONE
n: FOLDED: ONE SALT SELL TO CC5-OKR, 1 UNIT AT RM90, GOODS OUT AND NOTHING PAID. The row went in as an advance dated 25 Sep 2026: 1 unit moved the same day, RM0 of RM90 received. The total clears the RM56.71 floor for 1 unit and sits RM50 under the ask of RM140, ceiling RM160, and matches the party's own median rate of RM90 exactly, so the pricing is unremarkable against both ladder and habit.

UNUSUAL: THE CREDIT SIDE, NOT THE PRICE. CC5-OKR already carried RM138 outstanding and 2 unit on credit against a cap of 1, and this row adds a third unit and RM90 more with nothing in. The drafter flagged that, and flagged that RM48 a unit is the inventory average across more than one lot rate, not the lot this row draws. Neither flag is answered by the figures here, so both stay open for the desk.

THE INVENTORY: 1 unit of salt left the book on the sell, costed at the desk's own inventory rate of RM48 a unit, so no separate cost was carried against the row and the basis is untouched. Stated stock holds at 16.5 unit against a reorder mark of 32.2 and RM18.5 owed out, with the salt count standing at 23 Sep 2026. Replacement cost remains RM49.43 a unit, above the RM48 basis.

t: TWO ADVANCES CLOSED BY QR IN ONE CLAIM
n: FOLDED: TWO FULFILMENTS ON CR3-DAM, RM170 IN, NO GOODS MOVING. A single payment claim dated 25 Sep 2026, taken by qr via tngbiz on the statements site, is split across s179 and s193: RM80 against the order of 18 Sep and RM90 against the order of 22 Sep. Both were collected in full at the time and stood as advances. Each row is marked by the drafter as settling in full, and both were preapproved by phone.

UNUSUAL: A LONG-RUNNING ADVANCE BOOK CLEARED IN ONE SITTING. CR3-DAM came in with RM195 outstanding and 2.27 unit on credit across 16 orders, median rate RM80 with a range of RM80 to RM92.50 and nothing defaulted. The fold leaves RM25 of that outstanding balance untouched, on s136. The inventory did not move: no unit changed hands on either row, so stock stays at 16.5 unit and the cost basis stays at RM48 a unit.

t: A PHONE SET TO MALAY READS THE COUNTER IN MALAY, AND EVERY WORD COMES FROM ONE TABLE
n: STAGE 13, THE FIRST MALAY SLICE (his D12). A phone set to Malay reads the welcome, the door, saving the app, Home, paying, the claim, an order's money and its thread, This device and the banners in Bahasa Melayu; a switch, English or Bahasa Melayu, sits on the door, the welcome, One step to finish and This device, and is remembered on the phone. The rest stays English and is marked so for a screen reader. The sign-in message he sends carries a Malay half after the English.

EVERY WORD BY KEY. Every word the Counter draws comes from one table a language (stmt/words.js), English complete, and a key a language lacks is English's. Every refusal a customer can meet carries a code the page words, the Worker's English standing for a code the page does not know; a refusal now reads as a sentence, and a claim over what is owed names RM.
SUITE. An associate's links answering after the page has closed no longer throws into the next section.

t: ACCOUNT TAKES TWO COLUMNS ON A COMPUTER, AND COMING UP IS ONE LIST
n: STAGE 7, POLISHED AFTER THE MERGE. On a computer, Account puts the statement on the left and This device on the right again; Salt Admin's account card had borrowed its name. On Home, Coming up is one list: a part he entered on the desk wears the same row as an order, with its mark, size, Due when you receive it, day and amount, and an order's part shows once, as that order.
REWARDS. The card's date no longer runs into the next column on a 320 phone, and on a computer its month strip starts at the card's edge.

t: HOME OPENS FIRST, AND THE PLACES SIT UNDER THE THUMB
n: STAGE 7, WITH STAGE 8'S REWARDS (his answers D11 and D14 of 24 Sep 2026). The Counter opens on Home, and its places, Home, Prices, Orders, Account, and Rewards for an associate, sit on a bar under the thumb with a word under each and a count where one waits; from 1080px the bar is a rail, each place takes two columns and a sheet opens as a drawer. A header names the place and says who is signed in. Each place has its own address, and a banner's order still opens at that order.

HOME. What is to pay now with its due date and the one Pay, what needs them, what is coming and how it is paid, and Order again: a tile a size, way and place they have ordered, at today's price, placed in two taps. A new account opens on Nothing on your account yet, with its first sizes to order. The notice is a still card: nothing runs or changes, and a Set on the desk asks first, because it wakes every phone.

ACCOUNT AND REWARDS. Account holds the statement as stacked lines with one month filter, All first, earlier statements at the foot, and This device. Rewards opens on the associate's links, each with its state in a word, its opens, Share ready before the tap and its QR, and the reward in units with Ask on any order to take it.

t: PAYING IS ONE SHEET, AND A PAYMENT STAYS A CLAIM UNTIL HE CONFIRMS
n: STAGE 6, THE SECOND PART (his answers D7, D8 as he amended it, and D9 of 24 Sep 2026). To pay now heads the statement with its due date and Pay, Overdue and Coming up beneath. Pay opens one sheet: the figure and what it is for, All or Part, Transfer or Scan a code, Pay into the account of his they choose, the username as the reference with Copy, and Show the account number or Show the code opening the pay page at that rail and amount. The Counter carries no account number.

A CLAIM, NEVER PAID ON THEIR WORD. Back from paying, the sheet asks once, Did you send RM x?, with Not yet. What they say they sent reads sent, waiting for us to confirm, everywhere, and the chase pauses while it waits. His Received books it; his Not found takes the claim and its queued mark off in one event and wakes them with Payment not found yet. A claim against the account for rows he entered himself is drawn on the desk oldest first, row by row, and one tap approves exactly those rows.

THE HOLD. The RM 100 hold counts only what is past its term, lists each part with its due date, keeps Prices readable, and a claim reopens ordering. Cash on handover is offered only where the rule allows, and says why when not.

t: AN ACCOUNT TELLS HOW THEY GOT IN, AND EVERY DEVICE CAN BE SIGNED OUT
n: STAGE 9, THE SECOND PART (his answer D13 of 24 Sep 2026). An account in Salt Admin opens on one filled Send a sign-in link, made as the account opens so the share runs inside the tap, beside Show a code, View as them, Copy password and Sign out everywhere. How they got in lists the last ten ways in, link, code or password, each with its moment and the device in words, such as iPhone, Safari; no address is kept.

PHONES AND COMPUTERS. Each account lists its devices, added and last used, each with its own Sign out. Sign out everywhere, on a second tap, ends every device, unused link and code, and alert, and says how many; the account's own record is never rewritten.

THIS DEVICE. A customer's This device card leads with saving the app, then alerts on or off, their other devices with This one marked, Sign out other devices, and Sign in another device with its code and QR. Salt Admin's count of what waits on the desk is now the desk's own Today count, as at the moment the desk read it.

t: ORDERING IS A SHEET, AND A MOVED PRICE IS CAUGHT BEFORE PLACING
n: STAGE 4 OF THE REDESIGN (his answer D11 of 24 Sep 2026). New order lays a sheet over the page: the product as its mark, sizes as tiles with their prices, the size they order most tagged your usual, the way and the place from last time, the total and Review in reach. Every size on Prices opens it at that size, and Prices reads as at its day and time. An associate is asked Who is it for? first; the five-order limit is said before the form, with the open orders to cancel; one delivery sentence everywhere.

A MOVED PRICE. The publish seals a keyed digest of each price list, and Place carries the digest of the list the page opened; when the list has moved the Worker answers 409 with the new sealed list, and the check shows the size's new price with Place at RM X, one tap. The site compares stamps and prices nothing.

SENT. Place answers in the sheet and asks A buzz when it is confirmed? from that tap only; See the order opens its screen. A lapse closes the sheet and signing back in reopens it with what was typed. The level mark has left Prices.

t: SALT ADMIN OPENS ON WHAT NEEDS HIM
n: STAGE 9, THE FIRST PART (his answer D13 of 24 Sep 2026). Salt Admin opens on Needs you, one card a thing with its action on the card: an associate's waiting link (Approve, the tier pin, Decline), a customer locked out with the cause and Send a sign-in link or Show a code, an ID with no account and the Silver link, and the accounts not yet sent with Send them in turn, each ticked as its share goes.

ONE LIST OF ACCOUNTS. Accounts replaces Send and Review: search, filters, and chips for owes, locked, no account, opened how and when, alerts on and sent; a row opens the account's card beside the list on a laptop. View as them opens their page read only with Back to accounts. His places are the App bar on a phone and the Desk rail from 1080px.

ITS OWN APP. Salt Admin has its own icon, the ring with a keyhole, and when Access lapses it says the sign-in has ended with a way to sign in again, instead of Failed to fetch; the Access session is now a week. Each owner app counts what waits in the other, with no link and no name.

t: EVERY ORDER HAS ITS OWN SCREEN, AND NO LINE IS LOST
n: STAGE 5 OF THE REDESIGN (his answer D11 of 24 Sep 2026). The orders list is rows: Needs you first, then Open, then the earlier orders folded and not drawn until opened. A row opens the order's own screen: the goods on the Steps recipe, the money on its own lines, his when line, one filled Pay while something is due, Cancel at the foot while the goods have not moved, and what happened folded. On a desk the list sits beside the open order.

THE CUSTOMER'S WORDS. Sent, Confirmed, Ready to collect or deliver, Collected or Delivered, Complete, Not taken and Cancelled by you or by us, with his reason where he gave one; a short delivery closed says so; units above one.

MESSAGES THAT KEEP EVERY LINE. Their lines show Sending, Sent, or Not sent with Tap to try again under the line's own request id; his lines are marked New until seen; Return sends; a half-typed line is kept. The poll patches only the order that changed and never redraws what is being typed, and a return, a lapse reopened or a notification tap goes the same way.

t: WHAT IS DUE, AND WHEN, SEALED WITH THE STATEMENT
n: STAGE 6, THE FIRST PART (his answers D8, as he amended it, and D9 of 24 Sep 2026). The live statement now carries what is owed as the engine reads it: To pay now, each part due on its order date plus the desk's own credit term, soonest first; Overdue, the parts whose due day has passed; and Coming up, orders agreed but not yet handed over. Rows entered on the desk count as well as site orders; gifts, write-offs and cancelled orders count in none. Nothing draws them yet.

A PAY LINK THAT OPENS AT THE RAIL AND THE AMOUNT. stmt/pay.js gains payHref, which builds QR Command's #account/rail/amount/reference link for the two ways, Transfer and Scan a code, and never carries a number; QR Command (shipped first) opens that rail with the amount and the reference beside the code.

t: A GUEST KNOWS WHAT TO DO NEXT, AND THE WORD CHECKS READ MALAY
n: STAGES 8 AND 13, THE FIRST PART (his answers D12 and D13 of 24 Sep 2026). The guest board ends with its next step, To order, reply to the person who sent you this link, and every shut link, unknown, withdrawn, declined or waiting, answers one styled page with the same words, so the door gives nothing away. An associate's reward line says how to take it: Ask on any order to take it.
KEPT OUT OF THE TRANSLATOR. Every Counter page carries translate="no", so Chrome never offers to send an opened statement to a translator.

THE WORD CHECKS READ MALAY. siteWords and the desk's siteSafe refuse a level's Malay name after a cue (tahap emas, ahli gangsa, Keahlian Emas) while ordinary Malay passes (Ipoh, Perak; peluang emas), warn on every book's name and its Malay word (garam, minyak, gula-gula, beras), and every scan in the suite reads the same lists. His answer on an order asks before sending a line that warns, as the bulletin does.

t: A WALK-IN CAN SIGN IN ON DAY ONE
n: STAGE 14 OF THE REDESIGN (his answer D15 of 24 Sep 2026). The laptop mints a pool of spare accounts (node tools/stmt-account.mjs --pool, ten by default, refusing without the master): each a username, a record with an empty bundle and its password sealed under the master, marked spare in the clear. The publish writes a spare like any account, never retires one and lists none as a customer; the door treats a spare as no account at all.

BOUND AT ADD ID. The fold binds the next free spare to a new code where the username is minted today, so the binding lives in the repo and needs no key in CI; the next publish seals the customer's statement and prices into it and the account opens by password and by link. With no spare free it falls back to today's road, and Salt Admin says: Made at the next laptop update; until then, show the Silver link. The gate refuses two codes on one username, and the pool mint proves the content key as well as the master.

t: ONE CARD, ONE TAP A STAGE, THE ROW SHOWN BEFORE THE YES
n: STAGE 11 OF THE REDESIGN (his answer D6 of 24 Sep 2026). Site orders opens on Waiting on you: one row per customer act, oldest first, filtered New, Paid?, Cash and Asked, the notice folded below; Today and the Enter badge count the same rows from a cold open, and on the laptop the card sits beside the list.

FIGURES BEFORE THE YES. A new order's card drafts the row it would make and shows it first: their card today against the quote, the margin, the floor, their usual, the drafter's flags, and what the customer was told. The delivery charge is a chip with none chosen for a delivery.

ONE TAP A STAGE. Accept, Collected, Cash received and Received approve the row they make in the desk Worker only when the drafted row equals what he was shown in every field, flag and pricing version; anything different waits under Approve, marked. A stage before the first row lands is a pre-approval spent when its row is drafted (migration 0011). A rejection writes back and the move can be offered again under a fresh entry; their withdrawal drops only a still-pending acknowledgement.

AT THE COUNTER. A handover with nothing paid raises Cash to record, whose tap stops the chase; Delivered part takes a stepper and Close at what was handed over; Decline and Cancel take a reason the customer reads as by us; saved quick replies and No reply needed. His wakes name the kind of act and never a code or an amount.

t: NOBODY IS STRANDED: THE LINK KEEPS THE PHONE, A LAPSE REOPENS ITSELF
n: STAGE 3 OF THE REDESIGN (his answers D1, D2 and D3 of 24 Sep 2026). The sign-in link opens on a page that names the account and spends nothing until Continue, so a WhatsApp preview cannot use it up; an in-app browser is told to open it in Safari or Chrome; Continue keeps the phone signed in with the same split key as the tick, and the link now lives three days. Its message carries the username.

STAYING IN. Remembered phones are filed under a hash of their token; Keep me signed in runs thirty days from the last open; a lapsed session reopens itself and repeats the tap once; the page re-reads whenever it comes back. Only with nothing remembered does a sheet say you were signed out, keeping what was typed.

THE DOOR. One username field and one password field that a password manager can save and fill, Show, a paste of the whole message that keeps only the password, and a line on how to ask for a new link. Signing in over another account asks first.

THE SAVED APP. On an iPhone, Keep it on your Home Screen draws the phone's own buttons and a one-use eight-symbol code minted when the sheet opens; the saved app starts at /app and takes the code by Paste or typing. Android and desktops get an Install button where the browser offers one. Salt Admin can show a customer at the counter a code and a QR. The hand-over answers 'not switched on yet' until its secret is set.

t: A COUNT WINS AND THE FLOORS LIFT
n: FOLDED: ONE RICE COUNT, DATED 24 SEP 2026. Ninety four unit counted by hand against 95 on the book, a drift of -1. On his word the count stands over the ledger, so the stated rice inventory is set to 94 and COUNT_ON for rice moves to 24 Sep 2026. No party, no cash and no goods movement sit against this row, and no order cost is carried, so nothing books to the inventory's own rate.

UNUSUAL: THE DRAFTER RAISED TWO FLAGS AND THE FIGURES ANSWER ONLY ONE. The missing unit books as shrinkage across every unit sold, and the floors lift with it: floor1 from RM3.40 to RM4.08, floor2 from RM6.80 to RM8.16, floor125 from RM42.50 to RM51, with the ask at RM8 for 1 unit unchanged and self use moving from 0 to 1. The second flag, 9 unit owed out and already paid for, is left outstanding: the dossier says no more.

t: THE GROSS MARGIN READS AGAIN
n: TWO SALT ROWS COSTED: s183 AT RM240 AND s196 AT RM96, RM48 A UNIT. Both were booked pending and handed over by a correction raising the delivered quantity. That road moved no units through the fold, so the shelf cost was never written, although each note of the day stated RM48 a unit. One uncosted live row blanks the gross margin across every book; with both costed it reads RM16,504.

THE FOLD NOW COSTS A SALE WHENEVER GOODS HAVE LEFT. tools/fold.mjs filled the cost only on an amendment moving units; it now also fills it when the row carries a delivered quantity, so a correction handing over a pending order is costed like a fulfilment. The suite drives that correction on a copy of the book, proved red without the change.
OIL SHELF COST RM7.60 TO RM8.00. v834 received 50 unit of oil at RM8 a unit and left the stated basis at the older lot rate; the book rule is the newest received lot, so the basis follows it.

t: TWO LOTS IN, BOTH ABOVE THE QUOTED TIER
n: FOLDED: TWO PURCHASE ROWS, BOTH DATED 24 SEP, BOTH PAID AND RECEIVED IN FULL. SP7-PUD delivered 50 unit of oil for RM400 and SM4-KEP delivered 15 unit of candy for RM630, RM1,030 of cash out on the day with no delivery and no freight beside either row. Neither draft carried a flag, both parties sit on the roster with nothing outstanding and nothing defaulted, and neither is an associate.

UNUSUAL: EACH TOTAL SITS ABOVE THE 23 SEP QUOTE FOR ITS SIZE. The oil pays RM400 against the quoted 50 unit tier of RM380, named on his word of 23 Sep 2026 along with the 10 unit tier alone. The candy size of 15 unit falls between his quoted tiers of 10 unit at RM55 and 20 unit at RM47, so no tier answers it directly. The dossier gives no reason for either gap, and none is recorded here.

INVENTORY: THE SALT POSITION DID NOT MOVE. Both lots are oil and candy, so the stated stock of 16.5 unit stands, cost basis unchanged at RM48 a unit against a replacement of RM49.43, reorder at 32.2 and RM18.50 owed out. The salt count stands at 23 Sep and the oil count at 24 Sep, with candy, rice and spare uncounted. Nothing was promised out against these rows.

t: A COUNT OF NOTHING, AND NINE UNIT BACK ON THE SHELF
n: TWO ROWS FOLDED, ONE COUNT AND ONE CORRECTION. The oil count of 24 Sep 2026 read 0 unit against 35 on the book, a drift of -35 on the first count since 19 Sep 2026. A count wins over the ledger, so the stated oil inventory is set to 0 and COUNT_ON for oil moves to 24 Sep 2026. The dossier gives no reason for the gap and none is supplied here.

THE SECOND ROW MOVED GOODS, NOT MONEY OF ITS OWN. A correction on s195 for CM4-TO cuts deliveredQty from 10 to 1, so 9 unit of rice roll back to the shelf while the RM50 paid on 23 Sep 2026 stands untouched. On the oil side the desk's floors hold at RM7.82 for 1 unit, RM15.65 for 2 and RM97.80 for 12.5, ask RM10, with self use read at 104 after the count against 79 before.

t: TWO CASH ROWS, BOTH SHUT THE SAME DAY
n: FOLDED: TWO COMPLETED SELLS DATED 24 SEP, BOTH PAID AND HANDED OVER ON THE DAY. CC5-OKR took 10 unit of oil for RM130, and CZ4-MK took 4 unit of candy for RM200. Cash matched the totals in both cases, the goods moved the same day, and neither row leaves a balance, a pending quantity or a carriage line behind it. One flag was raised, on CC5-OKR, and it is recorded unanswered.

UNUSUAL: BOTH DRAFTER WORKINGS STATE A GOODS FIGURE THAT DOES NOT MATCH THE COSTED ROW. The oil row costs at RM7.6 a unit, RM76, against a working that reads RM54 at 41.5%; the candy row costs at RM38 a unit, RM152, against a working that reads RM48 at 24%. Both are left as the desk's own inventory cost. The salt inventory did not move on either row and the cost basis stands.

t: SITE ORDERS IN ONE SAFE STORE, EVERY MOVE AN EVENT
n: STAGE 10 OF THE REDESIGN (his answer D10 of 24 Sep 2026). Site orders move into one Durable Object, OrderBook: every move on an order is an appended event with the device's own id, so a retry lands once and no writer can erase another's move. The study's six erasures (a line, a payment, a handover or a withdrawal lost to a stale copy, and a payment counted twice) replay in the suite and none can happen now; a seventh found on the way, a queued payment falling back, is closed too.

THE MOVE IN. The first call copies every KV order in, pauses moves for one minute with a plain 'try again in a minute', copies again what changed, and takes moves. For a week every change is also written back to KV and the hourly check compares the two; rollback is one switch, ORDER_STORE kv. Retiring the KV keys after a clean week is still to come.
NOTHING ELSE CHANGES. Every customer and desk route answers as before, and the reconcile, the return leg and the chase run unchanged over the new store.

t: THE DESIGN SYSTEM FIRST: NINE RECIPES, AND EDGES YOU CAN SEE
n: STAGE 2 OF THE REDESIGN (rule 6: a look is a recipe in Code/salt-ds first). Salt-ds v1.3.0 adds the nine patterns the new Counter and Salt Admin are built from: Sheet, Option, App bar, Steps, Bubble and thread, Line, Code field, Inbox row, Plain ledger, and the Orb in its own section. The Counter now carries them and the recipes it will use from stage 3 on; nothing draws them yet.

THE ONE VISIBLE CHANGE. Field and ghost edges rise from about 1.1:1 to 3:1 or more, a focused field gets a 2px brass ring, placeholders and recipe prose move to mist-light, and type is set in rem, which maps today's pixels exactly. No page height moved in any of the rig's 332 shots.

t: A BANNER SAYS WHAT KIND OF NEWS IT IS, AND THE CHASE IS FAIR
n: STAGE 12 OF THE REDESIGN (his answers D4 and D5 of 24 Sep 2026). A customer's phone keeps its subscription's encryption keys, and a wake carries the kind of news sealed for that phone alone (RFC 8291 in the Worker's own WebCrypto): Your order is confirmed, Your order is ready, A reply on your order, Payment received, A payment is due, and the rest of an order's life. Never an amount, a product, an order or a name; a phone with no keys on file keeps today's wake and words until it next signs in.
THE TAP OPENS THE ORDER. The banner opens the Counter at the order it is about, and a window already open re-reads rather than only coming forward.

THE CHASE, TWICE A DAY. v700's hourly chase now wakes at 10:00 and 18:00 Kuala Lumpur, from the day after a handover, only for goods received and not yet paid, paused while a payment claim waits, one wake a slot, in its own words: A payment is due.

t: THE COUNTER AND SALT ADMIN DO WHAT THEY PROMISE
n: STAGE 1 OF THE REDESIGN (his instruction of 24 Sep 2026: customers found the Counter hard to follow and hard to keep as an app; he answered all recommended to the plan's fifteen decisions). Fifty fixes that need none of those decisions, each its own commit with its own assertion, proved red first.

GETTING IN. A new account with no rows opens on Nothing on your account yet, with Prices and Order working, where it was a blank page or a refusal. A lapsed session says so in the bar with Continue; a dropped request says Not sent beside what was tapped; a server fault on a remembered reopen keeps the phone; Log out drops its wrap and this phone's notifications; notifications wait for the service worker and show this phone's real state.

ORDERING AND PAYING. The pay step takes the system's pill, ghost and field, one filled control a card, and the RM 100 page answers every tap. Check this over is exactly what Place sends; Place and I have paid carry a request id, so a retry lands once; a half-typed line survives a redraw; the Amount column lines up; the tab strip wraps at 320px; a product with no priced size reads coming soon.

THE STATEMENT. Its account line shows the username, never the roster code; its table sits in its own scroll box; Still to collect is one line a book; the faces load on the link and guest pages; every short date says Sep.

SALT ADMIN. Approve, Decline, Withdraw and Restore on a link now post, where every one had answered 405 since 10 Sep; Decline is its own state, Not approved to the associate. It saves as Salt Admin, its manifest fetched with credentials. Review reads the account's orders and offers no order form; a row with no account offers nothing to send; a customer's typo no longer brakes his override; Opened counts every open, and how.

THE DESK. Site orders keeps a typed charge and answer across its poll; Today counts site orders from a cold open; a customer's line wakes him as A customer wrote on an order; Approve asks before rejecting a row a site order made and writes the rejection onto the order; his cancellation is noted as his; a status note passes siteWords; the cards' buttons are the system's recipes.

UNDER THE COUNTER. The customer reads a whitelisted view of an order, never ledgerKey, queued or sync; a stored move never answers not placed when a shared mark fails; the chase and the cash rule read an advance as the engine does, goods moved beyond goods paid.

t: PUTRAJAYA ON COVERAGE, ITS PRECINCTS TO CHOOSE
n: PUTRAJAYA HAD NO DISTRICT (his instruction of 24 Sep 2026). It is now a core district made from its state outline, and that outline is cut out of Sepang as a hole; Cyberjaya and Dengkil stay Sepang's, so CA6-CYB still reads Cyberjaya, Sepang.

ITS AREAS ARE ITS PRECINCTS. Its one federal seat, P.125, is the whole territory, so a tap on it said nothing; the twenty precincts and Presint Diplomatik come from OpenStreetMap (ODbL, credited under the map), and each is a place to choose at Add ID and Amend ID, reading Presint 8, Putrajaya.

A SMALL AREA NAMED BY THE LOCALITY DECIDES. A party's point is kept to 0.01 degrees, about a kilometre, which a precinct can round out of: Presint 6's point read Sepang. Where the locality names an area under three kilometres across in the point's own district, that area is the reading; a seat is wide enough for the point, so Ampang in Kuala Lumpur never takes Selangor's Ampang seat.

t: EVERY PAGE SAYS WHAT IT IS FOR

t: RESTOCK SIZED FROM MEASURED DEMAND, BOOK BY BOOK
n: A BUY SIZE AND RESTOCK CARD ON STOCK, FOR THE BOOK IN VIEW (his instruction of 24 Sep 2026: the typical buy size, so he can restock properly, inefficient inventory being as costly). The typical order and its spread, the order sizes as shares of orders and of units, the next 7 and 14 days, cover now, the reorder point, the next lot and whether the next price break pays. Salt today: a median order of 2 unit, but orders of 3 unit and over are 30% of orders and 67% of units; 7 unit free, 1.3 days of cover, next lot 62.5 unit at RM56.

THE FORECAST USES ONLY MEASURED INPUTS, engine/position.mjs restockPlan: a recency-weighted daily rate (half-life 14 days, a young book read over 28 days), a weekly trend shrunk and capped at 50%, the book's own weekday and pay-window rhythm from the Whiteboard, holidays flagged, and the named customers due on their own cadence as a floor under each window.

THE REORDER POINT IS DERIVED, NEVER UNDER 4 DAYS AND NEVER OVER 14 (his bound): lead time plus a 95% safety stock over the lead and the measured gap between lots, in days of forecast demand. It replaces the typed 15 and 20 unit marks, which stay only for a book with no demand, and every reader follows: the Stock headline and tiles, the chart's trigger line and Today. Candy and rice had borrowed salt's 15.

THE NEXT LOT IS THE CHEAPEST TO HOLD: each quote tier in whole lots, from the smallest that covers the need up to what the forecast sells in 28 days, scored on the rate plus the measured leakage over the days it is held. Oil's 50 unit break wins over 40 unit at RM10; candy's 60 unit break outlasts the forecast; rice's 90 unit free reaches no reorder point inside it. The approach board's side panel carries the same 14 days against what is free.

t: THE APPROACH BOARD SORTS BY WHAT TO DO
n: THE RAIL IS THREE ROWS, AND THE ROW IS THE ACTION (his decisions of 24 Sep 2026). Chase first holds every name that owes, with what it owes on the chip, and its profit is no longer counted as waiting. Due now holds names past their own date by up to twice their usual gap, ranked by profit. Lapsing holds names past it by more than twice that gap, a win-back rather than a routine offer: CG5-SB at 81 days had sat first on the rail beside a name one day late.

AN ASSOCIATE AND THEIR BUCKET ARE ONE NAME. The board is built on owner codes, so the habit, the usual lot and the last three orders read the code and the -R bucket together, and a bucket's debt is added to its owner's. CN6-WM had sat on the 28th while CN6-WM-R sat on the rail.

FIVE WEEKS FROM THIS MONDAY, NOT THE CALENDAR MONTH. By the 24th two thirds of the grid was dimmed and empty and next month's dates were a count in a side panel; they are days now, and anything later is one line under the grid. The side panel is the hit rate alone, last month and this month so far, and it now counts a due date nobody came back for, which it left out until today, and reads a bucket with its associate, so August reads 22 of 39 met (56%) where it read 25 of 41 (61%).

EVERY CHIP CARRIES ITS RM, what is owed on a chase and what the order would earn otherwise. A NAME THAT HAS BOUGHT ONCE sits in Tried once under the grid, newest first, eight and a count, where it was a sentence pointing at the foot of the page. ON THE PHONE the grid gives way to a list by day with 44px taps. The copy says their habit, not his.

t: WHEN THE MODEL IS NOT USED, THE PHONE IS TOLD SO IN PLAIN WORDS

The raw error stays in the run's log and in the version entry, where it is read by whoever fixes the call.

Stated salt fell to 25 unit and the floors lifted with the thinner cover: floor for 1 unit from RM55.94 to RM57.49, for 2 unit from RM111.88 to RM114.99, for 125 unit from RM699.25 to RM718.68, with the ask for 1 unit held at RM140 and self use from 77.7 to 78.7. The candy shelf rolled back 5 unit to SM4-KEP, the difference the correction states, landed 23 Sep. Cost basis untouched at RM48 a unit.

t: THE VERSION HISTORY LEAVES THE DESK
n: HIS WORD OF 23 SEP 2026: cut the history too. With the Journal gone (v802), nothing on the desk read past the current version, yet every download carried 479 version entries. The master now holds one, the current version, which is what the version chip, the phone's payload and the price sheets read; master/changelog.json holds every entry ever written, and every entry dropped was proved to be in it before the cut.

A FOLD REPLACES THE ENTRY RATHER THAN PREPENDING IT. tools/fold.mjs writes the array as the one new entry, the previous one being in changelog.json already because the gate refuses a version the changelog lacks, and tools/foldcall.mjs reads its style sample from changelog.json instead of the master.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE DESK'S COPY CARRIED AND THE RECORD DID NOT, CARRIED HERE RATHER THAN WRITTEN INTO THE OLD ENTRIES, because changelog.json never rewrites one. To v535: The map part now says what it is a map of: where the buyers are, revenue by locality as heat inside the Kuala Lumpur boundary. To v326, replacing its last sentence: CORRECTED AT v328: the claim that collected and delivered floors are now the same number is true only above 1 unit. floorTotal still lifts the floor to the cost of SERVING the lot where that bites, and at 0.5 and 1 unit it does, so the delivered floor stands at RM40.99 and RM65.32 against a collected RM30.59 and RM61.18. The delivery saving is real at exactly the sizes a delivery is worth most. Three more differ only where the desk's copy blanked a place name for the public page (v347, v384, v385); the record keeps the names.

t: THE JOURNAL IS OFF THE DESK
n: HIS WORD OF 23 SEP 2026: the journal does not have to be on the desk; it is a separate file for reference when looking at the changelogs. The Journal part leaves Record, with the correction strip only it drew and their styles. Nothing it showed is lost: every note stays on its row in the book, and every version is in master/changelog.json, which is the file he reads. Nothing on the desk now reads past evolution[0]; the array keeps its window because the fold, the changelog tool and the suite read it as a list, and cutting it is his call.

t: THE P&L RUNS SIX MONTHS, THEN QUARTERS, THEN HALVES, THEN CY, WITHOUT A SCROLL
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 23 SEP 2026: show the last 6 months (when available), then quarterly, semi-annually, followed by CY to date, and fit them without the need to scroll. The table was last month, this month and the year since v403. It is now up to six months from the book's first, this calendar year's quarters and halves that have begun and hold trading, and the calendar year to date, which is what the FY column always summed and is now called CY.

IT FITS BY SAYING RM ONCE. The currency sits in the corner cell and every figure is a bare number under a three-letter head, with the padding tightened and a rule opening each group, so salt's ten figure columns fill 876px of the desk's column at desktop width and 705px at a 1,024px window without a scroll. A phone cannot hold ten columns worth reading, so there a switch draws months, quarters or halves beside CY, the months being the latest three, and each group fits the 325px column exactly. The heading's long subtitle, which pushed the whole page 256px wider than a 1,280px window, is cut to its first clause and the rest moves into the caption.

t: THE CONSOLIDATED HEADS SAY EVERY BOOK
n: HIS SCREENSHOT OF 23 SEP 2026: Receivables headed Both books on a desk of five. The Financials and Receivables heads read Every book, as the three Today pages do since v794.

t: P029'S 25 UNIT REACH THE SALT SHELF, AHEAD OF HIS COUNT
n: THE STATED SALT SHELF READ 1 UNIT WITH 25 UNIT OF SALT ON IT. p029, 25 unit from SA5-BTR received on 22 Sep, was booked as rice and corrected to salt at v791, and a correction moves no stock, so the lot never rolled onto the salt shelf; v791 said so and left it for a count or a roll. It is rolled by hand now, 1 plus 25 is 26, on his word of 23 Sep 2026, because he has counted 25 today and a count measured against 1 would have booked 24 unit found where 1 is missing, a surplus that nets off real shrinkage and lowers every salt floor.

t: CZ4-MK'S RM20 REFUND IS CLOSED, SET OFF ON 21 SEP
n: HIS WORD OF 23 SEP 2026: close the CZ4-MK refund; his orders came to RM920 and he paid RM900 after the set-off, 5 unit of salt and 10 of candy. The RM20 over-tender of 26 Aug is marked paid on 21 Sep, the day it was set off against s190 and s191, and its note says how. No refund is open anywhere on the book, so Now on Today loses its one Now-from-the-day-it-is-raised item.

THE ROWS KEEP THE GROSS, AND THE CASH COMES OUT RIGHT. s190 and s191 carry RM460 each as paid, RM920, while RM900 changed hands. Closing the refund on the same day books the RM20 back, so cash reads RM920 in and RM20 out on 21 Sep, which is the RM900 he handed over: trading cash falls from RM6,456.50 to RM6,436.50, the RM20 it had been overstating. His statement shows the orders paid and the overpayment returned to him on 21 Sep. Closed by hand in ledger/book.json, the one road for a refund, since nothing on the phone reaches that list.

t: EVERY DESK DEPLOY DEPLOYS THE COUNTER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 23 SEP 2026: make sure every push on the Desk pushes the Counter too. The Counter's content was already published on every run; its CODE deployed only when a push touched its own paths, and even then only by a diff the job read when the phone already had the build. Workers Builds usually ships the desk first, so a desk push left the Counter's code where it was, and a change to its clock needed a hand deploy.

THREE ROADS, ONE RULE. The job's site deploy runs on every run that deploys the desk, and the statements-path diff that fed the old gate is gone with it. tools/update.mjs deploys the Counter once the desk reads live on the phone, so a desk deploy that failed never ships the Counter alone. npm run deploy deploys both. Workers Builds still ships the desk alone; the job this push starts brings the Counter behind it within minutes.

t: NEXT 30 DAYS IS EVERY BOOK AT ONCE, THE CASH WALKED ONCE FOR THE BUSINESS
n: THE CASH IS THE BUSINESS'S, SO IT IS WALKED ONCE. Each live book is walked on its own for its inventory, its rate and its lots. Their cash events go into one list, an event every book's walk raises (the refund you owe, the supplier default) going in once, and forecast() walks that list through its own day loop, so there is still one walk. Added book by book instead, the RM20 refund to CZ4-MK came off five times: the business's thirty days read RM130 where they are RM210.

EACH BOOK'S INVENTORY STAYS ITS OWN. A table gives each book its daily rate, the day it empties and what it still owes out, and the first to run empty leads the page, because that is the order to place. The chart draws each book as a share of what it holds today, in its own colour read off the design tokens, so one unit of salt and a hundred of rice read on one scale.

WHAT LANDS, AND WHEN carries every book's lots, receivables and bills, each tagged with its book; the refund is untagged. The agreed-buy switch offers every book's pending buys at once. Every book is now on all three Today pages; the book switch is gone from them.

t: RULES IS EVERY BOOK AT ONCE: MONEY ADDED, UNITS LEFT WITH THEIR BOOK
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 23 SEP 2026: combine Rules and Next 30 days too, after Today (v794). Rules read the book in view, so salt's credit breach and its supplier default were off the page whenever oil was open.

ONE RULE PUTS THE BOOKS TOGETHER: MONEY ADDS AND UNITS DO NOT. Each live book is read on its own through eachBook, as it always was, and a figure in ringgit is summed with each book's part in the note beside it, as the Financials head does: pending orders, what is still to come in, inventory at cost, revenue, margin, receivables, what has been bought. A figure in units stays with its book: the inventory note gives each book its own count, and in transit reads in lots with each book's units beside them.

THE REGISTER IS EVERY BOOK'S. boundaryPanel takes the merged list: a row every book raises is shown once, and a row one book raised names that book, or two books' Margin floor rows read as one rule said twice. Deferred deliveries and advances are merged by party with each book's cap named where it is broken. Concentration is read on each customer's revenue across the books. The supplier default, which only salt's reading carries, is shown once whichever book is open, and the latest ledger is the newest orders across the books, each tagged.

t: TODAY IS EVERY BOOK AT ONCE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 23 SEP 2026: combine every book on Today, because not every book has something to note or watch, and keep it a great overview that is not convoluted to read. Today read the book in view alone, so a restock due on oil sat unseen while salt was open, and the Today badge counted one book's Now.

ONE LIST. allActions runs actions() on every book and puts the book in view back. An item the same on every book, a refund, a rule, a site order or the queue, is listed once with no tag; one a book raised on its own carries that book's tag in its own colour. The Today badge counts Now across every book.
A BOOK WITH NOTHING ON IT SAYS NOTHING. A book with no lot and no sale is left off the list and the band alike, or spare would report itself under its own reorder trigger every morning.

ONE ROW A BOOK. The band under the list is a table of the live books: held, out (promised and not yet handed over, a dash when none) with any shortfall, cover in days (red under its trigger) and what is owed on it, short enough headings to sit on a phone without scrolling sideways. Units are never added across books; the money is, once, on the line under the table with the cash. The cover chart draws each book beside its own trigger.
AND THE REFILL SAYS LOTS. Salt's quote is one 12.5 unit tier bought in multiples since v793, so a refill of two reads 2 lots of 12.5 unit rather than a 25 unit tier nobody quotes.
WHAT IS STILL ONE BOOK AT A TIME. Rules and Next 30 days, the two working pages behind Today, keep the book switch: a day-by-day forecast of one inventory is not a thing to add across books.

t: THE PRICING_V2 WORKBOOK: SALT IS AMBASSADOR AND FOUR TIERS ON RM56, CANDY AND RICE ARE STATED A UNIT
n: HIS WORKBOOK OF 23 SEP 2026, salt-command pricing_v2.xlsx. Salt's COGS is the supplier's quote, RM56 a unit, and moves only when the quote does. Ambassador is COGS plus half again, up to the ten. The four tiers are the sheet's columns: 2.1 times COGS rounded down, 2.1 up, 2.5 down and 2.5 up, each multiple falling 0.045 every half unit past half a unit and never under Ambassador. One unit reads RM90, 110, 120, 130 and 140.

HIS FOUR ANSWERS THAT DAY. Bronze goes, so the tiers are Titanium, Platinum, Gold and Silver and a stranger is quoted Silver; nobody held Bronze. COGS is the quote, not the live landed cost. Candy from 10 to 29 unit is RM55 a unit. And the engine keeps its two guards over the sheet, a better level at least a ten under the next and a rate that never rises with size, which moves fourteen of the sheet's 48 tier cells (all four at half a unit and at twelve and a half, three at 2 unit, and Gold at 1.5, 2.5 and 3): half a unit reads 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90 where the sheet had 50, 50, 60, 70 and 70, and twelve and a half reads 1,050 to 1,090 where every column met Ambassador at 1,050.

CANDY AND RICE ARE SINGLE TIER, STATED A UNIT, AS OIL IS. Candy RM60 a unit under 10, RM55 to 29, RM50 from 30; rice RM8, RM7 from 5, RM6 from 10. Both round to the ringgit. A size between rungs is its rung's rate times the size, so at a break a bigger order can cost less in total: 29 candy is RM1,595 and 30 is RM1,500, 9 rice RM63 and 10 RM60. That is the rates as he stated them. The rice board's inversion under the ten-rounding, open since v791, is gone with it.

THE QUOTES AS HE RELAYED THEM. Salt from SA5-BTR in multiples of 12.5 unit at RM700 each. Oil from SP7-PUD at 10 for RM100 and 50 for RM380, the 15, 20 and 30 unit tiers dropped. Candy from SM4-KEP at RM55, 47, 38 and 30 a unit for 10, 20, 30 and 50. Rice from SM4-KEP at 100 for RM320. Oil's own board is unchanged.

A TIER IS SALT'S ALONE. His words that day: each customer is quoted differently for salt, and everyone the same for oil, candy and rice. The Tiers card, Accept all and Add ID offer a tier on a tiered book only, so no level is proposed or held where it moves no price. The two oil tiers already held stay on the book and price nothing. On the Counter a stated board now carries no level, so the page draws no mark beside it and says it is the same price for everybody; since 19 Sep it had drawn Ambassador's mark beside oil for every customer and told them their own rate followed their first order.

THE COUNTER FOLLOWS THE NUMBER OF TIERS. The standing guest links are one a tier rather than exactly five. Bronze's link is kept, because an id handed out must keep opening something, and it opens the stranger's board, which is Silver's.

t: THE FOLD NO LONGER STOPS FOR WANT OF A MODEL
n: NO KEY, NO CREDIT, NO ANSWER: THE FOLD LANDS ANYWAY. tools/foldnotes.mjs writes the same notes object off the same dossier the call was going to be handed, and tools/foldcall.mjs takes it on three roads: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a call that will not go through, and a reply twice against the house rules. The Fold step's own exit on a missing key is a warning now, and --no-model asks for the tool's notes outright. On 22 Sep a credit balance of nothing exited that step twice inside a minute and left two approved rows staged with the deploy, the marks, the mirror, the statements and the suite all behind them.

WHAT IS LOST IS THE JUDGEMENT, AND IT IS SAID WHERE IT IS READ. A model reads the drafter's flag against the figures and says whether they answer it; the tool names the flag and stops there. So every row note it writes ends on the line that no judgement is recorded in it, and the version entry says the same, because a reader holding one row should not have to come to the Journal to learn which kind of note they are holding.

THE ONE UNTRUSTED STRING IS SCRUBBED FIRST. The reason is quoted into the notes, and an API error can carry an em-dash, the wrong unit, the word this house does not write, or markup, every one of which the checker refuses. Notes that could not pass would leave the batch staged for the very reason this road exists to remove, so the tool's notes are put through the same check a model's reply is. Eight assertions, each proved red by its own mutation, one at a time.

AND A LOT'S OUTSTANDING FIGURE IN THE DOSSIER WAS WRONG. partyDossier read the total less the row's own cash, so a lot carrying no cash field at all counted as wholly unpaid: SA5-BTR read RM3,260 outstanding where the engine's poOwed reads RM160, and every purchase note written off this dossier had been repeating the larger figure. It reads poOwed now, which reads the trail.

t: P029 READ AS SALT, AND THE RM160 CLOSED
n: FOLDED: TWO AMENDMENTS, BOTH AGAINST SA5-BTR'S LOT P029 OF 22 SEP. The first is a correction that sets the product on that row from rice to salt. The second is a fulfilment of RM160 cash on 22 Sep. Both were decided at the desk on 22 Sep and sit on the same order, 25 unit for RM1,400 at RM56 a unit, received in full on the day.

UNUSUAL: A BUY ROW THAT CHANGED WHAT IT WAS BEFORE IT CHANGED WHAT IT OWED. The correction moves no cash and no stock, it changes only what the row says about itself, and the drafter raised no flag on it. The fulfilment carries the drafter's flag that it settles the order in full, and the figures answer that: RM160 against RM160 outstanding, leaving nothing open. The inventory held at 1 unit of stock and did not reprice.

t: THE RAIL, THE BAR AND THE TAGS DRAW FROM THE SYSTEM'S RECIPES, AND NOTHING LOADS OFF GOOGLE FONTS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026: no Google Fonts, complete the work, one fold at a time, the rail, the bar and the tags first. v784 put the tiles, findings, pills, parts strip, version and aurora onto the design system's recipes. The rail, the bar with its orbs, and the state tags follow here: each recipe first synced to the desk's measured values in Code\salt-ds (v1.2.1, which also carries the recipes the next folds will take), then carried by class in the markup, the layer keeping bindings and geometry only.

TWO MECHANISMS CARRY THE DESK'S OWN STATE INTO A RECIPE WITHOUT A SECOND RULE. A state word binds to the chip's one tone variable (.tag.paid{--salt-status-tone:...}), so 38 tags and the ledger's own variants moved with eight one-line bindings; the open destination and its open page are read off aria-current, which the recipes honour beside their own modifier classes, so the desk's .on and .solo stay where its script and its suite read them. The rail's width and stickiness live in the recipe under the desk's own media rule, and on a touch phone the drawer's geometry stays the page's, measured: fixed, hidden until the button, the pane fill, the veil. The one base rule that outranked the recipe, the brand-hiding media rule, moved into the layer, where it wins.

THE BAR IS THE RECIPE'S FRAME. Glass with the hairline at the rail's offset, the wordmark in the display face, the quiet mono line, the version and the orbs, all from the system; the desk binds only where it sits (--salt-bar-top) and keeps its own cap once the page scrolls. The orbs are one recipe in three states: bare in the bar, raised over the page, lit as the way back to the top. Measured on the served build at 1180px and 375px against the recipes and against the previous build: the phone's bar is the same 105px it was.

NO GOOGLE FONTS ANYWHERE. The design system's remote stylesheet is gone, its brand plate links the local one, its files moved beside it into src/fonts/, its dist and its Claude Design bundle carry them, and both sync tools pull from the new home. Three suite sections were re-pointed from the layer to the recipes; one new section holds 8 assertions, each proved red on its own; the earlier sections still stand. Ghosts, fields, tables, tiers, product bands and tags, actions and journal entries stay on the layer, each a fold of its own.

t: ENTER, REDESIGNED: TILES FOR BOOKS, A TYPED PARTY, A DATE THAT STEPS, AND A SECOND BOOK
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026, reading the form on screen and naming what was wrong with it. The product dropdown becomes a TILE A BOOK: the dot in the book’s own accent, the name beneath, the chosen one lit in that hue. The select survives, hidden, and is still the value, so wbProdVal and every reader behind it are untouched; the tiles set it and fire its own change, the road setProdView was always reached by.

THE PARTY IS TYPED OR CHOSEN, over the same hidden-select trick, so every reader still gets a CODE. It matches on the code and on the drawn name, both case-insensitively, and it NEVER guesses at a partial: CZ4 leaves the select empty and the form refuses it, because a near miss that silently booked to the wrong party is the costliest slip this form could make. Every party list is already in alphabetical order since v783.

THE DATE STEPS A DAY AT A TIME, by tap or by arrow key, through one dateStep so the buttons and the keys cannot disagree. That is a TRADE and it is stated rather than discovered: a native date input uses Left and Right to move between its day, month and year segments, and binding them takes that away. Typing digits still advances the segments, which is how a whole date is entered, and Up and Down are left alone.

A SECOND BOOK IS A SECOND TRANSACTION FOR THE SAME PARTY. Tapping another tile adds a book with its own row of figures, and Record queues one entry a book, sharing the party, the date and the direction, each through the same entryFault and replayAnswer guards the first went through. Three rules on a tile: a book not in the entry joins and becomes active, a book in but not active becomes active, and the active book tapped leaves unless it is the last.

v409 CALLED TWO PRODUCTS IN ONE FORM A FAULT, and that ruling holds here. The margin, the free inventory and the price coach all read the ACTIVE book, so a form holding two read one and recorded the other. The active book still drives every reading; the books after it are plain orders. A gift, a reward cover and a resale are properties of ONE order, each judged against the active book’s cost, ladder and reward, so an entry carrying any of them with a second book is REFUSED and the message says which. That refusal stands ahead of every push, and testing is why: placed after the gift branch, which queues its row and RETURNS, a gift ticked with a second book queued the gift and dropped the other book in silence.

AND THE FULL SHEET OPENS FROM THE CORNER. The panel it opens was already a side drawer, fixed right at 100dvh; what sat in the flow was the button. It keeps the design system’s pill recipe that v784 put on it: the corner is where the control sits, not what it is made of.

t: THREE LOTS IN, TWO OUT, AND A BLEND STILL UNANSWERED
n: FIVE ROWS FOLDED, THREE BUYS AND TWO SALES, ALL CASH ON THE DAY. SM4-KEP supplied 35 unit of candy for RM1,140 and 100 unit of rice for RM320 beside RM20 freight, both paid and moved in full on 21 Sep. SA5-BTR delivered 25 unit of rice for RM1,400 on 22 Sep against RM1,240 cash, so RM160 stays open on an account already carrying RM3,100. Nothing on the two SM4-KEP rows is left outstanding.

THE SALES BOTH RAN TO CZ4-MK ON 21 SEP AT RM460 A ROW. Five unit of salt at RM92 a unit clears the RM259.22 floor for that size and sits RM100 under the RM560 ask, costed at RM48 a unit, the inventory's own rate. Ten unit of candy at RM46 a unit carries no cost and no ladder, the floor and ask for 10 unit both standing at zero. Both were collected and paid in full.

TWO DRAFTER FLAGS SURVIVE THE FOLD UNANSWERED. The salt row is costed on an inventory average of RM48 a unit while the shelf spans more than one lot rate, and the dossier carries no lot split, so the blend is not resolved here. The candy sale has no committed candy order for CZ4-MK to test the rate against. The inventory took the salt row out of a shelf of 6 unit counted on 21 Sep.

t: A GUEST BOARD NAMES NO LEVEL ON ANY BOOK
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026, reading the Bronze board after v786: drop the Bronze heading on the oil pane, and make sure it holds for every book, not both books. The oil pane was headed Bronze on every level's board, Titanium's included, while the salt pane had no heading. A book that falls back to ladderRow took that row's name onto the board as tierName, and the guest page printed whatever it was handed; a row pinned to the link's level has no name, which is why salt never showed one. Oil's fixed board is one price for everybody, so the name was not even true of it.

TWO RULES, ONE FOR THE DATA AND ONE FOR THE PAGE, BECAUSE EITHER ALONE CAN BE UNDONE WITHOUT THE OTHER NOTICING. The board carries no level's name on any book: the field is gone from boardList's product record, and the standing link's own level stays on the board itself, for his listing. And the page draws none: the pane's sub-line is the fallback note alone, The only price for this product, standing on its own now that nothing precedes it, and a name that reaches the page from anywhere is still not drawn.

FOR EVERY BOOK, WHICH IS WHAT HE ASKED FOR. The check nulls every ladder so every book on the board would take a named row, and walks all five standing boards and the two live ones asserting that no book carries a name; then it hands the page a product that does carry one and reads the visible text for every level's name and for Tier 1 and Tier 2. Each of the two went red under its own mutation and stayed green under the other's. What a level is called is the desk's; a stranger is handed prices.

t: A BOOK WITH NO COST HAS NO GUEST BOARD
n: HIS QUESTION OF 22 SEP 2026, whether the purchase cost and the selling price are synchronised. On the desk they are, by construction: one engine strikes the ladder off the last three lots received, and the customer's price lists and the five guest boards are re-sealed from the same snapshot on every publish. The check found the one place they were not. Candy, rice and spare had been on all five guest boards at RM 0 at twelve sizes each since the publish that followed v780, which opened them empty.

WHY. A book opened empty has inputs and a policy and no lot, so its cost stack is 0 and boardList's fallback row prices every size at 0. The test that a row is usable asked only that a price be finite, and 0 is finite; the guest page draws every row it is given. The customer's own price list was never wrong, because it gates on a tier and reads a book with none as coming soon.

THE RULE IS THE ENGINE'S OWN BASIS. A book is left off the board exactly when its landed cost is nothing, read through ladderCogs and not through a second test on the prices: a price of nothing is a symptom, and a laddered book with no lot would clear a price test at RM 10, 20 and 30, each level sitting a ten over the one below. Nothing else moves: salt and oil price as they did, and a book is back on the boards the moment its first lot is folded and published.

TWO ASSERTIONS, EACH PROVED RED ON ITS OWN. Salt keeps its ladder and is struck of its cost in a copy of the snapshot, and must vanish from the board while the rest stay; and the live boards carry no RM 0 at any size, which today's three empty books make a real check rather than a tautology. The first goes red under the price test as well as under no test at all, which is what it is for.

t: THE BRAND FACES REACH EVERY SURFACE, SELF-HOSTED
n: HIS YES OF 22 SEP 2026 to fetching the fonts, the one thing the design system pass before this left undone. Fraunces and JetBrains Mono were designed into the identity on 29 Aug and never loaded where it mattered: every surface's policy is self-only, so the desk, the Counter and QR Command have read in Georgia and Consolas since v472. The split between figure and sentence survived; the faces did not.

THE FILES ARE GOOGLE FONTS' OWN LATIN SUBSETS, fetched once with a browser's user agent and kept in the design system (Code\salt-ds\fonts\, 67 KB and 31 KB, both variable, with their OFL licences), declared by src/fonts-local.css from a fonts/ folder relative to whatever page carries it. Nothing was subset or re-encoded on this machine, and the weight ranges declared are the files' own, so a 700 resolves to the face and is never synthesised. Symbols outside the latin range fall to the system face, as they always did.

EACH SURFACE SERVES THEM BESIDE ITS PAGE, BY ITS OWN SYNC. The desk: designsync --pull takes the rules and the files into design/, --sync writes a THIRD generated block into the master, before the base and never at the foot, which is the desk layer's place, and copies the files to public/fonts/; --check proves both; the shell precaches them, so the desk reads in its own type offline. The Counter serves no files, so the two ride in stmt/fonts.js as bytes, written by tools/stmt-fonts.mjs, served at /fonts/ with a year of cache, under a policy that now admits font-src 'self' on both pages; the page carries the rules first. QR Command pulls the files into src/app/fonts/, hashes them into its build id, stamps their URLs in app.css and precaches them.

ONE SUITE SECTION, 12 ASSERTIONS, EACH PROVED RED ON ITS OWN, the Counter's route exercised against the Worker: a face answers the file with a year of cache, a missing one is the site's usual 404. The Counter's rule that its page loads nothing now reads: nothing but its own two fonts, the chevron included.

t: THE DESK, THE COUNTER AND QR COMMAND USE THE DESIGN SYSTEM, AND THE SYSTEM ITSELF IS FIXED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026, on the verdict that the design system was a good identity and a thin system: the desk, the Counter and QR Command are to use and import it, every bug listed is to be fixed, and full use made of it. Before this the master used 0 of the system's 252 classes: the design layer re-stated each recipe against the desk's own class names, four hand-kept copies of the palette had already drifted (the system's dist/ lacked the three hues added that morning), and the layer had grown two colours of its own.

THE SYSTEM FIRST, Code\salt-ds at v1.1.0. Its root clipped (overflow: hidden to contain an aurora that already clips itself), which made it the scroll ancestor of every sticky element inside it, so its own DeskBar and DeskRail never stuck: measured in the browser, the bar sat at -1200 after a 1200px scroll and holds at 0 now, the rail at its 22px. Nineteen rules set type under its own smallest token and read --salt-text-xs now. The field recipe was 15px on glass against its own principles 4 and 7 and is a well, 16px and 44px tall. The alarm (v557) and the opaque warm panel (v567) are identity tokens, --salt-alarm and --salt-panel, with --salt-mist-bright, --salt-line-strong and --salt-glass-hover for the three values the layer had written by hand; the layer points at them and writes no hex and no alpha of its own. The desk set's values were synced to what the desk had measured since v472.

THE DESK USES THE RECIPES WHERE A CLASS-FOR-CLASS SWAP WAS MECHANICAL. The markup carries both names: 94 tiles as salt-kpi with their label, figure and note, 39 findings as salt-insight, 46 filled buttons as salt-pill--sm, the parts strip as salt-tabs__pill, the version as salt-version, and the two orbs as the system's salt-aurora--fixed. design/desk.css holds no rule for any of them, and the base layer's tile rules, which outranked the recipe on specificity, are retired. Two mechanisms carry the desk's own state into a recipe without a second rule: the tile's tone letters set --salt-kpi-tone, and the strip's open pill is read off aria-selected, which the recipe now honours beside its own modifier. Measured on the served build at 1024px and 375px: every value is the recipe's, the phone tile is 20px, and nothing overflows sideways. The rail, the bar, tags, ghosts, fields and tables stay on the layer, each a fold of its own.

THE COUNTER TAKES THE FIVE RECIPES IT USES. tools/stmt-style.mjs slices the pill, the ghost, the field, the tab strip and the state chip out of the vendored stylesheet into SITE_RECIPES, the page carries them beside the tokens it already took, and its own layer keeps geometry only. The open tab is glass with a hairline now and not a filled brass badge, which decision 5 had always reserved for the one button. QR COMMAND TAKES THE TOKENS BY SYNC: its app.css carries the system's :root between markers, written by its own tools/designsync.mjs --pull, and its build refuses to ship on drift (244 of its assertions green).

TWO NEW SECTIONS, 25 ASSERTIONS, EACH PROVED RED ON ITS OWN, and one of them caught its author: the check that the root no longer clips matched the comment that says so, and reads the stylesheet with its comments stripped now. NOT DONE: THE BRAND FONTS. The CSP is self-only on every surface, so Fraunces and JetBrains Mono can arrive only embedded, and embedding needs the files fetched once, which is a network step and his call.

t: ENTER LOSES ITS PROSE AND THREE OF ITS FOUR BUTTONS, AND THE PARTY LISTS SORT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026, reading the form on screen. Three sentences went, named one by one: the paragraph beside the product control explaining which book an entry lands on and what the rail does; Cost, the four dates, the settlement flags, the row note beside the full sheet button; and Not in the list? …, a whole row of prose about registering a party, on the form for recording a trade. The control says the book and the book is lit in its own hue; a paragraph restating that is three lines to read before typing a figure.

FOUR BUTTONS WERE THREE TOO MANY. Record acts on what is on the form; Clear queued, Save queue file and Copy queue all act on the QUEUE, and on an empty queue every one of them is a control that can do nothing, since each already refused one. They appear when there is something for them to act on. The card is down from six buttons to two. The queue note went with them: Record pushes each entry to the cloud queue. It is drafted within seconds and folded the moment it is approved; nothing else to do. Copy queue still puts the lines on the clipboard. is now Queued. Drafted in seconds, folded when you approve it. Its laptop twin shortened the same way, and the build patch that carries the cloud wording moved with the line it anchors on.

THE WARNINGS WAIT UNTIL THE ENTRY IS DESCRIBED (his instruction). Every rule fired against a blank form, so opening Enter showed a column of red saying the goods must be more than zero before anything had been typed. They wait for the quantity, the goods and the cash. The rules still RUN, so Record stays disabled on a form that cannot be recorded; what waits is the saying, and nothing unsafe becomes recordable. Cash cannot be tested for emptiness, being born holding 0, which is a real answer, so it carries a touched flag, set by typing and by None, Half and Full. The flag is set in the SAME handler that previews: as a second listener behind it, it was set after the preview had already read it and the warnings stayed silent.
AND THE NOTE IS AT THE END. It sat in the middle of the figures row, between the carriage and the freight, so the eye crossed a free-text box on the way from one number to the next.

EVERY PARTY LIST IS IN ALPHABETICAL ORDER (his instruction). They were in ROSTER order, which is the order parties were registered in, so finding one meant reading the whole list. byName sorts on what is DRAWN and not on the code: ID() answers the name where the vault is open and the code where it is not, and a list sorted by code would sit in a visibly random order the moment the names appear.

t: A STATEMENT SAYS WHICH BOOK EACH ROW IS, AND UNITS OF DIFFERENT BOOKS DO NOT ADD
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026, on a defect found while opening three books and not caused by them. stmtRows filters by PARTY and never by product, the row shape carried no product, and the footer ADDED the quantities: CS6-BS read 117.5 unit over 47.5 of one book and 70 of another, on a document that goes to a customer. Six accounts on this book hold more than one. It has been wrong since the second book opened on 06 Aug and nothing on the page could have shown it.

THE MARK SITS WITH THE QUANTITY, because the quantity is what the book qualifies. Five unit of one thing and five of another are not ten. It is DRAWN and never named, which is the oldest rule on this site, and the drawing and its shape word come from stmt/page.js so a statement and the customer’s own page cannot diverge on what a book looks like. The SHAPE is the accessible name: an aria-label naming the product would put the word back for exactly the readers who cannot see it was taken away. A book with no mark draws the Ring.

THE MONEY STILL ADDS AND THE QUANTITY DOES NOT. A ringgit is a ringgit whatever it bought, so the totals, what is paid and what is outstanding are untouched; only the unit figure is kept apart, one a book. An account holding a single book reads exactly as it always did, with its mark in front of the figure.

SALT LEADS, and the first draft of this line broke that. The books were sorted alphabetically, which put oil before salt on every account holding both, against his standing instruction of 11 Aug restated on the 13th. They come out in the BOOK’s own PROD_ORDER now, and an id the order does not name sorts last rather than being dropped, which is the rule PROD_IDS already keeps on the desk.

THE CHECK READS THE TEXT, NOT THE SOURCE. The rule that no product is named in words cannot be tested against the raw document: the inlined stylesheet carries --salt-product-salt, so a search over the source would fail on a token name rather than on anything a customer can read. It strips the tags first, and it asserts the SUM is absent rather than only that the parts are present, because a footer could print both and still print their total.

t: WHO EARNS IS A FIELD ON THE BOOK, NOT A STRING COMPARISON
n: THE REWARD SCHEME WAS SALT-ONLY BY SEVEN BARE STRING COMPARISONS, five here and two in the drafter, so no book opened after salt could ever earn however the book described itself. That is a real decision of his and not an accident, but it was written where only a code edit could change it. PRODUCTS[p].reward states it instead: true on salt, false on every other book, which is exactly what those comparisons meant. Nothing moves today. What changes is that whether candy or rice ever earn becomes his decision and a data one.

THE FALLBACK IN THE DRAFTER IS NOT TIDINESS. The drafter reads state.PRODUCTS off the D1 MIRROR, and the mirror is re-seeded by the deploy job AFTER the Worker is already live. Between those two moments the mirror is the old shape and carries no reward field at all, so a bare read would have answered false for salt and refused every redemption in that window, in silence, on a scheme that has been running since v577. Where NO book states the field the old rule stands; where ANY book states it, the field rules. Both halves are asserted, the second against a mirror built without the field.

WHAT IS NOT TOUCHED. Four other comparisons against the literal salt stay exactly as they are, because they are the storage convention and not the reward: a row that names no product IS salt, so if (product !== "salt") row.product = product is what keeps 175 of 188 sales from carrying a field they do not need. Those are read in docs/PRODUCTS.md section 6 and are correct at five books for the same reason they were correct at two.

t: CANDY, RICE AND SPARE OPEN, AND THE PARITY SCAN FINDS THE SPLIT CLEAN
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026. Three books opened by tools/product.mjs --add, each registered in all six per-product maps and the order, each EMPTY: no quote, no stated count, no opening figure. The fold refuses a sale on a book with no cost, so the first lot on each goes in by hand, which is v228’s own bootstrap rule and not a gap. spare is the fifth slot, opened to prove that adding a book is repeatable rather than surgical, and given no mark on purpose so the Ring fallback is exercised by a real book.

THE PARITY SCAN FIRED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FIVE HUNDRED VERSIONS. It was written at v275 and its header says the point is product three. Its RULE 2 asks whether a book with no orders reports commitments or receivables of its own, which is the signature of a whole-book read presented as one product’s, and that rule could never once fire while every book had orders. Three empty books arm it. It reports NO rule 1 and NO rule 2: every empty book reads zero revenue, zero receivable, zero inventory and zero promised out. The unfinished product split of v228 is clean. What it does report, three times, is never counted and declared but empty, which are notes on a new book and not faults.

AND OPENING THEM PUT A FALSE FIGURE ON THE DESK, WHICH IS FIXED HERE. creditCapFor falls back to the default book where a book states no cap of its own, which is what keeps the breach arithmetic working on a book nobody has set a policy for. Printed book by book, that borrowed figure stated salt’s 1 unit as candy’s own, under a sentence that begins Credit caps are per book. The sentence now names the books that HAVE a cap and then says which ones borrow one: the borrowing is stated rather than hidden, and no figure is claimed where it is not true.

FIVE BOOKS FIT ON A PHONE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. At 375px the switch draws five buttons on TWO rows at 67, 60, 75, 67 and 75 pixels wide and 44 tall, every one at or above the tap floor in both directions, with no horizontal scroll; at 1280 it is unchanged and still carries each book’s headline figure. All five dots draw their own hue.

AND ONE OF THIS VERSION’S OWN ASSERTIONS WAS VACUOUS, WHICH IS THE LESSON.
