The check that no book is given a cap it does not have was inserted through a shell heredoc that ATE ITS BACKSLASHES, so the pattern it built was a backspace character followed by the plain letters s and d, where a word boundary, a space and a digit were meant. It matched nothing. It passed on every book, and it went on passing under the very mutation written to prove it, which is how it was caught: the mutation turned its neighbour red and left it green, and an assertion that will not go red is not an assertion. It is built from a regexp literal’s own source now, and its failure message carries the sentence it read, so the next person sees what it saw. Nothing else would have found it, because a vacuous check and a true one look identical in a green run.

t: THREE MORE HUES, TWO MORE MARKS, AND FIVE BOOKS FIT ON A PHONE
n: HIS CHOICE OF 22 SEP 2026, ahead of opening three books. The identity had two product hues and needed five. Each new one avoids the SEMANTIC four: ember, verdigris, steel and copper each mean something on this desk, so a product dot drawn in one would read as a status rather than as a book. The violet and cyan families were retired at v472 and are not used. candy is rose at hue 330, rice indigo at 235, spare olive at 68.

THEY GO IN THE DESIGN SYSTEM AND NOT IN THE DESK, because the Counter reads them too. tools/stmt-style.mjs generates the statement stylesheet from the :root of design/salt-ds.css, which is vendored from Code/salt-ds, so a hue added to the desk layer alone would never reach a customer and one added to the vendored copy alone would be reverted by the next --pull without a word. The edit is upstream, then pull, then sync, then the statement stylesheet: a hue that is missing there does not error, it resolves to nothing, and the product loses its accent in silence.

A LOZENGE AND A CAPSULE, AND SPARE KEEPS THE RING ON PURPOSE. A rhombus for candy and a seamed stadium for rice, drawn in the same hairline stroke as the cube and the droplet; the capsule carries its seam for the reason the cube carries its three inner edges, that without it a stadium is a shape and with it it is a thing. Neither is literal and neither is a word, which is the rule this site has kept since v659. spare is given no mark deliberately, so the Ring fallback is exercised by a real book rather than asserted about a hypothetical one.

AND THE SWITCH STOPS GROWING DOWN THE PAGE. Each button carries a dot, a name and that book at a 150px minimum and the strip wraps, so two books sat on one row and five would have stood THREE rows deep above every per-product page. Below 760px the figure goes and the button shrinks to its content; the figure is on the page underneath either way, so nothing is lost, only moved. It stays wrapped rather than becoming a sideways scroll box, which v466 forbids above the ledger, and the minimum holds at the tap floor because a control must measure 44px in BOTH directions.

t: A BOOK IS OPENED AND PUT AWAY BY A COMMAND, AND RETIRING ONE THAT TRADED IS REFUSED
n: HIS DECISION OF 22 SEP 2026, asked before the three new books are opened: add a retired flag and a re-key. Registering a product meant hand-editing ledger/book.json in six places, PRODUCTS, PROD_OPENING, COUNT_ON, PRICE_SET, COST_RULE and QUOTES, plus the order, and then remembering to sync. tools/product.mjs does all of it: --add, --rename, --retire, --unretire, --list. A book opens EMPTY, with no quote and no stated count, because nothing has happened on it yet and inventing a figure would be the one thing a ledger must never do.

RETIRED IS REGISTERED AND NOT SHOWN. prodLive() feeds PROD_IDS, so one flag takes a book off the switch, the Enter form, the tier grid, the ledger's filter and the parity scan, which is every one of the eighteen readers, while its rows, its opening and its tiers stay exactly where they are and the extract still carries it. A device that REMEMBERED a book before it was retired now falls back rather than opening on a book the switch no longer offers.

AND THAT IS WHY RETIRING A BOOK WITH ROWS IS REFUSED. PROD_IDS is read by the consolidated totals as well, so hiding a book that had a past would quietly take its revenue out of the whole-book figures with nothing on screen to say so. The flag is therefore only ever allowed on a book with nothing on it, which makes the filter safe by construction rather than by care. Retiring a book that traded is a different question, and the tool says so instead of guessing.

SALT CANNOT BE RE-KEYED, and the reason is the oldest rule in the book. A row that names no product IS salt, on 175 of 188 sales, so re-keying salt would silently re-attribute every row that names nothing. The tool refuses and points at the section of docs/PRODUCTS.md that states the convention. A rename of anything else moves the six map keys, the order, the id, the accent, every row's product field and every customer's tier for that book: proved on a copy of the real book, where renaming oil moved 24 rows and 2 tiers and left the old id nowhere.

t: THE TOOLS STOP TYPING THE PRODUCT ORDER AND READ IT OFF THE BOOK
n: TWO DEFINITIONS ARE TWO THINGS TO KEEP TRUE, AND THE ONE THAT DRIFTS DOES IT SILENTLY. tools/book.mjs carried PROD_ORDER = ["salt", "oil"], typed out beside the book that already states it, and tools/d1.mjs FAILED when the two disagreed. So a product could not be registered in one place: the book and that line had to move in step or the mirror check went red. The suite already guards the LEDGER map against exactly this and says why; the order was the one thing it did not cover.

THE ORDER IS THE BOOK'S NOW, read through prodOrder() and cached on first use, the book being a megabyte and bySalt being called once per comparison. Salt still leads, which is his standing instruction of 11 Aug restated on the 13th, and nothing about the order itself has changed.

THE MIRROR CHECK GOT SHARPER RATHER THAN WEAKER. It compared the STORE's copy of the order against a line in a tool, which is a comparison between two things that were both supposed to follow the book. It now compares the store against the book, which is what a staleness check on a mirror was always for.

WHAT THE SUITE CHECKS INSTEAD. That the tools keep NO typed copy, that what they read equals the book's own list, and that it leads with salt. Proved red by mutation: typing the list back in turns the first red, and handing prodOrder a reversed list turns the other two.

t: THE TWO QUOTE KEYS BECOME ONE MAP, SO A THIRD BOOK NEEDS NO CODE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 22 SEP 2026, to state what is product-specific and then to open three more books. The live quotes sat under two top-level keys NAMED AFTER THEIR PRODUCTS, supplierQuote for salt and oilQuote for oil, and they were the one per-product thing in this book that was not a map. Everything else, PRODUCTS, PROD_OPENING, COUNT_ON, PRICE_SET, COST_RULE, TIER_OF, is keyed by product and takes a new book as a data entry. The quotes took a new key, a new global and an edit in three files.

THE DESK'S OWN QUOTES WAS AN ACCESSOR OVER THE PAIR, {salt:()=>supplierQuote, oil:()=>oilQuote}, which is why it sat in NOT_LEDGER: stored, it would have arrived as {"salt":null,"oil":null} with nothing to say a lookup had been lost. QUOTES is the book's own map now, generated into the BOOK block like every other declaration, so it has moved out of NOT_LEDGER and into LEDGER. quoteFor reads the map instead of calling a function, and a product with no quote answers null exactly as an unregistered one used to.

THE LOOKUP THAT COULD NOT FAIL IS THE REASON THIS WENT FIRST. tools/foldcall.mjs read the pair as a literal two-entry object, so a product registered in PRODUCTS but absent from that object yielded undefined, fell to null, and its lot folded with no quote in the dossier while nothing errored and the note was merely worse. That is the shape of bug a third book would have shipped with.

v228 ASKED FOR THIS AND THE PANEL HAS SAID SO EVER SINCE. The supply panel's own comment reads one panel, driven by QUOTES, so a third product needs an entry there and nothing here, and with no quote recorded it tells him to add one to QUOTES. This is that, finished. Two deliberate whole-book reads of the bare salt quote are now QUOTES[DEFAULT_PROD], which is what they meant; oil's redundant product field goes with the collapse, the key being the product, and nothing ever read it.

t: A SECOND FREE UNIT ON THE REWARD: NO CASH, NO REVENUE, RM48 OF COST
n: FOLDED: ONE REDEMPTION ROW FOR CS6-BS, 1 UNIT OF SALT ON 21 SEP. Settled by the reward at RM48 rather than in cash, delivered in full the same day, so nothing is left outstanding. On his ruling of 11 Sep 2026 the row carries both rebate and goodwill, so it stays out of revenue and its RM48 sits as cost at the shelf's own rate. This is the second such redemption for this code since 17 Sep.

UNUSUAL: THE REWARD BALANCE IS THE DESK'S WORD AND CANNOT BE CHECKED HERE. The drafter flagged that 6 earned against 5 applied leaves 1 unit standing, worked out on the desk and not in the book, and the dossier carries no figure that answers it. No price test bites, since no price was charged: the RM51.95 floor and RM160 ask for 1 unit are recorded for the file only. The salt left the shelf and the inventory rolled by it.

t: ONE UNIT OUT AT RM90: UNDER THE PARTY'S OWN RUN, CLEAR OF THE FLOOR
n: FOLDED: ONE SALT SALE, CLOSED ON THE DAY. A single unit went to CS6-BS on 21 Sep for RM90, collected, RM90 cash in and 1 unit moved, so the row opens and closes on the same date with nothing outstanding. At RM90 a unit it sits above the RM52.06 floor for 1 unit and well under the RM160 ask. Costed at RM48 a unit, the inventory's own rate, RM42 on the goods at 46.7%.

UNUSUAL: THE RATE READS LOW AGAINST THE PARTY, AND THE BLEND IS STILL OPEN. The drafter flagged RM90 as 15.9% under the RM107 a unit CS6-BS typically pays across 19 orders, and flagged that RM48 is the inventory average rather than the lot this row draws. The first is a pricing call on his word at the desk; the second is unanswered in the figures given. The inventory released one unit and holds 8, above the reorder mark of 15 only in stated terms.

t: A COLUMN'S MEANING IS A HINT ON ITS HEADING, NOT A SECOND LINE UNDER IT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026, over a picture of the board with BRONZE half off the screen. Three headings carried a 9px line saying what the column was: break-even, the floor, the floor he may go to, the board, and what a stranger pays. A table lays its columns out by what is in them, and a nine-word line is in the heading whatever the figures under it are worth, so the three widest columns on the board were the three carrying prose.

THE WORDS ARE KEPT, IN FULL, AND MOVED ONTO THE HEADING. The heading is its name; the meaning opens under it on hover, as a small bubble. It drops OVER the figures rather than moving them, so nothing reflows when it opens.

HOVER IS NOT ENOUGH ON A PHONE. It opens on FOCUS as well, and the heading is focusable, so a tap opens it and a tap elsewhere closes it; a keyboard reaches it in reading order. The text stays inside the cell rather than in a title attribute, so a screen reader announces the column's meaning with its name and the one reader who cannot hover loses nothing. The heading says it has something to say, with a dotted underline and the help cursor.

AND THE LAST COLUMN'S DROPS LEFT. The board lives in a sideways scroll box, so a bubble reaching past the right edge would be clipped or would widen the scroll. The last column's is anchored to its own right edge; no other column can reach past the table, so no other one is.

THE CHECK THAT EARNED ITS KEEP. The rules first landed inside the 560px block, beside the two rules this table already had there, where a laptop would never have read them and the line would have come back as visible text at full width. The section reads them off the stylesheet the PARSER built, not off the file, which is the only reading that can tell a rule that applies from a rule that was written. Twenty assertions over both books: every heading free of a second line, the hinted ones focusable, the words kept verbatim and still inside their cell, the closed state, the three doors that open it, and the last column's anchor.

t: THE MONTHLY ISSUE IS RETIRED, AND A SEALED ONE IS MADE ONLY WHEN IT IS ASKED FOR
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026, straight after v769: retire the monthly routine. The account is one live document, written into every record by every publish, so it is never more than an hour behind the book. A monthly issue adds nothing to that, and a strip of them on the page says there is something to catch up on when there is not.

IT REFUSES RATHER THAN FORBIDS. A sealed issue is still a real thing, for a dispute or for a position on a day, so make_statements stops before a byte is written and names the way to ask for one in so many words: --new-issue. A rule a tool enforces beats a rule a document asks a reader to remember, which is the same reasoning as the re-issue guard it sits beside.

WHAT IS NOT REFUSED. A RETRY is not a new issue: a folder already holding this issue's files regenerates in place, which is what a re-run after a failure is. An --archive of a past month is not an issue at all, carrying no record, no password and no QR, and goes through. The issues already sealed and sent still publish and still open on the page, because a dated record is not corrected in place.

ONE THING IS HIS AND IS NOT IN THIS REPO: the Cowork task salt-monthly-statements fires from a registry Code cannot see or write. Until he removes it, it will keep waking to say an issue is due that this repo will now refuse to make. The document says so where a reader starts, beside what to run if he ever does want one.

THE CHECKS. Seven assertions: a new month refused with the reason and the flag, and nothing written; the flag sealing it as before; a retry going through without it; an archive going through; the command line carrying the flag to the guard; and the routine's own document saying it is retired, when, and what to run. Six mutations, each red.

t: THE MINT READS THE MASTER WHERE EVERY OTHER TOOL READS IT, SO THERE WAS NOTHING TO SET
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026: "help me set the environment so the accounts can be minted". There was nothing to set. statements/_secrets.json carries the master beside the key on his laptop, and has since the first issue; every other tool reads it from there, with an environment variable of either name overriding the file. v707 read the environment ALONE, so a laptop that already held the master was refused, and the sweep v767 added then reported him stuck on every run of the chain.

THE SAME RULE, READ OUT IN FULL. It is not loadSecrets itself, which returns as soon as a KEY is in the environment: in the cloud there is no file to fall back to and that is right, but here there is, and a shell holding STMT_KEY would lose the master sitting beside it. The file is read BOM-stripped and every value trimmed, for the reason loadSecrets states: a passphrase with an invisible byte on it derives nothing and says nothing about why.

AND WHEN THE TWO DISAGREE, THE ENVIRONMENT WINS, which is the only order that lets a shell correct a file that has gone stale. It is proved by making them disagree rather than by reading the line: the file is given a passphrase that unwraps nothing, and the mint still goes through.
THE CHAIN'S LINE NAMES BOTH PLACES now, where it named a variable; and the refusal it is keyed on says what is missing, a master passphrase, rather than the name of one way of supplying it.

THE CHECKS. Twenty assertions in v767's own section: the master in neither place still refuses and still names who; the master in the FILE alone mints, with a byte order mark and pasted spaces on it; the two disagreeing takes the environment's. Five mutations, each red, including the one that restores v707's reading exactly.

t: A TREE BEHIND ORIGIN DOES NOT SHIP, BECAUSE THE CHECK THAT SAYS SO NOW STOPS THE RUN
n: HIS PHONE READ YESTERDAY, AND HE ASKED WHY. At 14:36 KL a checkout sitting on the previous morning's v733 was put through tools/update.mjs. The preflight fetched, found origin four versions ahead, and printed FAIL. Then the run built, DEPLOYED v733 over v768, committed a version master already carried, and stopped at the push. The desk served yesterday's build for eight minutes until it was put back by hand.

THE CHECK WAS RIGHT AND DID NOT BITE. It has been in the preflight since 10 Sep 2026, written for exactly this, and it called fail(), which on this tool records a problem, prints it and RETURNS. Every other step that matters exits; this one did not. It is the same shape as a gate behind a pipe: the answer was correct, it was reported, and nothing acted on it.

THE VERDICT IS A VALUE NOW, in tools/preflight.mjs, because update.mjs runs its whole chain on import and nothing inside it can be put under an assertion; commitmsg.mjs was carved out for the same reason and says so. The chain reads the verdict and exits on it.

AND THE LINE MOVED, from "not going to push" to "not going to touch anything". The old gate excused a run with --no-push, which still DEPLOYS, and the deploy is the half that reached his phone. Only --dry, which writes nowhere, is told and allowed to carry on.

THE CHECKS. Eight assertions: level carries on; four behind stops, and says how far, what to run and what it is refusing; a dry run is told the same and not stopped; the count arrives as the string git prints and as a number and both stop; nothing empty is read as behind. Six mutations, each red, including the one that restores the old behaviour exactly.

t: THE ACCOUNT IS ONE LIVE DOCUMENT, AND THE MESSAGE THAT HANDS IT OVER SAYS SO
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026, reading the message he was about to send. "There will be no monthly statement, just a single live version." Both messages opened Your statement of account for September 2026 is ready and closed by promising each monthly statement as it was issued. That was true of a monthly issue and is not true of this.

THE MESSAGE HANDS OVER AN ACCOUNT. It opens "Your account is ready to use", says the three things it is for (the statement of account, which keeps up with the orders; the latest prices; a form to place an order), and says where a question goes. A question goes ON AN ORDER, because that is where the thread lives (v751), and "ask us anything" would promise a channel that is not there. Then the home screen steps for both phones, and Remember me and Log out, in the door's own words so the message and the page cannot differ.

AND THE PAGE OPENS ON THE WHOLE ACCOUNT. v690 opened on the newest month because a monthly statement was what a reader had come for; with one live document it hid the rest of somebody's own account behind a tap they had no reason to take. A month is still one tap, for a reader who wants one. The issues already sealed and sent are untouched and still open on the page: a dated record is not corrected in place.
NEITHER MESSAGE TAKES A MONTH ANY MORE, so a caller that has not caught up cannot put one back by passing one, which is asserted by passing one.

THE CHECKS. Eighteen assertions over both messages: no month and no monthly promise anywhere, the opening line, the three things, where a question goes, the home screen steps and the two switches, the lock every word sent to a customer passes, no password in either, and what each road still has to say for itself. The statement's own section is restated: it opens on the whole account, a month narrows it, All brings it back. Seven mutations, each red.

t: THE MOMENT ON A CUSTOMER'S MARK ORDERS IT, AND THE WORD RIDES ALONG
n: FOUND BY THE FULL SUITE, ON A SECTION THAT PASSED ALONE EVERY TIME. v760 marks what a customer did as <moment>|<what>, one string so it still compares as one, and the desk compared the whole of it. On a TIE in the millisecond the word decided, and "cancel" sorts under "pay": a withdrawal landing in the same millisecond as a payment read as OLDER than the mark and woke nobody. Two moves made in memory land in one millisecond often enough that a full run found it three times; a run of that section alone never did.

THE MOMENT IS THE ORDER. The prefix decides, and where the prefix ties, anything else on the mark means something happened. That is the whole of the fix, and it is the second time this week that a thing which passes alone and fails in company turned out to be an instrument that could not force the state it proved (v754 was the first).

THE TIE IS NOW FORCED RATHER THAN WAITED FOR: the section writes both marks on the same millisecond with the lower-sorting word last, and asserts the wake. Three mutations, each red, including the old comparison restored.

t: AN ID ADDED IS AN ACCOUNT, MINTED BY THE LAPTOP'S OWN CHAIN WITHOUT BEING ASKED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026: Add ID and Amend ID must carry the username, the account and its password. v707 built the mint and left it a command somebody had to think of running, so CZ5-TM, registered on 19 September, held an address and nothing behind it for two days: named on every publish, in a log nobody reads.

AMEND ID WAS ALREADY WHOLE, and it is worth saying why rather than leaving it to be rediscovered: an account is keyed by the USERNAME. A re-key moves the username to the new code and the password with it, so the record behind it never moves at all, and the customer signs in on the same address the next morning.

WHERE IT CAN RUN, STATED RATHER THAN WISHED. An account is a record sealed under the CONTENT KEY, with a password sealed under his master. Neither may reach the cloud, which is rule 2 and is the whole reason a stranger with the runner's secrets cannot open every statement on the site. So the fold that mints the username in CI cannot mint the account behind it, and this is not a limitation to engineer around. THE LAPTOP'S OWN CHAIN DOES IT, before the build, so what it writes is committed by the same run and uploaded by the next publish: the gap closes at the next update rather than at the next monthly issue.

AND WHERE IT CANNOT, IT SAYS SO IN HIS TERMINAL. Without the master it names exactly who cannot sign in and the one command that fixes it, as a WARNING, which is the difference between this and a line in a CI log. It does not stop the run: an update held over an account is a worse trade than an account minted a run later. Asking who is stuck no longer needs somebody already able to fix it, which is why it can be asked at all.

THE CHECKS. Seventeen assertions: who is stuck read off the records with no master and with a bucket and a supplier on the roster, the sweep declining off the laptop, naming them with no master and writing nothing, minting with it, the password it minted answering the verifier it wrote and sealed under the master so Send can hand it over, nobody stuck afterwards, a second run doing nothing, and what the chain SAYS in each of its seven states, driven as a function because everything in that file happens on import. Nine mutations, each red.

t: WHAT IS WAITING ON THE SITE IS ON TODAY, RANKED AGAINST EVERYTHING ELSE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026: SITE ORDERS REACH THE DESK COMPREHENSIVELY. An order lived on one card under Enter. Today exists to rank everything that needs him by the money at stake, and it ranked everything EXCEPT the one item with a customer standing at the other end of it: a stranger who had ordered and was waiting for a yes appeared nowhere on the list a visit to the desk begins with, and nowhere in the count on the rail.

A PLACEMENT IS NOW, because somebody is waiting on him, and the money is what was ordered, goods and carriage together, which is exactly what the pending row will carry. An order waiting on an ANSWER (v752) is named in the same row rather than ranked as a second item: it is the same card, and one trip answers both.

AN ORDER ALREADY AGREED SAYS NOTHING HERE. It is a row, and the book's own readings, the receivable, the advance, the cover, carry it from the moment it folds. Counting it here as well would put the same money on the list twice, which is the fault v385 fixed on the debts and v578 fixed on the breaches.

ONE READING, FOR THE LIST AND FOR THE RAIL. The count on the rail is this same list filtered to Now, so it follows without being told; and because actions() walks the whole forecast to answer, the rail is recounted when what is waiting CHANGES and not on every thirty-second draw.

THE CHECKS. Seven assertions: nothing said with nothing read off the site, two placements as one Now row at RM325 with the carriage in it, the answer named in the same row, the rail's Now count moving by exactly one, an acknowledged order saying nothing, and the one reading counting a placement and not an order he has already answered. Six mutations, each red.

t: APPROVE KEEPS ITSELF CURRENT WHILE IT IS ON SCREEN, AND NEITHER CARD POLLS A POCKET
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026. Site orders has followed the site at the phone's own pace since v499. Approve never did: a row that landed while he was looking at it did not appear until he left the part and came back. v762 makes that the likeliest minute of all to be sitting here, because a tap on Site orders now queues and drafts in about a second.

THE SAME PACE, STATED ONCE, and it lives only while the part is on screen: the moment the card is gone, the timer clears itself rather than reading a keyed endpoint for something nobody is looking at.

TWO GUARDS, AND BOTH CARDS TAKE THEM. Not while a decision is in flight, because a redraw would put the buttons back under a thumb mid-tap. Not while the page is hidden, because a phone in a pocket reading a keyed endpoint every half minute is a battery and a bill and answers nobody. Site orders had neither and now has both.

THE CHECKS. Eight assertions, driven through a captured interval rather than a slept thirty seconds: the read and the pace, the timer existing at all, a tick reading again, a tick over a decision reading nothing, a tick while hidden reading nothing, the page coming back, the timer standing down when the part leaves, and both cards carrying one pace and the same two guards. Six mutations, each red.

t: WHAT HE RECORDS ON THE DESK REACHES THE CUSTOMER'S ORDER, AND THE CHASE STOPS
n: EVERY ROAD BUILT SINCE v694 RUNS ONE WAY. The customer says what they paid, he says what he handed over on the card, and the reconcile queues the entries. Nothing ran the other way. So a payment he took in cash and typed on the desk reached the ROW and never the ORDER: the customer's page said nothing had been paid, and the site's hourly chase asked them for it again every hour, day and night. That happened on 20 September and was patched by hand, which is not a fix.

THE ROW IS FOUND BY THE KEY THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT WROTE, among EVERY sale and not the open ones. The case this exists for is a row he has settled in full, and a settled row is exactly the one that has left the open list. The figures are the engine's own readings of that row, so the desk and the row cannot disagree about what has been paid.

IT ONLY EVER RAISES, AND IT MOVES THE MARK WITH IT. A customer's own word is never erased by a row that has not caught up, and the figure travels with the mark moved to match, or the next pass would queue an entry for a payment already on the row and count it twice. Both guards are real and they are in different places: the desk decides what is worth saying, the site decides what it will take, and each is proved on its own.

ONCE A BOOK, NOT ONCE A MINUTE. A fold mints a version and re-seeds the mirror, so the pass compares that version against what it last told the site: one cheap read a minute, a full pass only when something has actually landed, and not one call to the site in between. The mark moves only on a clean pass, so an order the site refused is tried again the next minute rather than waiting for the next fold. The order settles itself on what it was told, exactly as it does when the customer pays, and they are woken: their payment has been recognised.

THE CHECKS. Eleven assertions: an order reading nothing paid over a row settled in full, the telling, the mark moving with it, the order completing and saying where the figure came from, the chase having nothing left to ask for, the forward pass queueing nothing afterwards, a second pass asking the site nothing at all, a row behind the customer not being sent and being refused if it were, and a refusal leaving the mark where it was. Eight mutations, each red.

t: A CLOSED ORDER CAN BE OPENED ON THE CARD, READ AND ANSWERED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026. The card has shown the OPEN orders since v499 and, since v752, any whose last line is the customer's. So a question about an order he finished last week was answerable for exactly as long as they happened to be the last to speak, and an order that went through without a word could never be looked at again at all. The relay has taken every order since v694 and nothing on the phone ever asked it for them.

ONE SWITCH, AND THE SAME CARD. Show the closed ones asks the relay for all of them, newest first; the line beside it says which list is on screen, and so does the line where a list is empty. A closed order draws its figures, the ledger's own word for it and its thread, with the box to answer in; what it does not draw is a move, because there is none left to make.

THE SWITCH SURVIVES BEING USED, which is not free: it sits outside the box the card redraws, so it is disabled on the tap and re-enabled on the draw. Left as it was, one tap would have been all it ever took, and the second would have done nothing at all. The check that caught it is the one that taps it twice.

THE CHECKS. Nine assertions: the switch and its line, the first read asking for the open ones, a tap asking for all of them, the label and the empty line both following, a second tap putting it back, and a finished order carrying its thread, its answer box, no move and the word Completed. Five mutations, each red.

t: AN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, A HANDOVER OR A WITHDRAWAL REACHES THE LEDGER ON THE TAP
n: THE ROW USED TO WAIT FOR THE NEXT MINUTE. v694 made the every-minute reconcile the ONE road that queues a site order's stages, so nothing could queue a stage twice, and it ran on the cron alone. He acknowledged an order and then waited up to a minute, looking at an Approve card with nothing on it, before the row existed at all.

THE SAME CALL ON THE SAME ROAD, BESIDE THE ANSWER. A move of his runs the reconcile in the request's own tail, so the row is queued and drafted in about a second. The cron still runs every minute as the net, and the marks the reconcile writes onto the order are what stop a stage being queued twice, so it does not matter which of the two gets there first: that was the point of writing them on the order rather than counting on one clock.

ONLY A MOVE. A mark is the reconcile's own bookkeeping written back onto the order, and answering it with another reconcile would be the desk talking to itself; a line on the thread moves no goods and no money. And it does not wake him, for the same reason a row he typed does not (v759): this is his own tap, and the desk draws the row under Approve while he is looking at it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE. A handover's Correction still WAITS for the pending row to be folded, because it amends a row that has to exist first. The tap makes the desk ask sooner; it does not let a stage jump the order they happen in.

THE CHECKS. Seven assertions: the acknowledgement queueing inside the same request, the entry being the row the reconcile has always written with goods and carriage apart, the road named in the log, no banner, a mark and a message queueing nothing and not even asking, and a handover asking and being told to wait. Four mutations, each red.

t: A NOTICE REACHES EVERY PHONE THAT ASKED, AND THE BANNER IT DRAWS IS THE NOTICE'S OWN WORDS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026, beside the three wakes on his own phone: the notice for the customer side as well. Since v732 it was written to the store, drawn on the door at first paint and picked up by an open page's poll, so anybody who had shut the page found out whenever they next opened one. A notice that says the shop is closed on Friday is worth nothing on Saturday.

EVERY PHONE ON THE SITE, WHICH IS WHO A NOTICE IS FOR. The reader that lists one customer's subscriptions now takes no customer and lists them all, and both roads share one send, so a notice and an order update cannot drift apart in how they are signed or in how a dead subscription is cleared. Its own collapsing topic, so a notice does not replace an order's banner on the lock screen and neither replaces the other. Clearing a notice wakes nobody: there is nothing to read.

AND THE BANNER SAYS WHAT THE NOTICE SAYS. A push carries no payload, so the wake itself cannot say which kind it is. The notice is the one thing this service worker may read, because the notice is PUBLIC: the door draws it before anybody signs in and the page polls it unsigned-in. It carries its own moment, and one set inside the last two minutes is what this wake is about. Being wrong costs a customer the notice's first line instead of a line about an order that is on their page anyway; being right means the notice actually arrives. Nothing about a statement is read, held or cached, which was the whole of this script's posture and still is.

THE CHECKS. Eleven assertions: one customer's own wake still reaching their phones and nobody else's, a notice reaching all three and clearing the one the service has given up on, the two topics, setting waking them and saying how many, clearing waking nobody, and the banner over a fresh notice, a one-line notice, an old one, no notice and a site that will not answer. Seven mutations, each red. The script still carries no lone backslash and no backtick, being shipped inside a template literal.

t: A CUSTOMER PAYING OR TAKING AN ORDER BACK WAKES HIM, AND THE BANNER SAYS WHICH
n: THE SITE HAS WRITTEN THE MOMENT OF EVERY CHANGE SINCE v694, AND NOBODY READ IT. The desk asked the site for it every minute, took the placement and the line written on an order, and threw the rest away. So a customer settling RM435 at midnight, or taking an order back before the goods moved, woke nobody: it sat there until he next opened the desk. Measured 21 Sep 2026, beside the two wakes v759 found.

A MARK ONLY THEIR OWN MOVES WRITE. Waking on last-touched was never the answer, because HIS moves write it too: the reconcile has to list after a handover, so his own tap would have buzzed his own phone. last-theirs is written by a payment and a withdrawal and by nothing else. Choosing a rail is not news, and a line they wrote already has its own mark.

IT CARRIES WHAT HAPPENED, NOT ONLY WHEN. The moment first, so it still compares as a string and the mark still works; then the word. The desk cannot ask afterwards, because by then the order reads the same whichever it was. The banner is built from the summary and from nothing else, so the desk remembers the line for ten minutes and the wake reads A customer has paid over what is waiting, rather than reporting a count that was as true an hour ago.

THREE MARKS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A placement, a line and a payment each keep their own: with one between them, the second thing to happen in a minute looks older than the mark and is never seen at all. One wake still goes out, because four banners is a chore and a chore is swiped away unread.

THE CHECKS. Fourteen assertions: his acknowledgement writing the shared mark and not theirs, and waking him not at all; a rail chosen writing nothing; a payment writing the moment and the word; the site handing it over on the desk key alone; the wake, and the same payment not waking him every minute after; a placement and a withdrawal inside one minute both seen and one banner sent; the summary carrying the line and dropping it once stale; and the banner in both states. Nine mutations, each red.

t: EVERY WAKE THE DESK MINTS REACHES THE PHONE, AND THE BANNER NAMES WHAT IS WAITING
n: THE DESK MINTS THREE KINDS OF WAKE AND HIS PHONE ASKED FOR ONE. Measured on the live store, 21 Sep 2026: all three subscriptions carried topics: ["orders"], from the day v675 brought the switch back, and sendPush drops what a subscription does not name. So a row drafted from a CUSTOMER'S order waited under Approve in silence, and the morning round has not reached a phone since 16 September. v708 says that round is what chases money he is holding that is somebody else's; the RM20 over-tender has been open since 26 August and nothing ever rang.

HIS INSTRUCTION OF 21 SEP 2026: ALL THREE. The switch now asks for the order, the row waiting for approval and the morning round, and an old subscription is widened without a tap: the record is keyed by the endpoint's hash, so the card posts it again once a load where one is already on file. A switch he turned on in September must not have to be turned off and on again to hear what it was always meant to hear.

WHAT v675 WAS PROTECTING IS KEPT, AT THE SOURCE. The reason for orders-only was that a row he had just typed should not buzz the phone he typed it on. That is now where it belongs: a row drafted ON ARRIVAL pushes nothing, and the two roads that find a row he was NOT watching for, the orders reconcile and the quarter-hour net, still do. Narrowing it at the subscription silenced the morning round as well, which is the shape of that mistake.

AND THE BANNER STOPS HIDING THINGS. It returned on the first customer order before the list was even built, so while any order was waiting the wake said nothing about a row owed a decision, an entry refused, or a shelf not counted. The order still leads, because it is the one thing a customer is waiting on, and the rest follows it. The refund is named first and the summary counts it, read exactly as the nudge reads it: without that, the round he now actually receives could say square over money that is somebody else's.

THE CHECKS. Fourteen assertions: the three wakes fired against the shape his phone really carried and the shape it carries now, the switch's one list, the silent upgrade and that it happens once a load and not once a draw, both roads to the drafter drafting the same entry with only one of them ringing, the summary counting an open refund and neither a paid one nor a row that will not parse, and the banner in three states. Seven mutations, each red. THE SUITE'S OWN FIXTURES WERE WIDER THAN HIS PHONE: v675's second device and v708's both carry no topics at all, so both proved a send his own device would have filtered, which is why this section pins the shape rather than the send.

t: THE LIVE-BOOK CHECKS PROVE THE RULE, NOT THE DAY'S FIGURES
n: THREE RUNS WENT RED THIS MORNING ON A BOOK THAT WAS RIGHT. His three folds of 21 September, two orders settled, three sales landed and a hand count of the salt, turned three assertions red at the last step of a live run: the salt was "last counted on 19 September", the stated inventory "stands where v744 left it" at 22.65 unit, and CE4-CHE's reward pool was RM1,017. Every one of them was true when it was written and none of them was the rule it was there to prove. The phone was already serving the build; what failed was the instrument.

A CHARGE IS A DIFFERENCE, SO IT IS MEASURED AS ONE. v733's rule is that a free unit shrinks the reward and a withdrawn one does not. That is now proved by dropping the row and recomputing: the gift CE4-CHE never received must move their pool not at all, a live gift must give back exactly its cost, and CN6-WM's two must give theirs back on an associate's pooled figure. None of the three pins a pool, and the cost is read off the row rather than stated, because a row carrying no cost of its own is charged at the book's weighted average, which moves with every lot.

A COUNT THAT COVERS THEM, NOT THE COUNT THAT WAS NEWEST. v750's three September orders may not roll the stated figure, and what proves it is a salt count dated on or after the last of their days, plus a note trail carrying no roll of that version's. A row dated past every count now fails it, which is the fault worth catching; a later count does not. The census of gifts is loosened the same way: four are named because four were here, not because a fifth would be wrong.

THE CHECKS. Seven mutations, each red: a withdrawn gift charging the pool with both its guards dropped (one guard alone changes nothing, the status test already catches it, which is the sort of thing only a mutation tells you), the gift standing again, the charge added instead of subtracted, a gift marked as a redemption, a roll of v750's written into the stock trail, and one of the three rows dated after every count. 37 assertions over the two sections, green.

t: A HAND COUNT OF SALT CUTS THE BOOK BY 3.15 UNIT
n: FOLDED: A SALT COUNT DATED 21 SEP. Eight unit counted by hand against 11.15 on the book, a drift of minus 3.15 unit. The last count was 19 Sep, two days back, so the gap sits in a short window with no moves recorded between. A count wins over the ledger, so the stated inventory is set to 8 and COUNT_ON for salt moves to 21 Sep. No cash and no party attach to this row.

WHAT IT DID TO THE DESK. The shrinkage books across every unit sold, and the floors lift accordingly: one unit from RM50.39 to RM52.06, two unit from RM100.79 to RM104.13, and 12.5 unit from RM629.93 to RM650.80. The ask holds at RM160 for one unit. Self use cost rises from RM74.55 to RM77.70. At 8 unit the stock sits under the reorder mark of 15, with nothing owed out and nothing promised.

t: A CORRECTION ON S187: THE 19 SEP SALT SALE MOVES TO R3 AND TO CM4-MK
n: FOLDED: one correction, recorded 21 Sep against s187, the 19 Sep salt sale of 4 unit for RM340 with RM20 of delivery, RM360 cash in and 4 unit delivered. The patch sets the stream from R2 to R3 and moves the row from CS6-BS-R to CM4-MK. No cash and no stock move: it changes only what the row says about itself, and the row is not rewritten here.

UNUSUAL: the drafter flagged three things. RM360 stands against goods of RM340, so RM20 reads as overpaid; CM4-MK usually pays about RM102.17 a unit over 10 orders, against RM85 here, 16.8% below; and RM48 a unit is the inventory average across more than one lot rate, not the lot this row draws. The figures carried here do not settle the blend, which stays open for checking.

INVENTORY: nothing moved. Stock stays at 11.15 unit on the counts of 19 Sep, costed at RM48 a unit against a replacement of RM45.56, with nothing owed out, nothing promised and no loans open. Reorder still sits at 15 unit, so the book remains under that mark. CS6-BS-R carries nothing outstanding and nothing on credit after the move.

t: TWO ORDERS SETTLED IN FULL AND THREE 19 SEP SALES LANDED
n: FOLDED: TWO FULFILMENTS AND THREE NEW SALES. The 20 Sep fulfilments close s177 for CK4-SEN, RM350 and 5 unit, and s159 for CM4-MK, RM110 of money only. Both drafts flag that they settle the order in full, and on the figures given nothing is left outstanding on either. Neither row is recomputed in the note: ovAmend in the master applies the fulfilment, so there is one definition of what a fulfilment does rather than two.

UNUSUAL: THE R2 ROW AND THE LOT BLEND. CS6-BS-R's 4 unit at RM85 a unit is booked as R2 through CS6-BS with CM4-MK named as end buyer, credited nothing and sent no statement, and the rate sits 20.6% under the RM107 a unit CS6-BS usually pays across 19 orders. Against the desk's own ladder it still clears the RM203.95 floor for 4 unit and stays under the RM500 ask.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. Three sales of 19 Sep land against stock: 2.5 unit and 4 unit of salt and 5 unit of oil, all paid and moved on the day. Salt and oil were last counted on 19 Sep. The salt rows carry RM48 a unit, the inventory's own rate, and the blend flag on that average is left open on both. No lot landed, so the cost basis is unchanged at RM48 a unit.

t: THE COLLISION TEST SPENDS THE MILLISECOND THE QUEUE HOLDS, NOT THE ONE THE HISTORY SHOWS
n: THE SUITE WENT RED ON A SECTION NOTHING HAD TOUCHED. v731 proves that a withdrawal stamped in the acknowledgement’s own millisecond takes the next one rather than vanishing into its draft id. To force that, the test restamped the withdrawal onto the acknowledgement EVENT’S moment. The millisecond that is actually spent is the acknowledgement ENTRY’S, the mark queued.ack, and the two differ the moment two orders are acknowledged inside one millisecond: queueSale gives the second the next free stamp, so the mark moves and the event does not. On a full run of 230 sections that happened; alone it never did.

IT PASSED ALONE AND FAILED IN A FULL RUN, WHICH IS THE SIGNATURE OF AN ASSERTION THAT CANNOT FORCE THE STATE IT PROVES. The test now reads the mark and restamps the withdrawal onto that, so the collision is guaranteed whatever else the queue holds, and the bump is proved rather than hoped for. No code moved: the behaviour was right on every run, and the instrument was the thing that could not see it.

THE CHECKS. Two mutations each turned the section red: the line that gives a collided stage the next millisecond removed, and the marks not read as spent at all. A third, aiming the collision back at the event, is NOT listed as a proof: alone it stays green, which is the whole fault being fixed here and cannot be shown in one section.

t: HE ANSWERS ON THE ORDER, AND THE WORDS ARE CHECKED ON THE DESK BEFORE THEY LEAVE IT
n: THE OTHER HALF OF v751, and the end of what he asked when this work began: a customer may write on an order, and now he writes back. A box under the thread on the Site orders card, a line, sent. It is a move of his like any other, so it wakes them on their phone; it is not a state, so nothing about the order moves but the thread, which the suite asserts field by field.

THE SAME LOCK AS THE BULLETIN, siteWords, and the same one rather than a second copy of it. What he types here lands on a page that never names this desk, never shows a roster code and never names a level, and a slip of the thumb is how one gets there. It is checked on the DESK and not on the site, because the site holds no roster and would not know a code if it saw one. A refused line never reaches the site at all, which is asserted by counting the calls. A product's name is his to spend, exactly as it is in the bulletin: the phone warns and lets it go.

TWICE, AND ON PURPOSE. The phone refuses it before it leaves, which is the kinder place to be told; the Worker refuses it whatever asks, which is the place that has to hold. NO CAP ON HIS OWN LINES: the twenty v751 set counts THEIRS, and a man answering his own customers is not a thing to ration.

THE CHECKS. Seventeen assertions: the answer on the thread with its spacing collapsed, the order's state, payment, handover and history all unmoved, the order no longer waiting so a closed one leaves his card, an empty answer refused, a long one cut, more answers than the customer's own cap allows, the three refusals each proved to have reached the site zero times, a product's name going through, the lock being the bulletin's own, the box and the button on the card, and the phone's own reading of the same four lines. Ten mutations each turned it red, including the two that matter: the desk relaying his words unchecked, and the desk checking them and relaying them anyway.

t: THE DESK READS THE THREAD ON ITS CARD, KEEPS AN ORDER WAITING FOR AN ANSWER, AND IS WOKEN BY A LINE
n: v751 LET A CUSTOMER WRITE ON ANY ORDER AT ANY STAGE, AND TWO THINGS ON THIS SIDE HAD NOT CAUGHT UP. The Site orders card lists the OPEN orders, so a question asked about one he had closed reached a record nothing on his desk drew; and nothing woke him for a line either, because the nudge compared the newest PLACEMENT against its one mark and a message is not a placement.

AN ORDER WAITING FOR AN ANSWER IS STILL HIS TO LOOK AT. The test is the thread's last line: theirs, and it is waiting; his, and it is not. So a closed order a customer has written on comes back onto the card and leaves it again when he answers, which means the card carries exactly what is owed a reply and nothing else. The read that asks for every order still gets every order.

A LINE WAKES HIM, ON ITS OWN MARK. The site's one-read-a-minute answer carries when a customer last wrote beside when one was last placed, and the nudge holds two marks. On one mark a message arriving in a quiet hour would be measured against the newest placement and read as old news, and a placement would bury an unanswered line; each is asserted the other way round. A mark moves whether or not the push reached anybody, because a wake that failed is not a reason to wake for the same line every minute until it does.

THE THREAD IS DRAWN ON THE CARD, oldest first, his lines marked You and theirs marked by their code, under a heading that says when the order is waiting for an answer. Every line goes through esc: a customer's own words are the one free text on this desk that a stranger typed, and an order card is built by interpolation.

THE CHECKS. Seventeen assertions: the waiting test on four shapes of thread, the card's list holding the open order and the closed one that asked a question and neither of the other two, the site's one read carrying all three moments, then a placement waking him, the same placement not waking him twice, a line waking him on its own, the same line not twice, a later placement not re-reading the old line and a later line not re-reading the placement, a line waking him on a site where nothing was ever placed, and the card itself drawn three ways: waiting, answered, and an order nobody wrote on. Nine mutations each turned it red, including the customer's words written onto the card raw.

t: A CUSTOMER MAY WRITE A LINE ON AN ORDER, AT PLACEMENT AND AFTER, AND IT NEVER REACHES A LEDGER NOTE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 20 SEP 2026, and the last part of what he asked when this work began: can a customer chat about an order, or leave a comment. Both, and they are one thing. An order carries a THREAD, msgs[], each line {at, by, text}, and the line typed on the order form is simply its first message rather than a comment field sitting beside a conversation. One list to read, on their page and on his.

ON ANY ORDER, AT ANY STAGE. A question about an order that has been withdrawn or completed is still a question about that order, and sending them elsewhere to ask it is how a conversation leaves the record it belongs to. Twenty lines of THEIR OWN an order, two hundred characters each, and the cap counts only theirs, so an answer never uses up their allowance; the line on the form is shorter at 140, being an aside rather than a reply. Every line is collapsed to single spaces and trimmed, because whitespace is where a long silent block hides and a line drawn on a page has to be one line.

IT NEVER RIDES INTO A LEDGER NOTE. This is the second piece of free text a customer types, after the general location v694 takes for a delivery, and it is held to exactly that rule: a note reaches the committed book, and what a customer typed could carry a street or a name. The four entries an order can queue are built from fixed words and figures, and the suite now forces a customer's own words and a street into an order and asserts that not one of them reaches an entry.

THE SITE MARKS WHEN SOMETHING WAS LAST SAID, last-said, beside the marks that already say when an order was last placed and last touched. Nothing reads it yet; it is what will wake him rather than making him poll.

THE CHECKS. Fifteen assertions driving the site's own Worker: the line on the form opening the thread with its spacing collapsed, an order placed with nothing to say carrying an empty thread rather than a missing one, a later line appended to the same thread, the mark moving to it, an empty line refused, the route taking a session like every other, a long line cut, the twenty-first of their own refused, an answer counted as his, a line still reaching a withdrawn order, and the four entries built from an order carrying a street and a name and clean of both. Ten mutations each turned it red, including the one that matters most: the customer's words put into the ledger's own note.

t: THE THREE ORDERS OF 16, 18 AND 19 SEPTEMBER EACH READ 5 UNIT, RM420 AND RM15 OF CARRIAGE, COMPLETED
n: HIS WORD OF 20 SEP 2026: there should be three completed orders of 5 unit at RM420 plus RM15 of delivery, on 16, 18 and 19 September. Two of the three did not say so. The 16th's row, s168, had its carriage zeroed by a correction of that same day and took RM420 where RM435 was owed, so it alone of the three carried no delivery charge and RM15 less cash; the 18th's, s173, carried its carriage but said nothing about who moved the goods, which on this book is not a third answer but no answer. The 19th's already read right.

THE GOODS ARE UNCHANGED AND THE CARRIAGE IS BESIDE THEM, which is where it has sat since v727: RM420 of salt, RM15 to bring it, RM435 owed and RM435 in. Both rows now say the salt was delivered rather than collected, because a delivery charge is what he drove for, and a row that charges for the trip and says the customer came to fetch it is a contradiction the drafter refuses at entry.

NOTHING ROLLS OFF THE SHELF, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE CARE HERE. Only money and a word move: the salt left the shelf on the days those rows already state, all three of them on or before 19 September, and salt was COUNTED on 19 September at 0.9 unit. A count is the truth at its moment, so everything sold before it is already out of the counted figure; rolling these would take the same 5 unit off twice. The stated inventory stands where v744 left it at 22.65 unit, and no roll note is written, which is itself asserted.

AND THE SITE DISAGREES ABOUT THE 16th, DELIBERATELY LEFT. That order was placed on the website to COLLECT with no delivery charge, and the website holds nothing paid and nothing handed over against it. His word is what the book follows. The customer's own page still shows that order as it was placed; aligning it is a separate decision, because it rewrites what a customer sees rather than what the book says.

THE CHECKS. Nine assertions over the three rows read through the engine: one on each of the three days, each 5 unit with RM420 of goods and RM15 of carriage, RM435 owed and RM435 in, each Completed, each saying the goods were delivered; then the count of 19 September, that all three days fall on or before it, that no roll note was written for this version, and that the stated figure has not moved. Five mutations each turned it red: the carriage zeroed again, RM420 taken again, the handover unsaid again, the shelf rolled by the 5 unit, and a roll note written after all.

t: THE PRICE STACK CARRIES EVERY LEVEL, AND THE FIVE-TIER CARD IS FOLDED INTO IT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 20 SEP 2026, on the two cards side by side: show it for all tiers, probably combinable. The stack gave the size, COGS, break-even and then ONE level, the board's last, with its rate, its margin and its multiple of break-even; the other five sat further down the page as bare totals with none of those three. So the question the stack answers, what a price is worth against what it costs, was answered for the one level a stranger pays and for no other.

ONE TABLE: THE SAME THREE COLUMNS, THEN A COLUMN A LEVEL, each carrying the four lines the ask has carried since v564. Margin is what is left over break-even and the multiple is the price over it, the same arithmetic the ask's own cell has always used. v564 said five columns was what 325px of a 375px screen had room for and it was right: the table scrolls sideways, which is what the card being folded in already did with its six. The separate card is gone rather than left beside it, because one set of prices printed by two pieces of code is how the two drift.

AND THE HEAD IS EACH BOOK'S OWN LEVELS, WHICH IT HAS NEVER BEEN. Salt's rule carries five multiples and yields six levels with Ambassador at the floor; oil's is a fixed price a size, so it yields two, Ambassador and the one a stranger is quoted. The card folded in here printed all six names over oil's two cells from v641 until today, ragged on the page, because its head was asserted against TIER_NAMES and its body against the engine and the two were never asked to agree with each other. A book shorter than six now takes the first name and the last of the rest: its top level IS the board, and the board is the last name.

NOTHING THE OLD CARD SHOWED IS LOST. It drew every rung and marked the ones the board does not print, while the stack has only ever drawn the board's own sizes; the merged table draws every rung, in the ladder's order, and a size off the board still says so. The under-floor census below it still reads the board alone, because that question is about what is printed and not about what is priceable at the counter.

THE CHECKS. Seventeen assertions over both books: the head against each book's own levels, every row as wide as the head, every cell carrying the four lines, every price the engine's for every rung, every margin struck on break-even and every multiple the price over it, one table on the page rather than two, and the levels' sentence moved with them. A size is FORCED off the board to prove the marker, since every size is on it today. Eight mutations each turned it red, including the two faults being fixed: only the board's level drawn, and all six names taken on every book.

t: A CORRECTION ITEMISES WHAT IT CHANGED, ONE LINE A FIELD, IN THE DESK'S OWN MONEY AND UNITS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 20 SEP 2026, on seeing s137's correction render as total 835 → 850; delivery 15 → (cleared) in one right-aligned run: simplify it, or itemise it. It was the fold's own sentence with every to in it rewritten as an arrow and the parts joined by semicolons, so a two-field correction read as prose, the figures carried no RM and no unit, the fold's own (cleared) and (unset) markers were shown to a reader in their brackets, and a flag read true.

ONE CHANGE, ONE LINE. Each claim takes its own line with the field named in words ahead of it, money as RM, quantities in units, a flag as yes or no, and cleared or not set said rather than bracketed. The correctable fields are a closed list, so a claim is cut ONCE, at the first to after its own field name, and the rest of the sentence reaches the page as it was written: where an old value carries the word itself the cut is genuinely ambiguous and the line cannot say which was meant, which is a reason to leave the words alone rather than to rewrite all of them. A claim this desk cannot parse at all is still drawn, in the fold's own words, because going quiet about a correction is the one thing this trail must not do.

THE READER MOVED OUT OF THE TRAIL. It was defined inside tabLedger, so nothing could ask it anything. modBits and modHtml stand at module scope beside the strip that reads the same mod string, and the suite drives them directly.

THE CHECKS. Thirteen assertions: two fields read as two claims, a claim from another day left off the line, a corrected note cut once with its other words whole, a restatement naming no field drawn in the fold's words and reaching the page, five changes as five lines, RM on a money field, the unit on a quantity, yes and no on a flag, the markers in words, no semicolon left, s137's own two lines off the built desk, and the computed display of a change line measured rather than read off the stylesheet. Eight mutations each turned it red, including the two faults being fixed: the claims joined into one run again, and the split made on every to in the sentence.

t: THE LEDGER DESTINATION IS NAMED RECORD, AND ITS OLD ADDRESS STILL LANDS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 20 SEP 2026: the destination called The book becomes Record or Database. Record, because this desk already calls a row's own account of itself the record, and Database names the file rather than what he opens it for. It also ends a collision the rail has carried since v341: two of the seven destinations were called book, and the other one, Order book, is about money owed rather than the ledger.

THE ID IS UNTOUCHED. An id is an address here, /desk#book since v341, and the rule that old tab ids remain addresses is older than the label. So VIEWS carries {id:'book', name:'Record'} and the rail's own button says Record, which is the pair the suite has checked against each other since v571.

THE CHECKS. Four assertions, run red on the desk as v746 left it: the destination's name and its id together, that one destination is left with book in its name, the rail's button read off the built desk, and the old address still opening the section. Three mutations each turned it red: the old name back in the list, the old name left on the button, and the id renamed with the label, which is the one that stops the address landing.

t: THE CORRECTION SENTENCE ON s173 AND s183 STANDS ONCE, AND NO ROW MAY SAY THE SAME THING TWICE
n: v738 WROTE ITS CORRECTION NOTE ONTO BOTH ROWS TWICE. The fold's own applier prepends the note it is handed ahead of what the row said, which is where a row's history comes from; the hand fold that carried v738's two corrections prepended it as well. So s173 and s183 each opened with the same sentence twice, on the desk's card, in the row's own record and in the dossier the next fold is written over. The figures, the trail and the mod line were right throughout: the fault was prose, and nothing on the book could see it.

ONE COPY STANDS, AND THE CENSUS IS THE INSTRUMENT. Every note on the book is read for a row that opens with the same sentence twice over, which is the shape a second prepend leaves. The sentence may close inside a tag, a note opening in bold, so the closing tag is part of the unit and not the end of it: the first cut of this check missed exactly that and passed a doubled note whole.

THE CHECKS. Run red on the book as v745 left it, naming s173 and s183, and green after the repair. Four mutations each turned it red: a note doubled again on the book, the census reading no rows, the applier prepending nothing, and the applier prepending twice, which is the fault itself.

t: THE CARRIAGE CHECK READS THE RESTATED ROW'S NOTE, NEVER THE CARRIAGE IT HOLDS TODAY
n: THE SUITE WENT RED ON MASTER WITHIN THE HOUR OF v744. v740 named the twelve rows v727 restated and then looked them up among the rows that carry a carriage TODAY. v744 folded s137's RM15 of carriage back into its total on his own instruction, so s137 left that set, the check counted eleven of twelve and failed, on a row it had nothing to say about and a fold that was entirely correct.

WHAT v727 DID IS DONE, AND THE SENTENCE IS ITS RECORD. The twelve are looked up by rid on the book itself: each must still be there, and each must still say on its own row that its carriage was moved out of the total rather than re-priced. Whether a row still carries a carriage is that row's own business and is tested beside it, on every carriage row there is. This is the third shape of this check in a day: every row with a carriage (v727, red the moment a site order folded with one), a threshold on the rid (v737, red the moment a row older than the cut was given a carriage), and now the set and its sentence, which nothing later can move.

THE CHECKS. Run red against master as v744 left it, eleven of twelve, and green after. Four mutations each turned it red: a row of the set taken off the book by re-keying its rid, the sentence misspelt, the set read off today's carriage again, and the sentence struck off one restated row of the book.

t: TWO ORDERS CLOSED, ONE WITHDRAWN, A CARRIAGE LINE FOLDED INTO THE PRICE
n: WHAT WAS FOLDED: five rows. SA5-BTR's lot p026 of 19 Sep takes its second half, 18.75 unit on 20 Sep with no cash, and closes; CS6-BS-R pays the RM15 of delivery left on s183 and that order closes too. CE4-CHE's pending s180, 2 unit for RM230, is withdrawn on 20 Sep with nothing paid and nothing moved, so it counts nowhere.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL: s137 to CJ4-BJ has the RM15 carriage cleared and the total set to RM850, so the whole figure is now goods on a row already delivered in full with RM50 unpaid and 0.52 unit against the cap. The drafter flagged that RM48 a unit is the inventory average across more than one lot rate, not the lot drawn, and that flag stands open on two rows.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID: a new name, CZ5-TM, buys 1 unit for RM110, collected and paid on 19 Sep, well clear of the RM51.10 floor for that size and under the RM160 ask, with no history of theirs to test it against. The 18.75 unit of p026 land on 20 Sep against a book of 4.9 unit counted 19 Sep, with the reorder mark at 15.

t: TWO CODES FILED: ONE REGISTERED, ONE PLACED, NO FIGURE MOVED
n: FOLDED: A REGISTRATION AND A PLACING. CZ5-TM is appended to the roster as a customer buying direct, opening at Titanium on salt and Titanium on oil, with a point on the map to about a kilometre and a statement username issued if the party has none, kept for life. CA2-SEN is filed as a point on the map at its recorded place, to about a kilometre, and nothing more.

UNUSUAL: NOTHING TO RECONCILE. Neither row touches cash, stock or credit, so no floor, ask, rate or outstanding shifts, and the drafter raised no flag against either. The directory is not touched by the fold: codes and points travel, the names do not. The inventory did nothing: it stands as counted on 19 Sep at 4.9 unit, cost basis unchanged, and no lot landed on this fold.

t: THE ROLL'S BASELINE IS THE ENGINE'S READING AND FOLLOWS THE BATCH, SO TWO AMENDMENTS ON ONE ROW ROLL ONCE
n: v739 STRUCK A CORRECTION'S DIFFERENCE AGAINST THE BOOK AS IT STOOD BEFORE THE BATCH, found the same afternoon by two of three independent reads of its diff. The site queues a correction on every change of an order's running total, so a handover in two stages inside one hour staged corrections of 2 and then 5 and would have rolled 7 for 5 moved; a fulfilment followed by a correction restating the same figure would have rolled twice. And a lot stored without receivedQty, which the engine reads as received in full, read as nought against the raw field, so stating the figure would have landed the lot a second time.

THE PLAN KEEPS WHAT EACH ROW HAS MOVED SO FAR IN THE BATCH, keyed on the book row: a correction is struck from that figure and then sets it, and a fulfilment's units advance it, so the second amendment on a row is measured from where the first left it. The first figure is the engine's own reading, poRecvUnits for a lot and the delivered quantity for a sale, never the raw field, so stating the receipt of a lot the engine already holds moves nothing, and stating that nothing of it arrived rolls it back off the shelf.

THE CHECKS. A section of five assertions on the fold's plan: a handover of 2 then 5 rolling 2 and then 3; a fulfilment of 2 and a correction restating 2 rolling once; a correction restating 5 after it rolling the other 3; a lot held without a received figure moving nothing when the receipt is stated and rolling back 10 when nought is. Three mutations each turned it red: the difference struck against the book before the batch, a fulfilment not carried into the running figure, and a lot's first figure read off the raw field.

t: THE ENGINE'S STATUS AND DATES, THE CUSTOMER'S STATEMENT AND THE ROW EDITOR READ WHAT IS OWED AS THE GOODS AND THE DELIVERY
n: v738 NAMED SIX READERS AND MISSED FOUR, found the same afternoon by three independent reads of its own diff, each finding then put to a refuter. txStat measured paid in full and the paid fraction against the goods, so s183 read Paid and Completed on the Ledger, the Order book, the Workbench's pills and the desk's open count while the Order book's cash table chased its RM15 on the same page. txDates measured paid in full the same way and put the paid-on date v738 had cleared straight back from the cash trail, so v738's correction of s183 changed no reading. The statement's own owed and billed figures read total less cash, so the customer's page said Settled, the footer said Balance nil and the send sheet said the account was clear, with an amount cell whose sub-line still said the delivery was inside the total, which v727 ended. The row editor's outstanding figure read the goods, so Paid in full was not offered on the row that owed it and the panel said nothing was outstanding.

THE SAME ONE READER, txOwed, in all four: txStat's paid in full and paid fraction, txDates' paid in full, the statement's owed and billed, and a sale's total in the row editor, the lot's branch beside it unchanged. The amount cell now says plus delivery. On RM420 paid of RM435 a row reads Partial and Open, Advance, derives no paid-on date, owes RM15 on the statement with Balance outstanding, and offers Paid in full for the RM15; RM435 completes it on the day the RM15 arrived.

THE CHECKS. A section of twelve assertions: the status on RM420, RM435 and with no delivery; the dates with the RM15 owed and the day it arrives; the row editor on a sale with and without a delivery and on a lot; the statement's rows on a copy of the book carrying the case, owed RM15 and Balance outstanding, and settled at RM435; the amount cell's wording; and the live book, no row reading Completed while it owes, which read s183 red before the change. Six mutations each turned it red: each of the three engine reads, the statement's owed and its wording, and the row editor's total, put back to the goods.

t: THE SUITE'S CARRIAGE CHECK NAMES THE TWELVE ROWS v727 RESTATED, BECAUSE A ROW MAY BE GIVEN A CARRIAGE AFTER THE FACT
n: v737's CUT HELD FOR A MORNING. It scoped the check to rows at rid s182 or below, the last rid on the book when v727 restated it, on the reasoning that a rid says which convention wrote a row. v738 then gave s173, a row older than the cut, the RM15 of carriage it never had at v727, and the full suite went red on the same line again: a threshold on the rid says which rows EXISTED that day and not which rows the restatement touched.

THE SET IS THE RECORD. The twelve rows v727 restated are named by rid, s137 to s172, and the check asks two things of them: that each is still on the book with a carriage, and that each says on its own row that it was restated rather than re-priced. Every other carriage row, whenever it was minted and however it came by its carriage, is held to the test beside it alone: the goods are the total and what is owed is more than the goods.

THE CHECKS. The section was run red on the book as v739 left it, thirteen rows against a count of twelve, and green with the set named. Four mutations each turned it red: s173 added to the set, s183 added to the set, the sentence misspelt, and the sentence struck off one restated row of the book.

t: A CORRECTION THAT RESTATES WHAT MOVED ROLLS THE SHELF BY THE DIFFERENCE, AND THE 5 UNIT OF 19 SEP COME OFF
n: THE SHELF SAT 5 UNIT HIGH. v735 folded zhim2a's handover as the Correction v694 routes a handover through, and the fold's rule since v358 was that a correction moves nothing: it adds nothing to the moves the roll is struck from. That rule was written when a correction could not touch deliveredQty. It has been able to since 25 Aug 2026, when what has actually moved became a thing a person states, seven rows on the book carry one, and a site handover is one. So the goods left the shelf on the row and never left the stated figure, while v736's fulfilment to CJ4-BJ the same day did roll: the stated inventory read 9.9 with 4.9 on the shelf.

THE ROW IS THE RECORD OF WHAT MOVED, AND THE ROLL FOLLOWS THE RECORD. A correction naming deliveredQty on a sale, or receivedQty on a lot, now pushes a move for the difference against the row as it stands, in either direction, so a reversal puts the goods back; a lot's is marked landed. It is dated the moved-on date the correction states, else the correction's day. A correction that restates the same quantity, or names none, still moves nothing. The applier is unchanged: it writes the row, and the shelf follows through the plan, which is where every other roll is struck.

THE 5 UNIT ARE ROLLED OFF ON THE BOOK, 9.9 less 5 is 4.9, in the fold's own sentence, a roll and not a count: they came off the 37.5-unit lot landed on 19 Sep, after that day's count, so the count did not already hold them. A count would confirm the figure; nothing else on the book moves.

THE CHECKS. A section of eleven assertions: the plan rolling 5 unit off for a handover, dated the row's own day; a reversal rolling them back on the correction's day; a lot corrected as received rolling on, landed; the same quantity and no quantity moving nothing; the apply taking the stated figure down by 5 and writing the roll in the fold's sentence while the row says what was stated; and the live book carrying v739's roll. Six mutations each turned it red: the roll not pushed, its sign turned, the difference read against nought, the date read off the correction alone, the lot's roll not marked landed, and the book's own roll misfigured.

t: WHAT A CUSTOMER OWES IS THE GOODS AND THE DELIVERY TOGETHER, WHEREVER IT IS READ
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 20 SEP 2026: the amount owing from the customer for the delivery is not to be excluded from the ledger entry. v727 moved the carriage out of a sale's total and gave the engine txPrice on the two together, and six readers went on measuring what was owed as the total less the cash. The open-order shape the drafter reads off the mirror owed the goods alone, so it said RM420 SETTLED a RM435 order; the fold's paid-in-full stamp and the desk's own applier read the same way, so s183 carried paidOn with RM15 still owed; the dossier the fold's note is written over read RM35 left on s137 where the row says RM50, and RM420 outstanding on s183 where it was RM435; the drafter's overpayment flag on a new row would have called RM435 on RM420 of goods an overpayment; and the Workbench's outstanding line on a sale read the goods.

ONE READER NOW, THE ENGINE'S txOwed, exported beside txPrice and txPaid: the goods and the delivery together. The open-order shape owes it and carries the delivery beside the goods as dv, so the Approve card reads 5 unit for RM 420 with RM 15 delivery, RM 435 owed; the fold and the desk stamp paidOn only when the cash reaches it; the dossier's outstanding and defaulted figures read it; the drafter measures a new row's cash against it; the Workbench's sale branch reads it, the lot branch beside it unchanged. Nothing prices on it: the rate and the floor are still struck on the goods, as v727 left them.

TWO ROWS ARE RESTATED ON THE BOOK, THROUGH THE FOLD'S OWN APPLIER. s183, CS6-BS-R's delivery of 19 Sep, has its paid-in-full stamp cleared: RM420 was taken against RM435 and RM15 stays outstanding. s173, CS6-BS's row of 18 Sep, was drafted from site order rkoi5a and filled in by hand at RM420 for the delivery of order 4l1kkq, whose RM15 of carriage was off the book and whose payment of RM435 the site has held since 18 Sep; it now carries delivery 15 and cash 435, so its key becomes CS6-BS|2026-09-18|435, the key that order has waited on since the 18th. Both corrections are on their rows in the mod line and the trail.

THE CHECKS. A section of nineteen assertions: the engine's reader, the fold's stamp on RM420 and then RM15, the open-order shape at RM420 and RM435 and with no delivery, the desk's applier through ovAmend in the built desk, the Workbench line as a source pin, the drafter against a snapshot carrying the delivery and on a new row paid RM435 and RM450, the dossier's figure, and the live book: no row stamped paid while its delivery is owed, and s173 carrying its carriage. Nine mutations each turned it red: the engine dropping the delivery, each stamp and each figure put back to the goods, the delivery taken off the shape and off the card.

t: THE SUITE'S CARRIAGE CHECK IS SCOPED TO THE ROWS v727 RESTATED, SO A SITE ORDER FOLDED WITH A DELIVERY NO LONGER TURNS IT RED
n: THE SUITE HAS BEEN RED ON MASTER SINCE THE v734 FOLD AT 07:48 KL, one assertion of 3,067, on each of the three fold runs since. s183, the pending row folded from site order zhim2a with RM15 of delivery beside RM420 of goods, carries no note saying THE CARRIAGE MOVED OUT OF THE TOTAL. It cannot: v727 wrote that sentence onto the twelve rows it restated, and s183 was born under the new convention with nothing to restate. The check read every carriage row on the live book, so the first row folded with a delivery after the restatement was bound to trip it, and the road v731 repaired delivered exactly that row.

THE CUT IS THE RID. s182 was the last row on the book when v727 ran, and a rid is minted at fold time above every rid on the book, so a carriage row at s182 or below was restated and must say so, while one above it was born with the two figures and is held to the other half of the same check, that the goods are the total and what is owed is more than the goods, which s183 passes. The cut is not the date: a row entered late and dated before 19 Sep carries a low date and a high rid, and it is the rid that says which convention wrote it.

NOTHING ON THE BOOK MOVES. Writing the sentence onto s183 would have gone green in one line and lied on a dated record. The fold runs of v734, v735 and v736 each shipped, proved the phone, marked the rows committed, re-seeded the mirror and published, and turned red only at the suite that runs after; the hourly runs since publish alone and run no suite, so nothing had gone green on master since. The second failure reported beside this one, a desk window still carrying its document after the section that opened it closed, does not reproduce on the jsdom the lock file pins, on this machine or in Actions.

THE CHECKS. The section was run red against the book as v736 left it before the cut was written, and green after. Five mutations each turned it red again: the cut moved one rid up so s183 is asked for a sentence it cannot have, the count moved to thirteen, the sentence misspelt, the cut read on the date instead of the rid (which also pulls s183 in), and the sentence struck off one restated row of the book.

t: TWO FULFILMENTS CLOSE OUT 19 SEP: ONE ORDER PAID IN FULL, ONE MOVED IN FULL
n: FOLDED: TWO FULFILMENTS AGAINST STANDING ORDERS, BOTH DATED 19 SEP. CS6-BS-R's s183 takes RM420 in cash with no units moving, the goods having gone out on the correction of the same day, and the drafter flags it as settling the order in full. CJ4-BJ's s137 takes the remaining 6.25 unit of the 12.5 unit order of 7 Sep with no cash, leaving RM35 outstanding on that row. Neither row is recomputed here: the master applies the amendment.

UNUSUAL: ONE ORDER CLEARS ITS CASH, THE OTHER CLEARS ITS GOODS. The two rows run in opposite directions, so the book loses RM420 of receivable on one side and 6.25 unit of salt on the other. CJ4-BJ's RM35 is the delivery charge left on s137 and stays outstanding. Cost is unchanged at the inventory's own RM48 a unit, a blend of lots, with replacement at RM45.56. No loans are open and no party sits over a cap.

t: A PENDING SALT SALE IS BOOKED OUT: THE GOODS MOVE, THE RM435 DOES NOT
n: ONE CORRECTION FOLDED, NO CASH AND NO STOCK BEHIND IT. The fold patches s183, CS6-BS-R's salt sell of 19 Sep, 5 unit for RM420 with RM15 delivery: delivered quantity from 0 to 5, delivered on from unset to 19 Sep, handover from unset to delivered.
