It changes only what the row says about itself, so the inventory stands where the count of 19 Sep left it, at 16.15 unit against a reorder mark of 15.

WHAT IS UNUSUAL IS THE CREDIT, NOT THE PATCH. The drafter flagged an advance: the goods go out with RM435 unpaid, on top of RM420 outstanding before, against a credit cap of 1 unit with nothing on credit before. He also flagged the RM84 a unit against CS6-BS's usual RM107.5, 21.9% below, and that the RM48 cost is a blend of lots, not the lot this row draws. Neither flag is answered by figures in this fold.

t: A PENDING RESALE ORDER AT RM84 A UNIT: NOTHING PAID, NOTHING MOVED
n: FOLDED: one salt sell to CS6-BS-R, 5 unit for RM420 with RM15 of delivery beside it, RM435 owed, dated 19 Sep as the day it was agreed and taken from order 20260919121050-zhim2a on the statements site. Nothing was paid and nothing was handed over, so the row sits pending: it draws no stock and books no revenue until something moves. Booked as R2, CS6-BS buying to sell on.

UNUSUAL: the rate of RM84 a unit is 21.9% below the RM107.5 a unit CS6-BS typically pays across 18 orders, and below the party's own median of RM96.67. The drafter also flagged that the inventory spans more than one lot rate, so RM48 a unit is the average rather than the lot this row draws, and asked for the blend to be checked before approval. The inventory stands unchanged at 16.15 unit.

t: A FREE UNIT IS A TAP, AND THE REWARD SHRINKS WITH THE GIFT
n: HIS DECISION OF 19 SEP 2026, put to him as a question and answered yes, the reward shrinks with the gift. A free unit handed over alongside an order cost the shelf real salt and was charged against the reward NOWHERE, so a customer earned on the full margin of what they paid for and kept what they were given as well. A gift now comes off the margin the reward is struck on, by what the salt cost.

A GIFT IS goodwill AND NOT rebate, and that distinction is already on every row. A REDEMPTION carries both: it is the customer spending a unit they earned, netted at the reader through rebateApplied, so charging it here would take the same unit twice. rewardMargin is the one place margin becomes units, read by the associates' card and the customers' table alike, so the charge is written once and both follow.

IT IS A SECOND WALK AND NOT A WIDER FILTER, and that is not a matter of style. The tempting one-line version is to stop dropping goodwill rows from pricedSales. It would shrink nothing: a gift's total IS its cost, so its margin is exactly zero, and s056, whose total is the price it was first written at, would ADD RM26.50, the wrong direction entirely. What the rule needs is the gift's COST subtracted, which membership can never produce. An assertion says so, before somebody tries it.

AND A FREE UNIT IS A TAP. Every gift on the book was typed at the laptop, because the only route that minted a goodwill row was Redeem, which settles against a balance the customer earned. A gift is not that. It needs no pane of its own, because a gift IS the sale form with the money taken out: the tick shuts the price, the cash and the carriage and CLEARS them, through the gate v728 built, and the drafter prices the row off the shelf. The price is not his to type, and an entry carrying one is still booked at cost. The Approve card gains a head of its own, because approving a gift and approving a redemption is the same tap and they are opposite transactions.

WHAT IT DOES TO THE BOOK, AND WHAT IT NO LONGER DOES. CC5-OKR is charged the RM48 of s176 and their pool falls to RM163; CN6-WM, an associate, is charged the RM51.50 of s031 and s056 on their pooled figure. Neither crosses a hurdle, so no customer loses a unit. This version was written when one would have: CE4-CHE held s181 and the charge took them from two free units to one. v730 withdrew that gift while this was being built, the unit never having left the shelf, so the row is cancelled and the guard excludes it. The rule did not change; the guard did its work on a row that moved under it, which is the case a fixture can only imitate, and the check now proves it on the live book.

AND v728'S THREE EM DASHES ARE GONE. The gate's labels were written with them, against a standing rule of this project that there are none in files, code or copy. Commas instead. The ones left in the master are older changelog prose, and a dated record is not corrected in place.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 27 assertions: the zero-margin proof that says why the filter cannot be widened, the four gifts and three redemptions told apart on the live book, the charge on a fixture where every figure is known, the redemption NOT charged, the cancelled gift not charged, the tick driven in a real window shutting and clearing three boxes, the entry it queues carrying no money figure, the drafted row against the convention, and both Approve cards DRIVEN rather than pinned as text. Fourteen mutations, every one red; two were green first time and both were weak assertions, one a text pin that a dead branch walks straight through.

t: A BULLETIN RUNS OR CHANGES ACROSS THE TOP OF SALT COUNTER, SET FROM ENTER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 20 SEP 2026: on the top of Salt Counter, leave some space for a running bulletin, which he can set to be changing or running, from Enter on the desk. One clear key in the site's own store, bulletin, with no prefix, so no listing under an account, an order or a push ever sees it, and the publish, which retires only account and lock keys, never touches it. It cannot be sealed and should not be: the desk holds no content key, and a notice for everyone is not a document for one.

THE ROAD IS THE ONE THAT EXISTS. The desk's keyed /bulletin relays to the site's /desk/bulletin over the binding on the desk key, the road the orders take. The site tidies each line to one, caps it at 120 characters and eight lines, keeps running or changing, and an empty set clears the key. A public GET /bulletin answers the page's poll; anything past it is still the site's 404.

ON THE PAGE IT IS THE FIRST THING IN THE BODY, above the door and the signed-in bar alike, spliced in at first paint so the door carries it with no request, and read again every sixth poll on an open page, so a change reaches a customer within a minute. Running joins the lines into one track that scrolls, its speed set from its length and stopped where the reader asks for less motion; changing shows a line at a time, four seconds each. Hidden when there is nothing to show. The marquee lives in the nonce'd style block, so the page's CSP is untouched.

THE WORDS ARE CHECKED WHERE THE DESK'S NAME MAY BE HELD. A customer's page never names the desk, a roster code or a level, and nothing under stmt/ may hold those words, so the check is the desk Worker's, on the relay: a line naming Salt Command, carrying a code's shape or a level's name is refused and the site is left as it was. The phone refuses the same before sending and asks about a product's name, which is his to spend on his own notice board; the page draws a mark for a product and cannot for a bulletin.

FROM ENTER. A Bulletin card at the top of Site orders on the cloud desk: what is showing now, a box with one line per item, Running or Changing, Set and Clear, keyed as every write on the desk is, with the refusal or the confirmation on its own line.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 33 assertions driving both Workers and the page in jsdom: the desk key on the site's route, the tidying and the caps, the public read and the 404 kept past it, the door carrying the band first and unhidden with the marquee in the nonce'd style, a line escaped on the band and in the script's copy, the clear, the page drawing the served line and changing to the second after four seconds, a read that finds a change redrawing it running with a duration from its length, the every-sixth-poll read, the desk's route behind the write key, the four refusals leaving the site unchanged, a product's name allowed, the relay without a binding, the publish retiring only account and lock keys, and the Enter card read, wired, tidying its lines, refusing the desk's name and asking about a product's. Twenty mutations each turned it red.

t: THE ROAD FROM A SITE ORDER TO THE QUEUE IS REPAIRED, AND THE DESK SAYS WHAT BECAME OF EACH STAGE
n: HIS QUESTION OF 20 SEP 2026: why Salt Counter's site orders are not synced with the desk as one book. Measured on the live stores: the desk's orders queue key, q:orders, had held a hand-written value with its quotes stripped since 19 Sep 03:49 UTC, so every write to it threw, the reconcile swallowed the stack, and its log read failed for order zhim2a and waiting for order 4l1kkq every minute for a day. The friend order acknowledged and delivered on the 19th, RM435 of advance, never reached the book, while the site chased the customer for it hourly.

THE KEY WAS CORRUPTED BY tools/drain.mjs --forget, which handed the rewritten queue to wrangler as a JSON argument through the win32 shell, and the shell stripped the quotes. The tool writes through --path now, names a device key it cannot parse in --status and --forget instead of counting it as empty, and the destructive drain never deletes one. The Worker's own writer starts an unreadable key afresh and logs the head of what it held, because nothing the book needs lives only there: an entry reaches that key from one place, is drafted on arrival, and its stage is marked told only after the write, so anything lost is still owed and comes round next minute.

EVERY ENTRY QUEUED IN ONE PASS CARRIED THE PASS'S CLOCK, AND A DRAFT'S ID IS THE ENTRY'S AT. On 18 Sep 03:05 three acknowledgements queued in one tick collapsed to one draft in the drafter's map, and the pending row for 4l1kkq was never made; its payment and handover have waited on a key no row carries since. An entry is stamped with the moment its stage happened on the site instead: the acknowledgement's history event, the last payment, the handover (the site records movedAt beside movedOn now), the withdrawal. Two stages are two moments, so two ids; a stage queued again after a failed mark lands on the same id and is not queued twice; two stages in one millisecond take neighbouring ones; and the pending row is dated the day he agreed it, which sits inside its own key, rather than the day the cron noticed.

WAITING AND FAILED WERE INVISIBLE ON EVERY SURFACE, AND THE ONE SURFACE THAT SPOKE SAID THE OPPOSITE. The cron logged neither a wait nor the reason for a failure; the Site orders card said the entry was queued within the minute whatever had happened. The reconcile writes what it made of each order onto the record as sync, queued, waiting or failed with the reason, only when it changes, through the mark road it already had; the card reads it and says waiting since when, or that the desk could not tell the ledger and why; the log names a wait and carries the thrown reason.

WHAT STILL NEEDS HIS HAND. The live q:orders key is deleted once this is on the phone, so zhim2a's row is dated the 19th; the row then drafts, he approves it, and the handover Correction follows. 4l1kkq's payment and handover were booked by hand on s173 at RM420, so the RM15 of carriage is off the book: a Correction on s173 and a mark on the order are his decision, named in the plan.

THE CHECKS. Two new sections of 42 assertions driving both Workers: two acknowledgements in one tick as two ids each dated its own day, a failed mark coming round onto the same id with one copy kept, a handover stamped with its moment and dated the site's day, the payment and the withdrawal likewise, the same millisecond twice over, the corrupt key started afresh with the log line, a thrown write named, the wait on the cron's log line; then the sync state written once per change and read by the card, an unmapped account told it waits for a publish, the mark branch capping what it stores, the card escaping a reason, and the drain naming an unreadable key, rewriting through a file in the Worker's shape and deleting nothing it cannot read. Thirty-one mutations each turned a section red.

t: A FREE UNIT IS WITHDRAWN: S181 CANCELLED, NOTHING DRAWN, RM278 STILL OPEN
n: ONE AMENDMENT FOLDED, NO GOODS AND NO CASH MOVED. The fold carries a single cancellation recorded 20 Sep against s181, CE4-CHE's row of 1 unit for RM48 dated 18 Sep, the unit promised free with s180. The order is withdrawn and counts nowhere: no stock drawn, no revenue booked, no rate to test against a floor or an ask, since the dossier sets none for this size.

THE FLAG IS ANSWERED BY THE ROW'S OWN FIGURES. The drafter warned that cancelling a row that has moved is not the same as cancelling one that has not. On the target, settled cash and settled units both stand at 0 after the correction of 20 Sep, so nothing has to be taken back. Stock holds at 16.15 unit on the counts of 19 Sep, cost basis unchanged at RM48 a unit.

t: A FREE UNIT UNSETTLED: THE ROW SAYS NOTHING WAS SETTLED
n: ONE CORRECTION FOLDED, NO CASH AND NO STOCK. The fold applies a patch to s181, the free unit promised to CE4-CHE on 18 Sep against the sale on the row above it: cash to 0, delivered quantity to 0, settled RM from 48 to 0 and settled units from unset to 0. It moves nothing on the shelf and nothing through the till, it only changes what the row says about itself. The row itself is not rewritten here.

THE DRAFTER'S FLAGS STAND UNANSWERED ON THE FACE OF IT. RM48 a unit is 47.8% under CE4-CHE's usual RM92, and RM48 of goods is RM4.83 below the RM52.83 floor for this size. The inventory spans more than one lot rate, so RM48 a unit is the average rather than the lot this row draws, and the blend wants checking. Stock stands at 16.15 unit on the 19 Sep count, unchanged by this fold.

t: THE HANDOVER IS ONE WORD, IT DECIDES WHETHER THERE IS A CARRIAGE AT ALL, AND THE FORM TYPES THE TWO FIGURES THE LEDGER STORES
n: HIS INSTRUCTIONS OF 19 SEP 2026, three of them, and all on one field. Shorten the prose to collected or delivered; a sale the customer collected leaves the delivery box inactive and not editable; a lot he collected himself must carry its freight, and one the supplier delivered must not. By them and by us was the register of a longer sentence and the two words carry the whole of it, which is also what lets the SAME control answer a purchase: collected is the buyer came and delivered is the seller drove, and on a lot the buyer is him. No new field, so the thirty-five correctable attributes are still thirty-five.

AND THE QUARTER OF v727 THAT NEVER LANDED. His instruction was to separate the sell price and the delivery price from the ledger, the ENTER, the statement and the order. v727 did the ledger, the statement and the order. The entry form still said Of which delivery while nothing downstream subtracted it any more, so the next delivered sale typed on the phone would have been booked owing its carriage twice: goods 105, carriage 15, owed 120 on an order of 105. Six more places on that path still assumed the charge was inside the total, the two cover plans among them, which subtracted a carriage from a figure it is no longer in. The form asks for Goods and Delivery now, the two columns the row actually has, and what they owe is the two together everywhere it is read: the state pill, the cash refusal, the queue line and the Approve card, which called an order paid in full while its carriage stood beside it unpaid.

WHAT THE GATE HAD TO BE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS VERSION DOES NOT WORK. Hiding or disabling a box does not stop it being read: wbNum reads .value with no test of the element's state and FIVE sites read the delivery, two of them inside arithmetic where the field name is a string argument and no scan for the derivation could see it. So the gate zeroes on closing, v457's idiom, and assigns disabled on every pass so it re-opens. It lives in wbApply, because renderPart restores values and never disabled, and the thirty-five callers of render would each have quietly re-opened it. And wbHand is lifted out of the list that only ever gave a field wbPreview and given its own handler: without that one line the gate is correct and never fires, which is how this change would have shipped looking right.

THE REFUSAL REPLACES ONE THAT HAD LOST ITS PREMISE. A delivery above the total was a real rule while the charge sat inside it and is a meaningless one beside it: half a unit driven a long way genuinely costs more to carry than the salt is worth. What is refused now is the contradiction, on the form and in the drafter alike so the phone and the laptop cannot disagree: collected with a delivery charged, a supplier delivery with freight charged, a collected lot with no freight. Not stated is the way past all three and stays a real answer, because an unasked row is not an answered one and the delivered share is measured over the rows that answered. The more bag is held to the closed list a correction is held to, which it never was.

ONE FAULT IN THE SUITE'S OWN INSTRUMENTS, FOUND THREE TIMES. v727's derivation scan read the master's raw bytes, and the master carries evolution, so v727's own note, which says in as many words that total - delivery was written by hand in twelve places, matched its own assertion. The v727 run went red after the phone was live and was reported here as green. A dated record is not corrected in place, so the note stands and the scan stops reading the changelog; the copy pins read the markup rather than the file, or every comment explaining a change is a failure and the only way to stay green is to stop writing down why. A second assertion pins the shape the first cannot see, total-wbNum(, which is how two of the twelve survived.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 26 assertions, the gate driven in a real window: the word typed, the box shut and ZEROED with wbNum reading nought, re-opened on the word changing back, surviving a re-render, the freight the mirror of it on a lot, the three refusals and the three legitimate answers, a purchase carrying its handover to the drafter, and an order of RM90 with RM15 of carriage reading RM90 of RM105 paid. Eighteen mutations, every one red, one of them by throwing rather than failing, which is why the harness reads exit status and never counts FAIL lines. 2,971 assertions over 214 sections.

t: THE SELL PRICE AND THE CARRIAGE ARE TWO FIGURES, AND THE ORDER KEY IS STILL WHAT THEY AGREED TO PAY
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 19 SEP 2026: completely separate the sell price from the delivery price, through the ledger, Enter, the statement and the order, and do the same for the buy price and the freight. A SALE'S TOTAL IS THE GOODS ALONE NOW and the carriage stands beside it, which is the convention a purchase has always had.

THE TWO SIDES CARRIED OPPOSITE CONVENTIONS AND BOTH FAILURE MODES HAD JUST BEEN SEEN, A DAY APART, ON THE LIVE BOOK. A purchase's freight sits BESIDE its total, and p025 double-counted it because a person added it into the total as well: the landed rate read RM8.08 against RM7.84 and v715 was built on the wrong figure. A sale's delivery sat INSIDE its total, and s172 absorbed its carriage into the rate because there was nowhere else to put it: RM52.50 a unit against the RM90 he had actually charged. One shape double-counts, the other absorbs, and the field list stated both contradictions one line apart.

TWELVE ROWS RESTATED AND RM198 OF CARRIAGE MOVED, WITH NOT ONE FIGURE RE-PRICED. Every one says on its own row that it was restated rather than re-priced, because a ledger that changes a number without saying why is worse than one that is wrong.

THE KEY IS WHAT THEY AGREED TO PAY, AND THAT IS WHAT AVOIDED A COLLISION. v694 names a row by the engine's ovKey to the character, and it is written onto a LIVE order at acknowledgement, so a key that moved would orphan every order in flight. On the GOODS alone, s155 and s157 both become CN6-WM-R|2026-09-12|110, and four of the twelve carriage-bearing rows are still open. ovKey therefore stays on the goods and the carriage TOGETHER, which is also what the customer agreed to pay, and not one order key moved.

THE DERIVATION IS NOW WRITTEN IN NO PLACE AT ALL. `total - delivery` was restated by hand in twelve places across seven files, so nothing forced them to agree and nothing said what the total MEANT. They read the total, which is the goods. txGoods stays as a named function rather than being inlined, because a reader that means "the goods" should say so: on the day the convention changed, a bare `total` was right by luck in twelve places and wrong in the twelve that meant what is owed.

AND THE SITE WAS ALREADY RIGHT. stmt/orders.js and stmt/page.js have always kept the two apart, the page even printing "RM x for the goods and RM y delivery". It was src/orders.js, the desk's own relay, that folded them back into one figure on the way to the book. It passes them through now and keys on the two together.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 17 assertions: the goods are the total, what is owed is the two together, the two answers coincide where there is no carriage (which is why twelve wrong derivations looked right), the key on what they agreed to pay, s155 and s157 sharing goods and not a key, every restated row saying so, the relay carrying the site's two figures, the desk's key and the engine's ovKey the same string, and the derivation absent from all seven files. Six mutations each turned it red, including the one that puts the key back on the goods and collides the two rows. Nineteen existing fixtures and source pins were restated to the new shape. 2,941 passing.

t: A 37.5 UNIT BUY AT RM46 PAID IN FULL, HALF THE LOT ON THE SHELF
n: FOLDED: ONE PURCHASE ROW TO SA5-BTR. The desk booked 37.5 unit of salt for RM1,725, RM46 a unit, RM1,725 cash paid on 19 Sep with RM45 freight, and 18.75 of the 37.5 unit moved the same day. The size falls between the quoted steps of the 20 Aug sheet, so it is priced between the RM48 of the 25 unit tier and the RM44 of the 50 unit tier. The drafter raised no flags.

UNUSUAL: A SIZE WITH NO TIER OF ITS OWN, AND HALF THE GOODS STILL TO COME. Payment is complete while receipt is not, so 18.75 unit stay to be delivered on a row already settled in cash. RM46 sits under the party's median of RM56 and at the low end of his range of RM44 to RM64. Sixteen orders, on the roster, nothing defaulted, RM3,100 outstanding before this row.

t: AN ADVANCE OF 2.5 UNIT GOES OUT TO CN6-WM: RM40 IN, RM210 AND THE CAP LEFT OPEN
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL AT THE MEDIAN. CN6-WM is booked for 2.5 unit at RM250, RM100 a unit, collected and moved in full on 19 Sep with RM40 paid. The total clears the RM134.61 floor for this size and stops well short of the RM360 ask, and the rate sits on his own median inside a range of RM75 to RM110. Cost is the inventory's own RM48 a unit, RM120 on the goods.

Eight orders, an associate and on the roster, nothing defaulted. The inventory took no lot in, so the RM48 basis is untouched and RM210 stays outstanding.

t: S175 SETTLED IN FULL: RM100 IN, ONE UNIT OUT, NOTHING LEFT OUTSTANDING
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, 19 SEP. The fold carries a single fulfilment against CF5-WM's s175, the SELL of 1 unit for RM100 agreed the same day and corrected down from RM110 earlier on 19 Sep. RM100 and 1 unit move against RM100 and 1 unit outstanding, which clears the order. The row itself is not recomputed here: the master's amend path applies it, so there is one definition of what a fulfilment does.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. Salt was counted on 19 Sep and stock stands at 0.9 unit, below the reorder mark of 15, with RM7.14 owed out and 8.12 promised. Cost stays the inventory's own RM48 a unit against a replacement rate of RM46, so no basis moves on this fold. t: THREE ADVANCES PAID DOWN IN CASH, AND A PENDING SELL RESTATED TO RM100
n: FOLDED: three fulfilments and one correction, all recorded 19 Sep and all decided at the desk. RM110 came in against CN6-WM s170 and RM80 against CR3-DAM s165, settling both orders in full; a further RM80 went against CR3-DAM s179, which had RM160 standing. All three orders were collected in full when they were agreed, so no unit moves with the money and the fold is cash only.

UNUSUAL: CR3-DAM is paid against twice in one day and still leaves RM80 open on s179, against RM265 outstanding and 3.27 unit on credit before the fold. s165 had already been restated on 19 Sep on his word, so the fulfilment lands on a row amended the same day. CF5-WM s175 is corrected from RM110 to RM100, which follows the carriage of RM10 dropped from that row earlier.

THE INVENTORY: nothing drawn and nothing landed. Stock stands at 0.9 unit on the counts of 19 Sep for salt and oil, cost basis unchanged at RM48 a unit against replacement of RM46, with the reorder mark at 15 unit. s175 stays pending at 0 unit moved, so the correction books no revenue and touches no stock. RM7.14 owed out and RM8.12 promised are unchanged by this fold.

t: THE ADMIN PAGE SAVES TO HIS HOME SCREEN AS ITS OWN APP, AND OPENS WHERE HE SAVED IT FROM
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 19 SEP 2026: can Salt Counter include a button to the admin page, so he can reach it from the app too. The need is real and the reason is simple: a standalone app has NO ADDRESS BAR, so from inside Salt Counter there is no way to reach /all at all.

IT IS AN APP OF HIS OWN, NOT A BUTTON ON EVERY CUSTOMER'S PAGE. A link on the door would be served to everyone who finds the site, and the door is drawn before anybody has signed in; v687 took the owner's script off that page deliberately. `start_url` resolves against the MANIFEST'S own url, so the customer manifest served at the root opens at the root however he saved it, and saving from /all would have given him a second copy of the customer door under another name. His page therefore links its own manifest, scoped to /all and opening there, so the page he saves is the page he gets back.

IT SITS INSIDE THE PREFIX AND IS GATED LIKE EVERYTHING ELSE THERE. An expired Access session refuses the manifest exactly as it refuses the page, which is the right failure: an admin app that kept working after the session died would be the wrong kind of convenience. He bootstraps it once from Safari with Access, as he said he would, and saves it from there.

AND IT DOES NOT CARRY THE DESK'S NAME. Salt Admin. The rule that the DESK is never named on this site is the one this change could most easily have broken, because an admin app is exactly the thing somebody would name after the ledger it reports on. It is asserted rather than remembered.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 8 assertions driven behind a REAL Access token, RS256 against a generated key: gated without one, served as a manifest with one, opening at /all and scoped to it, installing standalone rather than as a bookmark, the customer's manifest untouched and a different app, the desk's name absent, and each page linking its own, with a customer's page naming the prefix nowhere. Six mutations each turned it red. ONE OF THEM CAUGHT THE HARNESS LYING: the first proof counted FAIL lines, and a mutation that makes a section THROW prints no FAIL line at all, so a crash read as a pass. It reads the exit status now, and the mutation that removes the route is recorded as having thrown rather than failed.

t: OIL HAS NO PRICING TIER: ONE TYPED BOARD OF FIVE SIZES, FIXED FOR ALL, AND EACH PRODUCT STATES ITS OWN COST BASIS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 19 SEP 2026: for oil there will no longer be a pricing tier, since it is not the main product, just a single one. Start at 130 for 10 to 450 at 50, with 240, 330 and 400 between. This is the only price for oil, fixed for all. RM13 a unit falling a ringgit every ten to RM9, margins of 39.7% down to 12.9% on landed cost, and every rung clearing its own floor.

A TIER_RULE CARRYING `fixed` IS A BOARD HE HAS TYPED, and it is read in ONE place. fiveTiers is the choke point every oil price passes: the guest boards call it directly, the desk's ask and cardQuote reach it through fiveTierAt, and the customer's page reads the snapshot's precomputed ladder. Stating the board anywhere else would have meant teaching five readers the same thing and watching them drift. A size between rungs is quoted pro rata on its rung's own rate and ROUNDED DOWN, because rounded up 15 unit came out at RM13.33 against the RM13 he typed at 10, and the rate per unit may not rise as an order grows: that is one of the engine's four laws and the one a customer can check by hand.

THE CAP IS SALT'S RULE NOW, on his decision. A card is never above what the customer pays, his rule of 15 Sep, exists to stop a TIER sitting above somebody's own rate. With one price for everybody there is no tier to be above them, and the cap would only have held two customers below the board he typed. He was asked and chose the board. Four oil cards now sit above what those two have paid, and there is an assertion saying so with the date on it, so the change cannot quietly grow.

FIVE SIZES, NOT SEVEN. He typed five prices and the engine does not extrapolate his taper, so 80 and 100 would have held flat at RM9 a unit and quoted RM720 and RM900. Asked, he dropped them. His decision of 15 Sep that oil's grid carries 80 and 100 is superseded, not corrected away: it stands in the Journal at v641.

AND THE TWO PRODUCTS STATE THEIR OWN COST BASIS. COST_RULE.oil is `landed`, purchase plus freight and nothing else: he uses most of the oil himself, so its leak is high by design and is never costed into a sale, though it is still measured and still reported. It replaces a buyPlusPct 15 PLACEHOLDER from 09 Sep whose own note said the fifteen per cent stood in for freight and leak together, which with the freight now in the floor directly would have counted it twice. COST_RULE.salt is `stack`, the measured stack, and changes not one salt figure: what it changes is that the difference between the two books is written down rather than being one of them merely lacking an entry. Oil's floor at 10 unit goes RM87.17 to RM78.44.

IT TOOK FOUR ROUNDS AND EVERY ROUND WAS THE SAME SHAPE: a signal that had to be looked up twice rather than travelling with the data. tools/book.mjs mapped each ladder row to {q, prices} and DROPPED the fixed flag, so the customer's page could not tell a one-price board from a tier index gone out of range, and silently returned every oil size as unpriced. Then the desk's own cardQuote held the same no-tier refusal, so his printed card and the customer's page would have disagreed about oil on the same day. Neither was visible until the suite drove them, and neither would have been visible on screen.

THE CHECKS. Nineteen assertions restated across the suite, each recording that this decision supersedes the one of 15 Sep rather than erasing it: the five-tier laws now say plainly that they are SALT'S, because oil no longer has tiers, and the grid of forced costs runs 35 rather than 70 for the same reason. Eight mutations, each run against the whole suite because this change reaches the engine, the snapshot, the desk and the customer's page and no one section holds it: a typed price under its floor, the pro rata rounding up, the cap applied after all, the landed rule ignored, the flag dropped from the snapshot, the page falling back to no-tier-no-price, and the desk refusing to quote a board. All eight turned it red. 2,916 passing.

t: A RE-KEY CARRIES THE PASSWORD WITH THE CODE, AND A SEED CANNOT RUN OVER A VAULT IT HAS NOT PULLED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 19 SEP 2026: keep Salt Counter and the desk in sync. An Amend ID already reaches the vault from the phone and the statement username through the fold, both since v628. It has never reached `_passwords.json`, which is filed by CODE and which nothing moved, so every re-key left that customer's password under the name they had left. FOUR WERE IN THAT STATE ON THE LIVE BOOK: CM3-OUG's sat under CH5-OUG, CA5-BAN's under CA5-KER, CA7-AMP's under CA7-JTR and CA2-SEN's under CA11-SEN.

WHAT IT BROKE WAS HIS SIDE, NOT THEIRS, which is why it went unseen. A customer's account is keyed by USERNAME, kept for life, and their password unwraps their own content key; neither moves with the code, so nobody was ever locked out of Salt Counter and a re-key cannot lock them out. What broke is Send: he could not hand those four their password from his phone, because the tool looked under a code the customer no longer had.

SO THE FOLD MOVES IT, AND IT IS THE FOURTH FILE A RENAME REACHES, NOT THE THIRD. The comment beside renameUsers, renameLocs and renameSuiteText has said 'the three files' since v628 and three was never all of them. `renamePasswords` never writes over a password the new code already holds, because that one is somebody's, and it is a silent no-op where the file is absent, which is the CLOUD fold's case: `_passwords.json` is gitignored and the cloud has none to move.

AND THE SEAL WRITES BACK THE PAIRING IT PROVES, rather than proving it again for ever. v705 taught it to match an orphaned password to its record by VERIFIER, which answers one password and no other, and then threw the answer away every run. Proof is the right safety net and the wrong mechanism. It now moves the password onto the code it has just proved owns it, only where that code holds none, and writes the file only on a real run so --check still reports without changing anything. Run once on the live issue: all four moved, 41 entries in and 41 out, and the next --check has nothing left to pair.

AND A SEED CAN NO LONGER RUN OVER A VAULT IT HAS NOT READ. Add ID and Amend ID both file names into the vault FROM THE PHONE, and the laptop's directory is behind it until pull-vault.mjs runs. The Names rule has said to pull first since v528 and NOTHING ENFORCED IT: a seed replaces the whole vault, so it could silently drop every name the phone had filed since the last pull. It happened twice on 19 Sep, in this session, before the guard existed. The seed now reads the live vault and refuses while it holds a code the directory lacks, naming the tool that fixes it; it refuses just as hard when the passphrase will not open what is there, because a seed it cannot read is a seed it must not replace. `--force` is for the case where the vault is the thing that is wrong.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 8 assertions: the move, the refusal to write over a password the new code already holds, the no-op where there is no file, and the one that matters more than the move itself, that every password which existed still exists afterwards under the code its customer now has. Then the seal's write-back and its --check silence, and both halves of the seed's refusal. Seven mutations each turned it red, including one that deletes the old entry without writing the new and so LOSES a password, and one that restores the warn-instead-of-refuse the seed had on the morning it dropped names twice.

t: A GIFT IS NOT A PRICE ANYONE PAID, AND ONE NOT YET COLLECTED WOULD HAVE BECOME A DEBT
n: A GIFT HAD BEEN COUNTING AS A PRICE THE CUSTOMER PAID, AND THE COMMENT BESIDE IT HAD PROMISED OTHERWISE SINCE v406. The drafter reads a party's own history and the product's observed range to decide whether a rate is odd, and both sets filtered on `s.total > 0` alone. That was right while a free unit was written at total NOUGHT, and inert from the day the book's convention became total = COST settled by settledRM with goodwill true, which is s031 on 21 July. Every giveaway since has entered both sets at the inventory rate as though it had been paid for. Measured on the live book: CJ4-BJ's own median read RM68 against a real RM70, and CS6-BS RM107 against RM107.50.

IT IS THE MARK THAT SAYS SO, NOT THE TOTAL, so both sets now read one predicate that excludes a giveaway by its goodwill mark and a nought by its total. Both, together, because v407's own lesson was that v406 fixed one of the pair and left the twin live, and the note beside it says so in those words. The zero test stays beside the mark: it guards a different casualty, which is that a row at nought pulls the observed LOW to nought, at which point `rate < lo/2` is `rate < 0` and the low-side check can never fire again.

AND A GIFT THAT HAD NOT BEEN COLLECTED YET WOULD HAVE BECOME A DEBT THE MOMENT IT WAS. s181, the unit promised free to CE4-CHE, was entered at v718 with no settledRM because nothing had moved, while the other six giveaways on the book all carry it. Driven forward: the row reads RM0 owed today and RM48 owed the instant the unit is handed over, at which point CE4-CHE enters the debtor list, counts against their own credit cap and joins the hourly chase, for a gift. A gift is settled when it is given.

AND THE ONE ROW HIS NEW RULE EXISTS TO STOP WAS SITTING OPEN ON THE BOOK. s175 carried RM10 of carriage on an order marked COLLECTED, which read the goods as RM100 against CF5-WM's own card of RM110. His instruction of 19 Sep is that a collected order cannot carry a delivery charge at all. Nothing was paid and nothing had moved, so it is set right rather than corrected, and the goods are now exactly their card.

THE CHECKS. Three assertions driven through the drafter with EIGHT giveaways in the fixture, five at cost with the mark and three at nought, because the check is a MEDIAN and one of either is invisible to it over the two real salt rates this book holds. A fourth proves the subtler half, that a gift must not switch a check ON by padding a sample below its own threshold; a fifth proves the zero guard on OIL, which is the only product here with the three rates the range check needs. Four mutations each turned it red. The wiring assertion that pinned the old text is restated on the property rather than the string, because the two sets now share the predicate instead of agreeing by copy.

t: HIS BOOK MADE TRUE: AN ERROR ROW HAD BEEN HOLDING EVERY SALT FLOOR A TENTH TOO LOW, AND A LOT'S FREIGHT WAS COUNTED TWICE
n: HIS CORRECTIONS OF 19 SEP 2026, AFTER AN AUDIT OF FIVE DAYS' TRADING. Eleven changes to the book, every one on his word and every one verified by reading the book back rather than by trusting the write. The audit that found most of it ran five lenses over eighteen sales and two lots and put every finding to a skeptic that had to refute it from the book; sixteen stood of forty-two raised.

ONE ERROR ROW HAD BEEN CORRUPTING EVERY SALT PRICE FOR THREE DAYS. s169 was cancelled at v669 and its five unit were never put back on the shelf: v665 drew them, v669's own note says it "kept the position at 9.5 unit stated", and v673 then counted 14.5, found a +5 drift and recorded that "the dossier offers no cause, so none is recorded". That phantom surplus nets off real shrinkage in pxLeakCharge, which is read over the last three count cycles, so the measured leak read 8.47% against a truth of 19.23% and EVERY SALT FLOOR SAT ABOUT A TENTH TOO LOW. It is how s172 was let through. The row is gone on his word, the count reads a drift of nought, and the floor at one unit goes RM51 to RM54.11.

THE OIL LOT'S FREIGHT WAS COUNTED TWICE, AND v715 WAS BUILT ON IT. p025 carried a total of RM392 with RM12 standing beside it in the freight field, and RM380 plus RM12 is RM392: the freight was inside the total AND next to it, so the landed rate read RM8.08. He gave the true figure, RM380. v715 had rolled PROD_STOCK_COST.oil to 7.84 off 392/50 three hours earlier, which was the right number from the wrong arithmetic; the corrected lot makes it 7.60 and it is re-rolled. This is the fault that separating buy price from freight exists to end.

A FREE UNIT IS ITS OWN ROW, WHICH IS THE ONLY READING ON WHICH A FLOOR MEANS ANYTHING. s172 read 2 unit for RM105, so RM52.50 a unit, RM75 under CC5-OKR's own card and RM3 over break-even. What happened was one unit sold at their usual RM90, one given free, and RM15 of carriage. Read as one row it is under the corrected floor; read as a sale plus a gift, the sale clears its floor and the gift is visible as a gift, costed and never counted as revenue, which is the book's own convention for a giveaway (s031, s050, s056, s153, s171) on his ruling of 11 Sep. The same split is applied to the new CE4-CHE order.

ONE ROW IN 158 CARRIED NO COST AT ALL. s148 stated RM44 a unit in its own note and held no cost field, so the desk charged it the weighted average of every lot, RM49.58. The cause is in the fold: the cost fill runs only when an amendment moves units, and the 15 Sep Correction raised deliveredQty from nought to one with no units in the amendment, so a unit left the shelf without a cost following it. The whole sales book was swept: it is the single instance.

FIVE MOVEMENTS ENTERED AND TWO COUNTS TAKEN. CK4-SEN 6.25 unit for RM500 part paid and part collected; CR3-DAM 2 unit for RM160 collected and unpaid, which with s165 restated to RM80 unpaid puts RM240 of advances against that one customer; CE4-CHE 2 unit for RM230 pending with a unit free beside it; CJ4-BJ to RM800 in, leaving RM50 and 6.25 unit open. Salt counted at 0.9 unit against a stated 3.25, a drift of -2.35 that is left as the real shrinkage it is rather than explained away; oil counted at 40. Both COUNT_ON dates move, which they would not have done if the count alone had been written.

A NEW CUSTOMER, AND A DIRECTORY THAT HAD BEEN STALE SINCE THE RE-KEYS. CS6-DAM is on the roster, recorded as CM3-OUG's introduction, in the encrypted vault and holding a statements account proved on every road a reader takes. Seven customers had no name on the laptop directory and four of them had one filed under the code they had LEFT, the same fault v705 fixed for passwords; those four pairings are proved by each record's own verifier, so they were carried across. CE5-TBC to CE5-SA is not proved and was left alone, because a name against the wrong customer is worse than no name.

THE QUEUE IS EMPTY AND THE THREE DRAFTS ARE DECIDED. Every queued entry was already on the book by another road, so all twelve were withdrawn and the three pending drafts recorded as rejected with the rows that replaced them named in the decision, because approving them would have booked the same trading twice.

THE CHECKS. Eighteen assertions written to read the book back after the write, including that no real name reached it and that every rid is still unique. The suite is 2901 passing. The book had to be re-sorted into date order afterwards, which four separate checks caught at once: appending a row dated the 17th after one dated the 19th breaks the gate, the extract, the book-block sync and the date-order sweep, and it is the one mistake a hand fold makes that the real fold cannot.

t: THREE IDS THAT COULD NOT SIGN IN HAVE AN ACCOUNT, THE MINT STOPS STAMPING THE WRONG ISSUE, AND THE MORNING NUDGE READS THE CRON'S OWN DAY
n: CF5-WM, CE5-SA AND CB7-BJ HAD A PLACE ON THE ROSTER AND NOTHING BEHIND IT. CB7-BJ had no username at all, so it was minted one first and that is its address for life. Each now carries a password, the verifier it answers, the content key wrapped under it, the same key wrapped under the master, the password sealed under the master so Send can hand it over from the phone, and a bundle holding its live position. This is v707's tool doing the job it was written for, on the three accounts it has been naming on every publish since.

AND THE TOOL WAS STAMPING THE WRONG ISSUE, WHICH NOTHING WOULD HAVE REPORTED. newestIssue answers the FOLDER, 2026-09, because that is what names the directory; every record carries the DATE, 2026-09-01, because makeStatements is handed a date and stamps that. On the record itself the difference is invisible. Three files downstream it is not: make_statements sorts _kv BY FILENAME, stmt-publish takes the store's issue key off records[0].issued, and the minted username 27a4-gkgw sorts ahead of the file that was first. So the live issue would have become 2026-09.

WHAT THAT WOULD HAVE COST. stmt/worker.js keys every tick as sent:<issue>:<username>, so all thirty-four September ticks would have been orphaned and every statement already sent would have read as never sent; and storedIssue !== issued would have read as a NEW ISSUE and cleared every attempt counter. Not one of those three effects is in the tool that was wrong, which is the whole reason a mint was audited before it was let near a real record rather than after.

IT TAKES THE DATE OFF ITS NEIGHBOURS NOW, RATHER THAN COMPUTING ONE. A minted record agrees with the records the publish will read it beside, whatever the convention turns out to be; the first of the month is only the fallback for an issue with nothing to agree with, and that fallback is still a date. Computing issue + "-01" would have been right today and wrong the first time an issue is cut on any other day.

THE FIXTURE WAS THE REASON IT SURVIVED. The v707 fixture carried issued "2026-09" itself, so it agreed with the bug and went green for the same reason the bug lived. It carries the date now, and a second fixture cuts its issue on the FIFTEENTH, because in a first-of-the-month fixture "read the neighbour" and "assume the first" give the same answer and no mutation can tell them apart. Two mutations stayed green until that fixture existed, and the temptation was to read them as proof the code was unreachable rather than proof the instrument was blind.

THE CHECKS. Five new assertions in the v707 section, each turned red by mutation, including one restoring the fault exactly as it stood. Proved on the real data too, not only on fixtures: 27a4-gkgw.json is now the first file in sort order exactly as predicted, it carries 2026-09-01, all forty records in the issue agree on one value, and each of the three accounts was put to every road a reader takes, the customer's password and both of his master routes, sixty checks with no failures. The laptop key was proved against all thirty-seven existing records first, so none of the three lands in the publish's wrongKey list.

AND THE MORNING NUDGE WAS READING THE WALL CLOCK, WHICH THE SUITE FOUND BY FAILING AT MIDNIGHT. The stale-count leg of the daily nudge compared COUNT_ON against new Date(), while everything else in scheduled() honours event.scheduledTime. So a tick that fired late, was retried or was replayed compared the count against the wrong day and would have woken him over a count already taken. It honours the cron's own time now; the other klDay reader is a request handler, where the wall clock is the right answer, and it is left alone. THE WAY IT SURFACED IS THE POINT: two v708 assertions went from green to red with no commit between them, because they pinned a scheduled time the code ignored and so were really asserting what day the suite was run on. They now drive two ticks carrying the SAME count and differing only in when the cron fired, so neither can pass by being run on the right day. Three mutations each turned it red, one of them by putting the wall clock back.

t: A PENDING SALT SELL AT THE ASK'S SHORT SIDE: AGREED, NOTHING PAID, NOTHING MOVED
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SINGLE UNIT OF SALT BOOKED TO CF5-WM AND LEFT PENDING. The sale is dated 19 Sep as the day it was agreed, RM110 in total with RM10 of carriage inside it and RM100 of goods, marked collected but with RM0 in and 0 unit moved. It clears the RM51 floor for one unit and sits under the RM160 ask and the RM150 ceiling. The drafter flagged nothing and the figures need no answer.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID: NOTHING, WHICH IS THE POINT. A pending row draws no stock and books no revenue until something moves, so the stated position is untouched and the cost basis is unchanged at RM48 a unit against a replacement of RM46. CF5-WM had a prior pending row of the same shape cancelled on 11 Sep, so the whole RM110 stays outstanding and the desk should watch for collection or lapse.

t: OIL'S SHELF COST IS ROLLED TO THE LOT THAT LANDED, AND MASTER IS GREEN AGAIN
n: HIS DECISION OF 18 SEP 2026, ASKED AND ANSWERED: roll it to the newest lot. PROD_STOCK_COST.oil goes RM7.5250 to RM7.8400, the rate of the fifty unit that landed from SP7-PUD on 18 Sep. The v713 fold booked that lot and did not roll the cost, which is the shape v384 named and the reason the check exists: a lot lands, the cost stays on the one before it, and nothing on the desk looks wrong.

THE SUITE HAD BEEN RED ON MASTER SINCE THAT FOLD, AND THE PHONE WAS ALREADY LIVE ON IT. The suite step runs after the deploy and is never rolled back, by design, so the failure sat on master turning every later push red for reasons that had nothing to do with it. Two other pieces of work were parked behind it. That is the cost of a red master rather than the cost of this row.

WHY IT IS A DECISION AND NOT A DEFAULT, which is what the assertion's own message says: the last four oil lots ran RM7.6667, RM7.6667, RM7.5250 and RM7.8400, so they are not monotonic and rolling to the newest is a different answer from blending across what is on the shelf. The check reads the newest RECEIVED lot out of the book rather than pinning a number, so it survives the next lot instead of breaking on it, and a genuine blend still fails it on purpose.

WHAT MOVES WITH IT. The shelf cost feeds the closing stock in Financials, the Stock value card, and the PRICING snapshot the cloud drafter approves rows against. COST_RULE.oil is buyPlusPct 15, so the pricing basis goes RM8.6538 to RM9.0160 a unit, RM0.3622 more. Nothing else on the book moves and no row is rewritten.

AND A SEPARATE INSTRUCTION OF HIS IS NOT IN THIS ENTRY. He also said oil's floor should be purchase plus freight alone, with the markup running nought to one and a half. The second half describes the ladder that already exists: TIER_RULE.oil.multiples is [1, 1.375, 1.75, 2.125, 2.5], which as markup on the floor is nought, 0.375, 0.75, 1.125 and 1.5, four equal steps. The first half is a change to the floor BASIS and moves every oil price, so it is being scoped and put back to him rather than ridden in on a cost roll.

t: TWO ORDERS DRAW DOWN, ONE ADVANCE TAKES RM80 IN: RM7.25 OFF THE SHELF, RM210 STILL OPEN
n: FOLDED: TWO FULFILMENTS AND ONE CORRECTION, ALL SALT, ALL RECORDED 18 SEP. CS6-BS's s173 settles in full at RM420 for 5 unit, CJ4-BJ's s137 takes RM650 and 2.25 unit against a 12.5 unit order of 07 Sep, and CR3-DAM's s165 is patched to show RM80 cash and paidOn 18 Sep. Each was decided at the desk. No new order was opened and no lot landed, so the cost basis stands at RM48 a unit.

UNUSUAL: ONE ROW CLOSES CLEAN, TWO STAY OPEN. s173 leaves nothing outstanding after a row that had shown not a sen paid and nothing handed over. s137 leaves RM200 and 6.25 unit, with the RM15 delivery charge still inside the RM850 total and the drafter's own line reading RM68 a unit against goods of RM66.80 a unit. s165 leaves RM10 unpaid on 1 unit already collected, and the drafter flagged the credit cap.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID: 5 unit went out to CS6-BS and 2.25 unit to CJ4-BJ on 18 Sep, both against orders already on the book, so the movement is drawdown rather than fresh sale. Salt was last counted 16 Sep and stands stated at 10.5 unit, ledger 86.45, self use 75.95, replacement RM46 a unit, reorder at 15 and 13.5 unit promised. Nothing is owed out and no loans are open.

t: A FIFTY UNIT OIL LOT LANDS AND IS PAID IN FULL, RM12 FREIGHT INSIDE THE TOTAL
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A PAID AND RECEIVED OIL PURCHASE. Appended to purchases: BUY from SP7-PUD, 50 unit of oil for RM392, RM7.84 a unit, RM392 cash paid on 18 Sep and 50 unit received the same day, so nothing sits outstanding. The drafter raised no flags, and the figures come from the queued entry as drafted. On his word the row is approved to the book at v713.

WHAT IS UNUSUAL IS THE RATE AGAINST HIS OWN QUOTE. The 07 Sep sheet holds 50 unit at RM380, RM7.60 a unit, and the row carries RM12 freight inside the RM392, which puts the unit rate above his median of RM7.53 and above the top of his range of RM7 to RM7.67. The salt position is untouched at 10.5 unit against a reorder mark of 15, cost basis held at RM48 a unit.

t: AN OIL SALE TO CH4-MAL, PAID AND MOVED THE SAME DAY, WELL UNDER THE ASK
n: FOLDED: one new oil sale to CH4-MAL, 10 unit for RM130 on 18 Sep, RM130 cash taken and 10 unit moved the same day, so the row closes as it opens and nothing is left pending. Costed at RM7.53 a unit from the desk's own inventory rate, RM75.25 on the order and RM54.75 on the goods at 42.1%. The drafter raised no flag and the figures in the dossier carry the row as drafted.

UNUSUAL: the total clears the RM87.28 floor for 10 unit but sits far under the RM230 ask and the RM240 ceiling, and RM13 a unit runs well below CH4-MAL's median of RM110 across 2 orders, in a range of RM11.50 to RM110. The dossier gives no reason for the level and none is supplied here. CH4-MAL holds nothing outstanding, nothing on credit against a cap of 10 and nothing defaulted.

t: A VERSION NOTE HANDED TO -m AS A FILE IS READ, NOT COMMITTED AS A PATH
n: IT HAS GONE WRONG TWICE IN A DAY, AND BOTH TIMES IT LOOKED FINE. The note was passed as JSON.stringify first, so v694 to v698 each landed as ONE line with backslash-n written out through the middle of it. Then v710's note was handed over as a FILE, because no shell here passes paragraphs without mangling them, and the tool committed the PATH. git log --oneline shows the subject alone and the subject was readable every time, which is the whole reason neither was seen.

SO -m TAKES EITHER. A message is a message; an argument naming a file that exists and has something in it is the note itself, read off disk with its paragraphs intact. A directory, an empty file and a name that merely looks like a path are all taken as typed, and the next flag is never swallowed as a subject, which would commit --no-push as a version note.

IT LIVES IN ITS OWN FILE BECAUSE update.mjs CANNOT BE DRIVEN. The tool runs its whole chain on import: drain, build, test, deploy, commit, push and then prove every surface level. There is no way to ask it what it made of an argument without shipping a version. tools/commitmsg.mjs is the one seam, and the suite holds update.mjs to reading it rather than keeping a second copy of the rule, because a seam the tool has stopped using proves nothing about the tool. That is exactly how it stood an hour ago.
NOTHING ON THE PHONE MOVES. No engine, no book, no page and no route: rev.json's id does not cover tools/ and was never going to.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 8 assertions: a file read with its paragraphs and its real newlines, a message typed straight in left alone, no -m and a bare -m both no message at all, the next flag never taken, an empty file and a directory both falling back to the argument, and the wiring itself. Six mutations each turned it red, one of them by restoring the v710 fault and one by restoring the v694 one.

t: THE SHARED LINK SIGNS THEM IN ONCE, SO NO MESSAGE EVER CARRIES A PASSWORD
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: when sharing the link, QR to the user, the site pre-fills their username and password. The username it has always filled in. The password it never can: two channels is a standing rule, a password in a message is a password in a chat log for good, and the suite fails the build the moment one appears in anything shareable. So the password is not put in the link. The LINK is made to sign them in instead, which is the same outcome by a road that leaves nothing behind.

THE WORKER IS NEVER TRUSTED WITH THE KEY. His page has the content key open already, having unwrapped it under the master to seal the account. It mints a token, wraps that key UNDER THE TOKEN, and hands over the wrap and the token's SHA-256. The token itself is written nowhere: ot:<hash> names the record, so a dump of this store opens nothing at all, exactly as rem: holds a wrap no copy of the store can unwrap. Opening posts the token back, the record is read and deleted in that order, and the page derives the key from the token in its own address bar. From there it is an ordinary session and nothing downstream knows the difference.

TWO LIMITS, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN PROMISED AWAY. A link inside its window IS a bearer credential, exactly as a guest link's id is; what it buys over sending a password is that it expires and it burns, not that it cannot be forwarded, and the words hand back say so. And single use is BEST EFFORT: this Worker has KV and nothing else, KV is eventually consistent, and two opens inside the propagation window can both succeed. The copy says once; the comment beside the code is where the mechanism admits it cannot swear to it.

THE ROUTE IS GATED ON THE TOKEN'S SHAPE, NOT ON THE TOKEN. A spent link and one that never existed serve the same door, to the character, so the door is not a probe for which links are live, and the difference is kept to the JSON route's ONE refusal, which a used token, an invented one and a wrong password all share. But anything that could never have been a link is still the site's usual 404, the old /s/<CODE> address included: opening the path to anything one segment deep would have retired that rule by accident.

AND THE PAGE FORGETS IT ON THE WAY IN. history.replaceState puts the address back to / the moment it is spent, or a reload would present a burnt token and refuse a page the reader is already sitting on. A link is tried FIRST and a remembered device is still there behind it, so the two ways in do not fight.

THE TRAP THAT COST THE MOST. stmt/owner.js is not loaded as a script: it is read as text and spliced into a template literal, so every backslash in it is eaten once before a browser ever sees it. The base64url line shipped as /+/g, which is not a regular expression, and it took down two panels that had nothing to do with this version. Character classes need no backslash and survive the splice, and the comment beside them now says why.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 32 assertions: the hash naming the record and the token nowhere in the store, the expiry, the wrap unwrapping the content key and opening the statement, the second open refused and the store left empty, the one refusal shared three ways, his mint route DRIVEN behind a real Access token with a username no account has refused and a mint that could store nothing handing back no link, the shape rule on both sides of the 404, the words carrying no password, the third door losing neither the associate mark nor the card, and the page DRIVEN in jsdom landing on a live link and signed in without typing anything. Seventeen mutations each turned it red, two of them against the door count in v703's own section.

t: AN ASSOCIATE MINTS THEIR OWN LINK, IT IS SHUT UNTIL HE APPROVES IT, AND HE MAY SET ITS TIER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: if they want to refer a customer they can mint their own link, just as he would, it needs his approval, and he can change the price tier if need be. The route is on a SESSION, beside the orders and never under his own prefix, and it refuses anybody whose record does not carry the associate mark, which is the publish's own reading of the report card, so nobody can make themselves one.

PENDING MEANS THE DOOR IS SHUT, FROM THE MOMENT IT EXISTS. The id IS the credential, so an associate could hand it out the second they made it: a link created openable and gated afterwards is a link that was open. It is written shut, and the guest door refuses it with the same 404 an id that never existed gets.

AND THE TEST IS approved === false, NEVER !approved. Not one link already in the store carries the field, so the loose test would have shut every link he has ever handed out, and shut it SILENTLY, because a pending, a withdrawn and an unknown id all answer the same 404 by design. Nobody would have reported it.

"IF NEED BE" MEANS IT WORKS WITHOUT HIM. An approved link with no tier follows the v658 rule, the associate being the introducer. A tier he pins is read off that level's own board and needs nothing published for the link itself, which is what v699 bought. Ambassador is refused, being the floor and never a guest's, rather than quietly serving the board. And standing stays false on their link, or the five he hands to strangers would quietly gain a sixth member.

WHAT AN ASSOCIATE IS HANDED IS THEIRS AND NOTHING OF HIS: where it points, whether it is open yet, how often it has been used. Not his label, not the introducer, not the tier, not who else holds one, and their page never names a level, which a customer's page never does. No label is taken from them either: a note typed here would be the first plaintext anybody but him has put into this store. Capped, in the shape of the open-order cap.

THEIR PANEL TRAVELS IN EVERY CUSTOMER'S PAGE, drawn only behind the mark. It cannot live in his own script, which is spliced on his route alone, and it cannot be spliced per viewer, because the door is served before anybody has signed in. So every customer's page carries the code for a panel they will never see drawn.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 27 assertions: minting on a session and refused without the mark, the door shut while it waits, a link from before this version still opening, his approve, decline and tier driven behind a real Access token, the floor and an unknown tier both refused, the five still five afterwards, one associate unable to touch another's, the cap, and the panel DRIVEN in jsdom through loading, drawing and minting. Fourteen mutations each turned it red.

t: MONEY HE IS HOLDING THAT IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S IS NOW, COUNTS ON THE RAIL, AND WAKES HIM
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: "IF PAID, I WILL NEED TO REFUND IMMEDIATELY." Everything about an open refund was already computed in six places and not one of them was urgent. The action row sat at This week with NO age rule, so it could never reach Now however old it got; the rail's Today badge counts only the Now rows, so an open refund badged nothing anywhere; navCounts added one for a default HE is owed and nothing at all for money he owes BACK; and the morning nudge tested pending drafts and a stale stock count, neither of which is this. The one open today is twenty-three days old.

THE RULE IS HIS INSTRUCTION. The desk's own note says severity is decided by a rule and never by feel, and immediately is the rule he gave. So an open refund is Now from the day it is raised, rather than ageing into it: he did not ask for an ageing. The row says whose money it is and how long he has had it.

THE MIRROR TERM ON THE RAIL. A supplier default he is owed counted one on the Order book; money he owes back counted nothing, so the destination that holds both under-counted by exactly the side he has to act on. And the refunds table carries an AGE now, like every table beside it: it was the one open figure on the page with no age against it, on the one thing he said to do immediately.

AND THE MORNING NUDGE WAKES HIM ON IT. customerRefunds is a COLLECTION, so it is read out of entry and never out of state, and it is keyed on the row's own paidOn rather than a date, because a refund carries `since` and the seed leaves entry.date null. A row that will not parse is not read as an open refund.

WHAT STILL CLOSES IT IS THE LAPTOP. Nothing anywhere writes paidOn onto a refund row: not the drafter, not the fold, not a Correction, whose findRow searches sales and purchases alone. It is closed by adding paidOn in ledger/book.json, then booksync and a build, and the six readers drop it of their own accord. A tap on the phone would need a migration rebuilding the draft table's CHECK, and that is its own fold.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 9 assertions: every open refund Now and saying whose money it is, the Today badge reached, the rail's mirror term, the table's age column and its total spanning the words beside it, and the daily nudge DRIVEN against a stubbed push service three ways: quiet on a refund already paid, waking him on an open one, and quiet again on a row that will not parse. Eleven mutations each turned it red.

t: AN ID WITH A USERNAME AND NO ACCOUNT CANNOT SIGN IN, AND NOW SOMETHING MINTS ONE AND SOMETHING SAYS SO
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: an Add ID or an Amend ID is applicable to the accounts available for sign in, and their password is minted properly. The fold mints a USERNAME when an ID is registered and stops there. A username is an address; an account is a record with a verifier, a wrap of the content key and a sealed bundle, and those were made only on the laptop at a monthly issue, because that is where the content key lives. So anybody added between issues had an address and nothing behind it and could not sign in at all. TWO WERE IN THAT STATE ON THE LIVE BOOK, silently, and one more had no username at all.

THE TOOL MINTS THE WHOLE ACCOUNT, and only for a code that has none: a password, the verifier it answers, the content key wrapped under it, the same key wrapped under the master, the password sealed under the master so Send can hand it over from his phone, and a bundle holding their position as it stands. A code with no username gets one first, exactly as the fold mints one. It runs on the laptop and nowhere else, for the same reason the seal tool does, and everything it writes is a committed file, so the next publish hands them out with no further step.

WHAT IT WILL NOT DO. It never touches an account that exists: re-issuing somebody's password is the seal tool's business and would lock out a customer who already has one. It never mints for a bucket, which is not its own person, nor for a supplier, which has no statement. And it refuses to start unless the master it is given unwraps a record that already exists, because a wrapMaster written under the wrong passphrase opens nothing and looks perfectly well formed.

AND THE PUBLISH SAYS WHO IS STUCK, ON EVERY RUN. It cannot mint one itself, deliberately: the content key and the master are laptop-only. So it names them and names the one command, which is the half of this that can never be silent again.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 16 assertions: who is stuck read off records alone, a bucket and a supplier never counted, an existing account left alone, the refusal with no master and the refusal with a master that unwraps nothing, and the minted account driven end to end: the password answers the verifier, unwraps the content key, opens the bundle, and is readable back under the master. Twelve mutations each turned it red, two of them by breaking the account so quietly that only opening it would tell.

t: AN ASSOCIATE SEES THEIR OWN CARD, BY MONTH, FROM THE START, AND NO SHARE OF HIS BOOK
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: in the customer's page, associates see their own live report card, by month, from the start, and for rewards they do not see the margin but a progress bar and a percentage to the next unit. It is a fourth sealed document on their own record, beside the statement and the price list and under the same content key, and a fourth tab that appears only where the record that opened actually carries one.

IT IS A DIFFERENT DOCUMENT FROM HIS. The report card of v691 is his view of EVERY associate and stays behind Access. This one is one associate's own, built by its own function off the same window the prices come from, so a card and a price can never be struck from different states of the book. Two functions rather than one, because the two audiences differ and the whitelist guarding his card would have had to widen to carry dated lines.

WHAT IS LEFT OFF IS THE POINT. Share is a ratio against the whole book's revenue, so an associate holding their own ringgit and their own share can solve for his total; stars are bands of that same share and give a range of it; rank is a position among other people. None of the three is theirs to know and none is needed to tell them what they did. The reward is in units, and the distance to the next travels as a share of ONE unit and is drawn as a bar, because the unit itself is a margin figure.

EVERY FIGURE ADDS UP TO THE LIST UNDER IT. The lines were struck off a different basis from the summary above them, so a pending order sat in the list and not in the total; they share pricedSales now. And the onward count was dsResell, which counts every R2 row including the pending and the cancelled: it read 14 above a list of 10. It counts the lines themselves now. Both are the lesson of v385, which is that a figure a reader can disprove by looking six lines down is worse than no figure.

AND EVERY MONTH PILL IS A REAL TAP TARGET. min-height was auto, so every pill on the month strip and the issue strip has been 29px tall since v690, on strips whose whole purpose is to be tapped on a phone. Swept across the class rather than fixed on the one new strip.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 18 assertions: no share, no stars, no rank and no margin anywhere in the card; the summary exactly its whitelist; every line a date, a kind, a size and a figure and nothing else; both books' figures adding up to their own lines; the reward's distance a share between nought and one; the seal only where there is a card; both doors driven with real sealed accounts; the tab hidden for everybody else and for an associate with no card; and the pills measured. Seventeen mutations each turned it red. Driven in Chromium at 375 touch and 1280 mouse: the bar drew empty until it was found that the fill is an i and not a span.

t: A PASSWORD FILED UNDER A NAME THAT HAS SINCE MOVED IS PAIRED BY ITS OWN VERIFIER
n: FOUR ACCOUNTS COULD NOT BE SENT, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM LOOKED LIKE A LOST PASSWORD. _passwords.json is keyed by the code as it was at the issue, and Amend ID re-keys a code wherever the book holds it. So a customer re-keyed after an issue has a password filed under a name that no longer exists: the pairing by name finds nothing, the account is never sealed, and Send has nothing to hand over. CA11-SEN had become CA2-SEN, CA5-KER CA5-BAN, CA7-JTR CA7-AMP and CH5-OUG CM3-OUG. Not one password was lost; all four were filed under the name the customer used to have.

A VERIFIER IS PROOF, NOT A GUESS. It answers one password and no other. So a record with no password under its own name is now tested against the passwords whose code is no longer on the roster, and the one that answers its own verifier is its password. Nothing is re-issued, and no customer is moved off a password they already hold, which matters: two of the four have opened their statements, so they have their password and only he did not.

ONLY AN ORPHANED PASSWORD IS EVER TRIED. One still filed under a live code is never claimed by another record, even in the case where it would answer that record's verifier, because it is somebody's and Send would hand it to the wrong person. And one password is one record: where two accounts were issued the same password and only one orphan sits between them, the second is reported rather than given one already claimed.
IT SAYS WHICH NAME IT FOUND IT UNDER. A code nobody recognises is otherwise a puzzle, and the answer is the whole explanation of why the account was stuck.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 11 assertions on fixtures: two re-keyed accounts each paired to their own password from two orphans listed in the wrong order, an account whose name never moved still paired by name, the sealed password opened back under the master and proved against its own verifier, a live customer's password refused to a record whose verifier it answers, one password claimed by one record only, and a wrong master refusing to start. Six mutations each turned it red, including the one that removes the pairing and restores the fault.

t: THE USER-FACING NAME IS SALT COUNTER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: name the user facing Salt Counter. It went Order Salt, then The Counter on his word that it be app-worthy, and now his own name for it, which keeps the counter and puts the trade back in front of it. Twelve characters exactly, which is what iOS gives a home screen. The manifest, the page title, the iPhone app title and the install tutorial all say the one thing.

THE PRODUCT WORD IS HIS TO SPEND THERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. Inside the page a product is still a mark and never a word, which is v695 and stands: the price list's headings, the order form's picker, the summary, the confirmation, every order card and the guest board all draw a cube or a droplet and write nothing. The app's name is the one place on this site where something has to be called something. What never appears anywhere is the DESK's name, which is a different rule and also stands.

THE CHECKS. The section is restated on the new name and now holds it to the desk's name never appearing, rather than to no product word at all, because that is what the rule actually is. The home-screen name is still held to twelve characters.

t: AN ASSOCIATE TICKS AN ORDER AS ON BEHALF OF A FRIEND, AND IT BOOKS TO THEIR BUCKET
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: an associate's own orders and the ones they place for somebody else can no longer be told apart by what they buy, so they get a tick. The words are his own, and they replaced an earlier phrasing he rejected. Nobody but an associate is offered it, and the placement cannot send it without the mark.

THE ENGINE DOES THE BOOKING, NOT THIS. A ticked order carries stream R2 and the associate's code, which is the shape the drafter already takes, and the drafter calls the engine's own bookR2, the same one the phone's downsell and the fold's correction call. A second copy of that rule would put two kinds of downsell in the book. The bucket is the engine's answer too, never a string with -R stuck on the end: a code that is already a bucket answers itself rather than growing a second suffix.

THE KEY NAMES THE ROW AS IT WILL STAND. It is built on the BUCKET, because that is the party the fold writes. Built on the associate's own code, the payment, the handover and the withdrawal would every one of them miss the row they were meant to amend, and the whole chain of v694 would quietly stop working for exactly the orders that mattered most.

WHO IS AN ASSOCIATE IS THE DESK'S OWN ANSWER. The publish reads the report card snapshot it already writes and marks that account's record, so the two readings cannot disagree about who one is. The mark travels in the clear beside the issue dates that already do: the tick has to be drawn before a password has opened anything sealed, and what it says is that this account MAY order for somebody else, which is not a figure, not a name and not a fact about the book. Both doors hand it over, a password open and a remembered one, or the tick would vanish the moment they stopped typing a password. The site checks nothing: it holds no roster, so it records the claim and the desk decides, exactly as with the quoted total.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 18 assertions: the tick taken only as a real true, the entry's shape against the drafter's, the bucket against the engine's own answer with a code that is already one, the key on the bucket and every later stage finding it, the drafter landing the row on the bucket with rev R2, an associate with no bucket on the roster not quietly landing one anyway, both doors driven with real sealed accounts, and the tick drawn for nobody else. Fourteen mutations each turned it red.

t: A TIER IS SET FOR CK4-SEN: PLATINUM ON SALT, NO CASH AND NO STOCK
n: FOLDED: one row, a tier setting only. CK4-SEN is put to Platinum on salt, recorded on the desk's word on 18 Sep. The drafter raised no flag and the row carries no order, no amount and no party history to test, since nothing is bought or sold. No cash moves, no stock is drawn, and no price changes until the quotes switch across to the new tier.

THE INVENTORY: unchanged at 10.5 unit, last counted 16 Sep on salt, with the cost basis held at RM48 a unit against a replacement of RM46. Nothing is owed out, 13.5 unit stands promised, and the reorder mark of 15 unit sits above the stated position as it did at v701. Outstanding from this fold: the quotes for CK4-SEN still have to be switched before the tier has any effect on rate.

t: THE STATEMENTS PUBLISH RUNS ON EVERY RUN BUT THE KEY PROBE, STATED AS WHAT IS EXCLUDED
n: HIS QUESTION OF 18 SEP 2026: CAN THE PUBLISH BE ON ANY TRIGGER? It can, and now it is. It needs nothing the job produces: it reads ledger/book.json and the master out of the checkout and never touches public/, so it depends on neither the fold, the build nor the deploy, and the checkout, the node setup and the install above it are themselves unconditional. Every credential it wants is already proved unconditionally in the same job.

THE RULE STATES WHAT IS EXCLUDED, NOT WHAT IT IS ON. That is the whole point of the change. A list of events goes stale the moment a trigger is added, and that is exactly how this broke: the publish was gated on the deploy alone, a scheduled tick sets deploy only when rows were actually folded, and so on a quiet day the sealed price lists were never refreshed at all while both the doc and his instruction said a price always follows the desk. v699 added the schedule beside the deploy, which fixed that day and left the same shape of bug standing for whatever trigger came next. One exclusion cannot go stale.
THE ONE EXCLUSION IS THE KEY PROBE, a dispatch whose whole purpose is one cheap call to prove the fold's credential and then stop. Publishing on it would contradict the only thing that step promises.

THE RETIRE SPLIT IS UNCHANGED AND NOW MATTERS MORE. A run that did not deploy passes --no-retire, so every sealed list, board, roster and report card is rewritten and no account is retired: retiring one whose record the newest issue does not carry is a judgement about a deploy he made, not about a clock or an approval, and a partial issue read would otherwise take accounts down on every tick rather than once.

THE CHECKS. The workflow section now asserts the shape of the rule rather than its cases: the publish is on unless the probe turns it off, and NOTHING anywhere turns it on for a named event, which is the list that went stale before. Seven mutations each turned it red, including the one that restores the v699 wording.

t: A CUSTOMER HOLDING AN UNPAID ADVANCE IS CHASED EVERY HOUR, DAY AND NIGHT, UNTIL IT IS PAID
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: the customer is notified every hour to pay if it is an advanced order. An advance is the book's own word, goods out with money owed, so that is the test: the order is agreed, something has been handed over, and something is still owed, the delivery charge included because that is what the customer is asked for. Somebody who has paid nothing on an order he has not touched yet is never chased, because nothing of his is in their hands.

THE FIRST CLOCK THE STATEMENTS SITE HAS EVER HAD. Until now that Worker woke a phone only as a side effect of the desk touching an order; it had no cron and no scheduled handler at all. It has both now, on the hour, every hour. A cron in that config reaches production only through a deploy of it: rev.json's id does not cover the file, so the update chain reports the phone current and ships nothing, and the file says so beside the cron.

ONE WAKE AN HOUR PER CUSTOMER, NOT PER ORDER. Two unpaid advances are one person's problem and one banner. The cap is the hour ITSELF rather than a timestamp to subtract from: the mark holds the hour bucket the customer was last woken in, so a tick that fires twice inside an hour, or fires late, cannot chase twice. It expires after two hours, so a customer who settles up leaves nothing behind and there is nothing to turn off. His test account is skipped, because it is counted nowhere and that includes being chased.

THE BANNER NAMES NOTHING, AND COULD NOT. It is the same payload-free wake the desk's own moves send, so the words are the service worker's one fixed string and no amount and no order can reach it.
