Every push path on this site swallows its own failures by design, so the tick logs its counts: a wake that reached nobody and a wake that was not needed look identical from outside.

AND A PAYMENT THAT COMPLETES AN ORDER WAKES THE PHONE. It is the one move of the customer's own worth waking for, because it is the only one whose answer arrives after they have put the phone down; every other one happens with the page in front of them.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 17 assertions: the predicate against goods out, money owed, a part payment, the delivery charge, and four things that are not an advance; the tick driven against a stubbed push service through four hours, proving the one customer woken, the test account skipped, the payload absent, a second tick in the same hour chasing nobody, the next hour chasing again, the mark and its expiry, the chase stopping of its own accord once paid, and a Worker with no push key waking nobody without throwing. Fourteen mutations each turned it red. The log is captured around the tick alone, because stubbing it across the block would have swallowed the suite's own failure line.

t: A STANDING LINK READS ITS LEVEL'S BOARD, AND THE STATEMENTS PUBLISH RUNS EVERY HOUR
n: THE HOLE v696 LEFT, ITS OWN SHAPE. The five standing links are minted the first time he opens the Links panel, and their boards were written by the publish under each link's own id. So any link minted since the last publish had no board and fell back to board:2, which is the LAST level: four of the five would have quoted Bronze until the next deploy, and nothing would have said so. A standing link IS a level, and a level's board does not depend on which link points at it, so the five boards are now written under tboard:1 to tboard:5 and a standing link reads its own level's. Nothing is published per standing link, so minting one can never be wrong. tboard: and not board:, because board:2 already means the last level and not the second, and reusing it would make 2 mean two things.

HIS INSTRUCTION THAT A CUSTOMER'S PRICES ALWAYS FOLLOW THE DESK, ACTUALLY KEPT. The publish was gated on the deploy alone, and a bare scheduled tick sets deploy only when rows were folded, so on a quiet day the sealed price lists were never refreshed at all. The job's plan step now carries a third output: a publish is any run that deploys, or the hourly tick. A price is at most an hour behind the desk, which is what the doc has claimed since the day it was written.

WRITING IS HOURLY; RETIRING IS NOT. The publish retires an account whose record the newest issue does not carry, and that is a judgement about a deploy he made rather than about a clock: a partial or botched issue read would otherwise take accounts down twenty-four times a day instead of once. The hourly run passes --no-retire, which leaves every list, board, roster and report card rewritten and nothing deleted.

A LINK THAT NAMES AN INTRODUCER IS UNTOUCHED. Its board does depend on who handed it out, so it still reads its own, and one minted since the last publish still falls back to the board every stranger sees, which is the cap a guest board cannot pass.

AND THE UPDATE CHAIN STOPPED MANGLING ITS OWN COMMIT MESSAGES. tools/update.mjs passed the message as JSON.stringify(message), which turns every real newline into the two characters backslash-n, so v694 through v698 each landed as one line with the breaks written out. Nobody saw it because git log --oneline prints the subject alone and the subject still read properly. The message goes through a file and git commit -F now, which is also the only route that survives PowerShell here: a heredoc breaks on an apostrophe and a pipe adds a BOM. The five messages already pushed are left as they are, because history is not rewritten with three writers on this branch; master/changelog.json carries the real record of each.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 13 assertions driving the guest door: each of the five serves its own level's prices with nothing written under its id, none of them falls back to the stranger's board, no gboard key exists for a standing link, an introducer's link still reads its own, a missing level board and a store with no tier names both fall back rather than guess or throw, and the publish writes the five and can be told not to retire. Twelve mutations each turned it red, three of them against the workflow's own section.

t: A FIVE UNIT SALT ORDER IS BOOKED PENDING: ACKNOWLEDGED, NOTHING PAID, NOTHING MOVED
n: FOLDED: one row, a salt sell to CS6-BS dated 18 Sep, 5 unit for RM420, taken off the statements site under order 20260916085105-rkoi5a and acknowledged for collection. No cash came in and no goods went out, so the row sits pending: it draws no stock and books no revenue until something moves. The total clears the RM254.98 floor for 5 unit and sits under the RM560 ask and the RM710 ceiling.

UNUSUAL: the drafter flagged CS6-BS at about RM107.50 a unit across 18 orders against RM84 here, 21.9% below, and the party record shows 12 orders at a median of RM100 with a range of RM11 to RM126.67. The figures show the gap but do not explain it. THE INVENTORY: untouched at 10.5 unit on the salt count of 16 Sep, costed at its own RM48 a unit, with nothing owed out.

t: THE APP ON A CUSTOMER'S PHONE IS THE COUNTER, AND THE THREE OLDER GUEST LINKS ARE WITHDRAWN
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: name the default as something else that is app-worthy. It was Order Salt for one version, which put the product word straight back onto the one surface v695 had just taken it off. THE COUNTER is the shop counter: where you are served, see what you owe, order and collect. It says what the app is FOR, it names no product and no business, and at eleven characters it fits inside the twelve iOS gives a home screen. The manifest, the page title, the iPhone app title and the install tutorial all say the one thing.

AND THE THREE OLDER GUEST LINKS ARE WITHDRAWN (a change to the store, not to this build), so what answers is exactly the five standing tier links of v696 and nothing else. Each was revoked rather than deleted, which is the rule this site already held: the record keeps what the link did, the id can never be minted onto a second party, and one tap on Restore brings it back. All three now answer the same 404 an id that never existed does, so a withdrawn link cannot be told from one that was never made.

THE CHECKS. The v695 section is restated on the new name and holds the home-screen name to twelve characters and to naming no product. Eighteen mutations each turn it red, two of them new: the name carrying a product word again, and a name too long for a home screen.

t: THE GUEST LINKS ARE FIVE, ONE FOR EACH TIER, AND EACH ONE IS A LEVEL AND NOTHING ELSE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: for the guest links, produce exactly five, for the five tier pricing. A link used to name the customer who handed it out and be quoted two levels above them; the five stand for the ladder itself. Titanium, Platinum, Gold, Silver and Bronze, and Ambassador is not among them, because it is the floor and never a guest's.

ENSURED, NOT MADE ON A TAP. Opening the Links panel makes whichever of the five are missing and hands all five back in the ladder's order. It is idempotent, and a level that already has a link keeps the id it was given, because an id handed to a stranger must never change what it opens. The level names come from the book, through the key the publish writes, so nothing under stmt/ states what the tiers are called; with no names to hand it makes none rather than inventing five.

A STANDING BOARD IS A LEVEL WITH THE LADDER PINNED. tierBoard is boardList with the level fixed, rather than a second way of reading the ladder, so a guest and a customer can never be quoted off different inputs. The publish writes one for each on every deploy, exactly as it does for the links that name an introducer, which still work and still follow the customer who handed them out. On today's book the five ask RM 860, 960, 1,060, 1,160 and 1,250 for the largest size of salt, the last of them what a stranger is quoted anyway.
ONE FAULT THE CHECKS CAUGHT. The clamp on the level read `+level || 5`, and zero is falsy, so a link asking for the floor would have been served the ask. Read the number, then decide.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 17 assertions: the five and their order, that ensuring them twice mints nothing, that a link named against a customer neither becomes one nor disturbs them, that the five boards are five climbing prices and each says which level it is, that a level off either end is held to the five, and the listing driven through the Worker behind a real Access token, made deliberately out of order so the order it comes back in can only be the ladder's. Twelve mutations each turned it red.

t: A PRODUCT IS A MARK AND NEVER A WORD, AND THE APP ON A CUSTOMER'S PHONE IS ORDER SALT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: the name Salt Command appears nowhere a customer can see, and neither does the name of a product if it can be helped. The products are written only as a symbol, a golden cube outline for the one and a golden water droplet outline for the other. So the statements site draws its products now and writes none of them: the price list's headings, the order form's picker, the summary line, the confirmation, every order card and the guest board a stranger opens.

THE MARKS ARE DRAWN HERE, NOT LOADED. Two paths in one table, stroked in the ink they sit in, so the cube on the chosen brass button is dark and the one beside it is brass. A product with no mark of its own draws a ring rather than nothing, because a blank reads as a fault and an omission should not. The order form's product dropdown became a segment of marks, because an option carries text and no drawing, and two products were a segment anyway.

A CONTROL THAT HOLDS ONLY A MARK IS NAMED BY ITS SHAPE. Cube, Droplet, Ring, never the product: a button holding a decorative drawing and nothing else cannot be used with a screen reader, and naming the product in its label would put the word back for exactly the readers who cannot see that it was taken away. The shape is what is on the screen, so saying it aloud gives away no more than looking does.

THE ONE NAME ON THE SITE IS THE APP'S. The icon a customer keeps on a home screen says Order Salt, his own word, and the manifest, the title, the iPhone app title and the install tutorial all say the same one thing. The desk is Salt Command and that name is on none of it.

AND THE LETTERHEAD IS GONE. The statement documents carried Salt Command as an eyebrow, kept deliberately until now because changing it rewrites every archive; his instruction outranks that. The live statement and every new issue carry no eyebrow at all rather than an empty one. The issues already sealed keep the letterhead they were issued with, because a dated record is not corrected in place.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 16 assertions: the two paths and the ring, the shape names against the product names, the guest board's words with its stylesheet taken out (every design token is named --salt-something, which is a variable nobody reads), the app's four names, the letterhead, and the page driven in jsdom through the price list, the segment, a product still waiting for its price and a live order's own card, with no product word anywhere on any of it. Sixteen mutations each turned it red. The v651 and v693 sections are restated on the mark and the new name.

t: AN ORDER REACHES THE LEDGER IN STAGES, AND MONEY AND GOODS MOVE APART
n: HIS INSTRUCTIONS OF 18 SEP 2026. An order used to reach the book once, at the end, as a sale paid and delivered in full on the day. It now reaches it as it happens. He acknowledges the order, with the delivery charge typed on the card rather than in a browser prompt, and that is the moment the row is made: a PENDING sale, the delivery inside its total, nothing paid and nothing moved. Every later step amends that row.

SITE ORDERS MOVES THE ORDER; APPROVE LANDS THE ROW. No tap on the card writes anything now. The Worker's every-minute reconcile is the ONE road that queues, so a stage cannot be queued twice by two roads racing: a payment queues a Fulfilment of the INCREMENT, because a Fulfilment accumulates; a handover queues a Correction stating the RUNNING TOTAL, the day and who moved it, because only a Correction may set those and it states rather than adds; a withdrawal queues a Cancellation, and the fold raises the refund itself. Each waits under Approve like every other row.

WHICH ROW A LATER STAGE AMENDS. A rid is minted at fold time and there is no route from the desk back to the site, so the site can never learn it. The desk writes the other identifier the drafter takes onto the order at the acknowledgement, and it is the engine's own ovKey to the character. Written here with toFixed(2) it missed every row by two noughts, which nothing but driving the chain end to end would have shown. An amendment WAITS while the row is not yet on the book, rather than queueing one the drafter would refuse and putting a refusal on his phone every time a customer paid early.

MONEY AND GOODS ARE TWO TRACKS, HIS RULE. He may deliver first or be paid first. The customer types what they paid, part payments accumulate and more than what is outstanding is refused; he types what he handed over. Paid ahead reads Open · Deferred, goods out ahead reads Open · Advance, and Completed is neither side's tap: it is what the record reads when both are complete, and the page then says his own closing words.

CASH ON HANDOVER IS WITHHELD from anyone holding an unpaid advance on another live order, because settling that at the door is how one advance becomes two. Either side may withdraw at any stage until the goods move, and the customer is told what a withdrawal refunds.

ON THE CUSTOMER'S PAGE. Nothing is placed on one tap: the order is reviewed in words first. A delivery says roughly where it is going, one line, a neighbourhood and not an address, which stays on the site and never rides into a ledger note, because a note reaches the committed book. And the dropdown he called bizarre is fixed: the open list is drawn by the system, and with no colour scheme declared it drew a white list under a dark field. It is told the page is dark, and the chevron appearance:none took away is drawn back out of two gradients, nothing loaded.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 36 assertions driving both Workers, the reconcile, the drafter and the fold end to end: the location, the review, the pending row, the key against the engine's own ovKey, the increment against the running total, both endings, the withheld rail, and the six entries folded in order onto one row through Pending, Open · Deferred and Completed. Twenty mutations each turned it red. The v499 section is restated on the new road.

t: THE SITE CAN BE KEPT AS AN APP, AND EVERY LOGIN ASKS ABOUT NOTIFICATIONS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: a short tutorial for saving the page as an app, and an ask for notifications on every login. Adding it to a home screen gave a screenshot with no name before this, because the site had no manifest and no icon at all.

THE ICON IS DRAWN, NOT BORROWED. The desk's plate is the brand, and nothing a customer keeps on a home screen may name the business, so this is a neutral tile: obsidian with a brass ring. The site serves no assets, so it lives as bytes in stmt/icons.js, written by tools/stmt-icon.mjs --sync (a PNG encoded by hand, no image library), and the gate checks the module against the generator. The app is called Statement of account.
THE DOOR TEACHES IT ONCE: three steps, the iPhone's Share and the Android menu, hidden the moment the page is running as an app.

THE ASK COMES ON THE WAY IN, AND ONLY WHERE THE ANSWER IS OPEN. A browser that has already granted or refused is never asked again; the button in the order tab stays for a reader who changes their mind. One fault it caught: the page registered a service worker before asking, so a browser that refused the registration never reached the question at all.

THE CHECKS: the module against its generator, the manifest and the icon as served (a real 512px PNG), the policy admitting the manifest, the tutorial shown in a browser and hidden in the app, and the ask fired once on a login and not at all after a refusal. Seven reverts each turned it red.

t: THE DOOR SAYS LOG IN, REMEMBERS A DEVICE WITHOUT KEEPING A PASSWORD, AND LOG OUT ENDS IT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: no three-minute lock, a Remember me, and a Log out. The lock was a privacy lock for a phone left on a table; what replaces it says what it does. The button reads Log in, the bar reads Log out, and nothing counts down.

REMEMBER ME IS SPLIT IN TWO, AND NEITHER HALF OPENS ANYTHING ALONE. The browser makes a random device key, wraps the content key under it, and keeps the key; the site keeps the wrap at rem:<token> for thirty days. A copy of the store opens nothing, a stolen device with no token opens nothing, and the password is kept nowhere. Remembering is minted on a session, which only a correct password mints.

LOGGING OUT IS A DEPARTURE. It drops the session and the remembered wrap on the site as well as everything the page holds, so a phone handed on is a phone signed out. A token only ever forgets its own account, and an unknown token is refused in the door's one refusal, which says nothing about what exists.
THE COPY FOLLOWED IT: the door, the QR caption on every statement, the message a customer is sent and the docs no longer promise three minutes.

THE CHECKS: the Worker's half (a session mints the token, the wrap expires in thirty days, no password in it, one device cannot sign another out, log out drops both) and the page's half end to end: signing in with the box ticked sends a wrap and keeps a key, a second page with only that key and token opens the statement with no password typed, and Log out forgets it. Eleven reverts each turned it red. One real fault it caught: the content key was imported unextractable, so Remember me could not wrap it at all.

t: THE ASSOCIATES REPORT CARD, IN UNITS AND SHARES, WITH NO MARGIN ANYWHERE NEAR IT
n: HIS DECISION OF 18 SEP 2026: the third item on the master account. One card an associate a book: what they bought from him, what they sold for him, what they brought in, how many onward sales and introductions, their share of all revenue and their stars, and the reward.

THE REWARD IS IN UNITS, AND THE PART-UNIT IS A BAR. Earned, taken and left are units, which a customer already sees; how far they are through the next one is a proportion drawn as a rule and a fill. What does not travel is margin: the distance to the next unit is a margin figure, which is why the phone payload dropped it at v616, so the snapshot turns it into a share of one and carries nothing else. A book with no reward, which is oil, says so rather than showing a zero.

READ OFF THE DESK, ONCE. associateSnapshot opens the same window the prices come from, sets each book, reads networkStats, rebateApplied, isDeparted and canRedeem, and puts the desk back on the book it found it on. It goes up as assoc in the same bulk put as the records, and is served only at /all/assoc, behind Access with the rest.
CODES ONLY, AND NOTHING OF THE PERSON. A departure is a yes or a no; his reason, the memorial and the note stay on the desk.

THE CHECKS: the snapshot against the real desk for its whitelist, its words, its codes, the book it leaves behind and oil's null reward; the publish carrying it and not inventing one; the route behind Access; and the panel drawn in jsdom, one card an associate, never the word margin, with the bar. Eight reverts each turned it red.

t: A CUSTOMER'S STATEMENT IS NOT BOUND TO A MONTH: EVERYTHING, FILTERED TO THE NEWEST
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: nothing customer-facing is time bound. It shows all, and the view opens filtered by month. The live statement already carried every order from the start; what was missing was a way to read one month of it without losing the rest.

THE ROW CARRIES ITS MONTH. Each dated row is tagged in the document itself, so the page builds the strip from the months that account actually has, newest first, with All at the end; an undated row belongs to no month and shows whatever is chosen. The newest month opens, because that is what a reader has come for.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. The filter hides rows and changes nothing else: what the account stands at is the account's, whatever is on screen, and the line under the strip says so in as many words.

THE CHECKS: the document's tags against the rows the statement was built from, then the page driven as a customer drives it, sealed bundle and stubbed door: the strip is the months plus All, it opens on the newest, All brings everything back, a month shows only its own, and filtering moves no text. Five reverts each turned it red.

t: A TEST ACCOUNT HE MAKES AND UNMAKES WITH ONE TAP, THAT COUNTS NOWHERE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: an account for trying the page out, working everywhere a customer's does, counted nowhere, and gone with one button. Username 0000-0000, password 0000-0000-0000-0000, both of them zeros, which no real username or password can hold: the alphabet has none, so it can collide with nothing and cannot be arrived at by mistyping an account.

THE WORKER MINTS IT ITSELF, with a key made on the spot, a plain statement that says what it is, and a small price list, so nothing real is behind it and no laptop secret is involved. It signs in with the zeros typed any way, opens in the reader's own browser like any account, and has a session, so the order tab works.

COUNTED NOWHERE. It is on his list marked as the test account and out of the count of accounts and of the send; the publish neither writes it nor retires it, where every other unknown record is retired; and no desk code maps to it, so an order it places books nothing. Deleting it takes its orders, its opens, its ticks and any phone it subscribed, and touches nobody else's.

THE CHECKS: the door's one exception, making it behind Access, opening it and decrypting its statement with the zeros, its place on the list, the publish leaving it alone, and the delete taking everything of its own and nothing of anyone else's. Seven reverts each turned it red.

t: SEND STATEMENT, WITH THE PASSWORD SEALED UNDER THE MASTER AND A TICK BOTH HIS DEVICES SHARE
n: HIS DECISION OF 18 SEP 2026: sending is done from the master account, password and all. A card an account carries the address, the message, the code and the password: Share, Copy message, Copy password, Open account, and a Sent tick. The laptop's send sheet stays as the fallback for a day the site or Access is down.

THE PASSWORD IS SEALED, NOT STORED. An issue now seals each password under STMT_MASTER beside its record, and tools/stmt-seal.mjs sealed the issue that had already gone out, on the laptop, from _passwords.json: it proves the master against every record first, pairs each password through the send sheet's own rule so a re-keyed code still finds its own, proves it against that record's verifier, and writes nothing else into the file. Thirty of thirty-four September records sealed; three are buckets, and four have no password on this laptop. The publish strips it from the record a customer fetches and carries it only in the account list behind Access. His page opens it in the browser and writes it to the clipboard; it is never written into the page, and no message ever carries it. The trade he took: an Access session now also signs in as a customer.

A TICK IS THE SITE'S. The laptop sheet kept its ticks in one browser, so sending half an issue on the phone left two half-finished lists. A tick is sent:<issue>:<username>, expiring with its issue, and both devices show the same. The words a customer is sent live in stmt/send.js, which the laptop sheet imports, so the two cannot drift.

THE CHECKS: a new section builds a fixture issue and seals it: idempotent, refusing a master the records do not answer to, refusing a password their verifier refuses, refusing a past issue, and changing nothing else in a record. Then the publish's split, the card's own data, the tick's four refusals and its expiry, and the page driven in jsdom: Copy password opens the sealed password and copies it, and the page never holds it. Fourteen reverts each turned it red. Checked in Chromium at 375 and 1280.

t: THE MASTER ACCOUNT OPENS ON ITS OWN PAGE, AND THE OWNER'S SCRIPT TRAVELS ONLY THERE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 18 SEP 2026: a master account that opens on what it can do. /all is that account, behind Access as before, and it opens on its items rather than on a list: Review statement, and the links below it. Send statement and the associates report card join it as they are built.

THE OWNER'S SCRIPT LEFT EVERY CUSTOMER'S PAGE. It sat inside the one script string served on both doors since v566, so the roster code, the guest-link calls and the word master travelled to every customer; only the markup was gated. It is stmt/owner.js now, spliced in on his route alone, which is what makes it safe to build the rest of the master account.

REVIEW SAYS WHERE EACH ACCOUNT STANDS AND WHEN IT WAS LAST OPENED. One word per account, owes, goods, refund, pend or clear, from the rule the review sheet has always used, now stated once in accountTotals and reviewFlag and read by the sheet and by the publish through partyTotals, so the laptop and the phone cannot disagree. The opens come from the seen: keys the Worker has written since v499 and nothing had ever read. A bucket is never an account of its own (his instruction of 18 Sep 2026): it keeps its username line and maps to nothing.

ON BEHALF OF A FRIEND (his instruction of 18 Sep 2026): a bucket's row on a statement reads that, where it read for resale. The row is the same row and books the same way; the word is the customer's rather than the trade's.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads the split, the flag rule, the publish's account list over the real book, and the route behind Access with an account list merged from a minted token; the master page is driven in jsdom from its items to Review and back. Nine reverts each turned it red.

t: A SALT SALE AT RM52.50 A UNIT: PAID, COLLECTED, AND BARELY OVER THE FLOOR
n: FOLDED: one salt sale, 2 unit to CC5-OKR for RM105, RM105 cash in and 2 unit moved on 17 Sep, collected, so the row closes on the day it opens. The total clears the RM101.99 floor for this size by a margin of a few ringgit and sits far under the RM300 ask and the RM290 ceiling. Costed at RM48 a unit, the inventory's own rate, RM96 on the goods.

UNUSUAL: the drafter flagged the rate, CC5-OKR having paid about RM90 a unit across 5 orders against RM52.50 here, 41.7% below, and the figures show the discount without explaining it. The party also carries RM90 outstanding from before and 1 unit on credit against a cap of 1. The inventory gave up 2 unit against a stated 12.5 and the cost basis did not move.

t: FROM 861 TO 1080PX, THE CHART PAIR, THE CALENDAR AND THE LEDGER FIT BESIDE THE RAIL
n: WHAT WAS WRONG: above 860px the rail takes 232px of the window on every screen, and three parts needed more than the column left them. Measured on v684 in Chromium with a mouse, a fresh load at every width from 861 to 1280px: the Pricing chart pair ran past the page column to 959px, the approach calendar on Network to 1027px, and the ledger on The book from 868 to 1033px; the page itself scrolled sideways to 923, 1009 and 1015px.

THE CHART PAIR takes two columns that may be narrower than the chart each holds, where a plain share would not go under a 330px chart. THE CALENDAR keeps one column up to 1079px, as it did up to 860px, because its three need 760px. THE LEDGER re-flows the same cells onto its narrow rows below 820px of its own width, where it was 600px: every column is its longest entry and none shrinks, so the two-row shape needed 765px on the book as it stands, and the margin is for the book to grow. Nothing is hidden at any width.

MEASURED AFTER: from 861 to 1280px, all seven destinations, nothing runs past the page column and nothing scrolls sideways. From 560 to 860px nothing moved. All seventeen parts at 1280 and at 375 as a phone read the same pixels as before.
THE CHECKS: a new section reads the three rules; three reverts each turned it red. v684's calendar check now holds that the fits start no lower than 860px.

t: ON A DESKTOP THE RAIL STANDS AT EVERY WIDTH; ONLY A TOUCH SCREEN FOLDS IT INTO THE MENU
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 17 SEP 2026: on a desktop browser the navigation bar on the left does not collapse. The menu was keyed on the window's width alone, so any desktop window at 860px or narrower lost the rail behind the menu button. It is keyed on a touch screen as well now: with a mouse the rail stands beside the page at every width, and a phone keeps its menu as before. A menu left open when its layout ends, a window widened or a keyboard docked, closes itself.

WHAT A NARROW DESKTOP WINDOW NEEDED WITH IT. The rail takes 232px from the page, so two fits the phone already had now start at 860px: a section heading wraps, and the approach calendar's panels may shrink. The week grid scrolls in its own box from 860px too, and the Coverage map and the place picker at Add ID are drawn for the page column rather than the window, so their names keep their size. Measured in Chromium with a mouse, no page scrolls sideways from 580 to 860px, nor at 1024 or 1280. Below 580px The book still does, and Enter by a pixel at 561px; at 861px Pricing and Network did before this version and still do.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED: all seventeen parts, at 1280 and at 375 as a phone, read the same pixels before and after. The pixel instrument was wrong for a phone: a full-page capture under touch emulation turns the touch pointer off, so a phone shot now grows the view to the page instead.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads every rule that folds the rail into the menu for the touch condition, the standing rail's width and hidden brand, and the fits; it draws the map and the picker for a 600px column and closes an open menu as its layout ends. Thirteen reverts each turned it red. The rail width check reads the new condition.

t: A REWARD UNIT GOES OUT FREE: COST IN, NO REVENUE
n: FOLDED: one row, a redemption of 1 unit of salt to CS6-BS dated 17 Sep, settled by the reward and not in cash. On his ruling of 11 Sep 2026 the row carries both rebate and goodwill, so it stays out of revenue and its RM48 of cost stands as an expense. The unit was delivered the same day, leaving nothing outstanding against the party.

UNUSUAL: the total of RM48 sits under the RM51 floor for this size because nothing was charged, the figure being the shelf cost carried through. The drafter flagged that the reward balance, 5 earned and 4 applied leaving 1, is the desk's word and cannot be checked here. The inventory rolled the stated shelf down by the unit and held the cost basis where it stood.

t: AT ADD ID AND AMEND ID THE LOCATION IS CHOSEN FROM A LIST
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 17 SEP 2026: all the locations listed, so he can choose one, holding his own areas. Both place boxes now offer 137 locations, each read as a party's location is: Bangsar, Lembah Pantai, Kuala Lumpur. Type a few letters and choose; a location chosen carries its own point, so it is placed at once with no search and no tap, the code is made from its locality and the locality is filed with it. A place typed that is not on the list is still looked up as before.

WHAT THE LIST HOLDS. The neighbourhoods on his map of Kuala Lumpur and the sub-districts on his Selangor list, 93 of them placed from GeoNames' Malaysia file inside the district he listed each under, the file downloaded on his word and never committed; every locality already filed, so a location he files joins the list; and every constituency. A name on his list keeps its own point over a party filed there. A district alone is too broad a place to choose and is not listed.

WHAT IS NOT ON IT. 66 of his names are not placed by GeoNames at all or stand for more than one place there, among them Kepong Baru, Shamelin, KLCC, Kota Kemuning and Taman Sri Muda; they are left off rather than guessed, and are typed and tapped as before. Setapak and Sungai Besi, on both of his lists, lie in Kuala Lumpur and are listed there once.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads the list as committed, the desk's locations and their order, the rule that his list wins, both place boxes and a choice from the list through to its code and locality; ten reverts each turned it red. Checked in Chromium at phone width: the list is on the form and a choice is placed at once.

t: SELANGOR AND NEGERI SEMBILAN ARE SHADED BY THEIR CONSTITUENCIES TOO
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 17 SEP 2026: do the same for Selangor and Negeri Sembilan. Their areas on Coverage are their federal constituencies of the 2018 delimitation, 22 and 8, from the same pinned MECo file as Kuala Lumpur's eleven, public domain under CC0. Each is filed under the district holding its centre, so Petaling opens on six, Klang on three, Seremban on Seremban and Rasah, and Sepang, whose seat centres in Kuala Langat, on the seats that meet its frame.

THE SURVEY'S AREAS ARE RETIRED. No core district is left with a mukim, bandar or pekan, so tools/areafetch.mjs no longer fetches ADM3 and its credit is gone from under the map. The 91 districts are byte for byte what they were, and so are Kuala Lumpur's seats. Coverage offers a district's constituencies, and its lead says constituency wherever one is opened.

WHERE A PARTY IS NOW READS ITS CONSTITUENCY IN ALL THREE STATES. CE5-SA reads Setia Alam, Shah Alam, Petaling where v680 read Bukit Raja; CY2-NIL reads Nilai, Seremban, the seat and the district named once. A point is still the old kilometre-rounded one until an Amend ID finds it again, so CM6-PJ reads Petaling Jaya, Damansara, Petaling.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads the two states' seats by name, the leads and two parties' locations, six reverts each turning it red; v630's survey counts and licence, v637's fixture district (Jelebu now holds one seat, so it drills Sabak Bernam's two), v678's spill check and v679's Ampang are restated to the constituencies.

t: WHERE EACH PARTY IS, IN WORDS, FOR EVERYONE: LOCALITY, AREA, DISTRICT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 17 SEP 2026: the location of each customer includes the locality and the district, where available, and everyone may see it. Coverage's party table has a Where column: CA5-BAN reads Bangsar, Lembah Pantai, Kuala Lumpur; CA7-AMP Ampang, Titiwangsa, Kuala Lumpur; CE5-SA Setia Alam, Bukit Raja, Petaling.

WHAT IT READS. The locality filed beside the party's point, with the short forms people write spelled out (Rd, Sg, Bkt, Bdr, Jln, Tmn, Kg); the area the point stands in, a constituency in Kuala Lumpur and elsewhere the sub-area on the survey his Selangor list follows; and the district. Each is named once, and what is not known is left out, so a place abroad reads its locality alone.

WHAT WAS FILED. Thirty-eight parties carry a locality: thirty-five from the places recorded in the directory, each at the point it already stood at, so nothing moved on the map; and his three at new points, measured inside Lembah Pantai, Titiwangsa and mukim Bukit Raja. CM3-OUG, CA2-SEN and CB7-BJ have no recorded place on the laptop, so theirs come through the vault road on Coverage or an Amend ID.

THE LEAK CHECKS FOLLOW HIS DECISION. The extract's scan and the suite's public-desk scan pass a directory place that equals a filed locality, through one definition in tools/book.mjs; every name is still searched, and so is every place not filed.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads his three off the book and through the desk, the rules off fixture codes, and the Where column as drawn; seven reverts each turned it red. v637's panel reader skips the new column, which this section reads.

t: A PLACE IS ITS LOCALITY, THEN WHERE THAT IS: THE CODE FROM THE LOCALITY, THE LOCALITY WITH THE POINT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 17 SEP 2026: BAN is Bangsar, KL; AMP is Ampang, KL; SA is Setia Alam, SG; and Amend IDs will follow to make every location accurate. A typed place now reads as a locality, then where that is.

THE CODE IS MADE FROM THE LOCALITY, the words before the first comma, where every word used to count. Bangsar, KL keeps BAN where it would have become BK, so writing the district after a place never re-keys a party. A place with no comma codes exactly as before, TBC included.

THE LOCALITY TRAVELS WITH THE POINT, as its third element, through Add ID, Amend ID and the vault road on Coverage; public by his decision of 17 Sep 2026, while the name still never leaves the vault. Amend ID sends a place entry when only the locality changed. The vault road now also takes each party whose point is filed without a locality, keeping the point and adding the locality. The drafter keeps a locality of one to sixty characters with no markup, trimmed, and refuses anything else in its place.

WHAT FOLLOWS THE LOCALITY CONFINES THE LOOKUP. A comma part naming a district or a state, KL for Kuala Lumpur and a lone SG or SGR for Selangor, keeps the search inside it, so Ampang, KL is never Selangor's Ampang. The districts on the desk now carry their state for it, which the map still never names.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads the code rule, the point, the lookup for his three places, the vault road and the drafter, twelve reverts each turning it red; v633's checks that the place never travelled are restated to the locality travelling and the name never, three more reverts proving Add ID and Amend ID carry it.

t: KUALA LUMPUR IS SHADED BY ITS ELEVEN CONSTITUENCIES
n: HIS DECISION OF 17 SEP 2026. Thirty of the thirty-five parties on Coverage stand in Kuala Lumpur, and the survey behind the finer areas gave the territory ten coarse ones, so a tap on it told him nothing. Its areas are now its eleven federal constituencies: Kepong, Batu, Wangsa Maju, Segambut, Setiawangsa, Titiwangsa, Bukit Bintang, Lembah Pantai, Seputeh, Cheras and Bandar Tun Razak, the names his own map of the city prints. The thirty now spread across nine of them.

THE SOURCE. The 2018 federal delimitation, in force since GE14, from the Malaysian Election Corpus (Thevananthan and Chacko), public domain under CC0, pinned to a commit in tools/areafetch.mjs and credited under the map. Every district and every area outside Kuala Lumpur is byte for byte what it was.

A POINT IS NAMED BY ITS OWN DISTRICT FIRST. The survey files mukim Petaling under Petaling and mukim Setapak under Gombak, yet 40% and 20% of them lie inside Kuala Lumpur, so twelve KL parties had been counted in a Selangor mukim. A point now takes its own district's area that holds it, then any area that does, then the nearest of its own. An opened district draws its own areas last, over a neighbour's that meet its frame, and its lead says constituency where that is what they are.

THE CHECKS: a new section reads the eleven seats, names each seat's own point against the rule it replaced, and reads the drawing order with Kuala Lumpur and with Petaling opened; five reverts each turned it red, one of them only after the Petaling check was added, since the seats happen to come last in the data.

t: CUSTOMERS IS NETWORK, WHO BUYS IS CLIENTS, AND MAP IS COVERAGE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 17 SEP 2026. The destination that held the people is Network. Its first page, Who buys, is Clients; Associates keeps its name; and Map, which he asked to be called something more fitting, is Coverage, his pick of four.

NAMES ONLY. The ids are the addresses, so #concentration, #network and #map still open the same pages, and nothing a page shows or computes moves. The board card's two lines that send him to set a tier now say Clients. Customers stays wherever it means the people themselves: the receivables heading, the observation family and the Coverage metric.
THE CHECKS: a new section reads the rail, each page's heading and the board card as drawn; each of its eight reverts, a name at a time, turned it red.

t: ONE UNIT OUT TO CN6-WM ON ADVANCE: AT THE ASK IT IS NOT, AT THE CAP IT STILL FITS
n: FOLDED: A SINGLE SALT SALE, GOODS GONE AND NOTHING IN. One row enters the sales book: CN6-WM, 1 unit for RM110 dated 17 Sep, collected on the day with RM0 cash in. The rate clears the RM51 floor for a 1 unit lot but sits well under the RM160 ask, and it matches the top of the party's own range at RM110 against a median of RM100 across 7 orders.

UNUSUAL: THE DRAFTER FLAGGED THE ADVANCE, AND THE CAP ANSWERS IT. RM110 goes out unpaid on top of RM100 outstanding, taking CN6-WM to 2 unit on credit against a cap of 2, so the row is at the limit and not over it. Costed at RM48 a unit, the desk's own inventory rate, leaving RM62 on the goods at 56.4%. The inventory gives up 1 unit and books no cash.

t: A CUSTOMER'S ORDER WAKES HIS PHONE WITHIN A MINUTE, AND ONLY FOR ORDERS
n: HIS REPORT OF 16 SEP 2026: AN ORDER CAME IN ON THE STATEMENTS SITE AND NOTHING TOLD HIM. The live store said why. The Worker's nudge had fired and marked the order placed at 22:19 KL, and there was no subscription to wake: the switch that turned alerts on left with the phone app at v387, and the desk never had one.

THE SWITCH IS BACK, ON THE ORDERS CARD, FOR ORDERS ONLY. Alert me to new orders subscribes this device, hands the write key to the service worker so the banner can read what is waiting, and offers Send a test and Turn off. The subscription names its topic, so a row he entered himself, the morning nudge and the fold do not wake him; a subscription naming none still hears everything. The banner reads New customer order and a tap opens Orders. On an iPhone the desk has to be opened from the Home Screen.

WITHIN A MINUTE, NOT A QUARTER-HOUR. A placement writes one marker on the site, and the desk's cron now runs every minute and reads only that marker through the relay, so a minute costs one read on each store rather than a listing of every order ever placed. The drafter's net still runs on the quarter-hour, after the nudge, so neither can swallow the other. The site still has no road to the desk.

THE CHECKS: a new section drives a placement through the schedule to a stubbed push service at 22:07 and 22:15 KL, the banner from the service worker as it ships, and the switch in the master; each of its thirteen claims was proved red by mutation.

t: THE THREE HEADINGS THAT CALLED THE GOODS STOCK NOW CALL THEM INVENTORY
n: HIS COPY RULE OF 11 SEP 2026, FINISHED. The goods are inventory in copy and Stock is the rail's destination. Three headings still used the rail's word for the goods, and the rule named all three: Spent on stock and Stock behind it on Financials, and Stock reconciliation on On hand. They now read Spent on inventory, Inventory behind it and Inventory reconciliation, beside the Inventory on hand, Inventory value and Inventory count the desk already carried.

WHAT IT TOUCHES: THREE WORDS. No figure, no total and no rate moves, and no row is read differently. The destination is untouched: the rail's tab and the view behind it still read Stock, which is what the rule asks for.

THE SWEEP, AND WHAT IT LEFT STANDING. Four other uses of the word remain in the desk. The tab and the VIEWS row behind it are the destination. Stock cover on Today is the name of the measure rather than a word for the goods. The Cash and Stock pair on a place's preview, and the Stock count: line a queued count carries, are the two that could go either way: the second is entry data the drafter reads rather than copy on a page, so both are put to him rather than changed here. THE CHECKS: one assertion that the three headings read Inventory and none still reads Stock, one that the destination itself is untouched, and the scan proved red by putting a single heading back. Built as v672 and re-landed as v674 after v672 and v673 shipped from the laptop under it.

AND THE EVOLUTION ARRAY IS NOT ONE ENTRY. This comment and tools/changelog.mjs both said it was, and this fold believed them and replaced the array to bump the version, dropping 347 entries of the Journal's own window before the diff caught it. The array carries that window from v324; master/changelog.json carries every entry ever written. Both comments now say a bump PREPENDS, and so does hard rule 1.

t: A HAND COUNT OF SALT CARRIES: FIVE UNIT MORE ON THE FLOOR, AND THE FLOORS COME DOWN
n: FOLDED: ONE COUNT, SALT, DATED 16 SEP. The desk counted 14.5 unit of salt by hand against a book figure of 9.5, a drift of plus 5, and on his word the count carries. The stated salt inventory is set to 14.5 and the salt count date moves from 15 Sep to 16 Sep. No party, no cash and no order sits behind this row, so nothing is owed out and nothing is promised against it.

UNUSUAL: A SECOND COUNT INSIDE A DAY, AND THE GAP IS UNEXPLAINED. The previous salt count was only 15 Sep, so the plus 5 drift arises over a single day and the dossier gives no reason for it. The inventory took the count as the ruling figure and reset the floors on the larger base: floor1 from RM60.25 to RM51, floor2 from RM120.50 to RM101.99, floor125 from RM753.15 to RM637.44, self use from 80.95 to 75.95. The ask holds at RM160.

t: THE WORD HE BANNED ON 24 AUG IS OUT OF THE DESK AND ITS CODE, AND THE FOLD CAN NO LONGER WRITE IT
n: HIS RULE OF 24 AUG 2026. One word is banned in every form, on every surface, comments included, and it had come back. The Pricing warning for a board whose Tier 1 costs more than its Tier 2 now says so in those words, and that the board falls to the right where it should rise. Twenty uses in eighteen code comments went the same way, one of them the pricing engine's, and nine lines of the suite. Nothing prices, counts or draws differently.

THE DATED RECORDS KEEP WHAT THEY SAID. The evolution entries, the changelog and the ledger's notes are left as written, as the Journal always is. A new suite section reads the master and the built desk outside their evolution, the engine, the Worker, the statements site, the tools, the design layer, the docs and the suite itself, and fails on the word in any form, capitals included.

AND THE FOLD CANNOT BRING IT BACK. The fold's own check now refuses a note carrying the word, as it refuses an em-dash or kg, and its house style names it, so a new entry is sent back to be rewritten. THE CHECKS: 3 assertions and 10 mutations: 9 turned the suite red, and the word written into an evolution entry left it green, which is the exemption working.

t: THE PROPOSAL MOVES A LEVEL ON HOW A CUSTOMER BUYS: LATE, SMALL, LOYAL, AND SALES SLOWING
n: HIS RULES OF 16 SEP 2026. The level a customer is proposed, read off what they pay, now moves on how they buy and on the stock. A customer who buys rarely and has been late twice drops a level at every size. A frequent small buyer drops a level from three units. A loyal customer buying bigger rises a level from three units, never past Platinum. And while sales have sat under half the typical for three days running, every level is offered one better, never past Platinum, until the next lot lands. A tier he has set is never moved by a rule, only offered one; but a proposal is what an un-held customer is quoted, so these rules move live prices.

NOTHING BETTER ON HALF A UNIT OR A UNIT, HIS DECISION THAT DAY. The plan gave frequent small buyers a better level on small orders. Measured first, the three of them were already proposed Titanium, where the only better level is Ambassador, his word alone, so the benefit had nowhere to go and the rule's only effect was the drop. He kept the drop and let their own rate carry the small price, which it already does: a card is never above what they pay, and they pay a keen rate on exactly those sizes.

WHAT MOVES TODAY: FOUR CUSTOMERS, 28 PRICES, NET +RM650. CM4-MK, loyal and buying bigger, is cheaper from three units, twelve and a half units RM1,060 to RM960. CR3-DAM, CA4-DAM and CC5-OKR, frequent and small, are dearer from three units, RM860 to RM960, and unchanged below. No slowdown is on for either product: salt last restocked on 15 Sep and oil on 8 Sep.

A RESTOCK ENDS A PROMOTION, AND A FORCED CHECK FOUND IT DID NOT. The slowdown was first counted straight through a lot, so a restock ended a promotion for a day and the next day's reading started it again; while sales stayed flat, no lot ever ended one. The count now stops at the latest lot, so only three quiet days after it start a new promotion. THE CHECKS: 9 assertions, each rule proved on forced inputs, the slowdown on forced sales and lots including a restock mid-slowdown, and a held tier left alone on a live quote. 10 mutations, each red.

t: A CUSTOMER'S LEVEL CAN DIFFER BY THE SIZE OF THE ORDER, READ BAND BY BAND IN ONE PLACE
n: HIS DECISIONS OF 16 SEP 2026. A tier on a product was one level at every size. It can now be a band set: one level for a small order of up to a unit, one for a mid-sized order, and one from three units, the cuts being the book's own quartiles of size. It is the mechanism his rules need, a habitual small buyer better on half a unit and a unit and a level worse from three, and a loyal bigger buyer better as the order grows.

ONE PLACE TURNS A SIZE INTO A LEVEL. The engine's levelAt, read by the desk for every quote and the printed board, and by the customer's own price list at each size, so the band a size falls in is never decided twice. One shape check, read by the drafter and the fold, so a band set travels through Approve and a shape that would not price is refused at the door and names itself. A customer's normal level is a mid-sized order's, and that is the mark their page draws.

AND A TRAP IT HAD TO CLOSE. On the Tiers card a band set cannot select one level name, so its dropdown would have sat on Not set, and Set would have read that as a clear and queued it. A band set is spelled out on the card now, its dropdown selects Keep the bands, and Set leaves it alone.

NOTHING MOVED. No band set exists on the book yet, so all 50 price lists were identical before and after; the rules that propose one come next. THE CHECKS: 7 assertions, the band edges exact, the shapes, the desk quote, the printed board and the customer's own page agreeing size by size, the drafter, and the card's safeguard. 7 mutations, each red.

t: EACH CUSTOMER HAS A PROFILE ON EACH PRODUCT, READ OFF THEIR OWN ORDERS, AND IT PRICES NOTHING YET
n: HIS DECISIONS OF 16 SEP 2026, AFTER THE BOOK WAS PROFILED. How a customer buys is now read off their own priced orders: how often, how big, how loyal and how late, one reading for each product. The Tiers card on People shows it beside the tier they hold, and the pricing snapshot carries it so the price list and the drafter read the desk's reading rather than working out one of their own. It prices nothing at this version. Four rules will move a level on it, and a rule is only as good as the reading under it, so it is measured and shown first, the way the five tiers were drawn beside the board before any quote read them.

THE NUMBERS ARE HIS, CUT FROM THE BOOK. Frequent is two orders a month, against a median customer at 1.83. Small is half a unit or one, his words, with six in ten of their orders that size. Loyal is six orders with the last inside thirty days, because the whole book is under three months old and time cannot measure loyalty yet. Buying bigger is four in ten at three units or more, the book's own upper quartile. Rare is under one order a month or nothing for sixty days. Late is twice past the ten-day credit term, his word. One constant holds them all, so a threshold is one edit.

WHAT IT READS TODAY. Small and often: CR3-DAM, CA4-DAM and CC5-OKR, the three he had in mind. Loyal: eight. Late twice: nobody, so that rule starts life as a forward-looking one. And CH5-KLC, who pays RM180 a unit for half-units, reads small and RARE, so a rule keyed to frequency will not hand a premium buyer the preferential rate. Orders a month are read over at least thirty days, or every new customer would arrive frequent off a single order.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 8 assertions on fixture customers dated off the desk's own day, so every boundary is forced: frequency telling the same small orders apart, loyalty needing both its halves, late past the term and not at it, rare on either count, the thirty-day floor, the card, the snapshot, and a proof that every one of the book's cards is unchanged when the profile reads the opposite of everything. 8 mutations, each red.

t: A CARD IS ROUNDED DOWN TO THE TEN, SO IT IS NEVER ABOVE WHAT THE CUSTOMER PAYS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 16 SEP 2026, AFTER A MEASUREMENT. The rule has read a customer's own rate to the NEAREST five since v651, and the nearest five rounds UP as often as down: a customer paying RM108 a unit was carded RM110. Across all 432 priced cells on the salt book, 63 sat RM1 to RM2 above the rate they actually pay, so the promise of never being above what they pay held only to the nearest five. It is rounded DOWN to the ten now, and never up. It costs RM385 across those cells and moves 93 of them; the biggest single cut is CA5-SEN's unit, RM110 to RM100 against their RM108. Oil does not move at all, because every oil rate already sits on the grid.

THE FLOOR IS THE ONE THING THAT CAN STILL PUT A CARD OVER A RATE, and it is meant to. A price may not go under break-even, so a rate below the floor lifts to the first ten above it: 22 cells today, every one of them the floor talking rather than the rounding, and the suite counts the two apart so a rounding fault cannot hide inside the floor's allowance. The grid is the same ten the ladder rounds to, so a card and a board price sit on one grid for the first time.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 5 assertions read off the whole live book rather than a fixture, because the claim is about every card the desk hands out: every card on a ten, none under its floor, none above the level they hold, none above their own rate except where the floor lifted it, and the customer's own page on the ten too across twelve accounts. Six assertions restated where they pinned the old grid. 5 mutations, each red, including one that showed the section could not see the tier cap being lifted out.

t: THE LABEL IS A SUBTLE MARK ON THEIR PRICES, AND THE GREETING IS AS PERSONAL AS THE SITE CAN BE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 16 SEP 2026: a very subtle tier level, in symbol and colour for each tier, marked in the pricing. Each product on a customer's price list now carries a small glyph in its level's colour beside the product's name, a level being held per product. The six shapes come from one Unicode block so they render the same on every phone, and none of them is a count: two customers comparing pages can see that their marks differ and cannot order themselves by them. The level is never named in the page, which is the whole of subtle; the name travels inside the sealed list, as it has since v651, and the mark is aria-hidden so it is not read out either.

AND EACH CUSTOMER IS GREETED AS PERSONALLY AS THIS SITE CAN MANAGE. The hour is theirs, off their own device, so the page opens with Good morning, Good afternoon or Good evening, and under the week's line it says the month their first priced order falls in, on the same rule the rate uses: a cancelled row, a defaulted one and an award with no cash are not orders placed at a price. NO NAME IS USED, BECAUSE NONE EXISTS ANYWHERE THIS SITE CAN REACH: plaintext names are kept off the cloud by rule, and every statement is built from codes alone. Sealing a name into a customer's own ciphertext would work and is HIS DECISION, not one to drift into: it would put names, encrypted, into records that today hold none.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 6 assertions, driven against the real page and the real crypto in jsdom: a mark for each product differing in both symbol and colour, the same level drawing the same mark on both products, no level named anywhere in the text, the greeting checked against the hour the run happens to be at, a customer with no first order greeted without the month rather than with a blank one, and the month itself. 6 mutations, each red.

t: A GUEST LINK NAMES ITS INTRODUCER, AND FOLLOWS THEM UP
n: HIS RULE. A referral link was pinned to Tier 1 or Tier 2, which were the two boards the desk had. It names the customer who is HANDING IT OUT now, by their username, and the stranger they bring is quoted two levels above that customer where there is room, else one, capped at the last. Above means dearer: the introducer's own level is earned and a stranger has earned nothing, and the cap means the worst a guest can do is the board every stranger already sees. Per product, like every tier since v646: an introducer on Titanium for salt with no oil history hands out Gold on salt and the board on oil.

AND THE LEVEL IS NEVER STORED ON THE LINK. It is computed on every publish from the introducer's tier AT THAT MOMENT and written as the link's own board, so moving a customer up moves every link they gave out on the next deploy, and a level frozen into a record can never fall out of step with the book. A link minted since the last publish has no board of its own yet and falls back to the board a stranger sees, which is also the cap, so nobody is ever shown an empty page. A username no customer holds is refused rather than minted onto nobody.

THE CHECKS. Four new assertions in the guest-link section and one restated: it posted a tier of 3 and wanted a refusal, which the introducer rule refuses for a different reason entirely, so it was passing while proving nothing about tiers. 7 mutations, each red: the level ignoring the introducer, one above instead of two, the cap removed, the link served the stranger's board, an unknown introducer minted anyway, a link with no introducer minted, and the introducer dropped from the record.

t: THE PRICING PAGE SAYS WHAT IT NOW DOES

It is gone, the last level is set in bold as the one the board quotes, and the rows that are not on the board say so, because a size off the board is still priced here. The suite now asserts the head ENDS at the six levels, not merely that it contains them.

t: THE BOARD IS THE LADDER: A STRANGER IS QUOTED BRONZE, AND A STATED PRICE DECIDES NOTHING
n: HIS DECISION OF 15 SEP 2026, OFF THE PRICING WORKBOOK. The ask at every printed size is now the LAST of the five levels, Bronze, the one a new customer starts at, struck on today's COGS by the workbook's own formula. Salt's board rises between RM10 and RM70 a size, from RM130 to RM160 at 1 unit and RM1,230 to RM1,250 at 12.5. Every size on both books now clears break-even.

AND NOT ONE CUSTOMER'S PRICE MOVES WITH IT. Measured over all 50 price lists on the book: every one is unchanged, because a named customer is quoted their own level capped at what they pay, which the board cannot reach. What moves is what a STRANGER is quoted, which is what the board has always been for. Their offers are unchanged too, RM11,265 on salt and RM1,730 on oil.

THREE THINGS RETIRE WITH THE DERIVED ASK. Tier 1's two stated ends, RM60 at half a unit and RM875 at twelve and a half, which were frozen figures where Titanium is now derived on live costs. His five typed oil prices, cleared from the book. And the typing of prices in Set the board, which is the hide list alone now: the drafter refuses a stated price outright, because a phone on an older build can still queue one and a folded figure nothing reads is worse than a refusal. The mechanism stays in the engine for a book with no ladder, and the suite forces one to prove it.

NRV IS TITANIUM, NOT THE ASK. The shelf was valued off the board, so the switch would have lifted the estimated selling price of every unit in stock to what a stranger pays: RM115.78 a unit against RM87.83. IAS 2.6 asks for the price in the ORDINARY COURSE, and the ordinary course is the levels his customers are on, so the basis is the lowest level any of them is quoted. The carrying amount is unchanged at cost either way, RM939.25; what changes is that the lower-of-cost-and-NRV test still means something.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 6 assertions and 6 mutations, each red. Thirteen assertions restated across the oil board, the two-tier rendering, the guest links and the staging check that held the board OFF the ladder, which is now inverted and compares the PRICES rather than the board object: comparing the object passed on the row's NAME alone and stayed green with the ask reverted.

t: A CUSTOMER'S OWN RATE IS THE BEST THEY HAVE PAID, AND THEIR TIER IS PROPOSED AT THE SIZES THEY BUY
n: HIS DECISION OF 16 SEP 2026, OFF THE ORDER BOOK. A sale struck is the best price strikeable with that customer, so the card reads the BEST of their last four priced orders where it read the middle one. The four-order window stands, so a price moved to in July is still the price seen in September and one old high day cannot set a card for good. Measured on the 133 priced salt orders: the rule would have earned RM10,349 over break-even against the RM9,013 they made, and RM9,209 under the middle-rate rule.

AND THE TIER IS READ AT THE SIZES THEY BUY, a unit, so a size a customer never takes cannot decide their level. It was measured across every size on the board, which handed the decision to the biggest rung: adding 80 and 100 unit to oil (v654) moved two customers a level on sizes neither buys. On the book today 24 salt customers and 1 oil customer sit on a different level, their cards rising at 106 sizes and falling at 182, and nobody is quoted above what they have paid.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 4 assertions: the window and the best of it, the tool reading the same four, a proposal that does not move when every rung above 2.5 unit leaves the board, and a card that rises to the best. Ten assertions restated across the statements, the bucket, the proposals and the two card sections. 5 mutations each turn their assertion red.

t: A CUSTOMER'S PRICE IS THEIR TIER FOR EACH PRODUCT, NEVER ABOVE WHAT THEY PAY, AND A PRODUCT WITH NO TIER READS PRICE COMING SOON
n: HIS DECISIONS OF 15 SEP 2026: THE TIER IS A CEILING. t: TWO SALT SELLS ON THE DAY: ONE ADVANCE ABOVE HIS MEDIAN, ONE PAID IN FULL
n: TWO SALT SELLS FOLDED, BOTH DATED 15 SEP AND BOTH HANDED OVER ON THE DAY. CR3-DAM takes 1 unit for RM90 with nothing paid, and CE4-CHE takes 2.5 unit for RM230 settled in full at the open. Both clear their floors, RM61.26 for 1 unit and RM153.15 for 2.5 unit, and both sit under their asks of RM130 and RM290. Cost on each is the desk's own RM48 a unit, so RM48 and RM120 on the goods.

THE UNUSUAL PART IS THE ADVANCE AND THE CREDIT ALREADY STANDING. The drafter flagged CR3-DAM at RM90 against a RM80 median, 12.5% above, and asked that the unpaid unit be checked against his cap: he held RM25 outstanding and 0.27 unit on credit against a cap of 2 unit, so the figures answer it. CE4-CHE drew no flag but already carries RM150 outstanding and 10 unit on credit against a cap of 1 unit. Salt was counted on 15 Sep at 23 in stock.

t: TWO UNITS OUT FOR CASH ON THE DAY: BOTH UNDER THE ASK, ONE PARTY STILL CARRYING RM180
n: FOLDED: TWO SALT SELLS DATED 15 SEP, BOTH PAID AND COLLECTED ON THE DAY. CC5-OKR took 1 unit at RM90 and CZ6-WM took 1 unit at RM100, RM190 cash in and 2 units moved, nothing left pending on either row. Both totals clear the RM61.91 floor for 1 unit and both sit under the RM140 ask and the RM150 ceiling. Each is costed at the desk's own RM48 a unit, so the inventory carries no outside rate on this fold.

UNUSUAL: ONE PARTY IS PRICED AT ITS OWN MEDIAN WHILE STILL CARRYING RM180. CC5-OKR held RM180 outstanding and 1 unit on credit before this row against a cap of 1 unit, with nothing defaulted, and this row was settled in cash so it adds nothing to that balance. CZ6-WM came in clean at RM0 outstanding. The drafter raised no flag on either row. The inventory took 2 units off the shelf at the stated cost and left the floors where they stood.

t: A 25 UNIT LOT LANDS AT THE QUOTED RATE: AN EMPTY SHELF REFILLED, COST BASIS RESET
n: ONE PURCHASE ROW FOLDED, PAID AND RECEIVED ON THE DAY. The fold appends a single BUY to purchases: SA5-BTR, 25 unit of salt for RM1,200, RM1,200 cash and all 25 unit moved on 15 Sep, with RM40 freight. The rate matches the 25 unit tier of the 20 Aug quote exactly, RM1,200 on his word of 07 Sep, so there was nothing to reconcile and the drafter raised no flag.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL WAS THE SHELF, NOT THE TERMS. The book stood at zero stock on the 15 Sep salt count, under the reorder mark of 15 unit and with 10.5 unit promised out, so this lot is the whole position. The inventory took the 25 unit in at RM48 a unit, above the RM44 that was carried before and above the RM46 replacement mark, and left the ledger and self use figures of 75.95 untouched.

t: SALT COUNTED AT ZERO: THE BOOK LOSES 1.5 UNIT AND THE FLOORS LIFT
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, AND IT IS A COUNT. Salt was counted by hand at 0 unit on 15 Sep against 1.5 stated on the book, a drift of -1.5 unit, with the previous count dated 14 Sep. A count wins over the ledger, so the stated salt inventory is set to 0 and COUNT_ON for salt moves to 15 Sep. No party, no money and no cost attach to this row, and no lot landed.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID WITH IT. The gap books as shrinkage across every unit sold, and the floors lift accordingly: RM60.83 to RM61.52 for 1 unit, RM121.66 to RM123.04 for 2 unit and RM760.37 to RM769.01 at 125 unit, while the ask for 1 unit holds at RM130 and self use moves from RM74.45 to RM75.95. With 10.5 unit promised against nothing on hand, the drafter's flag that open orders are unmeetable stands answered by the count itself.

t: EACH CUSTOMER HOLDS A TIER FOR EACH PRODUCT, AND A PRODUCT THEY HAVE NEVER BOUGHT IS PROPOSED NOTHING UNTIL HE SETS ONE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 15 SEP 2026: A TIER FOR EACH PRODUCT. A customer can hold Gold on salt and Silver on oil. The Tiers card on Customers carries a dropdown for each product, Not set among them; Set queues only the products whose choice changed, Not set on a tier held queues it cleared, and every change goes to Approve before it is folded. Add ID asks a starting tier for each product, Bronze by default, and leaves one set to not set out.

NOTHING IS PROPOSED FOR A PRODUCT NEVER BOUGHT. A product with no tier held is proposed the level nearest what the customer pays for it, read off that product alone. One they have never bought is proposed nothing and reads not set, and the card now lists customers who have bought nothing yet, so a tier can be set before they order. Still quoted nowhere: TIER_OF was empty, so nothing on the book changed shape.

THE CHECKS. The drafter and the fold check each product against the book and each level against the desk's names, and the fold clears a product on a null and drops a customer left with none. The v643 and v645 sections are restated for a tier per product, and a new section of 8 assertions covers the rest. 19 mutations each turn their assertion red.

t: ADD ID STARTS A NEW CUSTOMER AT THE TIER CHOSEN, AND THE FOLD FILES IT WITH THE REGISTRATION
n: HIS DECISION OF 15 SEP 2026: A NEW CUSTOMER INCLUDES A STARTING TIER. Add ID now asks the starting tier, Bronze unless he picks another, for a customer and for either kind of associate. An end buyer, a bucket and a supplier hold no tier and are not asked, and an appointment of a party already registered keeps the tier they hold.

ONE ROAD. The tier rides the registration: the queue line says where the customer starts and never carries the name, the Tiers card reads it as waiting for approval, the drafter checks it against the level names and refuses one for a supplier or a bucket, and the fold files it in TIER_OF as it adds the code to the roster.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 8 assertions, driven through the Add ID form with the vault and the network stubbed: the picker for the kinds that hold a tier and not the others, Record queuing the tier without the name, the Tiers card reading it, the drafter's row and its two refusals, and the fold filing it and refusing a tier the desk does not name. 9 mutations each turn their assertion red.

t: THE TIERS RUN EVENLY FROM 1.0 TO 2.5, SO 1 UNIT OF SALT READS HIS RM100, 110, 130, 150 AND 160
n: HIS DECISION OF 15 SEP 2026. His prices for 1 unit of salt include RM110 and RM130, which the 1.5 and 2.0 columns never printed. The five tiers' multiples now run evenly from 1.0 to 2.5, a step of 0.375: Titanium 1.0, Platinum 1.375, Gold 1.75, Silver 2.125 and Bronze 2.5.

WHAT MOVES. 0.5 unit of salt still starts the tiers at RM50, 60, 70, 80 and 90, and 1 unit reads RM100, 110, 130, 150 and 160. The middle tiers ease at the larger sizes: at 12.5 unit Platinum reads RM950, Gold RM1,050 and Silver RM1,150, against RM980, RM1,110 and RM1,180 before. Ambassador and Bronze do not move, and every rule the ladder keeps still holds on both books. Nothing quotes the ladder yet.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 2 assertions: the even spacing on both books, and RM50 to RM90 at 0.5 unit with his 1-unit prices on the workbook's COGS. v641's section now proves the workbook's 76 prices with the workbook's own four multiples, and v642's approved board moved with the multiples. 4 mutations each turn their assertion red.

t: EACH CUSTOMER HOLDS ONE TIER, SET ON THE PHONE AND FOLDED, PROPOSED FROM WHAT THEY PAY, QUOTED NOWHERE YET
n: HIS DECISIONS OF 15 SEP 2026: EACH CUSTOMER'S TIER COMES BEFORE THE SWITCH. A customer holds one tier across both books, TIER_OF on the book, a new ledger key. It moves only on his word: the Customers page queues it, the drafter drafts it as tierset, he approves it and the fold files it, and Amend ID's re-key carries it with the code.

PROPOSED FROM WHAT THEY PAY. A customer holding none is proposed the tier nearest what they pay: on the book carrying most of their revenue, the level whose prices sit closest to their own rate across that book's board sizes. Never Ambassador, which is his word alone, and Bronze where there is no rate to read. On the book of 15 Sep that proposes Titanium 8, Platinum 9, Gold 13, Silver 2 and Bronze 5 of 37 customers.

THE TIERS CARD. On Customers, every customer who has bought, largest first, with the tier held, the one waiting for approval or the one proposed, a picker to set one, and Accept for every proposal still open, in one entry. A tier set with the names open queues the code and never the name. Migration 0010 rebuilds the draft table once, for the tier and for the label still to be named.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 16 assertions on fixture customers and forced costs: the proposal against a restatement, never Ambassador, Bronze with no rate, the card's three states, Accept, codes alone in the queue, no price moving, the drafter's entry and its refusals, the fold with a rename, and 0010. The book now holds twenty-nine keys. 16 mutations each turn their assertion red.

t: THE LADDER IS AMBASSADOR AT THE FLOOR AND FIVE NAMED TIERS, TITANIUM TO BRONZE, STILL QUOTED NOWHERE
n: HIS RESTRUCTURE OF 15 SEP 2026. COGS, purchase plus freight, is the line no price goes under, and the floor is COGS plus leakage. Ambassador pays the floor itself, rounded up to the ten, on his word alone and earning no free units. Above it sit five named tiers: Titanium, Platinum, Gold, Silver and Bronze, where a new customer starts.

A NEW COLUMN, SO THE TIERS START WHERE HE SAID. The workbook's columns at 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5 are Titanium, Platinum, Gold and Bronze, and Silver is a new one at 2.25, halfway between Gold and Bronze, so 0.5 unit of salt starts the five at RM50, 60, 70, 80 and 90. The rule and the guards are v641's: each level at least a ten over the one below, the rate law walked under that.

EACH CUSTOMER'S TIER COMES BEFORE THE SWITCH. Measured on 15 Sep, switching the board's ask to Bronze would draw every existing customer's price list up toward it, all 36 salt customers and all 6 oil customers with history, because a list is drawn toward the ask. So the card stays quoted nowhere, and the next stage gives each customer a tier, starting nearest what they pay, before any quote moves.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 5 assertions: the names in order, the RM50 to RM90 start on the workbook's COGS, Silver strictly between Gold and Bronze at every size on both books, the board he approved on the costs of 14 Sep, and Ambassador at the floor rather than COGS plus 20%. v641's section now reads the workbook's four columns by multiple and the card by name. 8 mutations each turn their assertion red.

t: THE FIVE TIERS ARE COMPUTED OFF THE PRICING WORKBOOK AND DRAWN BESIDE THE BOARD, QUOTED NOWHERE YET
n: HIS DECISIONS OF 14 AND 15 SEP 2026, THE FIRST STAGE OF FIVE. Five price tiers from his pricing workbook: Tier I ◆ pays the floor, rounded up to the ten, and Tiers II ★★, III ★, IV ●● and V ● are the workbook's four columns, at multiples 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5. A new customer will start at Tier V and climb toward the diamond, paying less at every step. The floor stays what it was, COGS plus leakage.

ONE FORMULA, STATED AS A RULE. Each column is COGS to the ringgit times its multiple less a step a rung, rounded up to the ten: 1 + m × (1 − 0.05 × rung) for salt, m + 0.35 − 0.05 × rung for oil, whose board gains 80 and 100 unit. TIER_RULE states it per book and fiveTiers in the engine computes it under two guards: each tier sits at least a ten over the one below, which also keeps every tier over the floor, and the rate may not rise with size where a step down keeps that.

BESIDE TODAY'S BOARD, AND NOTHING QUOTES IT. The Pricing page draws the five tiers under the board with today's ask alongside, so they read against each other on live costs before any price moves. The phone, the board, the drafter, the price list and the guest boards read nothing new; switching them is the next stage.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 11 assertions: the rule reproduces all 76 of the workbook's prices from its own COGS, the approved board on the costs of 14 Sep, the guards on a grid of 70 forced costs that lifts 474 prices and steps 28, a column landing exactly on a ten, off-board sizes, the card cell by cell, and quoted nowhere. 13 mutations each turn their assertion red. Two Tier 1 checks that read the floor v639's count had lifted now force their own cost.

t: A PENDING SALE IS CORRECTED: PAID, COLLECTED AND RM20 LIGHTER
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, AN AMENDMENT AND NOTHING ELSE. A correction lands on CH6-SET's salt sell s148 of 11 Sep, 1 unit. The total falls from RM120 to RM100, delivery from RM10 to RM0, cash rises from RM0 to RM100, delivered quantity from 0 to 1 unit, handover moves from delivered to collected, and both paidOn and deliveredOn are set to 14 Sep. No cash and no stock move on the fold itself: the row is restated, not rewritten.

THE DRAFTER FLAGGED THE RATE AND THE FIGURES ANSWER IT. CH6-SET has paid about RM117.50 a unit across 2 orders and this row now reads RM100, 14.9% below that, against a median of RM115 in a RM110 to RM120 range. The desk let it stand on his word. Outstanding of RM120 on this party is settled by the RM100 cash and the RM20 reduction in total. The inventory held at 1.5 units, cost unchanged at RM44 a unit.

NOTHING OUTSTANDING ON THE FOLD. No lot landed, no loan opened and no count was taken, salt last counted 14 Sep and oil 9 Sep. Promised stock stays at 11.5 units against 1.5 units stated, with the reorder mark at 15 units and replacement at RM46 a unit. The amended row now carries a paid and collected date of 14 Sep, so it leaves nothing open behind it.

t: A HAND COUNT OF SALT CUTS THE BOOK BY 7.44 UNIT: FLOORS LIFT ACROSS EVERY SIZE
n: ONE COUNT FOLDED, NOTHING SOLD OR BOUGHT. The salt count of 14 Sep stands at 1.5 unit against 8.94 on the book, a drift of -7.44 unit, and the count wins, so the stated inventory is set to 1.5 and COUNT_ON for salt moves from 8 Sep to 14 Sep. The drafter flagged the 7.44 unit as unaccounted for and books it as shrinkage across every unit sold. The dossier gives no reason for the gap and none is offered here.

THE FLOORS MOVE WITH THE SHRINKAGE, AND THE DESK IS UNDER ITS REORDER MARK. The 1 unit floor lifts from RM56.21 to RM61.15, 2 unit from RM112.43 to RM122.29, 12.5 unit from RM702.67 to RM764.34, the ask on 1 unit from RM120 to RM130 and self use from RM68.01 to RM75.45. Stock cost holds at RM44 a unit against RM46 replacement. Nothing is owed out, 11.5 unit stands promised, and the position sits below the RM15 reorder mark.

t: NETWORK LINES RUN FROM EACH ASSOCIATE TO THE CUSTOMERS THEY BROUGHT IN
n: HIS CHOICE OF 14 SEP 2026, THE LAST OF THE FOUR MAP LAYERS: NETWORK LINES. A switch beside the view draws a line from each associate on the bench to each customer they brought in, the associate's end a ring and the customer's a dot, in the districts view, the whole peninsula and a district opened, where a line runs off the edge to the districts around. The switch is off until asked for. A note under the legend counts the lines, the associates, and the pairs not drawn because a party has no point.

ONE MAP OF WHO BROUGHT IN WHOM. The lines are read off introductions(), the one place the referral stamps on orders and the book's declared introductions meet, and the bench is associateIds(), so a banned party's lines go when it leaves the bench while its introductions stay in the ledger. Every line and ring is titled by code, even with the names open.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 8 assertions on a fixture associate with two declared introductions, one stamped on an order and one with no point: off by default, a line to each customer placed, each starting on the ring and ending on its dot, the note's counts, a district opened, codes with the names open, a banned associate, and Hide. 10 mutations each turn the assertion they target red. On the live book the switch draws 11 lines from 5 associates.

t: A TAP DRILLS INTO A DISTRICT OR AN AREA: ITS FIGURE, SHARE, RANK, TREND AND PARTIES
n: HIS CHOICE OF 14 SEP 2026, THE THIRD MAP LAYER: DRILL AND COMPARE. A district opened now carries a panel of its own under the map, and a tap on one of its areas, on the map or in the table, swaps in that area's: its figure for the metric and period in view, its share and its rank against the others at its level, a bar a month for its trend with the period's months in gold, and its parties by code, largest first. A second tap puts the area down, and closing the district puts the pick down with it. The area picked is outlined and its parties' dots are lit.

ONE READING FOR ALL OF IT. mapOwn is what each party carries on each metric over the orders a filter keeps, so the shading, the table and each month of the trend come off the same figures, and an area is ranked against the areas drawn in the district while a district is ranked against every district carrying the metric. Codes only, even with the names open, as everywhere on the map.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 12 assertions on three fixture customers sited in two areas of one quiet district, trading in two months: the district's panel, a tap dispatched on the drawn area, the toggle, the table's names, the period and the metric carried into the panel, codes with the names open, and closing the district. 14 mutations each turn the assertion they target red.

t: THE MAP READS A MONTH, A RANGE OR ALL TIME, AND PLAYS THE BOOK MONTH BY MONTH
n: HIS CHOICE OF 14 SEP 2026, THE SECOND MAP LAYER: THE TIME SLIDER. Under the metric switch, a slider picks a whole month, two dates pick a range to the day, each the desk's own date field with Today inside it, and All time takes the period off.
