Play by month steps from the product's first priced order to this month and stops on the last, or on Stop, and it stops itself when the map is left. The lead line names the period, so a shading always says what it covers.

THE PERIOD READS THE ORDERS PLACED IN IT. byCustomer takes a row filter now, so revenue, margin, units and customers are the desk's own figures over the period's orders, with one definition for both. Credit owed in a period is what is still owed today on the orders placed in it, not a balance rebuilt as it stood then.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 13 assertions on fixture customers trading in different months in quiet districts: all time, each month, a range to the day at both ends, credit owed in a period, and the player's start, tick, stop, end and leaving the map, with its timer caught rather than waited on, and Today on the From field moving the period. 16 mutations each turn the assertion they target red. On a phone every control in the row is 44 px tall, with no sideways scroll.

t: THE MAP SHADES BY REVENUE, MARGIN, UNITS, CUSTOMERS OR CREDIT OWED
n: HIS CHOICE OF 14 SEP 2026, THE FIRST OF THE FOUR MAP LAYERS: THE METRIC SWITCH. A switch under the map chooses what the districts and areas are shaded by, for the product in view: revenue, margin, units, the number of customers, or the credit they owe. The lead line, the tooltips, the legend, the deepest-area tile and the table's figure column all follow it, so the page never says revenue over a margin shading. The map still opens on revenue.

EACH FIGURE IS THE DESK'S OWN. Revenue, margin and units are byCustomer's, credit owed is txAdvance over the book's receivables, so a written-off sale is owed by nobody here too, and a resale account counts where its associate is on every metric, as revenue already did. A count is whole, so the customers legend names the counts that fall in each step and leaves out a step no count reaches.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 5 assertions on fixture parties placed in four quiet districts so each metric has a different deepest district, with a defaulted advance to prove credit owed reads what is owed. 12 mutations each turn the assertion they target red. On a phone the five buttons wrap to two rows at 44 px, with no sideways scroll.

t: A DEFAULTED SALE IS WRITTEN OFF: OFF WHAT IS OWED, STILL IN WHAT WAS LOST
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 14 SEP 2026: WRITE OFF THE DEFAULTED ENTRIES. Since 05 Sep a default was provisioned in full and kept as gross owed, so the desk went on treating the money as live: Today said to chase CA4-DAM for RM 260 and that CA4-DAM broke three rules, the register listed a credit cap breach and two credit age breaches, Advances out read RM 642, and the Customers board and Plans put the party up for an approach and a message. A defaulted sale is now written off. What it had out and unpaid leaves every reading of what is owed: txAdvance reads nothing owed on it, as poOwed has read nothing owed on a defaulted lot since v438, and a written-off sale holds no credit. Advances out and the debtors table read RM 382, and the table says under it what was written off.

NOTHING LOST LEAVES THE BOOK, AND NO PRICE MOVES. txWrittenOff carries the figure wherever the desk reads a loss. The Financials impairment line reads RM 328 as it did, now RM 260 written off and RM 68 loss allowance on open balances, so operating profit is unchanged, and the month's charge, the bad-debt rate in the price stack, the receivables signal and a party's quote adjustment read what they read before. The pricing snapshot, every tier's quote at every size and CA4-DAM's quote were compared against v633 and are identical. The customer's own statement is untouched: a write-off does not forgive the debt.

A PARTY WITH A WRITE-OFF IS NOT WORKED. His word of 09 Sep on CA4-DAM was that they had disappeared, with no more contact. The chase had been the one guard keeping them off the approach lists, so every list that skips a banned or departed party now skips a party with a write-off too: the Customers board, the phone's approach list, Today's reconnect count, and the message Plans suggests, which had never skipped a banned or departed party either. Paid back, the party can be approached again. The Order book card reads the write-offs from the rows that carry them.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 13 assertions on a forced fixture, a customer read before and after an aged advance is defaulted: what is owed moves by the advance on the desk and the phone, credit and rules clear, the chase and every approach go, and operating profit, the bad-debt rate, the month's charge, the signal, the pricing snapshot and the party's quote stay exactly where they were. 22 mutations each turn the assertion they target red. Three older checks encoded the old treatment and are restated: the engine's gross keeps the number, the Order book's claims marked and skipped, and a credit breach that leaned on CA4-DAM's live row, now a fixture.

t: A PARTY'S PLACE REACHES THE MAP ON ITS OWN, FROM WHAT IS TYPED AT ADD ID AND AMEND ID
n: HIS DECISION OF 14 SEP 2026: AUTOMATIC FROM THE TYPED PLACE. Names and IDs never moved the map: a party was drawn where the last letters of their code pointed, and a code whose letters named no known place was not drawn at all. Now the place typed at Add ID or Amend ID is looked up as it is typed, the whole place first, then its parts, then runs of its words, each wording as an official area name and then in a place list built into the desk. A place found is drawn on a map under the form at the point it will file; a place not found, or a name standing for places more than 3 km apart, is tapped on that map, and Record waits for the point. Only the code and the point travel, to 0.01 degrees, about a kilometre. The place typed stays in the vault.

THE PLACE LIST IS GEONAMES, HASHED. tools/gazfetch.mjs reads GeoNames' Malaysia extract (CC BY 4.0) and keeps every populated place and locality in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Negeri Sembilan under each Latin spelling: 5,149 names. The public desk may carry no place from the directory, and a plain list of the core states holds most of them, so each name is kept as seven hex characters of SHA-256 over its placeKey beside a packed point, 55 KB in geo/gazetteer.json, inlined by geosync. It is built from GeoNames alone, never from the directory. A five-letter word on its own counts only as an area name, since the list holds too many short words. Of the 42 places recorded on the directory, 33 are found as typed and 9 will need a tap.

WHERE THE POINT GOES. A registration and a rename carry it as geo. Amend ID keeping the code queues it as the new collection place, and so does the map's Place parties from their recorded places, shown with the names open, which looks up every party with no point from the vault, sends those found to Approve as one entry and lists by code those it could not find. The fold files the point in PLACED on the book, a rename moves it with the code, and placeOf reads it before the letters of a code. migrations/0009 adds place to the draft table's CHECK, applied on its own to the live D1 before this deploy. The map and the form credit GeoNames beside the boundaries.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 41 assertions: the engine's wordings, a fixture GeoNames extract through the real builder and read back by the desk, the drafter's point and its refusals, the fold's filing and a rename's move, the lookup order and the five-letter rule, the Add ID pane found, not found and tapped on a map shown at half size, Amend ID's three roads, the map's one-entry placement, the credits and the Approve card. 38 mutations each turn the assertion they target red. The v528, Add ID and v628 sections now tap a point before Record, as the pane requires.

AND ONE SECTION OF THE SUITE STOPS LEANING ON THE LIVE BOOK. The cloud's run for v631 went red after the phone was live: the v617 section counted the whole queue after the automatic offset had run over the real network, and on that day's book an associate still here held a free unit and an advance, which the desk rightly offered. The section now forces such an associate beside its departed one and reads the queue for the departed party alone, and the other associate's offer shows the offset really ran. Proved red four ways, the old reading among them.

t: AN ADVANCE ON THE BOOK SINCE 30 AUG IS SETTLED IN KIND, SO THE ROW NO LONGER READS AS OWED
n: ONE CORRECTION FOLDED, NO CASH AND NO STOCK BEHIND IT. The fold patches s124, CN6-WM's salt order of 30 Aug, 1 unit for RM110: settledRM from unset to 110, rebate from false to true, rebateKg from unset to 1. It changes only what the row says about itself, so the ledger stands at 76.95 and stock at 8.94 units. The desk decided it on 14 Sep and the drafter raised no flag against it.

WHAT IS UNUSUAL IS THE PARTY, NOT THE PATCH. CN6-WM now carries seven orders at a RM100 median in a RM75 to RM110 range, RM210 outstanding and 2 units on credit against his cap, with nothing defaulted. The RM110 on s124 sits at the top of that range. The inventory did nothing: no lot landed, cost basis holds at RM44 a unit against a RM46 replacement, and the reorder mark of 15 units is untouched.

t: A CASH SALE AT THE TOP OF HIS OWN RANGE, TAKEN WHILE HIS CREDIT LINE SITS FULL
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL TO CN6-WM SETTLED ON THE DAY. One unit at RM110, collected on 14 Sep with RM110 cash in and one unit moved the same day, so the row opens and closes together. The rate clears the RM56.21 floor for one unit and sits under the RM120 ask and the RM150 ceiling. The drafter raised no flag, and the figures came from the mirror and the desk's own pricing snapshot.

THE POINT OF INTEREST IS THE PARTY, NOT THE PRICE. CN6-WM carries RM210 outstanding and two units on credit against a cap of two, with nothing defaulted, so the line was full before this row. It was taken as cash rather than credit, which is why the fold adds nothing to his exposure. The inventory gave up one unit at its own RM44 a unit and holds the prior outstanding untouched; the count dates stand at 08 Sep for salt and 09 Sep for oil.

t: THE MAP SHADES NAMED DISTRICTS, AND A TAP OPENS THEIR MUKIM, BANDAR AND PEKAN
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 14 SEP 2026: a proper map, the way a council map shades its districts, but more advanced. His decisions on the day: districts first and the finer areas a tap away, area names always shown, each party a dot. This version is the map itself; a party's place following Add ID and Amend ID on its own comes in v631, and the metric switch, time slider, drill and compare and network lines in v632.

THE AREAS ARE REAL, AND COMMITTED. tools/areafetch.mjs takes the 91 districts of Peninsular Malaysia (geoBoundaries from citypopulation.de, CC BY 3.0) and the 370 mukim, bandar and pekan of the core states (geoBoundaries from Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0) from the basemap's own pinned release, thins them and writes the rings as encoded polylines, 113 KB in all. geosync inlines them, so the desk still loads nothing, and both credits print under the map beside the states' own.

WHAT THE MAP DRAWS. The core districts, shaded in five steps on the square root of each one's share of the largest, named where a name fits, with the state lines over them; the whole peninsula is a switch away. A tap on a district opens every mukim, bandar and pekan in its frame, shaded the same way, each party a dot and a supplier a square, with a way back. The two levels come from different surveys and do not share edges, so a party counts in the area its point lies inside, whichever district that area is filed under: all 36 parties in the core states stand on the area they are counted in. An associate's resale account counts where the associate is. Names never overlap or run off the frame, and on a phone the drawing takes the phone's width so they stay readable.

WHAT HIS DECISION CHANGED, AND WHAT IT DID NOT. v293 kept the map to unnamed heat because a named place beside a code identifies a customer on a public page. Area names now show on his word, and the leak checks exempt a directory place only when it is itself an official area name; six were. A party's name never reaches the map, with the names unlocked or not, and its tables name parties by code.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 18 assertions: the areas, their nesting and their licences; a point finding its district and its area; the deepest step and its figure; a resale account counted at its associate; the credits; no name on the map; a district opened with its dots and a way back; no party on bare ground; no names overlapping; the peninsula and its switch; a phone's drawing. 14 mutations each turn their assertions red, the leak check's exemption among them, proved on this laptop's own directory. Three older instruments are restated and each proved red again: the basemap check allows a state name only where it is also an area the map shows, the kg scan skips the generated geography, whose rings are letters, and the map's TBC reason is checked on a TBC code put on the roster for it, since v629 re-keyed the last two on the book and that check had failed there ever since.

t: SIX CODES RE-KEYED, NO CASH AND NO STOCK MOVED
n: WHAT WAS FOLDED. Six re-keys, all decided at the desk on 14 Sep: CE5-TBC to CE5-SA, CB7-TBC to CB7-BJ, CA11-SEN to CA2-SEN, CA5-KER to CA5-BAN, CA7-JTR to CA7-AMP and CH5-OUG to CM3-OUG. Each carries its orders across, one order on the first three and three orders each on the last three, with no lots on any of them. Every old code is retired outright once the batch has run.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL. Two of the six clear placeholder codes, CE5-TBC and CB7-TBC, and two shift the letter and number as well as the tail, CA11-SEN to CA2-SEN and CH5-OUG to CM3-OUG, so the roster reads differently at the head, not only the tail. No flag was raised on any row, and the name and the place stay out of the book, filed in the vault, encrypted.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. Nothing. No row in this batch moves cash or stock, so stock holds at 9.94 unit with stock cost at RM44 a unit against a replacement cost of RM46, the reorder mark at RM15, nothing owed out and 11.5 unit promised. Notes, the changelog and issued statements keep the old codes and stay true as written. Nothing is left outstanding on the batch.

t: AMEND ID: A NEW NAME OR PLACE RE-KEYS THE PARTY THROUGH APPROVE, AND THE USERNAME STAYS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 14 SEP 2026, ON HIS RULINGS OF 11 SEP. The Enter view could add an ID and not amend one. Amend ID sits beside Add ID on the phone: pick the party, type the name and the place as they should read, and the code is derived again by the Add ID rule, the party's own code counting as free. A spelling that keeps the code is filed in the vault and goes nowhere else. A code that changes is filed in the vault under the new code and queued as a rename, codes only, for Approve.

WHAT A RENAME MOVES, FROM ONE WRITER. The engine's renamePairs names the code and every code built on it, the -R account and an end buyer's, and renameInBook moves every whole value and every key that is one of them: the rows, the roster, the associates, the introductions, the people lists, the awards and the loans. The drafter counts the orders and lots for the card; the fold applies the rename after every other row in its batch, so a sale approved beside it under the old code moves too. Beyond the book it moves the statement key with the username unchanged, a place override while the code still ends in the same place, and the suite's fixtures, as v603 moved its three codes by hand. Notes, the changelog and issued statements keep the old code.

WHAT IS REFUSED. The drafter refuses a code off the roster, a resale account on its own, a code that does not change, a customer becoming a supplier, and a new code, or any code under it, that another party holds. The fold checks those again, and refuses a code the desk's own logic quotes, since it never edits the master's code: CJ4-OKR, SA5-BTR, SP7-PUD, and CM6-HCM in a comment. Those stay hand folds.

TWO THINGS A RENAME NEEDED WERE ALREADY BROKEN. The draft table's CHECK lists its collections by name and had never named repayment, so a repayment entered on the phone could not have reached Approve: migrations/0008 names repayment and rename, and drafts.mjs stages both as themselves. And the laptop's pull kept the directory's spelling over the vault's, so its next seed would have undone an amendment made on the phone: the vault's spelling now wins, the old one kept beside it as was. The unused queueRename is gone.

THE CHECKS. A new section of 29 assertions on fixture codes: the pairs and the walk, the card and six refusals, the CHECK against every collection the drafter returns, the fold's order and its hand-fold refusal, the three files beyond the book and the command line that writes them, the pull, and the phone's pane, plan, record, vault and card. 24 mutations each turn the assertions they touch red. The v528 pull assertion is restated for the new rule.

t: TWO OLD HALF UNIT ROWS RECLASSED FROM REBATE TO GOODWILL, NO CASH AND NO STOCK MOVE
n: WHAT WAS FOLDED. Two corrections, both against CN6-WM, both applied on 14 Sep. s031 of 21 Jul and s056 of 04 Aug, each 0.5 unit for RM50 with no cash in, are reclassed: rebate from true to false, goodwill from false to true. Neither touches quantity, total or cash, so the pair moves no money and no salt. The fold applies the patch only, leaving each row's own wording as it stood.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL. Both rows were carried as rebate redemptions and now read as goodwill, which changes what the rows say about themselves rather than what they settled. The drafter raised no flag on either. CN6-WM stays an associate on the roster, with RM110 outstanding and 1 unit on credit from s124, nothing defaulted, a RM110 median across 6 orders in a RM75 to RM110 range.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. Nothing. Stock stands at 9.94 unit on the salt count of 08 Sep and the oil count of 09 Sep, ledger 77.95 against self use 68.01, cost basis RM44 a unit with replacement at RM46, reorder at 15 unit, nothing owed out and 11.5 unit promised. No loans are open and no floors or asks move on these two corrections.

t: THE DRAFTER'S ADVANCE IS THE ENGINE'S, SO A ROW SETTLED IN KIND IS NO LONGER CALLED UNPAID
n: HIS REPORT OF 14 SEP 2026: CS6-BS AND CN6-WM EACH SHOWED A UNIT ON ADVANCE. CS6-BS holds none: all four of its rows are paid, s139 in kind by its reward. CN6-WM holds one, and it is real: s124, 1 unit handed over on 30 Aug for RM 110 with nothing paid, which Receivables and Rules have shown all along. The rest was the drafter. Its ADVANCE flag set cash against the total and never read settledRM, so every settlement in kind read as unpaid: s139's three correction cards said 1 unit with RM 110 unpaid, and CN6-WM's two pending cards said half a unit each.

THE FLAG IS NOW THE ENGINE'S txAdvance, the units handed over at the row's price less what was paid in cash and in kind, which is what Receivables and the credit cap read. Swept across the book's sales, fifteen rows settled in kind lose a false flag, and s137 (CJ4-BJ, 4 of 12.5 unit out, nothing paid) says RM 272 unpaid rather than RM 850, the figure Receivables carries.

A CORRECTION IS MEASURED AS THE ROW WILL STAND. The card took cash and units off the row before the patch and left settledRM behind, so a correction settling an advance was flagged as that advance, and cancelling the s152 redemption as a fresh one. The same fault said s139's unchanged RM 117.5 was under RM 117.95 paid, on the very card that brought its settlement to RM 110; the corrected-total and corrected-quantity lines now wait for that figure to be corrected. A lot keeps the row it corrects, because a lot marked paid reads paid at whatever total it is given. The more-than-the-order check runs on new rows only, as its own comment said, or every overpayment on a correction was said twice.

CARDS ALREADY DRAWN KEEP THEIR WORDS. A draft's flags are written when it is drafted, so CN6-WM's two pending corrections carry the old line until they are decided. What they fold is unchanged: a flag never reaches the book.

THE CHECKS. A new section of fourteen assertions on fixture rows: a row paid in kind is no advance and an unpaid one still is, a part delivery owes its delivered share, CN6-WM's and CS6-BS's corrections and the s152 cancellation raise none, each overpayment is said once, and a total corrected under what was paid in kind is still flagged. Twelve mutations, the v625 drafter among them, each turn the assertions they touch red.

t: A PER-PRODUCT PAGE SHOWS ONE PRODUCT'S DETAIL, UNDER A SWITCH THAT CARRIES EVERY PRODUCT'S HEADLINE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 14 SEP 2026. The summary for every product always shows, a button switches the product, and two products' detail never stand on one page, because together they made the page too long. Receivables, Financials, On hand, Sourcing, Pricing and Analysis drew salt's block and then oil's. They draw one now. Above it sits a switch with a button per product, lit in that product's colour when it is the one shown. Each button carries the product's headline, so every product's summary stays in view: its revenue, or on On hand what it has on hand. The both-books summaries that lead Receivables and Financials stay where they were.

ONE PRODUCT IN VIEW FOR THE WHOLE DESK, HIS RULE. The switch sets PROD through setProdView, the same road the badge on the single-book pages and the Enter form's product select already took. Picking Oil on one page shows Oil on the next, and this device remembers the choice.

THE RAIL'S SWITCH IS GONE. Its buttons only jumped to a block further down, and on half the pages there was none, so it dimmed and explained itself. With it went prodJump, prodHead, drawProdSw, markProdSw, the PRODUCT heading, the last heading the rail carried, and their CSS.

THE CHECKS. A new section of seven assertions: no switch in the rail, and one block of the book in view on each of the six pages, under a switch listing every product and lighting that one. The buttons carry revenue, and units on hand on On hand. The both-books summaries still stand. A tap on Oil shows Oil alone and is remembered, and the next page opens on Oil. Seven mutations each turned it red. The four board laws walk each product in turn, having leaned on perProduct to do it, and the 11 Sep rail section keeps only the tab's own dress.

t: EVERY PAGE CARRIES ONE NAME, AND FIVE NAMES SAY WHAT THEIR PAGES ARE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 14 SEP 2026: RENAME WHERE NECESSARY. Two rules decided where. A page carries one name, in the rail, across its page and in its heading. Six headings had named something else: To do opened under Today, On hand under Inventory, Who buys under Customers, Map under Where the buyers are, and the two renamed below. And a name says what its page is.

THE FIVE RENAMES. Overview is Rules: every rule the desk trades by, and the register of what is breached. Forward is Next 30 days. Network is Associates. Orders is Site orders, the orders customers place on the statements site, which no longer sits a word away from the Order book. Pricing's one page takes its destination's name in place of The board, so the Whiteboard's links read Pricing. The board is still the price board inside Pricing.

WHAT DID NOT MOVE. The seven destinations, every address (#overview, #network, #orders still land), the Whiteboard, Transaction, and every link on the desk, which reads its name from the same table. The Journal keeps the names its entries were written in.

THE CHECKS. A new section renders all eighteen pages and reads their headings against their labels, finds no two pages sharing a name, and finds no destination with more pages than one opening on a page of its own name. Four mutations each turned it red. The v622 and Views sections read the new names.

t: AN ASSOCIATE EARNS A UNIT PER RM 470, AND R3 COUNTS AGAINST A HURDLE 1.2 TIMES HIGHER
n: HIS RULINGS OF 14 SEP 2026. The same unit of salt could earn twice: once in its customer's reward, and again in the R3 of the associate who introduced that customer. So an associate's R3 margin now counts against a hurdle 1.2 times their figure, and their figure is RM 470 of pooled margin a unit. A customer stays at RM 500. Both figures are stated in REWARD. rewardUnitMargin takes who the reward is for, and rewardR3Hurdle gives the weighing.

WHY THOSE FIGURES. No unit is counted more than twice on this book. 1.2 is the average number of rewards a unit of salt bought was counted into on the day (1.19), where the average over the units rewards count was 1.45 and over R3's own units exactly 2. At RM 500 no weighing could bring CN6-WM near a reward, because their R3 is RM 63 of RM 893, so the associate figure came down. RM 470 is the round figure that met the two targets he named.

WHERE IT LANDS. CS6-BS is RM 12 from their next reward, at 4 earned and 4 taken, where they had held a free unit. CN6-WM is RM 57 from theirs, and shows 1 unit ahead until his two corrections fold: s031 and s056, the two half units, become goodwill on his ruling, leaving 1 taken. CS6-PER keeps 1 free unit. CJ4-OKR, CR3-DAM, CE4-AD and CI4-OKR stand level, and every customer balance is unchanged.

ON THE DESK. The associate's card marks the R3 row at a 1.2 times hurdle and says what its margin counts as, and the total names RM 470. What counts gives both figures and the R3 hurdle, and the appointment line on Enter states the customer and associate rules side by side.
ALSO. The laptop's update chain now checks the D1 mirror through wrangler's own login, where it had needed a key no shell holds, and printed "not checked" on every run.

THE CHECKS. A new section of six assertions on fixtures: the stated figures, R3 at 1/1.2 pooling to a unit, the introduced customer still counted in full on their own table, RM 480 earning an associate a unit and a customer none, the card, and What counts. Six mutations each turned it red. The v616, v618 and v570 sections were moved onto RM 470.

t: THE RAIL IS TWO LEVELS, AND THE ORDER BOOK OPENS ON RECEIVABLES
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 14 SEP 2026: TWO LEVELS AT MOST. The rail stacked three: four headings (Command, Current, Relationships, Actions), the seven destinations, and the open destination's pages. The headings grouped the fifteen flat tabs the rail carried before v341 made the destinations, which already group, and two of the four stood over a single destination. They are gone. The rail now reads Today, Order book, Stock, Pricing, Customers, The book and Enter, and the open one lists its pages beneath it.

A DESTINATION WITH ONE PAGE LISTS NOTHING. Pricing opened a block holding one row, The board, which named the level above it again. railSubs lists nothing under a destination with no other page and marks its tab solo, and design/desk.css draws an open solo tab as the whole block, with rounded corners and its bottom edge. Pricing is the only one.

RECEIVABLES, ON HIS CHOICE. The Order book destination opened on a page also called Order book. That page is Receivables now, in the rail, across the page and in its heading. The destination keeps its name, and every old address still lands.

THE CHECKS. A new section of seven assertions: no heading in the rail, the destinations in VIEWS order, the Order book's two pages and heading, Pricing's solo block alone, and a three-page destination listing all three. The 11 Sep section now asserts PRODUCT, the one heading left, against the tabs. Eight mutations each turned the new section red.

t: A CUSTOMER HOLDING A WHOLE UNIT CAN REDEEM ONE, ON HIS WORD
n: HIS RULING OF 14 SEP 2026, THE LAST OF THREE CUSTOMER VERSIONS. Covering a lower margin is the main road for a customer's reward (v620). Redeeming stays open on his word. On the Customers card, every customer holding at least one whole unit now has a button. It reads Redeem when they owe nothing, and Offset when they hold an advance. A tap takes one whole unit: salt, through Approve as any redemption goes, or an offset against their earliest advance of no more than one unit. Under a whole unit there is no button, and the road refuses.

ONE ROAD, TWO SIDES. redeemRebate looks for an associate first, who still takes all they hold, and then for a customer. The redemption states the balance they hold rather than the unit taken, so the Approve card reads the customer's whole position. The automatic offset stays with associates, as he decided on 11 Sep. On the book today, CM4-MK and CE4-CHE are offered an Offset against the advance each holds, CM6-HCM a Redeem, and CJ4-BJ, at 0.44, nothing.

THE CHECKS. Six assertions on fixtures: the card's Redeem, Offset and absent buttons, one unit redeemed against two held, the refusal under a unit, the offset capped at one, and the drafter taking a customer's redemption without an over-balance flag. Four mutations each turned the section red. A fifth, looking for customers before associates, stayed green, and should: the customer table holds no associate, so the order cannot matter.

t: A CUSTOMER'S REWARD COVERS A LOWER MARGIN ON A SALE HE MARKS, AT THE SALT'S COST
n: HIS RULINGS OF 14 SEP 2026, THE SECOND OF THREE CUSTOMER VERSIONS. A customer's balance is meant mostly for covering a lower margin rather than for free salt. On Enter, a sale to a customer who holds reward and is priced under the board's ask for its size now shows one line: the gap, what they hold, and what a tick would cover. The gap is struck on the goods, delivery aside. What is covered is the gap or what the balance is worth at the salt's cost, whichever is less, in whole hundredths of a unit, so the ringgit never runs past the gap.

THE ROW RECORDS IT. Two new fields, coverUnits and coverRM, ride through the drafter's existing check of correctable fields, and the fold copies them onto the sale. The row editor can reach both. rebateApplied nets a cover exactly as it nets a redemption, and the desk's overlay spends a queued cover at once, so the same units cannot be offered twice before the fold. The ledger line of a covered sale carries a reward tag. The drafter refuses a cover on oil, for an associate or missing either half, checks the ringgit against the book's cost, and says the balance is the desk's word.

THE CHECKS. Twelve assertions: the plan's invariants on fixtures, the form's offer, tick and clearing, driven through wbPreview and wbRecord on distinct days so no twin guard can swallow a drive, the overlay spending a queued cover, the ledger tag, and the drafter's three refusals. The editable-attribute count moves to thirty-five. Fourteen mutations each turned the section red.

t: AN ASSOCIATE TAKES SALT UNDER THE ASK AND OIL UNDER IT TOO, BOTH PAID ON THE DAY
n: TWO ROWS FOLDED, ONE PARTY, BOTH CASH AND BOTH DELIVERED. CS6-PER takes 6.25 unit of salt at RM460 and 10 unit of oil at RM110, each dated 13 Sep, each paid and handed over the same day, so nothing stays open and the credit cap is untouched at 2 unit on salt and 20 unit on oil. He carried no outstanding and no units on credit before either row, with no defaulted sum against him.

THE UNUSUAL PART IS PRICE, NOT PAYMENT. The drafter flagged the salt rate at RM70.4 a unit, 12% under his usual RM80 across 6 orders. It sits inside his RM60 to RM100 range but under his RM85.52 median and well under the RM610 ask for 6.25 unit, clearing only the RM351.33 floor. The oil at RM110 likewise clears the RM87.28 floor and falls short of the RM130 ask. Both were decided at the desk.

THE INVENTORY TOOK THE GOODS OUT AT ITS OWN COST. Salt costed at RM44 a unit, RM275 on the order, oil at RM7.53 a unit, RM75.25, both the desk's own rates, so no separate cost line is carried. Stock stands at 16.19 unit against a stated 16.19, counted 8 Sep for salt and 9 Sep for oil, with 11.5 unit promised and the reorder mark at 15.

t: A CUSTOMER EARNS AS AN ASSOCIATE DOES, AND A WRITTEN-OFF ORDER EARNS NOBODY ANYTHING
n: HIS RULINGS OF 14 SEP 2026, THE FIRST OF THREE CUSTOMER VERSIONS. One rule now serves both sides: a whole free unit per RM 500 of margin brought, over the whole ledger. A customer counts their own priced orders. The RM 975 and 12.5 unit hurdle, the margin bands, the 10 Aug window and CUSTOMER_REWARD_OPENING are gone, and REWARD states the one figure and nothing else. He chose the whole ledger over his earlier ruling that three customers rewarded by hand before 10 Aug were settled (CE4-CHE, CM4-MK, CJ4-BJ), so only the units the book records as taken are netted.

AN ORDER NEVER PAID EARNS NOTHING, for a customer or an associate. On the book that is the two written-off orders of CA4-DAM, RM 138 of margin, which leaves them short of a unit. No associate balance moves.

WHERE IT LANDS. Thirty customers. CM4-MK holds 2 unit, CE4-CHE 1, CM6-HCM 1, and CJ4-BJ 0.44 after the 0.56 they took: 4.44 unit owed. The Customers card shows margin, earned, taken, left and the margin to the next unit, as an associate card does. The band chips on What counts gave way to the one rule. Covering a lower margin at entry is v619, and a customer Redeem is v620.

THE CHECKS. The 11 Sep section that pinned the old hurdle is retired with it. A new section of eight assertions on fixtures: a customer order before 10 Aug, one after, a written-off order, a quarter unit taken, an associate held short of a unit by their own written-off order, the card, the payload and oil. The redemption window, v570 and v616 sections were moved onto the new names. Nine mutations each turned the section red.

t: A DEPARTED ASSOCIATE KEEPS EARNING, AND NOTHING IS REDEEMED UNTIL THEY RETURN
n: HIS RULING OF 13 SEP 2026, THE LAST OF THREE VERSIONS. Departure stops the handing over and nothing else. v616 already counts a departed associate's margin like anyone's. Now every road that gives a reward out asks canRedeem first: Redeem, the Offset it becomes against an advance, the automatic offset, the card's button and the Today prompt. On the Worker, the drafter refuses a departed associate's redemption, and refuses a correction that would add reward to their row. Undoing a redemption is not one, and still goes through. Returning is taking them off PEOPLE.departed, on his word.

ON THE BOOK TODAY NOTHING MOVES. CJ4-OKR, the one departed associate, stands level at 5 earned and 5 taken, so there is nothing held yet. When they earn their sixth unit, the card will say it is held while departed, and draw no button.

THE CHECKS. Nine assertions on fixture parties. The drafter's two refusals, and its drafting for a party still here or once returned. The undo that must pass. On the desk: earning continues, no queue from Redeem, Offset or the automatic offset, a held card, no Today prompt, and every road open again on return. Nine mutations each turned the section red, a guard that refused everyone among them.

t: AN ASSOCIATE EARNS A WHOLE FREE UNIT PER RM 500 OF MARGIN BROUGHT, POOLED OVER THE WHOLE LEDGER
n: HIS RULINGS OF 13 AND 14 SEP 2026, THE SECOND OF THREE VERSIONS. An associate's reward is one count now. Their own orders and their -R account pool as R1 and R2, since the two cannot be told apart, and every priced order of each customer they introduced adds to it as R3, one level only, from v615's map. A whole unit is earned for each RM 500 of that margin. There are no bands, no unit minimum and no part units, and a loss earns nothing rather than a debt. It is counted over the whole ledger, so REWARD_OPENING leaves the book: the recount replaced the 10 Aug openings rather than adding to them, and every unit ever taken is netted against it, the July units and the -R account included.

WHERE IT LANDS, ON THE BOOK AS IT STANDS. RM 9,042.27 of margin brought against 14 units taken. CS6-BS has RM 2,576.10 and 1 unit free to redeem. CN6-WM has RM 893.20 and is 1 unit ahead. CJ4-OKR, CS6-PER, CI4-OKR, CE4-AD and CR3-DAM stand level. Net nil, as the recount he approved said at RM 500. The card shows the two margin rows and their total, then earned, taken, left and the margin to the next unit; What counts, and the appointment line on Enter, say the one rule.
UNTOUCHED. The customer scheme: RM 975 and 12.5 unit, banded, from 10 Aug over its own openings. The Redeem and automatic offset roads, which read the same earned and taken. Oil, which has no reward.

THE CHECKS. A new section of ten assertions on fixtures (an order before 10 Aug, a resale, a redemption, a pending order, an introduced associate and their own introduction, RM 1,000 exactly, a loss), the redemption window rewritten to the whole ledger, the 11 Sep and v570 sections moved off the RM 450 figure, and the book back to twenty-eight keys. Twelve mutations each turned them red.

t: WHO INTRODUCED WHOM IS ONE MAP ON THE BOOK, AND CM4-MK SITS UNDER CS6-BS
n: HIS RULING OF 13 SEP 2026, THE FIRST OF THREE VERSIONS THAT CHANGE THE REWARD RULE. An introduction came from two places that did not know about each other: the referral stamp an R3 entry puts on a row, and a network list inside R0_NETWORK that only the founder could hold. CM4-MK, whose first order went through CS6-BS-R on 15 Jul and who has bought direct ever since, had nowhere to go. INTRODUCTIONS on the book now holds every introduction no row carries, each with its reason, and introductions() reads the stamps and the book together. R0_NETWORK names the founder and nothing else.

WHAT MOVES. On salt, CS6-BS's card lists CM4-MK, and its first-order R3 reads RM 220. No reward balance moves: the earning rule is v616. On oil, the lists now match salt's, because a stamp is read off every row of both books rather than the priced rows of the book in view; CI4-OKR's oil R3 reads RM 130 from an introduced customer's first oil order.

THE CHECKS. Twelve assertions over both books: every declared and every stamped introduction reaches the map, no customer has two introducers, and every card lists exactly what the map gives it. Five mutations each turned the section red.

t: CH4-KS IS BACK ON THE MAP: THE GAZETTEER'S KS RENAME REACHES THE DESK
n: HIS EDIT OF 14 SEP 2026, MADE ON GITHUB. geo/places.json renamed the key KLS to KS, following CH4-KS home: the code was re-keyed to CH4-KLS on 28 Aug and back to CH4-KS on 12 Sep, and from that day the desk read the suffix KS, found no such key, and left the party off the map. No sync ran with the edit, so the master's GEO block still said KLS, CI failed on the push, and the cloud fold, which runs the gate before it commits, would have stalled the next approval. The block is synced byte for byte and the stale example in the locality comment goes. The check that caught it is CI's own geosync --check, proved red by that failed run.

FOUND, NOT CHANGED. Three roster codes still carry a place key the gazetteer does not hold: CA7-JTR (JTR), and CE5-TBC and CB7-TBC (TBC, the directory's to-be-confirmed placeholder). A coordinate comes from the directory by hand through tools/geofetch.mjs.

t: THE NAMES PANEL'S UNREACHABLE UNLOCK HANDLER GOES, WITH THE VAULT STATE ONLY IT TOUCHED
n: A HANDLER NOTHING COULD REACH IS REMOVED. renderReveal wired an Unlock button, #vunlock, that no template has rendered since the v217 lock came off, so its decrypt, its hold on the passphrase and its messages could never run. It goes, with the one renderReveal local only it read. Show names on the phone, Import old vault and the laptop's Save are untouched.

AND THE VAULT STATE ONLY IT TOUCHED. vaultPass, vaultFileStamp, vaultLocalStamp and vaultSaveArmed were written and never read: only that handler ever held the passphrase, and the two stamps lost their last reader at v612. vaultLoad still takes the vault it is served and vaultSave still posts an ISO updated stamp, so nothing behaves differently and no assertion was added. The build's privacy note no longer says lockVault drops a passphrase.

t: SIX R2 RESALES MOVE INTO THEIR ASSOCIATES' BUCKETS, AND ADD ID READS THE VAULT FRESH
n: SIX RESALES MOVE INTO THE ASSOCIATES' BUCKETS, APPROVED ON HIS WORD OF 13 SEP 2026. The corrections drafted under his ruling of the same day are folded. CR3-DAM's 5 unit of 10 Sep goes to CR3-DAM-R, CS6-BS's 1 unit of 12 Sep to CS6-BS-R, and four of CN6-WM's single units, 11 to 13 Sep, to CN6-WM-R. Every row was paid in full and handed over, so nothing owed moves and the inventory does not move.

ADD ID READS THE VAULT AGAIN AT THE MOMENT IT FILES A NAME. The desk loaded the encrypted vault once, when it opened, and filing a name saved that copy back over the whole of the cloud's. A phone left open across a laptop reseed would have wiped every name the reseed added or re-keyed. The vault is now fetched fresh once the passphrase is given, and a read that fails registers nothing rather than filing over the copy in memory.

NO BROWSER COPY OUTRANKS THE CLOUD'S, AND THE FOUR NEW ASSERTIONS WENT RED FIRST. A saltNameVault key in a browser's storage, which nothing has written since the master came into this repo, made that device keep its own old vault ahead of every newer one. The read goes, with the two flags it set. With the old Add ID and the legacy read put back, all four new assertions failed; with a fresh read that falls back to memory, the two refusals failed. Restored, the suite passes.

t: AN R2 SALE BOOKS TO THE ASSOCIATE'S BUCKET, AT ENTRY AND ON CORRECTION, AND THE LEDGER LINE NAMES THE ASSOCIATE
n: HIS RULING OF 13 SEP 2026: R2 SALES ARE PARKED UNDER THE ASSOCIATE'S -R BUCKET ONLY, and a buyer whose name is known is not their own. The Enter tab said an unknown buyer books to the reseller's own -R account. It did not: the form wrote the bucket in as the end buyer, the drafter booked the row to the associate's plain code, and six resales since 10 Sep sit there now.

ONE WRITER, FOUR ROADS. bookR2 in the engine puts the row in the bucket and notes a named buyer beside it, credited nothing. The drafter's entry, the fold's correction, and the desk's queue branch and correction preview all call it, where each carried the same four lines by hand. An entry still queued the old way, with the bucket as the buyer, lands on the same row.

THE ROW NAMES ITS ASSOCIATE. Attribution reads the associate off the code the row sits on, bucket or plain, so the ledger line reads R2 · CN6-WM, a named buyer in its title. A correction that names the associate unchanged and clears the bucket from the end buyer is a real change, and it is the one that files the six. The Approve card and the fold's plan both say when a correction moves a row into the bucket, where the trail's field list, which reads the buyer, would not.

WHAT THE ENTER TAB SAYS AND CHECKS. End customer reads Not named and says the sale books to the -R account either way. Record is refused while the associate's bucket is off the roster. A resale's replay twin is looked for in the bucket. The re-enter seed books the way the row will. The drafter reads the associate's history and credit across the code and the bucket, and a correction's rate flags read the goods, as v606 put every other surface.

AND A STALE REWARD RULE LEAVES THE FORM. The R2 and R3 note quoted one free unit per RM 500 resold or RM 1,500 referred, read off a block retired at v280 and kept only so a stale reference would fail. It rendered instead. It now says where the sale books and nothing about what it earns.

PROVED RED FIRST. Twelve new assertions on forced fixtures, and the five older ones that pinned the plain-code booking rewritten to the bucket. With bookR2 and the attribution put back, the form's default restored, and the ledger line and replay twin reverted, every one of them went red; restored, all pass.

t: EVERY ASSOCIATE IS MINTED WITH A BUCKET, AND THE THREE WHO HAD NONE ARE GIVEN ONE
n: HIS RULING OF 13 SEP 2026: EVERY APPOINTMENT MINTS THE -R ACCOUNT. Until now only a reseller was given one, on the ground that a referrer never books to it. An associate's own buying and their buying to sell on are one stream for the reward now, and any associate may resell, so the bucket comes with the appointment whichever stream it starts on.

ONE ANSWER, THREE READERS. The Add ID preview, the drafter and the fold all read appointBucket in the engine, so the form, the gate and the fold cannot come to disagree about which appointment mints one.
CJ4-OKR-R, CI4-OKR-R AND CE4-AD-R JOIN THE ROSTER, so all seven associates now hold a bucket. None carries a row, a name or a username, and nothing on the ledger moves.

AND THE NAME CHECK STOPS CRYING WOLF ON A PLACEHOLDER. Writing the extract failed closed: the directory files one buyer's place as to be confirmed, and s134's note says those same words about another such buyer. It is what TBC stands for, so it joins tbc and general on the one stopword list, where the reason is written down.

PROVED RED FIRST. The rule reverted to resellers only and one bucket taken off the roster turned five assertions red, the three v570 checks that said a referrer gets none rewritten to the new rule among them; restored, all pass.

t: AN ASSOCIATE'S BUCKET IS THEIRS: THE STATEMENT, THE PRICE LIST AND THE USUAL RATE READ THE CODE AND THE BUCKET AS ONE
n: HIS RULING OF 13 SEP 2026: THE BUCKET IS NOT ITS OWN PERSON, AND IN THE ACCOUNT STATEMENTS IT APPEARS UNDER THE ASSOCIATE. An associate's -R account holds the salt they buy to sell on. Until now every code was a party of its own, so CN6-WM-R, CS6-BS-R and CS6-PER-R each had a statement and a username, and a resale booked to a bucket never reached the associate's own page.

WHAT NOW READS THE TWO AS ONE. The live statement and every issue from October, the price list sealed beside it, the board the desk prints and the rate the order card calls usual. A bucket's lines say for resale. The rule is stated once, in the engine, as ownsCode, so the statements tool, the price list and the desk cannot come to disagree about it.

THE THREE BUCKET USERNAMES RETIRE ON THIS DEPLOY. The publish leaves a bucket's record out, so its own delete step takes it off the site, and the username map the desk and the owner's list read no longer carries one. The lines stay in _users.json, kept for life. The September issue is untouched, exactly as sent; every row it held under a bucket reads on the associate's live statement instead.

NOTHING ON THE LEDGER MOVES. No row is rebooked and no reward changes. Filing new R2 sales into the bucket at entry, and correcting the six booked to plain codes since 10 Sep, are the folds that follow.

PROVED RED FIRST, ON FORCED STATE. Twelve assertions over a fixture associate and their bucket, none of them leaning on the live book: the engine's rule, the statement's rows and their resale marks, the publish leaving the bucket out, the username map, the price list's rate and loyalty, and the desk's three twins. With the rule reverted in every reader at once all twelve went red, and the files came back byte for byte.

t: THREE UNIT GOES OUT DELIVERED WITH A THIRD OF THE MONEY BEHIND IT
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A DELIVERED SALT SELL ON ADVANCE. CM4-MK takes 3 unit for RM330 on 13 Sep, RM310 goods and RM20 delivery, RM220 cash in and all 3 unit delivered the same day, leaving RM110 open. The total clears the RM320 ask for 3 unit and sits under the RM430 ceiling, well above the RM168.64 floor. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, RM132 on the order.

THE ADVANCE FLAG IS THE ONE THING LEFT STANDING. The drafter asked that 3 unit going out with RM110 unpaid be read against CM4-MK's credit cap of 1 unit. He carried nothing outstanding and no units on credit before this row, and his record over 9 orders shows no default, but the cap is 1 and the dossier gives no waiver, so the flag is not answered. Stock moved out on his word; nothing landed, so the cost basis holds at RM44.

t: A THIRD RM130 UNIT TO CN6-WM, AND CM4-MK CLEARS THE LAST RM110
n: TWO ROWS FOLDED, ONE SALE AND ONE FULFILMENT. CN6-WM takes 1 unit of salt for RM130, all of it goods, paid and collected on 13 Sep, booked as an R2 with downstream CN6-WM-R. The rate clears the RM56.21 floor and the RM120 ask for 1 unit and sits at the top of his RM75 to RM130 range. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, so nothing is restated.

THE FULFILMENT CLOSES CM4-MK. RM110 cash lands on 13 Sep against s143 of 09 Sep, 2 unit for RM220, and settles it in full with no unit left to move. The drafter leaves the row to ovAmend in the master rather than recomputing it here. The inventory reads 20.19 unit stated against a salt count of 08 Sep, above the reorder mark of 15, with 11.5 unit promised and nothing owed out.

t: A DRAFT'S MARGIN IS STRUCK ON THE GOODS, BECAUSE THE DELIVERY IS A PASS-THROUGH
n: HIS RULING OF 12 SEP 2026: the delivery is charged at cost, neither more nor less. It is a pass-through, so it arrives as revenue with no matching cost anywhere on the row, and counting it flattered every figure it touched. s157, 1 unit at RM110 with RM20 of delivery, read 66.2% where the goods are 60.0%. The direction of that error is the whole point: these two numbers exist so he can see when he is underpricing, and this made every delivered order look better priced than it was.

THE RATE WAS ALREADY RIGHT IN TWO PLACES OUT OF THREE, AND THE MARGIN IN NONE. v502 put the Approve card's rate on the goods and v602 the laptop list's; the drafter's own sentence still read RM130/unit, and all three struck the margin on the full total. All three now read the goods, and the drafter's sentence states the split as well: RM130, of which RM110 is the goods and RM20 the delivery.

WHAT THE GATE MEASURES DID NOT CHANGE, and that is worth saying: flagsFor has compared the rate against the floor and against a party's history on the goods since v502, so no entry was ever refused or passed on the wrong figure. This was what a person READ while deciding, not what the desk checked.

HE APPROVED s157 ON THE OLD FIGURE. The card showed 66.2% when he tapped it. Nothing about the row moves: RM130 in, RM44 of cost, 1 unit out, and the margin on its goods was 60.0% then as now. The row's note is left as it was written, because it records what the figures said at the moment it was approved, which is the thing an audit would want.

PROVED RED ON ALL THREE SURFACES AT ONCE, each reverted to the full total: four assertions went red, one per surface, and the other 2,139 stayed green. One of the new assertions was vacuous and the mutation is what caught it: it ran the Approve card's formula inside its own test and compared the answer to itself, so it stayed green while the three around it failed. It is gone, and the source pin that did go red carries that check with a note saying why.

t: TWO SALES OF 12 SEPTEMBER: TWO UNIT COLLECTED, AND ONE UNIT DELIVERED AS A DOWNSELL
n: CA5-KER TAKES 2 UNIT FOR RM200, PAID AND COLLECTED THE SAME DAY. RM100 a unit, which clears the RM112.43 floor for 2 unit with room. Cost is RM44 a unit, the inventory's own rate, so RM88 on the order and 56.0%. Nothing stays outstanding.

AND ONE UNIT GOES OUT AS AN R2 DOWNSELL, PAID AND DELIVERED. RM130 in all, of which RM110 is the goods and RM20 the delivery, booked to CN6-WM with CN6-WM-R downstream, the same shape as s155 a few hours earlier. The goods rate is RM110 a unit against a RM56.21 floor for 1 unit; cost RM44, so 60.0% struck on the goods, which is where every rate on this desk has been struck since v502.

THE PRICE ON THE FIRST ONE IS BELOW THAT PARTY'S OWN HISTORY, AND WAS PUT TO HIM BEFORE IT WAS FOLDED. CA5-KER paid RM120 a unit on both their earlier salt orders; RM100 is a 17% drop. The drafter flagged it, he confirmed it, and it is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered from the statement.
THE INVENTORY GOES 23.19 TO 20.19 UNIT, three units out on the day across the two rows. Both are settled in full, so neither adds to credit and nothing new is outstanding.

t: THE ENTER FORM'S MESSAGES ARE A LIST OF SENTENCES, AND AN EMPTY FORM CARRIES NO STATUS
n: THEY WERE A ROW OF SHOUTING PILLS. The three message helpers borrowed .warnpill, which the design layer sets in uppercase with letter-spacing, so a sentence of plain English came out shouting and broke across a flex row mid-phrase. They have their own classes now: one per line, marked by a sign rather than a border, in ember, brass and verdigris. .warnpill is left exactly as it was for the panel notices that still want a pill, which is why these are new classes and not a redefinition of that one.

NO STATUS ON AN EMPTY FORM. The line kept stating the last thing recorded while the form was cleared underneath it, so it read as the status of whatever was on screen. It clears the moment the form has nothing in it, and is left alone the moment something is typed. Six number fields rest at 0 by default and are read as empty: on this form a zero and a blank both mean none, and counting them as input made every form look filled and the rule never fire.
AND THE EM-DASHES ARE OUT OF THE COPY, his standing rule. Eight messages read as two sentences where they read as one clause.

THE BROWSER FOUND WHAT THE SUITE MISSED. The first version of the em-dash check matched only push('...') and went green while "Choose a customer — nothing is selected." sat in a TEMPLATE LITERAL a few lines away, rendering on the desk with the dash still in it. The check reads any quoting now, and is proved on both forms: the old one cannot see the template literal, the new one can, and it still catches the single-quoted kind.

MEASURED ON THE SERVED BUILD, with its id asserted against the local build first so nothing stale was being read. Three messages stacked one per line 23px apart, text-transform none, letter-spacing normal, no border and no radius, the three colours landing on their own tokens, and the status line quiet at 12px in mist.
WHAT IT TOUCHES ON THE BOOK: NOTHING. This is the Enter form's wording and its styling.

t: THREE PARTIES TAKE THE CODES THE RULE DERIVES, AND EACH KEEPS ITS STATEMENT USERNAME
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 12 SEP 2026. v587 said the derivation reproduces 37 of the 40 codes in the directory and named these three as the ones that do not fit. They are now what the rule gives: CH4-KLS to CH4-KS, CH4-MLR to CH4-MAL, CD3-SEG to CD7-SEG. Sixty occurrences across eight files, written all or nothing, with the roster checked first for a clash in either direction.

THE USERNAME NEVER CHANGES, which is his rule. In the statements it is the key that moves and the username that stays, so all three keep the address their customer already has and the account count is unchanged at 39. The monthly passwords move with them.

CH4-KS REVERSES A CORRECTION OF 28 AUGUST, KNOWINGLY. s065 was re-keyed from CH4-KS to CH4-KLS on 28 Aug 2026, and the derivation sends it back. That was put to him before anything was written and he confirmed it. The row's note and its mod now record both moves; the 28 August amend entry is left verbatim, because a dated record of what happened that day is not rewritten by what happened three weeks later.

WHAT IS LEFT ALONE: the archive, the changelog and every version note naming an old code, this one included. They are history and say what was true when they were written. Only the live book, the roster, the directory, the statements and the fixtures moved.

THE VAULT NEEDS RE-SEEDING, AND ONLY HE CAN DO IT. The directory's keys changed, and tools/seed-vault.mjs takes the passphrase from the shell and never from a file. Until he runs it the desk's name lookup will not find these three behind their new codes.

t: THE LAPTOP'S DRAFT LIST STRIKES ITS SELLING RATE ON THE GOODS, AS THE PHONE DOES
n: IT DIVIDED THE WHOLE TOTAL, THE DELIVERY CHARGE INSIDE IT. Every rate on the desk has been struck on the goods since v502, and the phone's Approve card shows it that way. node tools/drafts.mjs --list did not: the 10 unit oil order at RM 150 carrying RM 20 of delivery read RM 15/unit on the laptop and RM 13/unit on the phone, on the same row. It reads RM 13/unit now. This is the other half of v599, which fixed the cost and the margin on that same line and left the rate beside them wrong.

THE DELIVERY WAS NEVER A COLUMN, AND DID NOT NEED TO BE. It sits in the proposed row, which is the thing being approved, so it is read from there: no migration, and the live table already carried it. A row with no delivery is unchanged, which is every salt row to date, and a row whose blob will not parse reads as no delivery rather than printing no rate at all.
PROVED RED. With the old formula put back the suite fails on exactly one assertion, the one that names RM 13, and the other 2,125 stay green. Restored byte for byte afterwards.
WHAT IT TOUCHES: THE LAPTOP'S PRINTOUT. No draft moves, no row moves, nothing on the book moves. The drafter, the phone and the fold have always read the delivery correctly.

t: THE DESKBAR, THE DATE FIELDS, THE PAGE SIGNATURE AND THE HAND-FILED PLANS, ON HIS FOUR COMMENTS OF 12 SEP 2026
n: THE DESKBAR IS ONE BAR AGAIN. Glass at the rail's height with --dbtop, a stacked-obsidian cap once it sticks, the name in the display face, and the status, the as-at and the stamp collapsed into a single meta row with provBar on its own line. On the phone it is one 60px row where it was three rows at 135px. Measured on this build at 1280, 1024, 768 and 375: no horizontal overflow at any width, every deskbar control 44 by 44, and the backdrop filter applied at all four.

EVERY DATE FIELD ON THE DESK IS DRAWN BY ONE HELPER. dateIn(id,val,attrs) wraps each field in .dtin with a Today button inside the right edge, and a delegated handler fills today's date and opens the picker under (pointer:fine). All four date fields are wrapped, and the master's whole source now carries exactly one <input ... type="date">, inside the helper, so a fifth cannot be added any other way. Proved on this build: the button sets 2026-09-12 and fires its input event, on the desk at 63 by 44 and on the phone at 65 by 45.
THE PAGE SIGNATURE IS GONE. The #foot0 block that printed the desk's own name at the foot of every page, and the rule that styled it.

THE HAND-FILED PLANS LEAVE THE WHITEBOARD. The array, the state, the six functions behind it, the "Filed by hand" section and its form, the tenth Today action, the slipped-plan observation and the rules from both CSS layers. Two things are kept deliberately: the overlay still ignores a plan entry and the queue filter still drops one, so a plan queued before today cannot break anything when it arrives.

NINE ASSERTIONS, EACH PROVED RED against v595's master and design layer before this shipped. One of them started life vacuous, a brand-block check that was already green before the change, and was replaced by one that passes only while the key is unlit and the names are sealed. A vacuous assertion is worse than none, because it reads as cover.
WHAT IT TOUCHES ON THE BOOK: NOTHING. No row, no price, no figure. This is the desk's chrome and one retired section.

t: THE DIRECTORY NEVER REACHES THE DESK, AND THE GATE THAT SAYS SO CAN FIND IT AGAIN
n: THREE REAL ENTRIES WERE LIVE ON THE PUBLIC DESK. A supplier's name in the script comment beside the oil quote, and two places in Journal version notes: beside CH6-SET at v384 and CY2-NIL at v347. The comment names the supplier by its role now, and the two notes name the code's own suffix, SET and NIL, which is what both sentences were about in the first place. Nothing else on the desk carries one: 66 names and places checked with 48 codes taken out first.

THE GATE HAD NOT RUN SINCE 20 AUGUST. It resolved salt_bio.json relative to the master, which was right while the master sat beside the directory and wrong from the day it moved into this repo. The path pointed at a 10_Data inside the repo, nothing was there, and it printed "not on this machine" and passed. Three weeks of green meant nothing at all. It reads DATA_DIR now, the one place that knows where the project folder is, and hard rule 2 keeps the directory there deliberately.

AND IT WAS READING THE ONE FILE THAT NEVER CARRIED THEM. The check scanned the extracted ledger alone, so it saw row notes and nothing else; a name in a script comment or in a version note was invisible to it by construction, which is how three sat in plain sight. It scans the master beside the extract now and says which of the two is dirty.

PROVED BY RUNNING IT, on a throwaway directory holding one fictional party. With that word planted in a script comment the master goes red and the extract stays green, which is the exact shape of what was missed; on a clean master both pass. The suite runs both directions and needs no real directory, so CI proves it too and the check stays honest on a machine that has never seen the names.
WHAT IT TOUCHES ON THE BOOK: NOTHING. No row, no price, no figure, no count. The ledger extract moves only because it was still stamped v598.

THE ARCHIVE IS SWEPT NEXT, ON HIS WORD OF 12 SEP 2026. master/changelog.json carries 39 more, in entries the desk does not serve. The repo is private so it is not an exposure, but hard rule 3 says no real name is ever committed, and a sweep of the dated record is its own version rather than something that rides along with this one.

t: THREE READERS STOP PRINTING FIGURES THEY HAD NOT MEASURED
n: HIS REPORT OF 12 SEP 2026: A SALE OVER ITS FLOOR READ AS SHORT BY A NEGATIVE AMOUNT. The under-floor card chose its rows with the band formula v280 retired and measured them with the ladder's floor its evidence prints. At 12.5 unit those are RM 878.34 and RM 702.67, so CJ4-BJ's RM 850 fell between the two: caught by one ruler, measured by the other, and printed as short RM -147. Three of the five rows on show were above their floor, not under it. One floor now, the one the evidence prints. The card goes from 7 rows to 2, and both that remain are CH5-OUG, short RM 53 and RM 103 against RM 703.

AND A PENDING ORDER IS NOT A SALE. The no-cost card listed CH6-SET, CC5-OKR and CF5-WM, three pending orders of 11 Sep, as priced sales carrying no cost of their own. A pending order carries none by design, since the cost is stated when the salt moves. With them out the card has nothing to report on this book and does not draw at all. Its title agrees with itself in the plural now, and its reason no longer names RM64 and RM47, which were the buying rates on the day it was written.

THE COPY NAMES THE FLOOR IT USES, ON HIS WORD. The title and reason still said band floor, after v280 left nothing in that card computing a band. Three sites keep the phrase and are left as they are: two comments, on the engine and on the ladder solver, and the Boundaries all-clear, which is a different card with a check of its own.

AND THE LAPTOP PRINTED -401.7% FOR A 49.8% MARGIN. node tools/drafts.mjs --list read a draft's cost as a unit cost, which it has not been since v496. A draft for 10 unit of oil at RM 150 with a cost of RM 75.25 printed its cost as RM 75.25 a unit and its margin as -401.7%, where the phone's Approve card showed RM 75.25 (RM 7.53/unit) and 49.8%. Only a draft of exactly one unit read right, and by accident. It reads as the Approve card does now. The drafter, the phone and the fold have always read the cost as the order's, so no draft and no row moves.
NOTHING IN THE BOOK MOVES. All three are readers. No price, no row, no cost, and the inventory, the credit and the queue close where they opened.

PROVED RED FIRST, AND MEASURED ON THE BOOK. The two cards are counted before and after six planted rows, so what each gains is what is asserted: a sale just over its floor, one under it and a pending order, and two delivered sales with no cost beside a pending one. The guard asserts the retired band figure still exceeds the ladder's floor at 12.5 unit, so the two rulers can be told apart at all. The draft list is asserted on that same oil draft, red on the old formula and on the old label.

FOLDED OUT OF TWO SESSIONS, EACH OF WHICH HAD CLAIMED v596. The cloud had already spent that number on the cs6-bs corrections while both sat unshipped, so both are renumbered into this one version. Their own bumps are discarded; only the fixes and their assertions come across.

t: A SALT UNIT GOES OUT AT THE MEDIAN, PAID AND COLLECTED THE SAME DAY
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL SETTLED IN FULL ON THE DAY. SELL to CN6-WM, 1 unit for RM110 on 12 Sep, RM110 cash in and 1 unit collected the same day, so the row itself leaves nothing open. The rate clears the RM56.21 floor for 1 unit, sits under the RM120 ask and the RM150 ceiling, and matches the party's own median of RM110 across 7 orders.

THE FLAGS ARE ANSWERED IN PART AND THE INVENTORY MOVES BY ONE UNIT. The drafter's rate flag is answered by the party's median of RM110 and its RM75 to RM130 range. The flag that the row books as an R2 downsell through CN6-WM-R, leaving CN6-WM off the statement, is not answered here. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, so the basis is untouched and stock falls from 24.19 by the 1 unit moved.

t: AN OIL ADVANCE GOES OUT IN FULL AT THE ASK AND SITS ON THE WHOLE CREDIT CAP
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SELL TO CE4-CHE AT THE ASK. Ten unit of oil went out on 12 Sep for RM150, of which RM20 is delivery and RM130 goods, which is the RM130 ask for that size and well over the RM87.28 floor. Nothing came in as cash, so the whole RM150 stands open against a party that had RM0 outstanding and nothing on credit before today. Goods were handed over in full on the day.

THE UNUSUAL PART IS THE CREDIT, NOT THE RATE. The drafter flagged the row as an advance and asked that it be checked against the cap: ten unit on credit against a cap of 10 answers the flag exactly at the limit, with no room left. The second flag, that CE4-CHE has no committed oil order to compare against, is not answered here. The row carries RM75.25 of cost, which is not the inventory's own RM44 a unit.
THE INVENTORY DID NOT MOVE. The oil leg is recorded but not landed, so the salt position is untouched at 24.19 unit on the count of 8 Sep and the cost basis stays where it was.

t: TWO CORRECTIONS ON CS6-BS: A REWARD ROUNDED UP, A REDEMPTION UNDONE
n: FOLDED: TWO CORRECTIONS, NO CASH AND NO STOCK. Both sit against CS6-BS and both are on his word of 12 Sep. On s139 the reward now takes the whole unit, settledRM RM110 and rebateKg 1, where v591 folded RM110.45 and 0.94 unit. On s152 the 0.06 unit redemption is undone: cancelled on 12 Sep, nothing moved, nothing settled, no reward and no goodwill on it.

UNUSUAL: A CANCELLATION THAT PULLS A ROW OUT OF EVERY FIGURE. The drafter flagged that cancelling s152 removes the revenue, the stock it drew and anything owed on it, and that the row was priced at RM44 a unit against CS6-BS's usual RM107, 58.9% below, with RM2.64 of goods RM0.73 under the RM3.37 floor. The cancellation answers those flags by leaving nothing on the row.

THE INVENTORY DID NOTHING. Neither patch moves goods or money, so stock stands at 24.19 unit on the salt count of 08 Sep, cost basis unchanged at RM44 a unit against replacement of RM46 and the reorder mark of 15. CS6-BS had RM0 outstanding before and 1 unit on credit, nothing defaulted, across 11 orders with a median rate of RM100 and a range of RM11 to RM126.67.

t: A LOAN IS REPAID, IN PART OR IN FULL, IN WHAT WAS LENT, AND SETTLES WHEN NOTHING IS LEFT OWING
n: HIS RULING OF 11 SEP 2026: a loan is repaid in what was lent. Borrow or lend has a third choice, Repaid, which picks the open loan and asks for units against a salt loan and ringgit against a cash one. A part repayment is allowed, and the loan settles when nothing is left owing. More than is owing is refused, since interest is not a repayment.

A LOAN HAS A NAME NOW. The fold gives each loan a rid as it appends it, the way it names a sale or a lot, so a repayment names the one loan it pays. The three loans on the book are settled and need none.

WHAT IS OWING IS READ EVERYWHERE. The inventory walk, the lent-out and borrowed-in counts, the cash flow and the borrowed-in table read what is still owing on each open loan. That also ends the fault where a repaid loan out kept reading as lent: its count had no status filter at all.
WHAT IT TOUCHES TODAY: NOTHING. All three loans on the book are settled, and none is lent out. Interest is still to come.

PROVED THROUGH EVERY ROAD: the drafter, the planner and the apply on a copy of the book, the pane driven on the real master, the overlay across redraws, the Approve card and cashFlow. Ten mutations, each reddening its own, run on this same code before v590 to v594 went in under it.

t: A REWARD OFFSET IS PRICED ON THE GOODS AND SETTLES NO MORE THAN IS OWED
n: HIS DIAGNOSIS OF 12 SEP 2026: A REWARD PAYS FOR SALT, SO IT IS PRICED ON THE GOODS. s139 is one unit at RM 110.00 with a RM 7.50 delivery on the same line, and CS6-BS paid the delivery in cash. Both offset roads priced the unit on the whole line, RM 117.50, so v591's offset took 0.94 unit and settled RM 110.45 against RM 110.00 owed. offsetFor is the one rule now, for the Offset button and the automatic offset alike: the unit is the goods rate, as every rate on the desk has been since v502, the units never exceed what was sold, and the ringgit never exceeds what is owed, so an unpaid delivery stays owed. On it s139 takes the whole unit and settles exactly RM 110.00.

THE CLOUD SUITE HAS BEEN RED SINCE v591 WENT LIVE, through v592 and v593, on the same four checks and a book that was right. Two read CS6-BS's own rows and assumed every redemption of theirs predated the scheme; two looked s139 up in a statement window that closes on 01 Sep. None was a fault in the statement: s139 prints as the part-paid sale it is. The pair uses a fixture party now, and the part-paid check looks each row up with the window open, as the cancelled-order check beside it already did.
s139 IS LEFT AS FOLDED, 0.94 unit and RM 110.45, and so is v592's 0.06 unit to CS6-BS, the remainder the overshoot left free. Both go to him in Approve as corrections.

Seven mutations, each reddening its own, run on this same code before v592 and v593 folded under it: the unit priced on the whole line again, an offset settling more than is owed, a reward covering more units than were sold, the automatic offset and the Offset button each on arithmetic of their own, the reward window forgetting where it starts, and the statement reading any rebate row as a gift.

t: A FREE UNIT OF SALT GOES OUT ON THE REWARD, BOOKED AS COST AND NOT REVENUE
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A REDEMPTION AND NOT A SALE. CR3-DAM takes 1 unit of salt free on 12 Sep, RM44 of goods settled by the reward with no cash in, and the unit delivered the same day. It is booked as cost and not revenue on his ruling of 11 Sep 2026, the row carrying goodwill as well as rebate, so the RM44 sits as an expense against the inventory's own rate.

WHAT IS UNUSUAL AND WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. The RM44 falls under the RM56.21 floor for 1 unit and well under the RM120 ask and RM150 ceiling, which is what a free unit does to the ladder. The drafter flagged the earned and unredeemed balance of 1 unit as the desk's word, not checkable here, and the figures do not answer it. The stated shelf rolls down by the unit and the RM25 already outstanding on CR3-DAM stays open.

t: A REWARD UNIT GOES OUT FREE TO CS6-BS, COSTED NOT SOLD, AND THE SHELF ROLLS BY IT
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A REDEMPTION RATHER THAN A SALE. CS6-BS takes 0.06 unit of salt on 12 Sep with nothing in cash, the RM2.64 settled by the reward. On his ruling of 11 Sep 2026 the row carries goodwill as well as rebate, so it stays out of revenue and the RM2.64 stands as expense. Delivered the same day, so nothing is left outstanding on it.

THE LADDER AND THE SHELF. At RM2.64 the row sits under the RM3.37 floor for 0.06 unit and well under the RM10 ask and RM10 ceiling, which is what a free redemption looks like on the board. The salt leaves the inventory at its own RM44 a unit, so the cost basis does not move and the stated shelf rolls down by 0.06 unit from 25.25.

t: A REWARD OF 0.94 UNIT SETTLES RM110.45 OF THE 07 SEP ADVANCE IN KIND
n: ONE CORRECTION FOLDED, NO CASH AND NO STOCK. The fold patches s139, the 1 unit sale to CS6-BS of 07 Sep at RM117.50 with RM7.50 delivery inside and nothing paid: settledRM goes from unset to RM110.45, rebate from false to true, and rebateKg from unset to 0.94. The entry is the automatic offset of the CS6-BS reward against that order, so the row now says it is settled in kind rather than owed in cash. The row itself is not rewritten.

THE INVENTORY DID NOTHING. No units moved and no money was taken in, so stock stands at 25.25 units on the salt count of 08 Sep, costed at the inventory's own RM44 a unit against a replacement of RM46, with the reorder mark at 15, nothing owed out and 11.5 units promised. The drafter's flag on the RM110 advance asks for a check against the CS6-BS credit cap, and the dossier carries 1.94 units on credit before this row but states no cap, so that check stays open.

t: ONE UNIT OUT TO CS6-BS AT RM130 ALL IN, PAID AND DELIVERED THE SAME DAY
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL OF 1 UNIT. CS6-BS takes 1 unit on 12 Sep for RM130 with RM30 carriage inside that total and RM100 of goods, RM130 cash in and 1 unit moved on the day, so the row opens and closes together and leaves nothing outstanding. The rate clears the RM56.21 floor for 1 unit, sits RM10 above the RM120 ask and RM20 under the RM150 ceiling, and stands above the party's own RM100 median.

THE FLAG IS THE ROUTING, NOT THE MONEY. The drafter marked the row as an R2 downsell booked to CS6-BS, so that code is not the counterparty here and draws no statement from it. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, so no separate cost is carried. Prior outstanding of RM110 and 1.94 units on credit against a cap of 2 stand untouched by this row, with nothing defaulted.

t: A LOAN CAN BE CASH AS WELL AS SALT, AND A CASH LOAN MOVES THE CASH FLOW
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 11 SEP 2026: borrow and lend in salt or in cash. Borrow or lend asks what changed hands now. Salt is entered in units, as before; cash is entered in ringgit. On his ruling a loan is repaid in what was lent, so a cash loan is owed back in cash.

A CASH LOAN MOVES THE CASH FLOW AND NOTHING ELSE. While it is open, cash borrowed in adds to the flow and cash lent out takes from it. It is money that goes back, so it is neither revenue nor cost, and the inventory does not move. The drafter drafts it in ringgit with no units, the fold appends it and rolls nothing, and the borrowed-in table shows it in ringgit.

AND A QUEUED LOAN COUNTS ONCE. The overlay rebuilt every list from its snapshot on each redraw except the loans, which had none, so since v527 a queued loan was pushed again on every pass and a borrowing counted twice after two redraws. It would have grown the cash flow with each redraw, so the loans take a snapshot and a reset like the six lists beside them. The v527 test had measured against the grown list, which is how the fault passed it. The ledger extract reads that committed copy too, as it reads refunds, so a queued loan cannot reach the store unapproved.
WHAT IT TOUCHES TODAY: NOTHING. Every loan on the book is salt, and all three are settled. Repayment and interest are the next two folds.

PROVED THROUGH EVERY ROAD: the drafter, the planner and the apply on a copy of the book, the pane driven on the real master, the overlay across redraws, the Approve card and cashFlow itself. Eleven mutations, each reddening its own, two of them the redraw fix: without the reset, three redraws grew the loan book from 4 to 7.

t: A CUSTOMER'S STATEMENT USERNAME IS MINTED THE DAY THEY ARE REGISTERED, AND KEPT FOR LIFE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026: each customer has a permanent username for their statement. One used to be minted the month a customer was first issued a statement, so a new customer had no address for up to a month: no statement link, and no QR on a printed board. The fold mints it with the registration now.

ONE MINT AND ONE FILE FORMAT. The statements run and the fold both call userFor and usersJson, moved into stmt-crypto.mjs beside newUsername, so the two writers of the users file cannot drift. A username that exists is never replaced, and the amend that re-keys a code will carry it to the new code.
WHO IS MINTED ONE: a registered customer, associate or referrer, the kinds whose rows book to them. A supplier, a bucket and an associate's end buyer are issued no statement and get none.
WHAT IT TOUCHES TODAY: NOBODY. It runs only when a registration folds, and the 39 usernames already in the file are untouched.

PROVED IN MEMORY through mintUsernames and the two shared functions; the fold's own run is the one step read rather than driven, since the suite never runs fold.mjs as a process. Seven mutations, each reddening its own.

t: ADD ID DERIVES THE CODE FROM THE NAME AND THE PLACE, AND A CLASH TAKES MORE OF THE NAME
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026: the code is derived, never typed. C for a customer or S for a supplier, then the name's first letter and its length, then a dash and the place: its initials when it is several words, its first three letters when it is one. A blank place gives TBC, for a supplier too, which used to take no suffix. Names & IDs on the laptop already minted codes this way; the phone took a typed code and checked only its shape. Both call one function now.

A CLASH TAKES MORE OF THE NAME. Two people can derive one code: the same initial, the same length, the same place. Asked for something better than a refusal or a running number, the code takes one more letter of the name at a time, so a second four-letter A from the same place is told apart by the name people know them by. Only a name used up entirely, the same name twice in one place, falls back to a number. The preview says which code was taken.

APPOINTING SOMEONE ALREADY ON THE ROSTER is a pick under Who now, since there is no code box left to type into. Who lists the roster's customers who are not yet associates, so nobody can be appointed twice.

WHAT IT TOUCHES: NO EXISTING CODE. The rule reproduces 37 of the 40 codes in the directory it applies to. CH4-KLS, CH4-MLR and CD3-SEG do not fit it, and on his ruling they are re-keyed with the amend, which comes last in this round and carries each statement username with its customer.

PROVED ON FIXTURE CODES forced onto the live roster and taken off again: the rule, the clash walk, the pane and the laptop. Ten mutations, each reddening its own. The v528 and v570 tests moved with the pane, since they typed a code there is no longer a box for, and the bucket test uses a fixture associate now.

t: A REFUSED ENTRY STAYS ON THE PHONE UNTIL IT IS WITHDRAWN, IN ONE TAP
n: HIS DECISION, 11 SEP 2026: a refused entry is kept on the phone, with a Withdraw button. Until now one vanished at the next fold with no record. The phone cleared any acknowledged entry the watermark had passed, and the drafter deleted any refusal the watermark had passed, so an unrelated fold passed for proof that the entry had been dealt with. CR3-DAM's redemption of 11 Sep went that way: refused for carrying no payload, then gone.

THE PHONE KEEPS WHAT THE DRAFTS SAY IS REFUSED. A read of the drafts that succeeds records which entries are refused; a failed read records nothing, so it cannot wipe the list. The load keeps a refused entry however far the watermark has passed it, and does not call it stuck, since stuck means it never reached the cloud and a refused entry did.

THE CLOUD KEEPS A REFUSAL WHILE ITS ENTRY IS QUEUED, whoever wrote it. Once the entry leaves the queue, the drafter's own refusal goes at its next pass, since leaving is a withdrawal or a re-entry; one from the laptop's queue or the fold goes at the watermark as before, since their entries need never have been on the cloud queue. The fold's own notices keep their rule.
