WITHDRAW is one button on each refusal card whose entry this phone holds. It drops the entry the way a rejection does, takes the card off at once and syncs, and the cloud's copy and its refusal follow. A card not queued here says so; a fold notice says it clears itself. Nothing on the panel approves or rejects, as v309 built it.

PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The drafter runs twice against a fake ledger, including a withdrawal above the watermark, the one case where the old rule and the new part. The phone is tested through a real boot with a refused entry already in storage, a real apLoad with the network stubbed and a real tap on Withdraw. Fourteen mutations, each reddening its own assertion. Three source pins from v485 and one from the drafter's first round moved with the code.

ONE GAP REMAINS, AND IT IS NARROW. The phone learns of a refusal only when it reads the drafts: on opening, on Approve, and after a redemption. The load runs before the first read, so an entry refused after the phone's last read, then passed by a fold approved elsewhere before the phone next opens, can still clear at that opening. An approval on this phone reads the drafts first, so today only the laptop can open it.

WHO IT TOUCHES TODAY: NOTHING. The refused table is empty and the cloud queue holds no entries, so the first pass after this deploy clears nothing. It does not bring CR3-DAM's redemption back: their unit is still earned and unredeemed, and Redeem, which has carried a payload since v584, puts it to Approve in one tap.

t: AN ASSOCIATE'S REWARD IS OFFSET AGAINST THEIR ADVANCE AUTOMATICALLY, UP TO 1 UNIT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026: an associate's reward is offset against their advanced delivery order, up to 1 unit, automatically, and folded into the Approve tab. So nobody presses anything: whenever Approve has read the drafts, each associate holding an earned unit and an outstanding advance is offered an offset, capped at 1 unit, as the same Correction the Offset button has queued since v584. It waits in Approve for his tap like any row, and the Approve part says what it offered.

IT RUNS ONLY WHEN THE DRAFTS WERE READ. The check that stops it offering the same offset twice reads them, and a failed read would leave that check blind, so on a failed read it does nothing. It skips a row with an offset already queued, drafted or refused, so a refusal is not offered again on every load; once one folds, the row is settled in kind and stops being an advance, which ends it. Salt only, since oil has no reward. Associates only, on his word; a customer's reward is not offset automatically.

A DUPLICATE OFFER CANNOT REACH THE LEDGER. Two devices loading at the same moment could each offer the same offset. The drafter's own correction check already refuses a Correction that changes nothing, so the second is refused rather than drafted, and an assertion now holds it to that. A second guard for the same case was written, found unreachable when its own mutation stayed green, and taken out again, so this version does not touch the Worker at all.

PROVED WITH EVERY STATE FORCED, AND THE HOOK THROUGH apLoad ITSELF with the network stubbed, because a test that called the function directly would stay green with the hook removed. Thirteen assertions. Five mutations on the new code and one on the drafter's existing no-change check, each reddening its own.

WHO IT TOUCHES TODAY: NOBODY, READ OFF THE ENGINE. The two associates with an advance outstanding, CS6-BS on s139 and CN6-WM on s124, hold no free unit, and CN6-WM carries a deficit of 1, so nothing is offered until one of them earns one. CR3-DAM holds the one free unit among the associates and has no advance, so theirs stays a Redeem. Customers are outside the automatic offset on his word, and two of them hold both: CM4-MK a unit against RM 110 owed on s143, and CJ4-BJ a quarter unit against RM 272 on s137. That is put to him, with the customers' want of any Redeem button at all.

t: A REDEMPTION AND A REBATE OFFSET REACH APPROVE, AND REDEEM IS ONE TAP
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026: everything that goes through the ledger goes through Approve, and redeeming is a one-tap button. The Redeem button queued REDEEM and REBATE_OFFSET with no payload. The cloud drafter refuses an entry without one, and the refusal cleaned itself away at the next fold, so not one redemption or offset pressed on the cloud desk ever reached the book. CR3-DAM's, pressed at 07:01 that morning, was the one found. Both now carry a payload the drafter reads, and the tap lands on Approve, which reads the drafts again once the post has landed.

A REDEMPTION IS A SALES ROW THE DRAFTER BUILDS, BOOKED AS A COST. Salt out, no cash, settled by the reward. On his ruling of the same day it carries goodwill as well as rebate, exactly as s050 does, so revenue does not move and its cost is an expense. Its total and its settlement are the salt's own cost, read where every other row's cost is read. The drafter cannot check the reward, since rewards are worked out on the desk from the whole book, so the Approve card carries the balance the desk stated and says it is the desk's word. Oil, which has no reward, is refused, and so is a redemption naming no party, no units or no date.

THE 04 AUG RULE IS KEPT EXACTLY. A free unit offsets an outstanding advance first, in kind, with no salt moving. The offset is a Correction on the advance row itself, settledRM and rebate, which is how the ledger has always recorded one, and it ADDS to whatever that row already settles in kind rather than overwriting it. It travels the Correction road the drafter and the fold already had, so the drafter needed one new branch and the fold none.
THE APPROVE CARD READS A REDEMPTION AS ONE: units out, the cost as an expense, no revenue, no cash. The sale card would have shown it as a sale at nil margin.

PROVED WITH EVERY STATE FORCED. Revenue unmoved and the cost landing as an expense on the desk's own walk; the row reading In-Kind; the tap queuing an entry the drafter drafts and landing on Approve; an advance turning it into an offset Correction the drafter drafts. Twenty-one assertions, and six mutations across the drafter and the desk, each reddening its own.
STILL TO COME, EACH IN ITS OWN VERSION: the automatic offset of up to 1 unit, and the fix that stops a refused entry vanishing at the next fold.

t: BOTH BORROWED LOTS GO BACK, AND THE INVENTORY ROLLS DOWN BY 7
n: HIS WORD, 11 SEP 2026: both lots borrowed in on 08 Sep have been returned, today. CH5-OUG's 5.5 unit and CA11-SEN's 1.5 unit went back in kind, unit for unit. Both loans are settled on 11 Sep and the 7 unit leave the stated inventory: 33.25 less 7 is 26.25. A roll and not a count, so COUNT_ON stays at 08 Sep.

BY HAND, BECAUSE THERE IS NO ROAD YET. The fold's loan road only appends a loan; nothing settles one, and the Borrow or lend pane says so in terms. So it was written exactly as the fold would write a loan movement: the loans marked settled with the date, the same ROLLED sentence on the stated inventory, and the book written by writeBookFile so it stays one row per line. ledger/ledger.json is regenerated with it.
BOTH READERS AGREE AFTERWARDS. loanInUnits counts a borrowed loan only while it is open, so the ledger walk drops the 7 unit by itself, and the stated shelf rolls by the same 7.

FOUND FOR THE LOAN FOLD THAT FOLLOWS. The lent-out side has no status filter: loanOutUnits and the Inventory walk count every loan out, settled or not, so a repaid loan out would keep reading as lent. Both of today's loans were borrowed, so nothing on the book is touched by it; the repay road will need the filter.

AND ONE TEST THAT READ THE LIVE BOOK NOW CARRIES ITS OWN LOAN. The v527 borrow-and-lend section found its open loan by searching the live book, which held one only until these two went back: the correct fold failed its first check and threw on lender.party. It was run once without the change to prove the break, then given a fixture open loan of its own, so what it measures no longer depends on what the book happens to hold.

t: THE DEMAND YOU COULD NOT SERVE CARD LEAVES CUSTOMERS
n: HIS CALL, 11 SEP 2026. With Turned away gone from the Enter form at v581 the card had no writer, and the book holds no rows in it, so it could only ever read “Nothing recorded”. It goes, with the three figures only it read, and the Customers lead and its one-line description stop naming it.

ITS FIELD IN THE PHONE PAYLOAD GOES WITH IT. Nothing outside the desk reads it: no reader in the Worker, the tools, the statements site or the service worker. LOST_LABEL goes too, having no reader left once the card and the Turned away pane had gone.

WHAT STAYS. The turned-away rows stay on the book as data, and the drafter keeps its lost-sale road, for the reason v581 gave: a phone offline on an old build can still queue one, and an entry the drafter refuses is dropped in silence.

AND THE v581 WORDING CHECKS NOW READ THE CODE ONLY. They searched the whole master, and the version history quotes retired wording by design, so the first entry to quote it would have turned them red for the wrong reason. They skip the history now, as this version's own check does.

PROVED ON THE RENDERED VIEW AND THE BUILT PAYLOAD. Five assertions, with a turned-away row forced onto the book so the card had something to show and its absence means something. Four mutations, each reddening its own.

t: SELF-USE OR LOSS, TURNED AWAY AND FOLLOW-UP LEAVE THE ENTER FORM
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026, WITH HIS REASONS. Self use and loss are read from the counts already: the gap between the ledger and what was counted books as self-use, and the count always wins, so a form for typing it in again was a second road to one figure. A turned-away sale is at most something to derive from a cancelled order. A follow-up is not needed on this desk at all. The three modes leave the switch, with their panes, their previews and their records.

WHAT STAYS, AND WHY. Every row already on the book, and every view that reads one: the self-use split on Inventory, the turned-away table on Customers and the payload beside it. The drafter and the fold keep their loss and lost-sale roads, because a phone offline on an old build can still queue one, and v580 found that an entry the drafter refuses is dropped in silence on the next fold.

COPY MAY POINT ONLY AT A CONTROL THAT EXISTS. Inventory told him to record under Self-use or loss, Customers told him to log a turned-away sale under Enter, and the Enter part described itself by all three. Each now says what is true. Today raises no follow-up call: that call read rows nothing can write any more, so it would have been a standing item on the badge v580 had just made honest, with no visit able to clear it.

FOUND IN THE SWEEP, AND GONE WITH IT. Sixteen field ids still wired to listeners, the follow-up party list, and four follow-up helpers with no reader left: CONTACT_HOW, CONTACT_OUT, lastContact and contactsDue. LOST_LABEL stays, because it still labels the turned-away table.

OPEN, FOR HIS WORD. The turned-away card on Customers now has no writer and the book holds no rows in it, so it will read “Nothing recorded” until turned-away sales are derived from cancelled orders, which is his idea and is not built.

PROVED ON THE RENDERED FORM. Seven assertions, read off the mode switch as it draws rather than off the source, with a follow-up ten days overdue forced onto the book so the Today check can fail at all: the live book holds none with a date. Six mutations, each reddening its own.

t: A COUNT BADGE COUNTS EACH THING ONCE, ON TODAY AND ON ENTER
n: HIS REPORT, 11 SEP 2026: the badges counted one thing as two. On Today a breach was counted once as a breach and again inside the rule row that names it. v341 added the breaches to the NOW items, but actions() step 5 builds its RULE rows FROM those same breaches, grouped by party, and marks every one of them now. Measured the same morning: nine on the badge against the five items Today lists. The badge is the NOW list the page shows, which already carries every breach, so the number on the rail is the number of things a visit finds.

ON ENTER, ONE ENTRY WAS COUNTED TWICE WHILE IT WAITED. An entry queued on the phone stays in qTx() until the fold has passed it, and once the cloud drafter drafts it the same entry is also in AP_DRAFTS, so between the draft and the approval it was counted in both. A draft's id IS the entry's at, read off D1 rather than assumed, so the union on that key counts each entry once at every stage: drafted and waiting on a tap, approved and waiting to go live, or refused and waiting on him. Customer orders placed on the statements site stay a term of their own until one is done and queued.

THE PHONE'S PUSH BANNER WAS CHECKED AND IS CLEAN. It names four things, rows waiting for approval, shelves not counted, entries refused and customer orders, as separate phrases rather than one summed number, and the four sets do not overlap: an entry is drafted or refused, never both, and an order is placed until it is done.

FOUND IN PASSING, AND IT IS THE NEXT FOLD: A REFUSED ENTRY IS DROPPED IN SILENCE. His Redeem for CR3-DAM, pressed at 07:01 KL a minute after v577 made the unit real, was refused at 07:09 because the Redeem button sends no payload and the drafter refuses an entry without one. When v578's fold moved the watermark past it, the refusal self-cleaned and the phone cleared the entry from its queue as if it had been committed. Nothing on the book or the phone records the attempt. The unit itself is not lost, since the engine still shows it earned and unredeemed, but the request is. Every Redeem, Rebate offset, Rename and follow-up on the cloud chain has met the same end, and giving each a road to Approve is the fold that follows this one.

PROVED WITH BOTH STATES FORCED. Ten assertions, each proved red by putting the old formula back: a stubbed breach makes the old Today sum visibly wrong, and one entry placed in both the queue and the drafts makes the old Enter sum count it twice. Whether the live book happens to hold either state is the calendar's business and not the test's, so neither is read off the desk.

t: A SECOND ORDER FROM CF5-WM AT RM110 INCLUDING CARRIAGE, PENDING UNTIL SOMETHING MOVES
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL TO CF5-WM. One unit at RM110 total on 11 Sep, RM10 of that carriage, so RM100 of goods. Nothing was paid and nothing moved, so the row sits pending and draws no stock and books no revenue for now. The drafter raised no flags and the queued entry matched the mirror, so the fold went in as drafted with no amendment and no count attached.

THE INVENTORY DID NOT MOVE. Stock stands at 33.25 units on the salt count of 8 Sep, cost held at RM44 a unit against a replacement of RM46, with 10.5 units promised, nothing owed out and the reorder mark at 15. The two loans in, 5.5 units from CH5-OUG and 1.5 units from CA11-SEN, both dated 8 Sep, stay open and untouched by this fold.

t: TWO PENDING SALT ROWS DATED 11 SEP, NOTHING PAID AND NOTHING MOVED
n: WHAT WAS FOLDED. Two new salt sells dated 11 Sep, both agreed on the day and both pending: 1 unit to CH6-SET at RM120 with RM10 delivery, and 1 unit to CC5-OKR at RM90 collected. Neither carries cash and neither moved a unit, so neither draws stock nor books revenue. Both sit on the 1 unit ladder with a floor of RM56.21, an ask of RM120 and a ceiling of RM150.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL, AND WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. CH6-SET lands exactly on the RM120 ask and on its own median; CC5-OKR lands RM30 under the ask with RM90 already outstanding and 1 unit on credit against a cap of 1, after a cancelled row at the same terms on 08 Sep. The drafter raised no flags on either. Both are costed at the inventory's own RM44 a unit, and stock stands unmoved at 33.25 units.

t: THE REWARD HURDLES ARE STATED OFF THE BOARD, CARRY A UNIT MINIMUM, AND OIL HAS NONE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026. What an associate brings in, R2 and R3 together, hurdles at RM 450 and 5 unit instead of RM 470; what anyone buys directly, a customer or an associate's own R1, hurdles at RM 975 and 12.5 unit instead of RM 940. Both figures are his and both are struck off the board: the engine prints Tier 1 at RM 500 on 6.25 unit and RM 875 on 12.5 unit, so 500 less a tenth is 450 and 875 and a hundred is 975. The suite re-reads those two prices off the engine rather than trusting the config, so re-striking the board without re-striking the hurdle goes red rather than quietly leaving a figure whose reason has expired.

THE HURDLE WAS DERIVED AND IS NOW STATED, WHICH IS THE REAL CHANGE. It was base lot times cheapest unit cost times a multiple, so it moved every time a cheaper lot landed: a party could be RM 20 from a free unit on Monday and RM 60 from it on Wednesday having bought nothing. A threshold somebody is trying to cross should hold still. The derivation is kept beside the figures so it can be re-struck deliberately.

AND A UNIT MINIMUM BESIDE THE MONEY, WHICH REVERSES A v280 SENTENCE ON PURPOSE. v280 said “Everything is measured in MONEY, never in units”, because the old unit trigger paid most to whoever was sold to most cheaply. That objection is answered rather than ignored: the money hurdle still decides IF and the margin band still decides HOW MUCH, and where the unit minimum bites it scales the award by margin rather than refusing it, on his rule that a short crossing is “calculated based on the gross margin expected”. A party who clears RM 975 on 8 unit is paid what their margin is worth against the RM 172 the board expects on 12.5 unit at Tier 1, read from priceLadder and never typed, because the desk prices nothing. The scale is capped at 1, and that is a decision rather than a detail: uncapped, a short seller at a very high margin would earn MORE than the same money over the minimum, and the short path must never beat the full one.

OIL HAS NO REWARD AT ALL (his call, same day). The two figures are salt's Tier 1 and oil has no Tier 1, so there was nothing to derive an oil pair from and a formula he did not choose is worse than no scheme. Oil is ABSENT from the config rather than zeroed: rewardHurdle returns null, the customer table is empty rather than hurdle-less, and every card reads “no reward on this book”. That guard is load bearing, because the old arithmetic was H - (rev % H) and rev % null is NaN, which formats as RM NaN at three call sites.

IT APPLIES TO THE WHOLE WINDOW SINCE 10 AUG, ON HIS RULING, AND IT COSTS ONE PARTY. CK4-SEN stood at RM 945 against the old RM 940 and had a quarter unit showing; at RM 975 they are RM 30 short and it is gone, and they drop off the waiting line. CM4-MK, CJ4-BJ and CE4-CHE keep theirs. Put to him with those figures before anything was built, and taken deliberately rather than discovered afterwards. A scaled award now says why it is scaled: the row carries the units bought against the minimum, because a crossed hurdle paying a fraction was otherwise unaccountable to the person reading it.

PROVED ON THE THREE PATHS, BECAUSE THE LIVE BOOK EXERCISES ONE. Every party who currently clears RM 975 also bought over 12.5 unit, so the short path and the oil path have no live example and would go untested by anything read off the desk; all three are forced through the master's own functions in jsdom. Twenty-seven assertions, eleven mutations, each reddening its own. One instrument could not fail and was rewritten: rd() round-trips through JSON and JSON.stringify(NaN) is the string “null”, so the assertion written to catch NaN was equally true of null and stayed GREEN with the guard removed. It asks inside the window now, and carries a control that proves the probe tells the two apart.

t: ONE UNIT TO CN6-WM AT RM130, PAID AND COLLECTED THE SAME DAY, BOOKED AS AN R2 DOWNSELL
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SINGLE UNIT OF SALT OUT THE DOOR. The fold takes a SELL to CN6-WM, 1 unit for RM130 dated 11 Sep, RM130 cash in and 1 unit collected on the day, so the row closes on both legs. The rate clears the RM56.21 floor for 1 unit, sits above the RM120 ask and under the RM150 ceiling. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, so nothing was restated.

THE FLAGS AND WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. The drafter flagged the R2 booking with downstream CN6-WM-R, so CN6-WM takes no statement from this row, and the rate at 30% above the RM100 the drafter cites. CN6-WM's own history answers the rate: a median of RM110 in a range of RM75 to RM110. RM110 stays outstanding from the advance of 30 Aug, with 1 unit on credit against a cap of 2.

t: FIVE UNITS TO CR3-DAM AT RM90 A UNIT, PAID AND COLLECTED THE SAME DAY, BOOKED AS AN R2 DOWNSELL
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL DATED 10 SEP. SELL to CR3-DAM, 5 unit for RM450, RM450 cash in and 5 unit collected on 10 Sep, so nothing stays open on the goods. The total clears the RM281.07 floor for 5 unit, falls short of the RM500 ask and sits well under the RM710 ceiling. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, RM220 on the order, so no separate cost line was needed on the row.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL AND WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. The drafter flagged the booking as an R2 downsell through CR3-DAM-R, so CR3-DAM is not the counterparty on this row and takes no statement from it, and flagged the rate at 12.5% above the party's usual RM90 against a median of RM80. The figures answer both: RM90 a unit sits inside the recorded range of RM80 to RM92.50. The RM25 outstanding from s136 is untouched and stays open.

t: ONE UNIT OUT TO A NEW CODE AT RM100, PAID AND COLLECTED SAME DAY, ROSTER FLAG ANSWERED
n: FOLDED THIS PASS: a single salt sell dated 10 Sep, 1 unit to CB7-TBC for RM100, cash in full and goods collected on the day, referred by CI4-OKR on stream R3. It appends to sales with its note and leaves nothing open. The rate clears the RM56.21 floor for 1 unit, sits under the RM120 ask and well under the RM150 ceiling, so the desk took the order below ask on his word.

UNUSUAL, AND WHAT THE INVENTORY DID: the drafter flagged CB7-TBC as absent from the roster and wanting a code and a directory entry; the party record now carries the code and shows on roster, with no prior orders, no median rate, no range, nothing outstanding and nothing on credit against a cap of 1. Cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, so no override was written. Stated stock stays at 40.25 unit, with counts on 8 Sep for salt and 9 Sep for oil.

t: ONE CODE ONTO THE ROSTER, NO FIGURE MOVED, AND THE DIRECTORY STAYS AT THE LAPTOP
n: FOLDED: A SINGLE ROSTER LINE. The batch is one row, dated 10 Sep and decided at the desk: CB7-TBC is appended to the roster as a customer buying direct, with no parent above it and no note carried on the row. There is no order, no rate and no unit behind it, so no floor, no ask and no cost enter the book. The row was folded as drafted with no flag raised against it.

UNUSUAL: A CODE WITHOUT A TRADE. A registration is the one row that answers no floor and no ask, so nothing was checked against the desk's own terms and no history, median or range exists under the code yet. The directory is untouched, as the drafter set out: the name and the place are typed at the laptop and never travel with the ledger. Only the code stands here.

THE INVENTORY DID NOTHING. Stock stays as stated at 40.25 unit, cost basis holds at RM44 a unit against a replacement of RM46, the reorder mark stays at 15 and 8.5 unit stay promised with nothing owed out. Counts stand where they were, salt on 8 Sep and oil on 9 Sep. The two loans in remain open, 5.5 unit from CH5-OUG and 1.5 unit from CA11-SEN, both dated 8 Sep.

t: ONE CORRECTION ON THE BOOKS: THE RM25 ON S136 SETTLED IN CASH AND MARKED THE FIRST ASSOCIATE SALE
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A CORRECTION AND NOTHING ELSE. The fold carries a single amendment against CR3-DAM's salt order of 2 unit for RM185 dated 07 Sep, s136. It sets settledRM to 25, settledKg to 0 and settle to First associate sale, recorded 11 Sep. No cash and no stock move on the fold: the row changes only what it says about itself, and the row text is not rewritten here.

WHAT WAS UNUSUAL AND WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. The drafter flagged the rate at RM92.50 a unit, 15.6 per cent above CR3-DAM's usual RM80 across 12 orders, and flagged the advance of 2 unit against his credit. The settlement figures answer the second flag and the rate stands as recorded. Inventory holds at 40.25 unit on the salt count of 08 Sep, cost basis unchanged at RM44 a unit, nothing owed out and 8.5 unit promised.

t: A RAIL HEADING IS TOLD FROM A DESTINATION, AND POSITION AND TRADING BECOME CURRENT
n: HIS REPORT, 11 SEP 2026: nothing in the rail said which rows you could tap. He was right, and the measurement is blunt. .grouplbl and .tab were the mono face, uppercase, weight 500 and the same colour, --salt-mist for both, separated by 1.5px of size and a little tracking. Uppercase mono at wide tracking is this desk's LABEL signature, worn by .kick, .plbl, .dhname, the identity's eyebrow and every table head, so the tab wearing it was the confusion itself. A heading shouts; a destination is named.

FOUR AXES CARRY IT, BECAUSE RELYING ON ONE IS WHAT FAILED. CASE: the tabs and the rail's parts go sentence case, which TAB_LABEL and the markup already held, so no copy moved. SIZE: 9.5px against 13px, and 11px against 13.5px on the phone, where his floor of 26 Aug holds the heading at 11 and the destination clears it. COLOUR: the tab rises to --salt-mist-light at rest and salt when open, so the reachable row is the brighter of the two, which is the way round it was not. The heading is NOT dimmed to make the gap: mist on obsidian is 5.0:1 and small text under that fails, so the gap is made from above. POSITION: the heading sits flush at the rail's own padding on a --salt-line hairline running out to the edge, and nothing clickable on this desk sits on a line. The first cut drew that rule in --salt-line-faint, white 6%, and 97px of it could not be seen on this ground.

PRODUCT WAS THE ONE HEADING THAT KEPT THE OLD COSTUME, AND IT READ AS A HEADING ONLY BECAUSE SALT AND OIL ARE BORDERED PILLS, which is the accident this whole fix is about. One rule states the heading once and covers it. The switcher was also the rail's second alignment, inset 10px and 156px wide against every group's 176, and joins the column. The rail takes 12px, 200 to 212, because Orders and money measures 124px at 13px against 117px of text room and wrapped: the type is half of what separates a destination from a heading, so the type is not what gives way.

AND THE PHONE'S DRAWER HAS BEEN THE WRONG WIDTH SINCE v472, FOUND WHILE WIDENING THE RAIL. design/desk.css is a last-wins layer appended after the older CSS, so its bare .rail{width:200px} beat v371's width:min(272px,100vw - 28px) earlier in the file at the same specificity: a media query adds none. The drawer has been 200px instead of 268 for nine days. The width is scoped to min-width:861px and the material stays at every width; measured at 375px, the drawer is 268 again. Any width, position or display this layer sets on a class the narrow breakpoints also style needs the same guard.

HIS SECOND INSTRUCTION: POSITION AND TRADING ARE ONE GROUP, CURRENT. It holds Order book, Stock and Pricing. Naming and directory only, and the ids are untouched, so every /desk#tab address still lands: #receivables, #sourcing and #pricing were each opened and read back off the running desk. VIEWS[].name is read by nothing today and carries the same three names anyway, because a second hand-kept copy of a label is how the projects list drifted. Two things stand for his decision: Stock contradicts hard rule 5, which says inventory and never stock in copy, so that rule now describes a desk that is gone; and the Order book tab's lead part is also called Order book.

PROVED RED BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS TRUSTED. Twenty-two assertions over the layer and the markup, and every one was mutated first: ten faults put back, the uppercase tab, the shared colour, the 1.5px step, the faint hairline, PRODUCT leaving the shared rule, an indented heading, the width back in the unscoped .rail, Position and Trading returning, VIEWS keeping the old names, and a rename taking an id with it. Each reddened its own assertion and none stayed green. Colour and type are read out of design/desk.css under hard rule 6, the directory out of the master. No figure moved, no row was folded, and the book is exactly as v570 left it.

t: AN ASSOCIATE IS APPOINTED FROM THE ENTER TAB, AND CR3-DAM IS THE FIRST
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 11 SEP 2026: elevate CR3-DAM as an Associate, and he could not do it himself from the Enter tab. He was right, and the reason was worse than a missing form. Add ID has offered Associate, resells for you (R2) since v343 and the option did NOTHING: the payload carried the stream, the drafter wrote a roster row, and the fold appended the bare code and stopped. A party registered as an associate never reached associates, which is the only list associateIds() reads for an appointment, so the Workbench's picker, the network bench, the credit cap and the move off the customer reward table all hung off a list the form never wrote to. The Kind was a label over an act nobody performed.

AND THERE WAS NO ROAD AT ALL FOR A CODE ALREADY ON THE ROSTER, which is the ordinary case: a party is registered when they first buy and appointed when he decides, months apart. The pane refused any known code as a duplicate. It now refuses the two that really are duplicates, a plain registration of a known code and appointing an associate twice, and takes the appointment as the ordinary road. An elevation asks for no name and hides the Name and Place cells, because the party is already in the vault and asking again invites a second spelling of a name already filed.

THE -R ACCOUNT IS MINTED WITH THE APPOINTMENT. R2 books the row TO the associate and the desk fills <CODE>-R where no end buyer is named, so an associate without that account has every R2 sale refused at the gate as a code not on the roster. The fold appends it with the appointment rather than leaving a second act to remember. A referrer is appointed without one: R3 leaves the buyer on the row and never books to an -R. Which Kind appoints is ADDID_APPOINTS in engine/position.mjs, beside CORRECTABLE and for the same reason: the pane, the drafter and the fold all read it, and a table in three places is a table that will differ.

CR3-DAM IS THE FIRST, AND THE BENCH RANKS THEM FOURTH ON ARRIVAL. They joined on 29 Jun and have bought on 12 orders since, 13 unit for RM 1,080 with RM 25 outstanding, the steadiest run of repeat buying on this book. Read off the desk rather than asserted: rank #4, ahead of CE4-AD at RM 835 and CI4-OKR at RM 655, because rank is contribution and their own buying is the larger figure; no stars, since the star reads resale and referral as a share of all revenue and both are nil, so the first is earned rather than granted; the salt credit cap goes to 2 unit from 1. They leave the customer reward table for their own card, and RM 585 of own buying at 41.4% since the scheme was adopted has earned nothing under either reading, so the move costs them nothing. What they buy for themselves keeps the RM 940 customer hurdle; what they now bring in hurdles at RM 470.

TWO FAULTS FOUND IN PASSING, BOTH IN THE LINE BEING REWRITTEN. The Add ID branch of wbRecord wrote its success line to the status node captured BEFORE render() rebuilt the tab, so the node was detached and a registration has confirmed itself silently since v343; the named road has re-fetched it since v528 and the common tail always did, and this branch returned early and was the one that missed it. And the lead read as a Associate, and on another kind as a An associate's end buyer: the labels are whole phrases, so no article fits and one cannot be picked from the first letter either. The colon drops it, which is the shape the queue's own line has used all along.

PROVED, AND ONE INSTRUMENT REWRITTEN WHEN IT WOULD NOT GO RED. Thirty-nine assertions over the fold, the drafter and the pane on the real master, each mutated first: reverting the plan's refusal reddens seven, reverting the pane's gate reddens the elevation road, and removing the apply's guard reddens two taps appointing one code in a single batch. That last assertion first claimed idempotence on a re-run and stayed GREEN with the guard removed, because apply() re-plans and the plan refuses a second fold outright; what the guard actually covers is a duplicate the plan cannot see, since it does not mutate the book as it walks its items. Four assertions had used CR3-DAM as their example of a roster code that is NOT an associate, which this same version made false: they are re-keyed onto synthetic codes forced onto the running desk. ledger/ledger.json is generated from the running desk and a book change leaves it stale, so it is regenerated here.

t: CA7-JTR s140 SAYS RM430 THROUGHOUT, AND THE RM20 OVERPAYMENT IT REPORTED NEVER EXISTED
n: HIS RULING, 10 SEP 2026: “On the CA7-JTR s140, it is a correction in the agreed order, 50 unit oil to 430 instead of 450, paid and delivered.” So RM430 is the agreed figure and RM430 is what moved. The row already STORED that — total 430, cash 430, delivered 50, nothing outstanding — and three things inside it still said the opposite.

THE TRAIL SAID RM450 AND THE ROW SAID RM430. The 09 Sep Fulfilment step recorded the then-agreed RM450 settling the order; the 10 Sep Correction restated the total and the row’s cash to RM430 and left the step alone, so the three steps summed to RM450 against a stored RM430. On his ruling the step is the figure that was wrong, so it is restated to RM430 and the trail now adds to the row: 0 + 430 + 0 = 430. Nothing else about the row moves.

AND THE ROW WAS REPORTING A REFUND IT DID NOT OWE. Its own note read “RM450 already paid stands RM20 above it” and “the trail of two steps no longer adds to the total and the overpayment stays outstanding”, in the row note and again in the Correction note, four passages in all. That RM20 was the gap between a corrected total and an uncorrected trail step, not money anyone had handed over: there is no CA7-JTR row in customerRefunds and there never was, so the desk was describing an outstanding refund that no surface could act on and no figure carried. The passages are replaced rather than deleted, so the row still records what the correction did and still says plainly that RM430 sits RM6.43 under the RM436.43 floor — a stated price under break-even, quoted as such under v552.

WHAT IS NOT CHANGED. The mod line still reads “cash 450 to 430”, because that is exactly what the correction did to the ROW and rewriting it would erase the correction’s own record. No other row is touched, no count moves, no price moves: this is one figure and four sentences on one row, on his word.

ONE LINE OF THE BOOK, AND THE BOOK’S OWN WRITER WROTE IT. Worth recording because the first attempt used JSON.stringify(book,null,1) and produced a 3,784-line diff on a one-figure change: ledger/book.json keeps one row per line and writeBookFile in booksync.mjs is what preserves that. Re-serialising a ledger is not a formatting preference; it destroys the reviewable diff that is the whole defence against a bad fold.

t: WHAT A UNIT COSTS AND HOW A PRICE IS BUILT ARE ONE PART, AND THE STACK IS PRINTED ONCE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 10 SEP 2026: “What a unit costs and how pricing works should be one and the same, repetitive and lengthy prose is useless, and as always, if it doesn’t add value - it is definitely out.” He had sent two screenshots, one of each part, asking what the repetition was.

THE SECOND PART’S LOWER TABLE WAS THIS ONE MULTIPLIED BY A QUANTITY. Goods was the pricing basis over q, Delivery was the same delivery already charged in the stack above, and Cost to serve was their sum: one arithmetic, printed twice, a screen apart, under two headings. What only the second part carried was the step from a cost to a PRICE, so that is what moved up: cogs, the markup, the ask, the cost to serve and the margin now sit under the stack that feeds them, and the stack is not restated. The basis simply carries into the price, which is the whole reason it is called the basis. The fold is deleted rather than renamed, and the suite asserts there is no second copy of it.

THE WORKED SIZE COMES OFF EACH BOOK’S OWN BOARD NOW, AND THE CONSTANT IT REPLACED WAS WRONG ON OIL. The retired fold was pinned at q=2 for both books. 2 unit is a printed salt size; oil’s board runs 10 to 50 unit, so oil’s worked example priced a lot that book never quotes, and the merged part would have called it “the size the board is read at”. It takes the middle rung of tierBoard() instead: salt works at 3.5 unit for RM 360 and oil at 30 unit for RM 330, each matching its own board to the ringgit. Caught by RENDERING oil and reading the row back; the constant looks perfectly reasonable sitting in the file, and salt is green either way, which is why the assertion drives both books.

AND THE PROSE WENT WITH IT. Two paragraphs explaining the bridge between two tables are not needed when there is one table: the sentence that said the price has nothing else in it, and the closing paragraph restating what cogs and the cost to serve are, are gone. One sentence survives, because without it a reader sees a 1.012x markup beside a 45.2% margin and has no way to know they are struck on different things. Each book’s part now carries two short lines where it carried four long ones.

ONE ASSERTION WAS RETIRED AND FOUR REPLACED IT. v567’s check that Goods named the landed figure and the grossed one was checking a row this release deletes; the claim underneath it is kept and made structural instead — the two figures differ, each is named in its own row, and the word landed never attaches to the post-leak one. Beside them: the price build is inside the cost part, the old fold is gone, and the worked size is on the board. The board-size pair was proved red by pinning q=2 again, which reddens oil and leaves salt green, exactly as the fault did.

ALSO FIXED, AND IT WENT RED ON THE CLOCK RATHER THAN ON THE CODE. The CA4-DAM credit block asserted the cap AND that nothing but /^Credit/ rules fired. Overnight the receivable aged into Aged receivable, which is not a Credit rule, and the suite failed with nothing about the book or the code changed. Its own comment records the same thing happening on 07 Sep, when the fix was to WIDEN the tail clause rather than remove it. The block’s stated point is where the breach is NAMED, so it asks for the cap and stops policing what else a living, ageing receivable trips. An assertion that has to be re-widened every time the calendar moves is measuring the calendar.

NO PRICE MOVES AND NO LEDGER ROW CHANGES. Every figure on the merged part is the same call the board makes; nothing here prices anything, which is hard rule 1. The suite goes 1832 to 1839 over 119 sections.

t: THE TABLES STOP READING BLACK, THE FLOOR IS DRAWN ONCE, AND THE RATE ACTUALLY PAID IS DRAWN AT ALL
n: HIS REPORT, 10 SEP 2026, ON THREE SCREENSHOTS OF THE PRICE VIEW: “Still a lot of blackened table cells”, “floor and eff. cost being the same”, and a picture of an empty chart. Three faults, all of them on the surface he looks at most, and all three had been shipped by the two versions before this one.

218 CELLS ON THE PRICE VIEW ALONE WERE PAINTING NEAR-BLACK, AND THE TOKEN'S OWN COMMENT SAYS WHY. --salt-veil is rgba(5,8,10,.86) and the identity documents it as the fill for “sticky and floating surfaces over content”, which is exactly right for .menu, a menu that does float over the page. design/desk.css also handed it to thead th and to th.l,td.l, which are every table head and every label column on the desk and which sit INSIDE a card the aurora lights warm. A cold near-black slab in a warm card is what he was seeing, and it was the HUE rather than the weight: measured on the live desk, 218 cells under a luminance of 12 on that view, 0 after. THE FIRST CUT OF THIS FIX THINNED THEM TO .62 SO THE CARD WOULD SHOW THROUGH, AND HE CAUGHT IT BEFORE IT SHIPPED, on the earnings table, with the ORDERS column legible straight through the band labels; it had also dropped the backdrop blur thead th relies on, so 38 per cent of whatever scrolled under came through. Ghosting is arithmetic and not a matter of taste: a sticky fill at alpha a passes (1-a) of what is behind it, the .86 this replaced was already passing a readable 14 per cent, and 1 is the only value that cannot ghost. These tables scroll sideways, so rows really do pass under that column. The warmth fixes what he reported; the opacity keeps the fix from costing something else, and the assertion pins alpha at 1 rather than at some defensible-sounding number in between. --panel had been declared in the design layer since v472 and read by nothing at all, so the name was free and now carries the warm value.

THE FLOOR WAS DRAWN TWICE, AND v566 IS THE VERSION THAT SAID IT HAD STOPPED DOING THAT. That release swept a duplicate floorTotal(q,null,{collects:true}) series off the board chart and left its twin standing one line below: floor drew r.floor/r.q while effective cost drew c.eff flat, and v552 made effective cost, break-even and the floor one number. Measured live on both books at every printed size, the gap is RM0.01 on salt, a rounding artefact at 0.5 and 2 unit, and RM0.00 on oil. So the chart drew a second dashed line on top of the first and gave it a different name in the legend, which is the fault v566 was fixing. Sweeping the class before shipping the fix is the rule of 31 Aug and it was not swept. One line now, named for all three things it is, as the board's own column has been since v552.

THE RATE ACTUALLY PAID PLOTTED NOTHING, AND THE CAUSE WAS ONE MISSING WORD. Every dataset on that chart declares its own type, so the config carried no root type — and Chart.js then takes its SCALE defaults from the first dataset's controller, which is scatter, whose x scale is linear. Every x on this chart is a date STRING, which a linear scale cannot place, so the points were dropped in silence, labels was ignored and the axis collapsed to an empty 0 to 1. Measured before the fix: 116 salt points across three bands and 8 oil points, all present in the datasets and none of them drawn; after, 281 point objects positioned inside the chart area, none outside, none unplaced. The shape chart above passes type:'line' and was never affected, which is why only this one was blank. A dataset's own type still decides how it DRAWS, so the scatters stay scatters and the ask lines stay lines.

AND ONE WORD WAS DOING DUTY FOR TWO FIGURES SIX LINES APART. In How a price is built, Cogs reads “RM 46.72 landed” and Goods read “RM 56.21 landed and grossed for samples”. Only the first of those is landed; RM 56.21 is the landed figure after the leak is charged, which is the whole step between the two tables on that panel. It now names both figures and the step between them.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH. No price moves, no floor moves and no ledger row changes: three of the four are a stylesheet and a chart config, and the fourth is a caption. The suite stands at 1802 assertions over 118 sections, unchanged and green, and the three fixes were each measured on the running desk rather than read out of the source, which is the only way any of them could have been seen in the first place.

t: THE BOARD SAYS WHEN THE CHEAPER TIER IS NOT THE CHEAPER ONE, AND FIVE INSTRUMENTS LEARN TO FAIL
n: THE ONE RELATION BETWEEN THE TWO TIERS WAS MEASURED BY NOTHING. v564 walks Tier 1 against the rate law and against the floor, and against nothing else, so no surface knew whether the cheaper tier was still the cheaper one. It need not be: Tier 2 is DERIVED from a floor that moves with the cost of salt, while his two Tier 1 ends are figures he typed and do not move at all. A price stated at 5 unit, or a fall in the lot rate to about RM40 a unit against today’s RM46, walks Tier 2 down through a frozen Tier 1 from the small end up. The board then prints cheaper to the right under columns ordered cheapest-first, which is the one arrangement v247 says a board may not have. over now measures it in the engine beside under, ringgit by ringgit; the row carries a Tier 1 above Tier 2 tag, the census names every affected size and the gap, and the all-clear sentence requires BOTH tiers to clear break-even AND Tier 1 to be under Tier 2. Forced with a stated RM350 at 5 unit: three sizes inverted, three rows tagged, one sentence, no all-clear. It does not clamp. Clamping would make a second place that prices, which is what hard rule 1 exists to forbid, and a price he has stated is quoted anyway (v552).

TWO GATES STOOD ON ONE FACT AND THEY DISAGREED. ladderRow asked whether P.tier1 was truthy; priceLadder asked tier1Anchors, which needs two usable anchors. A book stating ONE end satisfied the second and not the first, so the payload carried a row named “Tier 1” whose every price was null, beside a desk saying the tier is not stated on this book. One gate now, the stricter one. And two keys naming ONE size ({0.5:60,"0.50":60}) passed the length check, landed hi===lo, and made the exponent Math.log(1)/Math.log(1), which is NaN: every rung priced NaN while reading TRUTHY at every guard downstream. A tier stated at one size is not stated.

OIL’S CHART SAID TIER 2 ON A BOOK WITH ONE TIER. The series label was hardcoded while every other tier-facing string on that view is conditional, so oil carried a legend reading “Tier 2 ask” three inches under its own table head reading “Ask”. One flag now, computed once, read by the label and by the Tier 1 series alike.

AND THE BOARD CHART DREW ITS FLOOR TWICE. A second series drew floorTotal(q,null,{collects:true}) beside the floor, on the belief that the two were one delivery apart. v502 made one floor per size and floorTotal ignores the collects option: measured at every printed size on both books, the two arrays are identical, max gap RM0.00. So the chart has been drawing a second dashed line exactly on top of the first and labelling it as a different thing, under a caption explaining a RM20 gap that stopped existing a week ago. The series is gone and the caption says what is drawn.

FIVE INSTRUMENTS LEARNED TO FAIL, AND EVERY ONE WAS PROVED RED BEFORE ITS GREEN WAS TRUSTED. “Tier 2 does not move” was pinned to RM70 and RM1,150, figures this book DERIVES, so an ordinary lot landing turned it red while proving nothing; it now asserts the ask is identical with tier1 in the policy and with it stripped out, which is the actual claim and does not care what salt costs. Nothing read a body cell against the column above it, so the two tier cells could be swapped and every tier assertion stayed green while the board quoted the wrong tier. “Tier 1’s rate never rises” could not fail on a falling pair, so a RISING pair is now forced and the law is watched dragging every interpolated rung back, with his two stated ends printing verbatim through it. And the desk’s pbAdjusted and tools/pricelist.mjs adjustedPrice, one rule written twice, had never been compared directly at all: 416 grid points, exact agreement. Eight mutations, eight reds, the board’s proved against the shipped v565 master itself rather than against a hand-made stub.

t: THE PEN'S ACTIONS STOP BEING CUT OFF BY THE ENTRY THEY BELONG TO
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026: “Better design maybe tapping the edit button, 4-5 button will appear floating from the edit button, for the 4-5 most probable action.” What he photographed was one box reading PAID IN FULL, and the menu was not the fault. v547 appended it INSIDE the entry’s card and .lcard carries overflow:hidden. Measured in a real browser at 1280: a folded entry is 72px and the menu was 144px, so one item of three was painted. Worse, the two that were not painted were still in the layout: a hit test at the centre of MODIFICATION reached the .lstate of the entry BELOW, so the control did the wrong thing rather than nothing. jsdom could not have found this and did not; it does no layout.

SO THE FAN LEAVES THE CARD. It is position:fixed at the pen’s own coordinates, thrown above the pen where it would run off the bottom, and closed on a scroll, because a fixed element cannot follow the pen that opened it. Each action is its own pill with its own ground, so four or five of them read as four or five buttons rather than as one block of rows. Measured after, at 1280 and at 375: every action reachable by hit test, 44px in both dimensions, nothing off screen, nothing overflowing sideways, and the flip proved on the last entry of the ledger at both widths.

RANKED ON HIS OWN BOOK RATHER THAN ON A GUESS. Of 117 settled sales, 101 closed with the cash and the goods on the same date, so Completed leads wherever both are outstanding; of 27 open sales, 18 owe cash alone, so Paid in full leads where they do not. Four are drawn and More is always the fifth. On the order he is most likely to tap the pen on it is five: Completed, Paid in full, Delivered in full, Back to pending, More. On a settled row it is three, because a settled row has three real actions and a button the fold would refuse is not an action. Every item is still a chip the editor already offers, on the editor’s own conditions, with updSet filling the outstanding figures, so a tap still cannot overpay.

THE PEN ITSELF WAS HALF THE TAP CONTRACT. Hit-tested at 22px by 22px, with no pseudo hit area, on the one control that opens all of this and the one he reaches for on a phone. It carries a 44px hit area now. That takes the entry’s top right corner, so a tap there opens the fan where it used to expand the trail; the rest of the entry still expands it, and the fan is what that corner is for.

AND THE ENTRY ANIMATION WAS WRITTEN, MEASURED AND REMOVED. The pills fanned out of the pen on a staggered keyframe from opacity 0 and scale .7, with animation-fill-mode:backwards. In a real browser whose animation timeline does not advance, the animation sits at currentTime 0 with playState:“running”, so backwards holds the FROM state and every pill is invisible and 30.8px tall while still answering a hit test. A control that can be invisible and under the tap contract is worse than a control that does not move, and the fan reads as a fan because it is separate buttons, not because of 170 milliseconds. Eight assertions, each proved RED before its green was trusted: by putting the menu back inside the card, by giving the container the ground back, by moving More off the end, by dropping its class, by restoring the v547 list of three, by deleting the pen’s hit area, by making the close a no-op, and by putting the keyframes back.

t: TWO TIERS ON THE BOARD, THE SUGGESTED PRICE TO THE NEAREST FIVE, AND THE SHEET SAVES AS JPG AND PDF WITH A QR
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 10 SEP 2026: “I want to have a 2 tier rate. The current one shown on the board is Tier 2. For Tier 1, the 0.5 unit is 60 while the 12.5 unit is 875.” So the board carries two levels. Tier 2 is the board that was there and not one of its figures moves, at any size, on either book: it is still what priceLadder().ask returns, still what the customer price list is drawn toward, still what the drafter measures a row against, and still row zero of the payload the phone and the D1 mirror read. Tier 1 is new and sits under it: RM 60, 110, 150, 200, 230, 270, 310, 340, 380, 410, 500 and 875 against Tier 2’s RM 70 to RM 1,150. Said as rates, RM 120 a unit falling to RM 70 against RM 140 falling to RM 92, so Tier 1 is 86 per cent of the ask at half a unit and 76 per cent of it at twelve and a half. Every rung clears break-even, from 2.13x at half a unit to 1.25x at twelve and a half, so nothing on either tier is quoted at a loss.

TIER 1 IS STATED AT ITS ENDS AND INTERPOLATED BETWEEN THEM, AND THE DERIVED ROAD WAS TRIED FIRST. The ask is a margin on the floor tapered at the supplier’s own exponent (v504), which is ONE number to set: a level pinned at 2.5 unit. His two ends are two numbers, and they do not fit on that shape. Measured, his pair implies a taper of -0.167 against the supplier’s -0.121, which is the whole point of a relationship price and not something a level can absorb; solved as a margin curve it wants an anchor of 0.324 and a taper of -0.308, and the clamps then bite. Worse, RM 875 is not a multiple of ten and the house rounding is up to the ten, so no derived curve can ever print the figure he gave; it would print RM 880. So the two ends are taken verbatim and only the sizes between them are rounded, which is the rule the retired tier board used and the only one that can be honest about a number he typed. Between them the RATE is interpolated in the log of size, the desk’s own method, and outside them it is clamped rather than extrapolated. Tier 1 obeys the same two laws as the ask: the rate never rises with size, and the gap to break-even is named in under rather than hidden.

OIL HAS ONE TIER AND THE BOARD SAYS SO. Its five prices are already his own stated ones and its 50 unit rung earns 3 per cent, so there is nothing for a second tier to sit under, and he has stated no ends for it. LADDER_BY.oil therefore carries tier1:null as an ENTRY rather than an omission: ladderFor spreads LADDER underneath, so leaving it out would hand oil salt’s anchors, clamp every oil size to 12.5, land the rate at RM 70 a unit and quote RM 700 for ten units of oil that Tier 2 sells at RM 130. The suite asserts oil is handed none, and the board head reads Ask on a one-tier book and Tier 2 on a two-tier one.

THE MARKUP COLUMN MOVED INTO THE ASKS RATHER THAN BEING DROPPED OR DOUBLED. v554’s rule stands: the multiple must say what it is OF, or 2.49x reads as +249 per cent. What could not stand is one Markup column beside TWO asks, which has to pick a tier and then silently describes one of them while sitting level with both. Each tier cell now carries its own total, rate, margin on price and multiple of effective cost, four lines, and the board stays at five columns because it gets 325px of a 375px screen. The “collect only” tag went with it, and it had been unreachable since v502: that release made one floor per size and the suite asserts collecting and delivering give the same figure to the ringgit, so the tag’s own condition has been impossible for a fortnight. The row now flags a price under break-even, on either tier, and names which.

HIS SECOND INSTRUCTION: THE SUGGESTED PRICE PER CUSTOMER ROUNDS TO THE NEAREST FIVE. It was the whole ringgit UP, which put figures like RM 97 and RM 416 on a sheet handed to a customer while the board beside it quotes in tens. NEAREST, not up: the four drawing rules that pull a customer’s own rate toward the board already decide the direction, and rounding had no business deciding it again. The floor is the one thing rounding may not cross: nearest-five can land up to RM 2.50 under break-even, so a price that does is lifted to the first five above the floor. The cap is not re-clamped, because it is a drawing target at three times COGS and not a refusal line. One rule, two places, and the suite holds tools/pricelist.mjs and the desk’s pbAdjusted together as it always has. Measured over all 39 parties on the roster: every price on every sheet is a multiple of five and not one is under its floor.

HIS THIRD INSTRUCTION: THE BOARD SHEET SAVES AS HTML, PDF AND JPG, WITH THE LOGO AND THE NUMBERS ONLY, THEN THE USERNAME AND A QR TO THE WEBSITE. HTML was already there. The image was a PNG and is now a JPG, which every message app and phone gallery takes without asking. The PDF is written out here, one A4 page embedding the same JPEG as a DCTDecode image, so paper, file and message are one rendering and cannot drift; no library, for the reason hard rule 4 exists and the reason engine/qr.mjs is written out rather than installed. And the username has moved below the numbers, with the QR after it, which is the order he gave; v538’s rule that there are no words at all on the sheet is not withdrawn and still holds.

ONE QR ENCODER, INLINED LIKE THE PRICING ENGINE. tools/qr.mjs was a build-time module for the statements; the desk needs the same encoder at runtime, and a second copy would drift exactly as two pricing engines would. It is now engine/qr.mjs, inlined into the master by tools/engine.mjs --sync beside pricing and position, with CI failing if the block is not the module to the byte. It draws rectangles, never a path and never a stroke, because the sheet goes to print, to a PDF and to a phone’s share sheet rather than only to a browser. The site’s address is never in this file: /desk is public by his decision of 11 Aug and the statements site is deliberately on its own cryptic name, so the address travels the keyed road the usernames already travel, written to the desk’s store by the publish and handed back by GET /stmt-users. No address means no QR, said on the card, because a printed code that opens nothing is worse than no code.

MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, NOT IN jsdom, BECAUSE jsdom HAS NO CANVAS. The QR was drawn on the canvas and then read back module by module against the encoder: 1,089 modules, none wrong, and the quiet zone light at every one of 344 samples round its edge. The JPEG carries its start and end markers. The PDF opens %PDF-1.4, ends %%EOF, and every one of its five xref offsets lands exactly on its own object, which is the whole difficulty of writing one by hand. With no address the sheet still renders and the PDF is still made, with no QR block at all. Four new suite assertions were each proved RED before their green was trusted, by moving the 12.5 anchor onto a ten, by removing oil’s tier1:null, by putting Tier 1 at row zero and by pricing Tier 1 above Tier 2.

t: CLEAR IS THE GHOST, NOT THE PILL: THE FILTER STOPS ANNOUNCING ITSELF
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 10 SEP 2026, ON THE LEDGER FILTER. v561 made the bar compact and the geometry was right: 44px on one row at 1280, 148px and two controls to a row at 375, every control 44px in both directions. What it left alone was weight. Clear was the only filled element in the bar, and on a bar he had just called not the main function of the ledger, the eye landed on it first.

THE DESIGN LAYER HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE ANSWER. Section 7 of design/desk.css says it in one line: the pill books or produces, everything else is a ghost. .vbtn is the booking pill. Clear books nothing, produces nothing and undoes a filter, so it was wearing the wrong component, not the wrong colour. No new CSS was written and no hex was added: it takes .ubtn, the secondary action Record plan, Undo last and Review in Transaction already wear, which carries the same --tap minimum. The other 28 .vbtn buttons on the desk are untouched.

MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, BOTH WAYS. Before: linear-gradient(135deg,#c5a059,#b87333), obsidian text at weight 700, a brass glow, 78 by 44. After: no background image, no shadow, brass text at weight 500 inside a 50 per cent brass outline, 58 by 44, still over the tap floor. A census of the bar named Clear as the only glowing element and the only gradient on the old build, and nothing glows on the new one; the four selects' gradients are their SVG arrows, not fills. The inline font-size:11px went with the pill, because the ghost rule already sets 11px.

THE BAR IS OTHERWISE EXACTLY WHERE v561 LEFT IT, 44px on one row at 924px wide, and the filter still does what it says: the search box keeps focus while typing, all four dropdowns filter, and Clear empties all five fields and removes itself. State “Pending” matches nothing today, which is correct rather than dead: engine/position.mjs returns it when nothing is paid and nothing delivered, and no row is in that state.

AND v562 WAS TAKEN WHILE THIS WAS BEING BUILT. The chain folded the CA7-JTR s140 correction from his phone and deployed it mid-flight. A fold that carries real rows owns its number, so this work was rebased onto v562 and renumbered. Nothing was lost either way.

t: CORRECTION ON CA7-JTR S140: TOTAL DOWN TO RM430, DELIVERED WITH RM15 CARRIAGE
n: ONE CORRECTION FOLDED, NO CASH AND NO STOCK MOVED. The desk applied the patch to CA7-JTR's oil row s140 of 08 Sep, 50 unit: total from RM450 to RM430, delivery from unset to RM15, cash from RM450 to RM430, handover from collected to delivered and cost from unset to RM350. The row is not rewritten, only its own terms restated, so the ledger position and the inventory both stand where they stood.

WHAT THE DRAFTER FLAGGED STAYS ON THE FACE OF THE ROW. The row carries a trail of two steps that no longer adds to the stated figure, RM450 was paid against a corrected total of RM430, and RM430 for the goods is RM6.43 under the floor of RM436.43. The typed RM350 becomes the cost every margin on this row is measured against, in place of the inventory's own rate. All four points are recorded, none is answered here.

t: THE LEDGER OPENS ON THE LEDGER, NOT ON ITS OWN FILTER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 10 SEP 2026: "Redesign this, to be more compact and functional, as this is not the main function of the ledger." The filter stood 273px tall on a 924px column, the search box and all four dropdowns each on a row of its own, so the first of 166 entries began 905px below the heading and the first thing the Ledger showed you was its own filter.

THE CAUSE WAS ONE RULE IN THE OLDER LAYER, AND NOT THE BAR AT ALL. A bare select{width:100%}, written for the stacked fields on the Enter view, catches every select on the desk. .ledbar has been a wrapping flex row since it was written; its controls were simply each as wide as the row. Measured in a real browser rather than read off the source, because this is layout and jsdom does none.

SO THEY WERE GIVEN A WIDTH, NOT A NEW BAR. The search grows, the four selects take their content and cap at 190px, the count and Clear sit at the right. On the desk the bar is 44px, one row, and the first entry moves up to 677px: 228px reclaimed. On a 375px phone it is 148px against 278px, two controls to a row instead of one, and every control still measures 44px in both directions, which is the tap contract.

IT STILL WRAPS, WHICH IS WHY THE CONTAINER WAS A WRAP FLEX ROW TO BEGIN WITH. Nothing overflows at 375px and no control shrinks below the tap size. The floating filter he offered as an alternative is not needed for this: the bar was never the wrong shape, only the wrong width.

t: SELL TO CE4-CHE: 2.5 UNIT AT RM230, PAID AND COLLECTED ON THE DAY
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A CLEAN SALT SELL. CE4-CHE takes 2.5 unit for RM230 on 10 Sep, RM230 goods with no delivery charge, cash in full and 2.5 unit collected the same day, so nothing stays open. The total sits above the RM140.53 floor for 2.5 unit but under the RM270 ask and the RM360 ceiling. The drafter raised no flag and the party carries nothing outstanding.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. The cost is the inventory's own RM44 a unit, RM110 on the order, and the drafter's RM120 has been set back to the desk's own rate. The salt count stands on 08 Sep and the 2.5 unit move is not shown landed, so the stated figure is untouched here. Two loans in remain open, and RM8.50 of promised units still sits ahead of the reorder mark at 15.

t: THE LEDGER FIGURES ARE ARRANGED RATHER THAN STACKED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 10 SEP 2026, ON A SCREENSHOT OF THE FIGURE COLUMN: "just arrange them nicely, not too packed." Nothing is removed. A live row carries up to four things in that one cell, and each was asked for and says something the others do not: what has been paid, what it is of, the margin, and what the figure was before a correction struck it.

WHAT WAS WRONG WAS THE SETTING, NOT THE CONTENT. A flex column at line-height 1.25 with no gap at all, so the three boxes sat at 0, 16 and 30 pixels: four separate facts read as one block of digits. Measured in a real browser rather than in jsdom, which does no layout.

THEY ARE GROUPED NOW, NOT MERELY SPREAD. Four candidates were measured in the live renderer: a flat 3px gap, a flat 4px, and two grouped settings. The one taken gives the figure its own clearance and sets the two notes tighter beneath it, 0, 21 and 38, so the cell reads as a figure with its notes rather than three lines of equal weight. It costs the same height as the flat 4px and reads better: 53px against 51, and 6px on the card.

AND A ROW WITH NO NOTES RESERVES NO ROOM FOR THEM. The first cut put the clearance on the figure unconditionally, so a plain row grew from 15px to 19px of empty cell for notes it does not have. The CSS pseudo-class for “only when something follows” is the whole of that condition. Three shapes proved in the browser: figure with margin and struck figure, figure with margin alone, and figure alone, the last back to exactly where it was.

THE QUANTITY COLUMN TAKES THE SAME TREATMENT, because it carries the same pair and the two sides of the row have to stay in step. The whole ledger grows 233px across 166 entries, about 1.4px an entry.

t: THE CONCENTRATION FIGURE HAD THREE READERS AND TWO RULES; NOW IT HAS ONE OF EACH
n: ONE FACT, THREE READERS, AND v557 SWEPT TWO OF THEM. The concentration figure is drawn in three places on the Sourcing tab: the Top supplier share KPI, the share cell in the table, and the sentence under it. v557 made the cell a watch and followed it with the sentence, and left the KPI four inches above both on the bare recentShare>80 rule. So Oil’s 84 per cent went on reading as an alarm on a book that has never lost a ringgit, on the same screen as the two that had just stopped saying it.

FOUND BY READING THE DEPLOYED BUILD, NOT THE DIFF. A verification pass over live v557 caught it, because the rendered tab is the one place all three readers are visible at once; the diff shows only what moved. The check that missed it sliced from the “Who you buy from” heading and so could only ever prove two of the three.

AND WIDENING THE CHECK FOUND A SECOND DISAGREEMENT, IN THE RULE ITSELF. The sentence alarmed when THIS BOOK had lost money, the cell and the KPI when THIS SUPPLIER had. On salt those differ: SA5-BTR holds 100 per cent with no default of its own, while SF6-KLC took RM750 in July. Both readings are defensible alone and cannot both stand on one screen. The narrower one wins: the alarm is about the name in front of him. The book’s history is not lost, it is stated in the sentence’s own words two clauses along, and it stops shouting a third time in a colour that is meant to be scarce.

THE CHECK NOW READS THE WHOLE TAB AND REQUIRES THE THREE TO AGREE, against the rule computed from that book’s own figures, so a fourth reader cannot be added quietly and neither can a fourth rule. Salt keeps one earned mark on the block, SF6-KLC’s 67 per cent received; oil keeps none.

t: A TRUE ALARM, AND IT IS SCARCE ENOUGH TO MEAN SOMETHING; THE DESK STOPS TELLING HIM TO CHASE A PARTY HE HAS WRITTEN OFF
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026: ADD A TRUE ALARM AND FIX THE THRESHOLDS. --crim and --rose both pointed at --salt-ember, the identity's third warm accent, so every warning on the desk was painted in a colour the headings also speak in: brass at hue 39, copper at 29, ember at 13, all on one dark ground. Measured rather than eyeballed. Ember sits dE 20.7 from copper, which is the collision he pointed at; the new alarm sits dE 32.5 from ember, 52.6 from copper and 68.7 from brass, at 5.6:1 on obsidian, so it clears small text as well.

IT IS A ONE-PLACE CHANGE, WHICH A PALETTE MOVE USUALLY IS NOT. The token lives in design/desk.css, the layer, because the vendored salt-ds.css is synced from Code\salt-ds and an edit there would be overwritten. --crim points at it and carries all 109 warnings with it; --rose keeps ember and has no reader at all. The chart series keep their literal #d4694c, because ember there is a SERIES colour and not a warning, so tokens.ts is untouched.

AND THE THRESHOLDS, WHICH ARE THE OTHER HALF OF WHAT MAKES AN ALARM AN ALARM. The supplier row lit four figures crimson and not one was a fault: 97 per cent landed of bought is a paid lot still to come, 100 per cent of a 30-day share is a supplier he chose, and 63 days quiet is a name that defaulted and is finished with. Quiet now needs a name he leaned on: over 30 days, no default, a quarter of the book or more. Concentration is brass, a watch, and takes the alarm only where that name has actually cost him something. A shortfall is a plain figure to 90 per cent and a colour below it.

THE SENTENCE UNDER THE TABLE WENT THE SAME WAY, which is the sweep rather than the fix: it was crimson on concentration alone, so Oil's 84 per cent read as an alarm on a book that has never lost a ringgit while the share figure four inches above it had just become a watch. Salt now carries two earned marks, SF6-KLC's 67 per cent and the concentration sentence that names the RM750; oil carries none, where the old thresholds lit two.

AND HIS WORD OF THE SAME DAY: CA4-DAM HAS DISAPPEARED. "No more contact. Just like SF6-KLC, I have lost contact with no way of recovering my losses." The Order book was telling him to CHASE FIRST a party he had already written off, on a row whose own note says the money will not come and whose ladder provision is 100 per cent. The book knew both ways: `defaulted` on the sale since 05 Sep, `writtenOff` on the supplier receivable since 31 Jul. The card read neither. Chase first now takes the oldest claim that can still be worked and, where none can be, says what became of the money instead of printing a dash. The claim list keeps the written-off rows, because gross owed is still gross owed; only the chase skips them.

PROVED AGAINST THE RULE, NOT A COUNT. The colour is asserted from the stylesheet with the same dE arithmetic that chose it. The thresholds are read off each rendered row against that row's own figures, so they hold whatever the book does next. And the alarm's scarcity is asserted as a rule: a book that has lost nothing may carry no alarm at all, which is what oil proves.

THIS WAS v555, THEN v556, BEFORE THE CLOUD GOT THERE TWICE. While it was being built, an approval on the phone dispatched the chain and the chain folded twice from his phone approvals and took both numbers: the CM4-MK sale as v555, then the fulfilment on SA5-BTR p021 as v556, each deployed and pushed. A fold that carries real rows owns its number; this work was rebuilt on top of both and renumbered again. Nothing was lost either way and no bad build ever reached the phone: update.mjs refused the push rather than forcing it, and .deployed.json still read v554 when the collision was found.

t: FULFILMENT ON SA5-BTR P021: THE LAST 12.5 UNIT IN, ORDER SETTLED
n: ONE FULFILMENT FOLDED, AND IT CLOSES A LOT. The remaining 12.5 unit of SA5-BTR's 50 unit lot p021, agreed 08 Sep at RM 2,200, moved on 09 Sep with no money attached, the RM 2,200 having been paid on 08 Sep. Against RM 0 and 12.5 unit outstanding, the move leaves RM 0 and 0 unit, so the drafter's flag that this settles the order in full is answered by the figures.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID. The row is not recomputed here: ovAmend in the master applies the fulfilment, so a fulfilment has one definition. The lot rate of RM 44 a unit matches the inventory's own RM 44 shelf cost, so the cost basis does not move and no cost override is carried on the row. SA5-BTR's RM 3,100 outstanding before this fold stands on the party's other rows, not on p021.

t: ONE SALT SELL TO CM4-MK: 2 UNIT AT RM220, HALF PAID AND DELIVERED
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A SALT SELL DATED 09 SEP. CM4-MK takes 2 unit for RM220, with RM220 of goods and delivery split as RM202 goods and RM18 delivery, RM110 cash in and 2 unit handed over the same day. The total meets the RM220 ask for 2 unit and clears the RM112.43 floor, well under the RM290 ceiling, and RM110 a unit is this party's own median. Costed at the inventory's own RM44 a unit, so RM88 attaches.

THE ADVANCE IS THE ONE THING TO WATCH. The drafter flagged the RM110 left unpaid against CM4-MK's credit cap of 1, and the dossier shows 2 unit going out on credit with nothing outstanding before and nothing defaulted, so the flag stands answered only in part. Nothing else moved: no lot landed, the cost basis holds at RM44 a unit with replacement at RM46, and the two loans in, CH5-OUG and CA11-SEN, are untouched.

t: THE BOARD'S MULTIPLE IS A MARKUP AND THE HEADING NOW SAYS SO
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026, ON A SCREENSHOT OF THE COLUMN: "Please correct them to markup then." The board's fourth column read Margin over 2.49x and 2.13x, and a multiple of cost is not a margin. On that same row the ask carries 60% margin, on price. One row, two arithmetics, one word.

THE HEADING IS MARKUP, AND IT SAYS WHAT THE MULTIPLE IS OF. A bare "Markup 2.49x" still misleads anyone who takes markup at its book meaning, where 2.49x would be plus 249 per cent; the figure is the ask as a multiple of effective cost, so the sub-label reads × eff. cost. The % margin under the ask is untouched, because that one was always a margin and always on price.

THE CLASS WAS SWEPT BEFORE THE FIX SHIPPED. Four columns on the desk are headed Margin. The customer reward table, the reward stream table and the Financials tier table all render a true percentage margin and are right as they stand; only the board's was a multiple. Checked rather than assumed, which is the rule the last three rounds were caught by.

AND THE HEADING IS ASSERTED NOW, NOT LEFT TO THE EYE. Five checks: the board draws, its fourth column is headed Markup, no column on it is headed Margin, the heading names its basis, and the true margin still sits under the ask. Copy that contradicts its own figures is the fault this desk keeps finding, so the copy is under test with the arithmetic.

t: OIL PRICES OFF THE BUY RATE PLUS 15 PER CENT, A PLACEHOLDER, AND THE LEAK STOPS CARRYING THE WHOLE BOARD
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026, AFTER ASKING WHY OIL'S EFFECTIVE COST WAS SO HIGH: "for oil, COGS is just the price to buy + 15%. That will be placeholder for now." The answer to the question was that the leak was almost all of it: goods RM7.59 and freight RM0.25 make a landed RM7.84, and a 23.08 per cent leak added RM1.81 to reach RM9.64, so 18.8 per cent of the effective cost was one drift figure.

AND THAT DRIFT CAME FROM ONE CYCLE. 15 unit missing over 65 sold, 23 Aug to 09 Sep, read from the count folded an hour earlier at v551. Salt's 20.32 per cent is read over three cycles; oil had one, on an anchor seventeen days stale. A flat markup on the buy rate is a coarser number and an honest one while oil has one cycle to its name.

IT MOVES THE PRICING BASIS AND NOTHING ELSE. eff and effEx both take the rule, because the FLOOR reads effEx and a rule that moved the headline alone would price the board one way and refuse it another. landed stays the IAS 2 inventoriable figure the accounts use, and shrink keeps reporting what the counts actually read, so the desk can still show the leak it is measuring while pricing off something else. Oil's board now runs 1.49x, 1.38x, 1.26x, 1.15x and 1.03x of break-even, so his RM450 at 50 unit clears on this basis and the under-floor flag of v552 goes quiet on its own.

THE RULE IS DATA, NOT CODE. COST_RULE on the book, per product, so the percentage moves without touching the engine, and `rule`, `rulePct` and `rulePlaceholder` travel with the cost stack so every surface can say which basis it is on. The Sourcing card said "goods plus freight, loaded 18.8% for leak", which described arithmetic that no longer ran; it now reads "RM 7.59 to buy plus 15%, a placeholder; freight and the leak are inside it, not added".

ALSO FOUND, AND NOT FIXED HERE: OIL'S 23 AUG COUNT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN ROLL. COUNTS records 15 unit. The roll chain only reaches the -35 that stood before v550 if that count was ZERO, and v384's note says so in terms. The entry carries no drift so it feeds nothing today, but it is wrong in the record and it will matter once oil has three cycles to read. Left for his decision.
SALT IS THE CONTROL. It carries no rule, still prices off its measured leak at RM56.21 effective on RM46.72 landed, and not one salt ask moves. Asserted as such, so the rule cannot quietly go global.

t: THE DESK QUOTES A PRICE HE HAS STATED, EVEN UNDER ITS FLOOR, AND THE BOARD READS ACROSS AS THE ARITHMETIC RUNS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026: "The desk quotes to 450, by lowering margin, then for others, quote proportionately." The v551 oil count read a 23.08 per cent leak from his own figures, which lifted the 50 unit oil floor to RM482.20 against the RM450 he had stated. v353 had the desk lift any stated price sitting under its floor, so the board read RM450 and the desk quoted RM490.

THE GUARD IS NARROWED, NOT REMOVED. From here it lifts a DERIVED ask only. The reason v352 wrote it still holds for one the desk invented: the ladder and the floor are struck on different bases, nothing forces them to agree, and an ask the desk made up below break-even is a fault. A price HE set below break-even is a decision, and the desk's job is to quote it and say what it costs rather than overrule him at the counter. The gap is named rather than hidden: `under` is the ringgit to break-even and `floorX` the multiple of it, so the 50 unit tier reads RM450 at 0.93x with RM32.20 under, and nothing else on either book moves.

AND HIS LADDER ALREADY QUOTES PROPORTIONATELY. Oil steps 1.35x, 1.24x, 1.14x, 1.04x, 0.93x of break-even across the five sizes, so the tier he has taken under cost is the end of a straight decline rather than a kink. The other four stand exactly as stated.

THE BOARD'S COLUMNS ARE HIS ORDER NOW: size, COGS, effective cost, margin in x, ask with its % margin. What stood there put the ask before the floor and headed a MARKUP column "Margin": ask over cogs less one, struck on LANDED, beside a "% margin" struck on EFFECTIVE cost. Two figures on one row shared a word without sharing a basis, and "2.00x" meant the ask was THREE times cogs. He asked what the difference was, which is the answer.

EFFECTIVE COST, BREAK-EVEN AND THE FLOOR ARE ONE NUMBER, equal to the ringgit at every size on both books, so the column carries all three names honestly and the multiple beside it is the ask over that: above 1.00x earns, 1.00x earns nothing, below 1.00x is a stated price under break-even and prints crimson.

PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ON THE DESK'S OWN COST STACK. Same size, same policy, same figures, the only difference being whether the price was stated: the stated one is quoted at RM450 and carries a RM32.20 gap; the derived one is still lifted clear of the floor and carries none. Against the unchanged engine the first reads RM490 and the pair collapses.

t: OIL COUNTED AT 60 ON 09 SEP: A DRIFT OF 15 UNIT AGAINST THE ROLL, AND THE FIRST OIL COUNT IN SEVENTEEN DAYS
n: HIS COUNT, 09 SEP 2026: OIL STANDS AT 60 UNIT. The roll put it at 75 once the two lots of v550 were on, so the drift is -15. A COUNT AND NOT A ROLL: COUNT_ON.oil moves from 23 Aug to 09 Sep, and the counted figure stands over the roll, as it does everywhere on this desk.

OIL HAD NOT BEEN COUNTED FOR SEVENTEEN DAYS, and everything between was rolled. The 23 Aug count is the anchor the whole run of oil figures has rested on, and it carried no `was` of its own, so until today oil had no measured drift at all: it was the one book whose leak could not be charged from its own counts. This is the second oil count on the book and the first that can be compared with anything.

WHAT THE 15 UNIT DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE. It is the difference between what the book expected and what he found, over a cycle in which 65 unit of oil went out. It does not say where the 15 went.
