A drift measured against a roll standing on a seventeen-day-old anchor carries that anchor's error as well as the cycle's, so the honest reading is that oil's leak is now measurable rather than that it is 15 unit of loss. The next count is the one that tests it.

IT ALSO SETTLES THE NEGATIVE INVENTORY. Oil had stood at -35 since v546 rolled a 50 unit sale out of a stated 15. v550 put the missing lots on and this count puts a measured figure under them, so the oil book stops reporting an impossible position and the Sourcing tab stops calling it empty.

t: TWO OIL LOTS THAT WERE NEVER RECORDED: 30 UNIT ON 04 SEP AND 80 UNIT ON 08 SEP
n: HIS ENTRY, 09 SEP 2026: two oil purchases that had never reached the book. 30 unit from SM4-KEP for RM 230 with RM 15 delivery on Friday 04 Sep, and 80 unit from SP7-PUD for RM 602 with a RM 12 collection trip on Tuesday 08 Sep. Both paid in full on the day, both received in full on the day.

THE 80 UNIT LOT IS WHY THE OIL INVENTORY HAD GONE NEGATIVE. CA7-JTR took 50 unit at RM 9 on order s140, and v546 rolled that out of a stated 15 to leave -35: the desk was reporting an oil book 35 unit short because the lot that covered the sale had not been entered. With both lots on, the roll runs -35 plus 110 to 75. The count that follows is a separate entry and a separate version.

BOTH RATES STAND UP. The 80 unit lot at RM 7.53 a unit beats every tier on SP7-PUD's live quote of 07 Sep, whose sharpest is 50 unit at RM 380, RM 7.60 a unit, so the largest oil lot this book has bought took size and rate together; landed at RM 7.67 with the trip, the 50 unit sale of 09 Sep carries RM 1.33 a unit, 14.7 per cent. The 30 unit lot at RM 7.67 is the same rate as the 26 Aug lot and RM 20 under the 30 unit tier as quoted on 07 Sep, though that quote is dated after the purchase and was not a choice he had on the day.

TWO OIL LOTS NOW READ AS TWINS ON THE BOOK, AND ARE NOT ONE. 26 Aug, 30 unit, RM 230, SP7-PUD, and 04 Sep, 30 unit, RM 230, SM4-KEP: the same quantity and the same total. Put to him at entry and confirmed as separate purchases from separate names. Recorded here so a later reader does not repair a duplicate that is not one.

AND OIL CARRIES FREIGHT FOR THE FIRST TIME. All three August oil lots were typed with none. These two carry RM 15 delivered and RM 12 collected, so oil's freight per unit stops being zero and its effective cost rises accordingly. SM4-KEP is also the first name other than SP7-PUD to supply oil, so that book stops being single-sourced.

t: THE SOURCING SECTION IS THE CURRENT LOT, NOT A NEXT LOT NOBODY PLANNED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026, ON A SCREENSHOT OF THE STATED LOT CARD: 'Outdated information', then 'generally no information on when I purchase', then 'in fact, this whole section should be the current lot, not the next lot'. The card read '50 unit, the 28th, by 2026-08-28, 12 days past its date'. SOURCING_PLAN had been typed on 24 Aug and the book had overtaken it four times since: 25 unit on 26 Aug, 25 on 31 Aug, 25 on 03 Sep and 50 on 08 Sep. A purchase date he does not fix in advance cannot be typed into the book without becoming a lie the desk repeats.

THE GREEN CARD WAS THE WORSE FAULT. 'Lands in time: none, the lot lands before the inventory empties' was drawn in green beside the stale date. `late` was daysToTarget minus the days of cover, so once the target date had PASSED the subtraction went safely negative and the check could no longer fail. The desk reported that the lot would land in time BECAUSE the plan had failed. An assertion that cannot fail passes, and so did this one, for twelve days.

WHAT THE SECTION SAYS NOW. The newest lot that actually landed, what it cost on the goods and effective, what is left of it and at cost, when the inventory runs dry on both rates, when the reorder mark arrives, and the lot against a month of demand. The cadence is MEASURED off the book, the gaps his last few lots really left, and the footer says in terms that the desk does not know when he will buy again and does not guess. The gap, the bridge, the pull-forward, the 'if it lands' cash and SOURCING_PLAN itself are retired; the ceiling fact inside its basis is kept in NOTES.SOURCING_PLAN. The section is no longer salt-only: a lot that landed is a fact every book has, so oil gets it too, and a book with no receipt gets a chip on the heading rather than an empty card.

AN UNDATED RECEIPT IS NOT THE CURRENT LOT, WHICH THE CENSUS CAUGHT. lotOutlook sorts undated lots last, so taking the final row outright made the v456 fixture's undated lot the current one and printed its date as the word undefined. Same rule supplierStats has kept for last paid since 08 Sep: an undated receipt is not known to be the newest. The newest DATED lot is taken, the final row still stands where nothing is dated at all, and the card says 'not dated' rather than going blank.

PROVED RED FIRST. Seven assertions. currentLot takes the lot outlook's rows as an argument, so the choice of lot is tested on synthetic rows with no fixture book near it: an undated receipt does not win, the newest dated one does, the last row stands when nothing is dated, an empty book returns null, and the cadence is the gaps the lots left. Two more read the rendered tab: it leads on the current lot, and no card says Lands in time, Stated lot, Gap to cover or Pull it forward. Against the master with the dated-lot rule reverted, the undated assertion reads back null and the census fails on sourcing again.

t: A PLACE STILL TO BE CONFIRMED CAN BE ENTERED, AND THE MAP'S REASON PRINTS ITS AMPERSAND
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 09 SEP 2026, ON A SCREENSHOT: the map's reason for a TBC code printed 'Names & IDs' with the entity showing, and a place still to be confirmed could not be entered when adding a name and ID. The first is one character in geo/places.json: the reason is escaped where it is rendered, so an entity in the source is escaped twice. The second was both forms refusing a blank place outright, 'Type the place' on the phone and 'A location is needed too' on the laptop, though the map has read the suffix TBC as 'nobody has recorded where this party is' since v347 and CE5-TBC was registered on 06 Sep on exactly that footing.

A BLANK PLACE IS AN ANSWER, AND IT TAKES THE SUFFIX TBC. On the phone, a blank place is filed into the vault as 'to be confirmed' when the code ends in TBC, and refused with the code it should be when the code names a place, because filing a place the party does not have is the wrong record. On the laptop's Names & IDs, a blank location derives the TBC suffix and files '(to be confirmed)'. Both fields say so in their placeholder. The code is re-keyed by Correction when the place is known, and the row keeps its id.

PROVED RED FIRST. Four assertions: the phone refuses a blank place on a code that names one with the TBC wording; a blank place on CZ9-TBC registers and the vault opens to 'Test Person (to be confirmed)'; the laptop panel derives CT11-TBC from a blank location; and the map's text reads 'Names & IDs' with no entity. Against the unchanged master the first three read the old refusals and the fourth found the entity.

t: THE LEDGER ENTRY IS TWO ROWS: THE ORDER AS IT STANDS, THEN WHAT LAST HAPPENED TO IT
n: HIS SCHEMATIC, 09 SEP 2026: AN ENTRY IS TWO ROWS. Row 1 is the order as it stands, the figure carrying the state: a part-delivered order reads 4 of 12.5 unit and a part-paid one RM 8 of RM 118. Row 2 is the transaction: the date when it differs from the order's, Open or Closed, the kind, then the units and the RM that moved. A closed entry folds to its first row; an open one keeps its latest line in view; a tap on the entry opens the whole trail. The credit-days collapse of v254 and the Opened role are retired.

THE FIRST LINE IS WHAT MOVED AT BOOKING, AGREED WHEN NOTHING DID, and a movement on the same day overwrites Agreed rather than following it. Open or Closed on every line is the entry's state after that line: the replay's reading, the last movement of a completed entry, a Cancellation or a Default. A Correction is a line of its own, saying in the row's own words what it moved, and inherits the state of the line before it.

THE SELL OR BUY TAG SITS UNDER THE E-NUMBER, at the entry's corner, so a folded entry still says which it is. THE PEN AT THE OTHER CORNER REPLACES THE UPDATE BUTTON: shown on hover and always faintly on a touch screen, it opens a short menu of the simple transactions, paid in full, delivered or received in full, completed, each the editor's own chip with the outstanding figures filled in, then Modification and More for the editor itself.
NO ROW MOVED AND NO FIGURE CHANGED. A display change only. The suite's ledger assertions were rewritten to the new shape and hold it: the fold, the tap, the roles on every line, the tag and the pen.

t: FULFILMENT ON THE 50 UNIT CA7-JTR OIL ORDER S140: RM450 AND 50 UNIT MOVE ON 09 SEP, THE ROW SETTLES IN FULL
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A FULFILMENT AND NOTHING ELSE. The pending oil order s140 with CA7-JTR, 50 unit for RM450 agreed 08 Sep, is met in full: RM450 cash and 50 unit recorded on 09 Sep against RM450 and 50 unit outstanding, leaving RM0 and 0 unit. The row itself is not recomputed in this fold, the master's amend path applies it, so there is one definition of what a fulfilment does rather than two.

THE INVENTORY DID NOT MOVE ON THIS FOLD. The movement is oil, 50 unit out to CA7-JTR dated 09 Sep, and the salt position stands where the count of 08 Sep left it at 32.25 unit, with cost at RM44 and replacement at RM46. The oil count still dates from 23 Aug, so this fulfilment runs against a count two weeks and more behind. CA7-JTR's outstanding of RM450 clears to nothing and no units sit on credit.

t: THE 6.25 UNIT CK4-SEN SALE OF 09 SEP: RM505 COLLECTED IN FULL, ABOVE FLOOR AND UNDER THE ASK
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A COMPLETED SALT SALE. CK4-SEN takes 6.25 unit for RM505, collected, RM505 cash and 6.25 unit moved on 09 Sep, so the row lands complete with nothing carried. Against the ladder for that size it clears the RM351.33 floor and sits under the RM610 ask, well inside the RM880 ceiling. The drafter raised no flags and the entry was decided at the desk, not on his word.

WHAT IS UNUSUAL IS THE COST LINE AND THE PARTY'S SHORT HISTORY. The draft costs the order at RM48 a unit, which is not the inventory's own RM44, so RM300 is booked against this order as its own cost rather than absorbed at the shelf rate. CK4-SEN shows one prior order, a median rate of RM73.33 and a range of RM73.33 to RM73.33, nothing outstanding and no units on credit against the cap of 1.

t: THE 50 UNIT SA5-BTR LOT OF 08 SEP: PAID IN FULL AT THE RM44 TIER, 37.5 UNIT ON THE SHELF AND 12.5 STILL TO COME
n: ONE PURCHASE ROW FOLDED, THE LARGEST TIER THIS DESK BUYS AT. The 08 Sep buy from SA5-BTR, 50 unit for RM 2,200 at RM 44 a unit, RM 2,200 cash paid the same day, is appended to purchases with its note. It matches the 50 unit tier of the 20 Aug quote exactly, RM 2,200, and sits at the bottom of the party's own range of RM 44 to RM 64.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID WITH IT. Paid in full but received short: 37.5 of the 50 unit moved on 08 Sep, so 12.5 unit stay outstanding against money already gone. The landed part carries RM 36 freight and comes in under the RM 48 shelf cost, so the cost basis moves. The salt count of 08 Sep stands behind the stated position; the drafter flagged nothing and the figures need no answer.

t: THE TWO CS6-BS UNITS OF 07 SEP AS THEY WERE: ONE RESOLD AND PAID, ONE ON CREDIT WITH ITS DELIVERY PAID
n: THE TWO CS6-BS UNITS OF 07 SEP, AS HE RECORDS THEM. One unit was resold and books to the CS6-BS-R account, paid in full on 07 Sep; one unit CS6-BS took for themselves on credit, RM 7.50 of delivery paid on 08 Sep and RM 110 outstanding. Both at RM 110 on the goods with RM 7.50 delivery inside, one RM 15 trip shared between them. Three entries on his word of 09 Sep: a correction moving s138 to CS6-BS-R, a fulfilment of RM 117.50 on it dated 07 Sep, and a fulfilment of RM 7.50 on s139 dated 08 Sep. At RM 110 a unit the goods sit RM 51.44 above the RM 58.56 floor for 1 unit and RM 20 under the RM 130 ask, costed at RM 48 a unit from the inventory.

TWO APPROVED PHONE AMENDMENTS WERE REJECTED ON HIS WORD, NOT FOLDED. An RM 7.50 fulfilment tapped on 08 Sep named the key both twins share, so the fold would have refused it as matching two rows; a correction tapped the same day zeroed s138's cash and delivered units, which contradicts the record above. Both are marked rejected in the draft table with the reason, their queue entries withdrawn, and the figures re-entered here by rid.

A FULFILMENT NAMES ITS ROW BY RID FROM THIS VERSION. The drafter resolved a fulfilment through the open-order snapshot by key alone, so of two identical orders only one could ever be fulfilled from the phone; it reads the rid off the book first now, shaped with the engine's own ledgerRow, and falls back to the key for an entry queued before rids existed. The suite holds it: a twin fulfilled by rid drafts against that twin, and one named by key alone still resolves.

THE INVENTORY DID NOT MOVE. No unit left or landed; the salt inventory stands at 1 from the 08 Sep count. CS6-BS-R stands at ten orders, every one paid on the day; CS6-BS has RM 110 open on 1 unit and nothing else.

t: A PENDING SALT ORDER IS WITHDRAWN IN FULL
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, A CANCELLATION. The fold carries a single amendment: the pending SELL to CC5-OKR of 1 unit for RM 90, agreed 08 Sep 2026, is withdrawn on the same day. No cash and no unit had moved against it, so nothing is reversed and nothing is booked. The withdrawn order counts nowhere from here, and the RM 90 and the 1 unit it had held out are no longer outstanding against that party.

THE INVENTORY DID NOT MOVE. Stock stands at 1 unit on the salt count of 08 Sep 2026, with the ledger at 68.95 units and self use at 67.95, cost basis unchanged at RM 48 a unit against a replacement cost of RM 48.67. Nothing is owed out, 59.5 units remain promised, and the reorder mark of 15 is untouched. The loans in from CH5-OUG at 5.5 units and CA11-SEN at 1.5 units stay open.

t: TWO PENDING ROWS TAKE THE DAY THEY WERE AGREED
n: WHAT WAS FOLDED: two sales, both pending, both dated 08 Sep 2026 from the entry as the day they were agreed. CA7-JTR takes 50 unit of oil at RM 450, collected, and CC5-OKR takes 1 unit of salt at RM 90, collected. Neither carries cash and neither has moved goods, so both are appended with their notes and nothing else follows them into the book.

WHAT IS UNUSUAL: the oil row lands exactly on the desk's RM 450 ask for 50 unit, while the salt row sits between the RM 58.56 floor and the RM 130 ask for 1 unit and repeats CC5-OKR's own median of RM 90. The drafter raised no flags on either row, and both are costed at the inventory's own rates, so no separate cost attaches to either order.

WHAT THE INVENTORY DID: nothing. Both rows are pending, so they draw no stock and book no revenue until goods move or cash arrives. Salt was counted on 08 Sep and oil on 23 Aug, and the salt cost basis stays at RM 48 a unit. Outstanding after this fold: RM 450 from CA7-JTR and RM 90 from CC5-OKR, with 51 unit still to hand over.

t: A PENDING ORDER IS DATED THE DAY IT WAS AGREED
n: THE FIRST TWO PENDING ORDERS APPROVED SINCE v487 FAILED THE GATE. His approvals of 08 Sep at 16:17 and 16:18 KL, 50 unit of oil to CA7-JTR at RM 450 and 1 unit of salt to CC5-OKR at RM 90, nothing paid and nothing moved on either, were staged, folded and refused in the same run: the book is in date order, but s140 and s141 carry no date. v487 made the rule that no undated row may stand and dated the three that did, and the drafter went on writing a pending order with no date, on the belief that a dated row draws stock and books revenue. It does not: the desk reads Pending, stock and revenue from cash and deliveredQty, so a dated row with neither is Pending and counts nowhere, which is how s119 has stood since 04 Sep.

THREE PLACES CHANGE. The drafter dates a pending row to the day the phone typed, and refuses an order typed with no date rather than draft it undated. The fold dates a draft that arrived undated from the entry it came from, so the two staged rows fold without being re-drafted, and refuses one with no date anywhere. And the fold's call reports an empty reply as what it is, with the stop reason, instead of the parser's Unexpected end of JSON input, which is how the second of the two dispatched runs failed. The batch stays staged in this commit; the job that runs on it folds the two rows as the next version.

t: NO PART REPEATS ITS VIEW'S NAME
n: AND FOR ALL OTHER TABS AS WELL (his instruction, 08 Sep 2026). v538 renamed the Today view's lead part To do because the rail's open block read TODAY then TODAY. The same doubling stood on three more views: Inventory over Inventory, Price over Pricing, Customers over Customers. Each lead part is now named for what it shows rather than for the view it leads: On hand for what is on the inventory and how long it lasts, The board for the ladder and its floors, Who buys for the buyers and who to approach next. Ids and addresses are unchanged; Order book, Ledger and Transaction already read apart from their views and stay.

t: THE PRINTED BOARD IN THE IDENTITY'S OWN COLOURS, THE RESELLER ROW TAGGED, AND TO DO
n: WHERE IS THE THEME COLOUR? NO NEED FOR BLACK AND WHITE (his call, 08 Sep 2026). v537 set the printed board on white with slate ink, the design system's light tone for paper. He wants the board as the desk is: the obsidian ground, brass and salt, brass hairlines between the lines. Paper, the saved image and the HTML file now carry that ground, and the print rule asks the browser to keep the colours rather than drop them for ink.

AND NO WORDS AT ALL (his second call, the same hour). No unit, no RM, no SALT and no Trading & Commodities: the crystal alone, the username the list is tagged to, and one line per size carrying two bare figures, the size in salt and the price in brass. The username is back on the sheet because the customer needs it to open his page; the wordmark is gone because the mark is the logo.

THE RESELLER ROW SAYS SO ON THE LEDGER (his question, 08 Sep 2026: which one of this is his reseller ledger entry). E158 and E159 are the twin 1 unit rows of 07 Sep and read identically on the ledger, CS6-BS both, because an R2 row is booked to the associate by the engine's own rule and keeps the buyer beside it as downstream. The row carried the attribution and the ledger did not show it. The party cell now carries a tag on an attributed row: R2 and the buyer behind the associate, or R3 and the associate credited, so E158 reads CS6-BS with R2 CS6-BS-R beside it and E159 reads CS6-BS alone.

TODAY, TODAY (his screenshot, 08 Sep 2026: a bit weird huh). The rail's open block is headed by the view and lists its parts beneath, and the Today view's lead part was also called Today, so the block read TODAY then TODAY. The part is what needs doing, ranked by the money at stake, and it is now labelled To do; the address #today and the view's name are unchanged.

t: THE BOARD YOU SET STAYS ON SCREEN, THE PRINTED BOARD IS THE LOGO AND THE NUMBERS, AND THE BRAND RIDES THE BAR
n: MAKE IT THE HOUSE BOARD LOOKED LIKE IT DID NOTHING. His report of 08 Sep: set the price is not working. The road itself was sound, proved end to end on the live desk: the tap queued the entry, the Worker took it, the drafter drafted it. What failed was the eye. The tap re-renders the part to lay the provisional prices on the board, and the re-render closed the Set the board section with the confirmation and the prices he typed inside it; on a phone that reads as nothing happening. The section now stays open after the tap and the confirmation is brought into view.

THE PRINTED BOARD IS THE LOGO AND THE NUMBERS, NOTHING ELSE (his instruction, 08 Sep 2026). The identity's horizontal lockup in its light tone, the crystal beside SALT and its descriptor, then one line per size: the unit and the price. The username line, the column heads and the week footer are gone from the paper, the image and the HTML file alike; the look is decided in the design layer, design/desk.css. Copy as text keeps the username, because a message cannot carry a logo and the customer needs the username to open his page.

THE MARK AND THE NAME PERSIST WITH THE HEADER (his instruction, 08 Sep 2026). The bar carried the brand on the phone only, and on the laptop the rail's own brand scrolled away inside the rail. The brand now rides the bar at every width, beside the date, the status and the version, and the rail keeps its own only where it is a floating menu. The bar is one glass surface with a hairline beneath it and a soft fall of shadow into the desk, rather than a veil fading into the first card.

t: BOTH 07 SEP CREDIT ROWS RESTATED TO RM 117.50, ONE OF THEM MOVED TO CS6-BS-R
n: THREE ROWS FOLDED, NONE OF THEM MOVING STOCK. Two corrections sit against the pair of 1 unit credit rows of 07 Sep, s138 and s139, both taken to RM 117.50 from RM 110, and one fulfilment of RM 60 cash settles CM4-MK s132 in full. No cash moves on the corrections and no unit moves on any of the three.

THE UNUSUAL PART IS THE SPLIT PARTY ON s138. That row leaves CS6-BS for CS6-BS-R, with assoc set to CS6-BS and stream set to R2, while its twin s139 keeps CS6-BS and takes the total alone. The drafter flagged that R2 books the row to the associate and that with no downstream named the end buyer is recorded nowhere, and the dossier carries nothing to fill that in. It also flagged that each correction leaves 1 unit out with RM 117.50 unpaid to be checked against a credit cap, and no cap figure for CS6-BS-R is given here, so that flag stands open. The two rows still share party of origin, date and size, so an amendment to either must name its rid.

THE INVENTORY DID NOTHING THIS FOLD. Salt was counted on 08 Sep 2026 and stands at 1 unit stated, ledger 68.95 and self use 67.95, costed at the shelf's own RM 48 a unit against a replacement of RM 48.67, reorder at 15, nothing owed out and 8.5 promised. Oil was last counted on 23 Aug 2026. Two loans in remain open, CH5-OUG at 5.5 unit and CA11-SEN at 1.5 unit, both dated 08 Sep.

t: THE STAMP IS THE CLOCK, NOT A GUESS
n: THE HEADER SAID 19:30 AT 14:16. Every version folded today by hand carried an updated stamp typed rather than read, and each one ran ahead of the clock; his question of 08 Sep, in the future?, was the right one. The stamp is now written from the clock at the moment a version is made, the gate refuses a master whose stamp is ahead of Kuala Lumpur time, and the as-at half of the chip spells the month the way the stamp does, Sep and not Sept.

t: NO DAILY RUN, THE ROW IN LOWER CASE, THE CLOCK IN KL TIME
n: FOUR COPY CALLS OF HIS, 08 SEP 2026. The queue's own lines still promised a daily run that has not existed since 24 Aug: a tap is drafted within seconds and folded the moment it is approved, and the three lines now say so. The Approve lead no longer shouts ROW. The clock on the Approve view names a bookkeeping entry as such rather than by its stamp, prints the time in Kuala Lumpur in the header's own shape, 08 Sep 2026, 10:03 KL, and a row from before the clock had a proof time says so instead of a dash.

t: THE CUSTOMERS CHART READS ACROSS AGAIN; THE QUOTE LEAVES THE LEDGER
n: WHAT THE REVENUE-AGAINST-MARGIN CHART IS. One circle per customer: across is the size of a typical order with them, revenue per order; up is their margin; the area of the circle is everything they have ever bought; the dashed line is the book's weighted average margin. Gold circles are the top quartile by margin, the customers who make the money; grey-blue the bottom quartile, the ones kept for reasons other than margin. Since some version after v261 every circle sat against the left edge with no figures on the axis: the chart has no top-level type, its first dataset is the average line, and a line's default x scale is a category axis. The axis is now told it is linear, with its bounds, and the circles spread across as they were drawn to.

THE SUPPLIER QUOTE LEAVES THE LEDGER. The table at the foot of the Ledger was Salt's quote alone, a bare copy of what Inventory, Sourcing already carries for each product as a ladder with the rate, the cash, the units after the leak, the cover and the profit at each tier; the oil quote of 07 Sep has been there under the Oil block since it was folded. The copy is gone and the quote has one home, beside the sourcing it informs.

t: A RE-KEYED PARTY READS BACK
n: THE TWO STATED CORRECTIONS THAT DID NOT HOLD, s032 and s046, held all along. Both were re-keyed on 26 Aug, CH6-TBC to CH6-SET and CZ4-TBC to CZ4-MK, and both rows carry the new code. The fold that wrote them named the field by its stored key, customer, where a correction's own name for it is party; the checker read the stored key, found it in no list, and reported that nothing had been written. His call of 08 Sep: this is a correction that can be done, and it had been. The checker now reads customer and supplier as the party field they are, and both rows read back as agreeing. Proved in the suite on a synthetic row each way, with a field that truly is unknown still called unknown.

t: ONE BUCKET: NON-REVENUE SALT, OR OIL
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026: nothing is parked under testers, promotion, shrinkage, own use or a shared non-revenue label. What left without a sale is one figure per product, non-revenue salt or non-revenue oil, at cost. The Analysis card says so and carries no split and no sentence about what went on purpose; the Inventory walk, its figure and the reconciliation prose use the one name; the statement of profit or loss has one line, inside the operating result, in place of marketing, abnormal loss and the drawing line; the pricing inputs name the leak charge the same way.

THE LOSS FORM ASKS FOR NO REASON. Units, date and a note; the entry is queued as non-revenue and the Approve card reads it so. The log keeps the reasons already recorded, and the split function that read them is gone.

t: THE LEDGER COLUMNS FIT THEIR LONGEST ENTRY
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026: size the ledger by the longest entry in each column. The tracks were fixed widths, so a column was either clipped or slack whatever it held. After every render of the Ledger part, ledFit() lets the grid out to max-content for one layout, measures every cell of every column across the head, the rows and the steps, and sets the widest as that column's track on the wrap, with the old width as its floor; the party column keeps its share of the rest. A desk with no layout engine measures nothing and keeps the floors, which is what the suite sees. The row's second line indents by the fitted E column, not a fixed 36px.

t: THE RAIL BLOCK, THE ROW LINE AND THE PERSISTENT HEADER
n: THREE DESIGN CALLS OF HIS, 08 SEP 2026, all in the design layer. On the rail, the open tab and its parts were a bordered card and a separate indented list under a faint line, two things where there is one: the open tab is now the head of a block and its parts the body of the same block, one border, one glass, and a part is marked by a brass bar at its left rather than a pill.

THE LEDGER ROW'S SECOND LINE put the role and the type at the far left under the E code and Update as a pill button at the far right, taller than the first line. The role now starts under the date, the type beside it in the same small capitals, and Update is a small brass pill on the same line; the grid keeps its tracks, so the row's contract with the suite stands, and an open row is a third shorter.

ONE PERSISTENT HEADER. The version chip and the names key stayed put on scroll while the date and status row scrolled away beneath them. The status row now rides in the desk bar: date and stamp at the left, status beside it, version and the key at the right, on one glass veil that fades into the desk. On a phone the bar wraps and the status row takes its own line.

t: THE NAME ON THE PHONE
n: PART B, STEP 10 OF HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026, and his rule of 05 Sep: a name and ID is committed every time. Add ID on the phone now asks for the name and the place beside the code. They go into the vault first, encrypted on the device with the passphrase asked there and used once, and the ID is queued only when the vault has saved; if the passphrase does not open the vault, or the save is refused, nothing is registered. Only a bucket has no name. The queue carries codes only, as always, so rule 2 stands: plaintext names never reach the cloud, the encrypted vault may.

THE LAPTOP PULLS. Until now the directory on the laptop was the source and seed-vault.mjs pushed it up; a name filed on the phone would have been overwritten by the next seed. tools/pull-vault.mjs brings the vault down first: it decrypts here, adds every code the directory lacks and never overwrites a name already typed on the laptop. The Names & IDs workflow runs it before anything else.

PROVED. On the real master, with WebCrypto lent to the test window: Add ID with a name and place files an envelope the same passphrase opens to the name, queues the ID with no name on it, and refuses when the passphrase is refused or the save fails; a bucket registers without a name; the pull's merge adds what the directory lacks and keeps what it has.

t: BORROW AND LEND ON THE PHONE
n: PART B, STEP 9 OF HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026. The two loans in of v518 were entered on his word in a Code session because the phone had no form for them. The Workbench now has Borrow or lend: which way, the party from the roster, the units, the date and a note. The drafter measures it against the position and the party's open loans and never prices it; the Approve card shows the units, that it is owed back in kind, and what the inventory does; the fold appends it to the loan book and rolls the stated inventory, in for a borrowing and out for a lending. The queued entry shows on the desk at once through the overlay, as a count or a loss does.

THE DRAFT TABLE WIDENS (migration 0007): loan joins the collections a draft may be, and priceset with it, which the drafter has returned since the price board could be set from the phone and the check of 0005 never named. Settling a loan stays a fold on his word for now: mark it settled with the date and roll the inventory the other way in the same version.

PROVED. The drafter drafts a borrowing and a lending and flags a lending over the inventory and a party with loans already open; the planner moves the units the right way; the apply appends the row and rolls the inventory on a copy of the book; the Workbench queues the entry with its figures; a loan draft passes the widened table on the real schema.

t: THE REPLAY QUESTION, ASKED ON THE PHONE
n: PART B, STEP 8 OF HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026. The fold refuses an entry that matches a row on the book by party, date, size and total, and it is right to: a double tap is the commonest way a row gets on the book twice. But two identical 1-unit orders to CS6-BS on 07 Sep were real, and the guard would have refused the second and left it for a person. The question is now asked where the entry is made. The same figures already queued from this device are a double tap and are refused outright, naming the stamp; the same figures on the book are put to him with the row named, and a yes travels on the entry as second.

THE DRAFTER NAMES THE MATCH EITHER WAY, so the approval reads it: marked, the fold will take it as a second order; unmarked, the fold will refuse it as a replay and the flag says to reject and enter it again answering yes. The fold honours the mark and writes that it did into what the row does, so the note carries it.

PROVED. The planner refuses the unmarked twin and takes the marked one; the drafter flags both ways; on the real master the editor refuses a double tap from the queue, refuses a twin of a real row when he says no, and queues it marked when he says yes.

t: REJECT MEANS DISCARD, WITH RE-ENTER
n: PART B, STEP 7 OF HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026. A rejected entry used to sit in every device's queue until the fold's watermark passed it, and a device that still held it re-posted it with its next tap; on 07 Sep two rejections were real orders retyped, and the originals waited for a person the next morning. Now the Worker drops the entry from every device's queue on the rejection, and a queue POST drops any entry whose draft was rejected, so no device can bring it back. The draft row stays, rejected: the decision is the record.

AND THE PHONE OFFERS IT BACK. The device that rejected drops its own copy too, so its next post cannot re-send it, and the Approve view offers Re-enter it, corrected: the rejected entry's own figures open in the editor, party, size, total, cash, units, date, delivery, handover, note and the associate on an R2, to be corrected and queued again under a new stamp. An amendment or a purchase is re-entered on the Workbench, and the message says so.

PROVED. In the suite the Worker drops the rejected entry from the store and filters it out of a re-post, leaving the other entries; the phone's seed maps a queued sale to the editor's row shape and refuses an amendment; the device's own copy goes and the rest stay.

t: ROSTER-ONLY PARTIES ON THE PHONE
n: PART B, STEP 6 OF HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026: what the drafter refuses, the form does not let you type. On 07 Sep an R2 sale left the Workbench with no party and an end buyer the desk had invented, the reseller's code plus -Gen, and the drafter refused it as naming no counterparty; a person had to re-read it the next morning. One validator, entryFault, now answers both entry forms: every party field is a roster code or nothing, with a message that points at Add ID; an R2 row's party is its associate, as the engine reads the row; a sale of a product with no lot has no cost and is refused; and an entry on which cash or units moved carries a date, the editor filling today when it is blank.

THE WORKBENCH'S UNKNOWN BUYER BOOKS TO THE RESELLER'S -R ACCOUNT, which the select has promised since v313 while the code invented -Gen; the three -R accounts on the roster are the one exception to a name and ID being committed with every code, and an associate without one is refused with the same message. The preview disables the button on the same answer the record step gives, so a refusal is read before the tap.

PROVED ON THE REAL MASTER. The validator both ways; the Workbench booking an R2 with the buyer unknown to the associate and its -R account, and refusing one for an associate that has none; the editor refusing a buyer not on the roster and filling today's date on a moved order.

t: THE GATE THAT DID NOT RUN
n: THE v522 GATE WAS A NO-OP ON THE RUNNER. Its main-module check built the file URL by hand, which matched on Windows and not on Linux, so on the runner it printed nothing and exited 0: the Gate step of the v522 deploy took one second and passed. The suite, running after the phone was live as v522 arranged, failed on its own red case for the gate and wrote the failure where the phone shows refusals, which is the loud failure that version promised. The check is now pathToFileURL, as fold.mjs does it, and the suite also asserts the green path: on the real master the gate prints every check and says GATE OK. The v522 note stands corrected: the gate runs in about ten seconds on the laptop and on the runner.

t: THE GATE BEFORE, THE SUITE AFTER
n: PART A, STEP 4: the full suite no longer stands between a fold and the phone. It is about two minutes of jsdom and until v521 it ran twice per approval on the same commit, once in the fold and once before the deploy. What must hold before a build reaches the phone is mechanical, and ci.yml already names it: the workflows parse, the book is in date order, the master's version is in the changelog, every generated block in the master is its module, the extract is the book, and public/ is what this master builds. tools/gate.mjs runs exactly those, in about ten seconds on this laptop, and both the Fold step and the deploy path run it instead of the suite.

THE SUITE RUNS AFTER THE PHONE IS LIVE, AND A FAILURE IS LOUD, NOT AUTOMATIC. It is the last step of the job, so the clock has stopped by then; a failure turns the run red, which emails, and is written where the phone shows refusals under a synthetic id above the watermark, so it stays on the Approve view until someone clears it. Nothing is rolled back: two of the three post-fold failures on 08 Sep were the suite's own fixtures moving with the live book, and an automatic revert would have pulled a correct ledger off the phone. Step 5 of the plan, the re-seed and the statements off the critical path, is met by this order: both already run after the proof and the mark, which is where the clock stops.

PROVED IN THE SUITE. The gate's list covers every --check that ci.yml runs; the gate exits 1 on a master whose book block is not the file; the workflow runs the gate before the deploy in both places and the suite after the last statements step; and the fold step no longer runs the suite before its push.

t: THE FOLD AS ONE CALL
n: PART A, STEP 3: the Fold step is one call to Claude over a dossier the tools compute. The Claude Code action booted a whole session for every approval, read the docs, explored the repo, ran the suite itself and pushed: 5 minutes 12 seconds on the CJ4-BJ chain of 07 Sep. tools/foldcall.mjs plans with fold.mjs, gathers what a person auditing the row would have looked up (the party's last rows, median and range, outstanding and units on credit against the cap; the desk's own floor, ask and ceiling for the size; the drafter's flags and sentences; the inventory position and open loans; for a count, the floors before and after), sends it once as JSON, and takes the notes back as JSON under a schema. The judgement is still a model's, on the same facts.

WHAT THE MODEL CANNOT DO. Every refusal rule stays in fold.mjs: a Linked or Rewarded amendment, an ambiguous key, a replay, a cancelled row. The reply is checked before it is used: the exact next version, a title in capitals, a paragraph for every row, no em-dash or en-dash, RM and unit only, codes only; a refused reply is sent back once with the reasons, and a second refusal leaves the batch staged. A refusal by the planner is recorded where the phone shows refusals and folds nothing. The step then runs the extract, the build and the suite, commits as the runner and pushes, which starts no second run.

WHAT IT NEEDS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. One new secret, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the Claude Code token is no longer read by the job. Nothing leaves the machine but codes, figures and the drafter's own sentences: the book carries no name. Proved in the suite on a fixture batch through a fake reply end to end, and on the validator both ways; the first real approval is the live proof and its clock (v519) is the measure.

t: THE CHAIN IN ONE JOB
n: PART A, STEP 2: stage, fold and deploy are one job of cloud-commit.yml. Until v519 they were three, each starting its own machine, checking out and installing, and the deploy waited for the agent's push to be picked up as a second run: about 45 seconds of job boundaries and 15 of push-to-run on the 8-minute CJ4-BJ chain of 07 Sep. One job does the checkout and install once and the deploy follows the fold in the same workspace. A plan step decides what the run does: fold when something is staged, deploy on a push, on a dispatch that did not ask to stage only, or whenever this run folded.

THE AGENT STILL PUSHES AS THE CLAUDE GITHUB APP, which starts a second run of the file. Two guards make that harmless: the concurrency group queues it behind this run, and an Already serving? step skips the deploy when the phone already has the build and no fold is waiting, republishing the statements only when the push touched them. After the agent, master is checked out again so the tip carries the fold and the runner's own token is back on the remote for the handoff commit. Step 3 replaces the action with one API call, after which the job pushes as itself and starts nothing.

UNCHANGED. The stage refuses to trample an unfolded batch and clears a replay batch itself; the deploy proves the phone is serving the build before any row is marked committed; the clock of v519 rides with the mark; the hourly net and the daily ship check stand. The repo's own workflow linter and the suite's three assertions on the file pass on the new shape. This build carries no fold, so its push is the first run through the one job.

t: THE CLOCK ON EVERY APPROVAL
n: PART A, STEP 1 OF THE CHAIN HIS INSTRUCTION OF 08 SEP 2026 ASKS FOR: everything within a minute of a tap on Approve, with a literal end-to-end check. Measured first: yesterday's CJ4-BJ approval took about 8 minutes from dispatch to the phone and 8 and a half to committed, of which the Claude Code action folding was 5 minutes 12 seconds and the full test suite in the deploy job 2 minutes 9 seconds. This version builds the clock the later steps are measured against and changes nothing else about the chain.

THE CLOCK. The draft table gains live_at (migration 0006): the moment the deploy job proved the phone was serving the build that carries the row. The tap is decided_at; committed_at follows the proof by seconds. The deploy job captures the proof time and passes it to drafts.mjs --committed --live, which writes both and prints tap-to-phone and tap-to-committed per row into the run summary. POST /drafts/<id>/committed accepts the same liveAt.

ON THE PHONE. The pending drafts response carries clock, the last committed draft's three timestamps, and the Approve view leads with it: how long the last approval took to reach the phone and to be committed, with the party and the time. A dash where a timestamp is missing: a fold stated directly has no tap, and every row marked before this version has no proof time. Four assertions in the suite: the route stores and returns the proof time on the real schema, the mock store agrees, the clock rides the pending view, and the phone's sentence reads it.

t: BORROWED 7 UNIT IN, AND COUNTED 1
n: TWO LOANS IN, ON HIS WORD OF 08 SEP 2026. 5.5 unit of salt borrowed from CH5-OUG and 1.5 unit from CA11-SEN on 08 Sep, owed back in kind, unit for unit, with no date set. The loan book only knew salt lent out, so a loan in is a new direction on the same rows: direction:"in" adds to the inventory while open and counts nowhere once settled, because the units came in and went back. The stated inventory rolled -1 to 6 for the two loans before the count, a roll and not a count. When either loan is returned, mark it settled with the date and roll the inventory down by its units in the same fold.

COUNTED 1 UNIT AGAINST 6 ON THE BOOK: 5 UNIT UNEXPLAINED. His count on 08 Sep, after the borrowings, with nothing delivered anywhere since the CS6-BS rows of 07 Sep; asked where the 5 unit went, he said the count stands. The count wins: the stated inventory is 1 and COUNT_ON.salt moves to 2026-09-08. The drift of -5 joins the last three counts (04 Sep 0, 06 Sep -1.3) and the leak rises with it, so every floor moves: 1 unit RM 54.87 to RM 58.56, 2 unit RM 109.73 to RM 117.12, 12.5 unit RM 685.82 to RM 732, and the board's ask for 1 unit RM 120 to RM 130, all read from the desk's own ladder before and after. The replacement cost is unchanged at RM 48.67. The self-use and shrinkage plug stands at 67.95 unit.

WHAT THE DESK NOW SHOWS FOR A LOAN IN. The Inventory walk prints Borrowed in (to return) as its own line and the movement chart a bar beside Received; the history walk lands the units on the day they were borrowed rather than at the opening, where a loan out still sits; the Order book folds the open borrowings under Salt you borrowed with the lender, the date and the units to return. loanDrawUnits is the net of out less in, so the position engine and the phone payload are untouched. Proved on the real master over a fixture book in the suite, red before the change on all four counts.

A HAND-STAGED COUNT WAS A SALE. drafts.mjs --draft wrote every collection but purchases as sales, so the count planned as SELL undefined; it now honours the drafter's five other collections. The desk's stated inventory of 1 stands against 8.5 unit still owed out to CJ4-BJ and 7 unit owed back to the lenders; the salt reorder mark of 15 unit is passed on every reading.

t: SALT QUOTE: THE 100 UNIT TIER IS RM 4,000
n: HIS WORD, 08 SEP 2026: SA5-BTR's 100 unit tier is RM 4,000, RM 40 a unit. Down RM 300 from the RM 4,300 (RM 43) quoted on 20 Aug; the other four tiers stand at 6.25 unit RM 350, 12.5 unit RM 650, 25 unit RM 1,200 and 50 unit RM 2,200. A quote, not a purchase: no lot, no cost and no floor moves.

THE TAPER STEEPENS AND FIVE ASKS COME DOWN. The salt ladder's taper is fitted from the quoted tiers and moves from -0.100 to -0.121 (fit 0.98 to 1.00), so the margin the ask carries falls faster with size. Every floor holds. The asks at 0.5 to 3 unit hold, RM 70 to RM 310; 3.5 unit RM 360 to RM 350, 4.5 unit RM 450 to RM 440, 5 unit RM 490 to RM 480, 6.25 unit RM 610 to RM 600 and 12.5 unit RM 1,150 to RM 1,120. Figures read from the engine on the desk's own snapshot before and after the edit, and the sealed price list follows on this deploy.

t: TWO UNIT TO CS6-BS ON CREDIT, AND S136 PAID RM 160 AT THE OPEN
n: THREE ROWS ON HIS WORD OF 08 SEP, re-read from the three taps of 07 Sep evening that never reached the fold. The 13:32 tap sold 1 unit at RM 125 via CS6-BS to a downstream party the drafter refused as naming no counterparty; the 13:34 tap sold 1 unit to CS6-BS at RM 110 and was rejected on the phone; the 13:35 tap paid RM 10 against s136 and was rejected with it. Read to him in a Code session on 08 Sep: there is no such party as the downstream code, both advances to CS6-BS are real, each is 1 unit at RM 110 with the RM 15 delivery divided equally at RM 7.50 inside each total, and s136 was paid RM 160 at the open. Drafted again through the same drafter, approved on his word, and folded here; the three KV entries clear as the watermark passes them.

TWO 1-UNIT ADVANCES TO CS6-BS, RM 110 EACH, NOTHING PAID. RM 102.50 on the goods of each after the RM 7.50 delivery inside the total. The desk's own ladder for 1 unit puts the floor at RM 54.87, the ask at RM 120 and the ceiling at RM 150, so each order stands RM 47.63 clear of the floor and RM 17.50 under the ask. Costed at the inventory's own RM 48 a unit, the 03 Sep lot of 25 unit from SA5-BTR, which is the figure the pricing snapshot carries: RM 62 on each order at 56.4%. RM 110 a unit is the rate CS6-BS paid on 29 Jul and sits inside their own RM 95 to RM 126.67 range on 1 to 1.5 unit; the drafter raised no rate flag. Both delivered in full on 07 Sep, so CS6-BS now carries RM 220 and 2 unit of credit, exactly the associate cap of 2 unit of salt. CS6-BS carried nothing outstanding before these rows: the two July rows with no cash were settled in rebate, not owed.

S136 CORRECTED: RM 160 PAID AT THE OPEN, RM 25 OWING. The row was folded at v515 with RM 150 paid and RM 35 owing; on his word of 08 Sep the cash paid when the order opened was RM 160, so the correction sets cash from 150 to 160 and CR3-DAM's balance from RM 35 to RM 25. A correction, not a payment: nothing moved on 07 Sep beyond what the row now says. The RM 10 fulfilment tapped at 13:35 was the phone's way to the same RM 160 and is superseded by this.

THE INVENTORY ROLLS 1 TO -1. Two unit went out to CS6-BS on 07 Sep against 1 unit on hand after CJ4-BJ's 4 unit the same day, so the stated inventory stands one unit below zero. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON.salt stays at 2026-09-06. A negative shelf says a lot has landed since the 06 Sep count that is not on the book, or the count was one short; no row is invented to explain it. With CJ4-BJ's 8.5 unit still owed out the salt reorder point of 15 unit is well passed.

t: 12.5 UNIT TO CJ4-BJ, NOTHING PAID AND 4 UNIT ALREADY OUT
n: ONE APPROVED ROW. 12.5 unit of salt to CJ4-BJ on 07 Sep for RM 850, of which RM 15 is the delivery charge typed on the order, so RM 835 on the goods at RM 66.80 a unit. Costed at the inventory's own RM 48 a unit, the 03 Sep lot of 25 unit from SA5-BTR, which is the figure the pricing snapshot carries, so no override was needed: RM 600 of cost against RM 835 of goods leaves RM 235, 28.1% on the goods.

ABOVE THE FLOOR, WELL UNDER THE ASK. The desk's own snapshot puts the floor for 12.5 unit at RM 685.82, RM 54.87 a unit, and the board's ask at RM 1,150, RM 92 a unit. The goods stand RM 149.18 clear of the floor and RM 300 under the ask. This is the wholesale band, whose policy anchor is 12.5 unit at RM 875, so RM 835 is RM 40 under the anchor and comfortably above the line that matters.

THE RATE AGAINST CJ4-BJ'S OWN BOOK. His seventh order. RM 66.80 a unit sits between his two August tranches, 6.25 unit at RM 64 a unit on 20 Aug and 6.25 unit at RM 72 a unit on 26 Aug, and just under the RM 68.00 a unit of the audited 15 Jul row. Those two August tranches were one split 12.5 unit order and came to RM 850 between them, the same size and the same total as this row written as one; they are separate rows on separate dates and the replay guard passed. No rate flag was raised.

AN ADVANCE OF THE WHOLE ORDER, AND OVER THE CAP. RM 0 of the RM 850 is paid and 4 of the 12.5 unit went out on 07 Sep, so 4 unit of credit is out against a retail cap of 1 unit of salt: CJ4-BJ is not an associate. The drafter raised this as its only flag and it was approved on the phone with the figure in front of him. CJ4-BJ carried nothing outstanding before this row, so RM 850 is his whole exposure, and it is the largest single balance on the open book.

THE INVENTORY ROLLS 5 TO 1. The second movement off the 7 counted on 06 Sep, after CR3-DAM's 2 unit earlier the same day. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON.salt stays at 2026-09-06. 8.5 unit of this order are still owed out against 1 unit on the shelf, and the salt reorder point is 15 unit.

t: OIL QUOTE OF 07 SEP: FIVE TIERS FROM SP7-PUD
n: HIS WORD, 07 SEP 2026: SP7-PUD quotes oil at 10 unit RM 100, 15 unit RM 150, 20 unit RM 180, 30 unit RM 250, 50 unit RM 380. Booked over the 06 Aug ladder: the 15 unit tier is new, 30 moved up RM 20 and 50 up RM 30, 10 and 20 stand. A quote, not a purchase: no lot, no cost and no floor moves. The oil ladder's taper is fitted from these tiers and eases from -0.231 to -0.186, but every carded ask holds: RM 130, 240, 330, 400 and 450 at 10 to 50 unit, on floors that do not move because no lot moved.

t: OVER CAP IS UNITS OUT AND UNPAID, ON EVERY SURFACE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026: CR3-DAM's RM 35 should not be over the cap. It was not, on the register: the Boundaries register measures credit out as the units handed over less what the cash covers at the row's price, and CR3-DAM's 2 unit sale with RM 35 left to pay is about a quarter of a unit against the 1 unit retail cap. The Order book row and the Today advances measured units DELIVERED instead, so the same row read "over cap" one tab over. One helper now, creditOutUnits and overCap, summed per customer per book, and all three surfaces ask it.

t: A REPLAY BATCH CLEARS ITS OWN HANDOFF, AND THE WATERMARK PASSES THE DUPLICATE
n: WHAT HAPPENED ON 07 SEP. The CR3-DAM sale of 2 unit at RM 185 was queued twice three minutes apart and both entries were approved. The first folded as v510 in nine minutes; the second was staged, refused by the fold as a replay of the row it had just written, and its handoff stayed in HEAD, where the stage stands down, so the chain was shut with every job green until it was cleared by hand.

THE STAGE NOW ASKS THE PLANNER FIRST. `node tools/fold.mjs --replays` answers yes when every staged row is refused because the same row is already on the book; the stage then marks those drafts committed, records each refusal where the phone shows refusals (`drafts.mjs --refused-note`, source fold), removes the handoff and stages on. Anything else still stands down as before.
THE WATERMARK moves to the duplicate's own stamp with no row folded, so the phone stops showing it as provisional and the ship check stops reading it as a replay.

t: A CUSTOMER'S RATE IS DRAWN TOWARD THE BOARD
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026, on the design fault that CR3-DAM's list read RM 160 at 2 units under a board asking RM 220: his rate adjusted slightly higher if below the ask, up more if below the floor, down more if above a 2x markup (three times COGS), and down slightly if above the ask but loyal, by tier. Booked as one rule, adjustedPrice in tools/pricelist.mjs and pbAdjusted on the desk, the suite holding them equal on the real book: slightly is a quarter of the gap to the ask, more is half, never under the floor, never above the cap, then up to the ringgit. Loyal is the desk's own badge, three or more priced orders and the last within fourteen days. A customer with no history sees the board's ask. CR3-DAM at 2 units now reads RM 175: RM 160 plus a quarter of the RM 60 gap to the board.

t: TWO UNIT TO CR3-DAM AT RM 92.50, RM 35 LEFT ON ADVANCE
n: ONE APPROVED ROW. 2 unit of salt to CR3-DAM on 07 Sep for RM 185, RM 92.50 a unit, collected in full on the day. Costed at the inventory's own RM 48 a unit, the 03 Sep lot of 25 unit from SA5-BTR, so RM 96 on the order and RM 89 gross, 48.1% on price.

ABOVE THE FLOOR, UNDER THE ASK. The floor for 2 unit reads RM 109.73 and the board's ask RM 220, so the order sits RM 75.27 above the floor and RM 35 under the ask. It is also CR3-DAM's first rate above RM 80 a unit since 03 Jul: each of their last nine orders was 1 unit at RM 80, and the drafter flagged this one 15.6% above their eleven-order average.
AN ADVANCE OF RM 35. RM 150 of the RM 185 was paid and both unit went out on 07 Sep. CR3-DAM carried nothing outstanding before this row, so the RM 35 is their whole exposure.
THE INVENTORY ROLLS 7 TO 5. The first movement off the 7 counted on 06 Sep. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON.salt stays at 2026-09-06.

t: THE LAST THREE PLACES THE BOARD SAID DELIVERED OR COLLECTED FLOOR
n: Seen on the printed proof of v508: the board table's last column still read "Floor, delivered", the sheet's read "Floor, collected", the board chart's dashed series was labelled "floor, delivered" and the sheet's under-floor notice named the collected floor. v502 retired the pair and these four captions were missed. They read Floor now. The board's third column reads Margin rather than Markup, the ask being a margin on the floor since v504; the figure beneath each ask already said so.

t: THE BOARD AS AN IMAGE OR AN HTML FILE, FROM THE PHONE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026: make it printable as an image, or HTML, in Files, on the phone. Two buttons beside Print: Save as image draws the same rows on a canvas (ink on white, the title, the username, one line per size, the week) and Save as HTML writes a standalone page with the same lines and no dependency. Either is handed to the phone's share sheet as a file, where iOS offers Save Image and Save to Files and Android its own targets; a browser that cannot share a file downloads it instead, and the card says which happened. Nothing loads from outside, and the rows are the ones the paper gets.

t: PRINT A BOARD: THE ID CHOSEN, THE SIZES TICKED, ONLY THE UNIT, THE PRICE AND THE USERNAME ON PAPER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026. A card on the Price part: choose the customer, tick the sizes, Print. What reaches paper is the unit, the price and the customer's statement username and nothing of the desk around it. The prices are the customer's own weekly list, the same rule tools/pricelist.mjs seals into his statement page (pbPrices, proved equal by the suite), so the sheet handed over and the page he opens agree. The username is read from the Worker (GET /stmt-users, keyed), which the publish writes to the desk's store; the laptop copy prints a blank line for it.

IF IT WILL NOT PRINT. Copy as text puts the same lines on the clipboard, and the card folds a checklist: a Home Screen desk with no print dialog (open the address in the browser, or Share then Print), a blank page (Save as PDF, then print that), no printer (copy and paste it into the message), a blank username (the laptop has no road; the cloud desk needs the write key).

t: FROM COST TO ASK, ONE ROW PER SIZE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026: I want to see COGS, then the floor (break-even), then the minimum ask; it seems disconnected. The Price part showed the cost stack, the ladder policy and the board as three cards and walked nobody between them. A table now does, one row per size: COGS (landed times the size), the leak the floor adds, the floor, the size's margin, the floor at that margin, and the board's ask, marked where the rate law stepped it. Every figure is priceLadder's own, so the walk cannot disagree with the board. The Level row reads as the margin on the floor where a book carries anchorG.

t: THE SUPPLIER'S 25 UNIT TIER IS RM 1,200
n: HIS WORD, 07 SEP 2026: the bulk quote for 25 unit is RM 1,200, RM 48 a unit, down from the RM 1,250 quoted on 20 Aug. The other four tiers stand. The two 25 unit lots of 02 and 03 Sep already landed at this rate, so the replacement rate does not move; what moves is the taper the ladder is fitted to, which the Price part reports with its r-squared.

t: THE LAST THREE LOTS, THE LEAK FROM THE COUNTS, THE ASK AS A MARGIN ON THE FLOOR, AND THE INVENTORY
n: HIS INSTRUCTIONS OF 07 SEP 2026, BOOKED AS ONE VERSION. The replacement window is the last three lots received, not thirty days: salt lands a lot every four or five days and oil every ten to fifteen, so one calendar window was six cycles on one book and two on the other. The rate and the typed freight both read off those three lots (pxWindowLots).

THE LEAK IS CHARGED FROM THE COUNTS. A count is taken when a lot lands and the inventory is near empty, so the drift at each count is that cycle's leak, every use included. The book now keeps COUNTS, every count as taken, seeded from the fold notes of v473, v489 and v498, and the fold appends one line per count. pxLeakCharge() takes the units missing over the last three cycles over the units handed over in them, and the cost stack applies that ratio to landed in place of the lifetime share and the attribution lever, which stand in only where no cycle can be read.

THE ASK IS A MARGIN ON THE FLOOR. One basis: the floor is what a size costs to take out, and the ask is the floor at the size's margin on price, sliding on the supplier's taper, pinned at anchorG on anchorQ (0.47 on salt's 2.5 unit, 0.36 on oil's 10, each set so the board did not move on the day) and clamped between gLo and gHi. ladderMargin() beside ladderMarkup(); the walk, the rate law and the floor guard are unchanged. The margin the board prints is now the P&L's gross margin to the point.

INVENTORY, NOT SHELF OR STOCK. Every place the desk's copy said shelf or stock now says inventory; the Stock view is the Inventory view at the same address. Identifiers, addresses and the history are untouched.

t: FREIGHT IS TYPED ON EACH LOT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026: for every sale and purchase moving forward, freight and delivery cost are input manually. Delivery on a sale landed at v502. This is freight on a purchase: a lot carries `freight` in RM, the trip it cost, typed on the Workbench (Freight, shown for a purchase), the phone, the row editor and the order sheet, and carried by the drafter into the row. It sits beside the total, so the lot rate stays the goods.

COLLECTION PER UNIT COMES FROM THE LOTS. pxFreightRate() sums the typed freight over the units of the same lots, over the replacement window first and over every live lot with a figure when the window holds none, and hands it to the cost stack as I.freightRate, which wins over the stated trip. COST_BASIS.freightPerTrip.rm is retired to 0 as the fallback, so a book with no typed freight charges nothing for collection and the Price part says so. The P&L's freight-in line is the sum of what was typed.

WHAT THAT MEANS TODAY. No lot on the book carries a freight figure yet, so collection reads RM 0 and landed equals the replacement rate until the next purchase is entered with its trip. The rows already on the book can be given one through the row editor.

t: ONE FLOOR PER SIZE, AND DELIVERY IS TYPED ON THE ORDER
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026: do not name it floor delivered; delivery will be an input per order. The engine returned two floors per size, collected and delivered, the second the first plus one delivery. There is one now: the goods after the leak. floorTotal and lotCost carry no delivery, board() publishes floors[q].floor and no deliveryCharge, the snapshot, the drafter and the price list read the one figure, and the copy on the Price part says so.

DELIVERY IS A FIELD ON THE ROW, INSIDE THE TOTAL. A sale carries `delivery` in RM, typed per order on the Workbench, the phone (Of which delivery), the row editor and the order sheet, and carried by the drafter into the row. It is part of the total, so nothing that reads what is owed or paid changes: the statement prints "incl. delivery" under the amount, the total to pay is the total. What changes is the rate: txGoods() is the total less the delivery, and the drafter's flags, the party's usual, the Approve card, the Orders card and the customer price list all strike the rate on the goods. A delivery charge larger than its total is refused by the drafter.

ON THE STATEMENTS SITE the list shows one price per size, for the goods. A customer who asks for delivery is told the charge when the order is marked ready: Ready to deliver on the Orders card asks for the figure, the customer sees goods plus delivery as the sum to pay, and Completed queues the sale with the delivery as its own field.

t: HIS TIME IS NOT CHARGED INTO THE FLOOR
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 07 SEP 2026: do not charge for my time. Given on reading how the salt floor and ask are struck at 1, 1.5 and 2 units, where the RM 25 per order was the whole of the gap between the leak-adjusted cost and the floor. PRICE_ENGINE.timePerOrder is 0.

WHAT MOVES. Every floor on both books falls by RM 25, at every size, collected and delivered alike, since v500 already took delivery out: the floor is now the leak-adjusted cost times the units and nothing per order. Salt at 1 unit reads RM 52.92 against RM 77.92 before; the ask is untouched, because his time was never in the margin curve, and no ask was floor-lifted so none moves. The customer price list lifts a rate to this floor, so a customer's own rate is now bounded by a lower line.

WHAT STAYS. The mechanism, the per-order argument and the measurement behind RM 25 are kept in the declaration for the day he states a figure again; the copy on the Price part names the figure it is given, which is now nil.

t: DELIVERY IS NOT CHARGED INTO THE FLOOR
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 06 SEP 2026: remove delivery cost. Every run since v498 stopped at the suite's gate on the oil board: the engine's floor at 50 units had reached RM 453.18 delivered against his stated RM 450, and the RM 10 of delivery per order was the whole of the excess (collected, the floor was RM 443.18). Asked whether to raise the price or gate on the collected floor, he chose neither: the delivery cost goes.

ONE FIGURE, IN THE COST BASIS. COST_BASIS.txnPerDelivery.rm is 0. Everything downstream reads it: delPerOrder is 0, so the delivered floor is the collected floor at every size on both books; the blended txn in eff is 0; the board's deliveryCharge is 0; the customer price list's delivered column equals its collected column and the page says delivery is not charged. deliveredShare stays as a measured fact. Nothing in the engine changed; the input did.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. A delivery still costs him the trip. It is no longer recovered in the floor, which is the position he has taken; the P&L's delivery line reads RM 0 per delivery until he states a figure again, and the desk's copy names the figure it is given rather than assuming one.

t: THE STATEMENTS SITE TAKES ORDERS, AND SHOWS EACH CUSTOMER HIS OWN PRICE LIST
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 06 SEP 2026: after the username and the password a customer can also find a price list based on his historical purchase price, changing weekly, and place an order: a lot size in, the price back, then the payment method, with a link to only the method he chose, from QR Command. He sees the payment options only after the desk has acknowledged the order and said it is ready for pickup or ready to be delivered, with live notifications, and an updated statement after completion.

THE PRICE LIST is a second sealed document beside the live statement, written by the same deploy under the same content key (tools/pricelist.mjs): the median unit rate of his last four committed orders of each product, read from orders dated before the week's Monday in Kuala Lumpur, never below the engine's collected floor for the size, and delivery quoted on top per order as the board does. A customer with no history on a product sees the board's ask. Nothing outside the engine prices: floorTotal and priceLadder are called, fed the desk's own PRICING inputs, the same the drafter reads.

THE ORDER lives on the statements site's own store (stmt/orders.js), on a session the site mints with the password. Placed, acknowledged, ready, done, declined, withdrawn; payment is offered at ready only; five rails, and one link into QR Command for the one chosen, the accounts read from the pay master by tools/paysync.mjs with no number shipped. The page follows the order every ten seconds while it is open, and a payload-free push wakes the phone when it is not (stmt/push.js, the site's own key pair), the banner naming no amount and no order.

THE DESK READS THEM THROUGH A SERVICE BINDING (src/orders.js): this Worker calls the site with STMT_DESK_KEY and the site has no road back. The Orders card in Enter is the taps: Acknowledge, Ready to collect or deliver, Completed, Decline. Completed queues the sale under q:orders, shaped as the Workbench shapes one, cash and units in full, drafted on arrival and approved here as every row is; the live statement follows the fold. The username-to-code map is written to the desk's own store by the publish; the site never holds it. A placed order also wakes his phone on the drafter's quarter-hour.
THE SEND SHEET now carries the statement address on every card as a link, and a Desktop shortcut, Send Statement, opens the newest sheet.

t: A NEW BUYER TAKES 1 UNIT, AND THE SALT SHELF IS COUNTED AT 7
n: ENTERED BY THE FOLD ON HIS WORD, 06 SEP 2026. A new customer is registered as CE5-TBC and takes 1 unit of salt for RM 110, paid and handed over on the day. The suffix is temporary: the code's place part is decided by the location, and the location is to be confirmed, so the code is re-keyed by Correction when it is, and the row keeps its id. The name and the location are on the laptop's directory only, as every name is.

THE SHELF IS COUNTED AT 7. After the unit went out the roll from 9.3 read 8.3; he counted 7, a drift of 1.3 unit. A count, not a roll: the stated salt shelf is set to 7 outright and the count date moves to 6 Sep. The last count was 9.8 on 4 Sep.
THE STATEMENT USERNAME IS MINTED WITH THE ID, as the rule of 05 Sep asks, and is kept for life under whatever code the party ends up with.

t: A BREACH IS NAMED ON ITS OWN BOOK'S REGISTER ONLY
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 06 SEP 2026: CA4-DAM breaks one rule in salt only, not in oil. The Boundaries register on the oil tab listed his salt credit-cap breach, 2.5 unit of salt out and unpaid, and named it as salt's. Round 5 had made the cap per book and kept the whole-book read on purpose, so a salt breach was shown on every tab. That is reversed: the credit rows are filtered to the active book before they are named, so the oil register carries no salt breach and the salt register carries it once, under the one rule he breaks. Every other rule in the register was already the active book's: the shelf, the cost basis and the margin floor read the product on screen, the receivables ladder reads the walk's own list, and a ban is a person, not a book, and stays on both.

PROVED ON THE LIVE BOOK. The assertion asks the register for CA4-DAM's rules on each book: on salt, exactly one, Credit cap; on oil, none. The same expression on the unchanged desk returned the credit-cap breach on oil. The render diff moves nowhere, because every shot is taken on the salt book, where nothing changes.

t: COST IS THE ORDER'S, IN RINGGIT, AND A MOVEMENT CARRIES THE COST OF WHAT IT MOVED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026, THE FIRST FOLD OF THE TWO-SHAPE SHEET: the delivered cost is a stored input, an absolute figure, because it determines the cost of goods sold and the pricing of the product over time. Until now a sale's cost was RM per unit, and every reader multiplied it by a quantity of its own choosing: the order's units in the Ledger's margin, the units not pending in the P&L, the whole quantity in the customer tables. The audit of 04 Sep had counted three definitions of COGS. The unit figure is now DERIVED, once, by txUnitCost in the position engine, with the caller's shelf figure as the fallback for a row with no stated cost; nothing else divides, and costOf on the desk is a wrapper over it. txCost reads the order's figure.

THE BOOK CONVERTED ONCE, BY tools/cost-migrate.mjs, RUN BY HAND. 128 stated costs became the unit figure times the order's units, to the sen; 52 product-moving steps took the cost of what they moved, unit times units moved, as amend[i].cost; and s107, the one live row that had never stated a cost, is stored at the product's weighted average buy price of RM 50.4042 a unit that the desk had been costing it at, RM 315.03 for 6.25 unit, with a row note saying so. The five cancelled rows without a cost stay without one: nothing was delivered. The tool refuses to run twice.

PROVED BY EVERY FIGURE HOLDING. On the book as it stood and on the book as converted, read through the running desk: salt COGS RM 16,325.43, goodwill RM 26.26, gross margin RM 10,679.57, receivables RM 142.50; oil COGS RM 615.33 and gross margin RM 271.17; the same to the sen. 153 of 154 Ledger cards print the margin they printed; the one that moved is s018, whose cost of 47.6 a unit on 10.4412 unit was RM 497.00112 and printed RM 213.00 of margin, and is stored as RM 497.00 and prints RM 213. The render diff against a v495 build shot the same day moves in four places and each is accounted for: the Ledger on that one cell; the Journal on its cost line and s107's note; Financials, where the gross margin card had printed a dash, 'a product has an uncosted row', because s107 had no cost, and now prints RM 10,951, salt 10,680 and oil 271, the walk's own figure; and Plans, where the watch count and the integrity count fall from 7 to 6 because s107 has left the row-with-no-cost item. The first cut of this fold left one reader unswept, the per-product summary behind that card, and it printed RM -76,350 of gross margin until the render diff caught it: the reader map had skipped the master's lines 5000 to 5999 as generated, and only the version entries there are.

THE WRITERS FOLLOW. The drafter's row carries the shelf's unit figure times the order's units, and its below-cost and recost flags read the row's unit cost through the engine. The fold's Fulfilment writes the movement's cost on the step, from the order's unit cost, after the shelf has filled an uncosted order and after a note has recost one, in that order; the suite found the step written before the fill and it is written after. A Modification rescales the order's cost to its new quantity, in the fold and in the desk's own preview alike, so the unit cost the order was costed at is kept. The editor's field reads Cost, RM, with a hint that it is the whole order's. The fold routine's note contract says the same.

ONE RED LINE IS NOT THIS FOLD'S, AND IS HIS TO DECIDE. The oil board's assertion that RM 450 clears both 50 unit floors went red on 06 Sep on the unchanged v495 desk as well: lot p012 of 6 Aug left the thirty-day window at midnight, the trailing rate rose from RM 7.00 to RM 7.25, and the delivered floor at 50 unit reads RM 453.18. That assertion exists to say his stated price needs his decision, and it is left red until he gives it.

t: AN ENTRY IS TWO ROWS, AND THE SHEET IS IN THE SYSTEM'S LEDGER RECIPE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026, ON A SCREENSHOT OF THE HEADING: the entry, its date, party, product, quantity, price, total and state on the first row; the step and the type on the second, running to the end, where the Provisional pill and the Update button sit; the pill dotted and transparent, Update a button; and the desk redone to the design system. The heading he shot had Qty running into Price/unit and the product on the second row beside the control.

ONE SHAPE ABOVE THE PHONE. The sheet had three layouts: eleven tracks on one row above 935px, two rows under it, three rows under 600px. On his own screen the rail leaves the sheet under 935px, so the two-row shape is what he reads, and the single row above it was a second design he never saw. The 935px tier is gone: its shape, re-laid to his order, is the sheet at every width above the phone, and the phone keeps its three rows. The product moves up beside the figures; the type spans the middle of the second row; the act cell spans the last two tracks so it ends the line. The price track is 84px so the heading's word fits it. A step stays one row, its kind on the party's and product's tracks.

THE ACT CELL SAYS WHAT CAN BE DONE, OR WHY NOT. The Provisional pill sat inside the product cell. A provisional row has no rid yet and so no Update, and the act cell was empty on exactly those rows; the pill sits there now, in the status chip's shape with a dotted line and nothing behind it, so the end of the second row reads Update on a row that can be edited and Provisional on one that cannot. Update is a bordered pill button rather than an underlined word, in the same shape, brass line, brass wash on hover. Figures on the sheet are tabular. All three are the layer's, in design/desk.css.

WHAT REDOING THE DESK MEANS HERE. The vendored stylesheet is byte for byte the design system's, so nothing was pulled; the whole desk was re-skinned to this system at v472 to v477. What the system adds for a list of the book is its ledger recipe, label in mist caps, value in salt, hairline between, tabular figures, and the sheet is laid to it. A change to the system itself would be a pull and a render diff, not this fold.

PROVED RED, TWICE. tools/ledger-probe.mjs, new and run by hand like the render diff, measures the sheet in a real browser: on the v494 build at 1280 the product sat 39px below the entry, the act cell 6px below the first row's foot, and Update was underlined; on this build the product shares the first row's top with the party and the state, the step, type and act cell all sit below it, the act cell ends where the state ends, and Qty ends before Price/unit begins. The suite reads the declared areas through the cascade, plants a provisional row and finds its pill in the act cell, dotted, and finds Update a solid bordered pill. Two faults in the instruments were found before the desk was trusted: a heredoc ate the backslash from a regex and the test then read every word with its s removed, and the probe compared cell tops on a row that centres cells of different heights. The render diff: the Ledger is the only part that moves, at either width.

t: A SALE IN ADVANCE CAN BE MOVED TO DEFAULT FROM THE EDITOR
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026: on updating a ledger entry, Pending can move to Cancelled, Open or Completed, and the move missing is Default from Advance. The Defaulted tick sat in the editor's field table marked buy-only, so a sale's editor never drew it, though every reader of CORRECT_BOOL, the drafter, the fold and the desk's own preview, already carried the flag for a sale: the chain could fold a default it could not be asked for. The tick now shows on both sides, with a hint saying what a default on a sale means, that what they still owe is written off and provisioned in full and the goods stay handed over.

THE RULE THAT COMES WITH IT, IN THE ONE RULER. The lot side's Default kind has refused a default on a lot that has received its salt since v435. correctionFaults, which the drafter, the fold and the desk all read, now carries the same shape for the correction road on both sides: a sale nothing has been handed over on cannot default and is cancelled instead; a sale paid in full has nothing to default on; a lot that has received its salt cannot be defaulted on. It fires on a correction that sets the flag, not on a row that already carries it, and it measures the row with the flag stripped, because a defaulted lot answers nothing received by design. Both of those were found by the suite before this shipped: the first draft refused a note edit on the book's one defaulted lot, and measured that lot with its flag on and passed it. A defaulted lot may still be cancelled, as v421 decided; a rule against that was drafted and withdrawn.

PROVED RED THROUGH THE FOLD'S OWN PLAN. Three planted sales and a planted settled lot go through plan() as Corrections setting defaulted. Against the unchanged engine the pending sale, the paid sale and the landed lot were all planned; now each is refused with its reason, the Advance sale is planned, and applied it reads Default and provisions in full. The desk's field table is read from the rendered master and offers the tick on a sale as on a lot. Nothing visible moves: the editor is a dialog, and every shot reads the same.

t: THE LEDGER CARD CARRIES ITS STATE AS A HINT OF COLOUR
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026, TO MAKE THE LEDGER MORE LEGIBLE: each card tinted by its state. Completed green, Open . Advance amber, Open . Deferred yellow, Default red, Pending blue, and a cancelled entry faded. In the identity's own words: verdigris for settled, which is Completed and In-Kind alike; copper for Advance, where they owe him cash; brass for Deferred, where he owes salt; ember for Default; steel for Pending; and a cancelled card at half opacity with a mist stripe and the party struck through. One stripe on the left edge and one wash behind the card, nothing else moves.

THE TINT EXISTED AND WAS SWITCHED OFF. The base layer had carried .lcard.s-* rules since the card was drawn, and the Ledger's list mode of v465 had a rule that set border-left:0 and background:none on every one of them, so no card in the Ledger had shown a colour since. The class itself knew one word, s-open, for both Open states, so Advance and Deferred could not have been told apart by any rule. The card's class now reads the engine's order in full: s-advance and s-deferred, beside the five it had. The pill inside a Deferred card takes brass so the word and the stripe agree; an Advance pill keeps the copper it had.

THE LAYER OWNS THE COLOUR, AS RULE 6 SAYS. The eight base rules and the list mode's off switch are retired from the master; the tint is written once in design/desk.css and rendered between the DESIGN markers by the sync. Nothing in the master's older layers names a state colour any more.

PROVED RED ON THE RENDERED CARD. The assertion plants six sales, one per state, renders the Ledger and reads each card's class and computed stripe through the cascade. Against the unchanged desk it named s124 carrying s-open where the engine says Open .
