Advance, the planted Advance rendering as s-open, and all six stripes resolving to transparent, the off switch's own value. Green now, and the check does not depend on the book holding every state on the day it runs, which it did not: no Deferred and no Pending sale stood on 5 Sep. tools/renderdiff.mjs shot every part before and after: the Ledger is the only part that moves, at either width.

t: THE ENTER PART'S PREVIEW ASKS THE ENGINE: THE FOURTH COPY OF THE STATE LADDER IS RETIRED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026: INCLUDE IT IN THE FIX. v491 put one state on each Ledger card and made it the engine's. The Enter part's preview, the Now and After pills a person reads before recording an amendment, still derived its state by hand: wbState took four scalars and re-ran the three-axis rule itself, so it knew nothing of unpriced, cancelled, in-kind, the zero-total rule or defaulted. The audit had measured it disagreeing with txStat on 18 of 130 sales; on today's book, with two declared defaults, it was 21 of 134. And its callers spelled a supplier default's preview 'Defaulted', a fifth word for one state.

wbState IS A WRAPPER NOW. It builds the row the four scalars describe, carries the flags of the row being amended when there is one, and asks the engine that reads every other row on the desk: txStat for a sale, poStat for a lot, because a lot's state is the lot engine's and the buy side of the form previews lots. Status is stripped on that side so poCash reads the cash given rather than 'paid' meaning the whole total, and the in-kind and advance fields are zeroed so the scalars are the whole truth of the hypothetical. The cancel preview, which hand-coded exactly what txStat's cancelled branch returns since v444, goes through that branch instead. The default preview goes through the engine and reads Default. wbStCls, a fifth copy of the class map that knew three of six states, is gone: the pills take the class the engine returns, the same one the Ledger uses.

PROVED RED ON THE DESK'S OWN ROWS. The assertion runs wbState over every sale on the book, as it stands, and demands the engine's word each time; against the unchanged desk it named 21 disagreements, the first three all in-kind rows previewing as Completed. A second assertion asks for a defaulted preview and demanded Default; it read Open . Advance. Both green. tools/renderdiff.mjs shot every part before and after: 32 of 34 shots identical, the Enter part the only one that moved, a 270 by 23 pixel strip at each width where the preview pills sit.

WHAT REMAINS OF T1.3. Six copies were counted. txStat is the authority; replayAmend feeds only the Ledger's collapse rule now and nothing reads it for a state; ledFinal, the card's cardCls and wbState all read the engine. Two small class maps are left, stateCls in the Ledger and wbPayCls in Enter, each mapping a word the engine already chose to a class name, and neither can produce a state.

t: THE LEDGER CARD CARRIES ONE STATE, THE ENGINE'S, AND A STEP IS ONE ROW
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026, ON A SCREENSHOT OF s107: a completed order whose card read PENDING on its opening line and OPEN . DEFERRED on its fulfilment step, and many others like it. Two things, and they had one cause. The card's states came from replayAmend, a second copy of the state ladder that sums cash and units across the trail. Line 10203 filtered Corrections out before the replay ran, so a delivery that arrived as a Correction, which is how s107's 6.25 unit arrived on 27 Aug, was invisible to it. Line 10209 took the opening line's state from the replay's FIRST step, which on an auto-built trail is "as booked", so every multi-step order opened as Pending whatever it had become. And ledFinal took the closing state from the replay's LAST step for anything not terminal. Three rows read wrong at the close (s103, s104, s107, each Completed in the engine), every multi-step order read wrong at the open, and s117 and s128 read Advance on the step where the engine has read Default since v488: the twin of that fold, unswept.

ONE STATE PER ENTRY, AND IT IS txStat'S. ledFinal is the engine's order and nothing else. The opening line carries it. The step lines and the closing line carry an empty state cell so the grid keeps its track, and nothing on them says what the entry is, because the entry says that once. replayAmend stays, because the collapse rule reads it for how long someone carried the other, a fact about the trail; nothing reads it for display any more. The same reader decided whether a card was completed at all (10230) and so whether it drew a close or collapsed, and it was swept in the same pass: s107 would otherwise have read Completed on its opening line above an unclosed trail. The Ledger's state filter goes through ledFinal too, so Default now matches the two rows it exists to find.

A STEP IS ONE ROW. Under 935px the card's grid had two rows for every line, "e date party qty price tot state" over "step step type prod act act act", because the opening line carries a party, a type, a product and a control. A step carries none of those, so it was spending a second row on four empty cells. A step's kind now takes the party's track and the cells a step never fills are not laid out; the closing line goes through the same builder and is classed as a step for the same reason. Above 935px nothing changes, and under 600px, the phone, a step still wraps, because four columns cannot hold a date, a kind, a quantity and a sum on one line.

PROVED ON THE RENDERED CARD, RED FIRST. The new assertion reads every card off the Ledger as rendered and demands exactly one non-empty state, the engine's, and none on a step. Against the unchanged desk it failed on s107 with the screenshot's own words, Pending / Open . Deferred. The v451 lot test asserted the old shape, paid ahead on the head and Completed on the close, and is rewritten to the new one. tools/renderdiff.mjs shot every part before and after: 32 of 34 shots identical, the Ledger the only part that moved at either width, shorter by 1,039px at 1280 for the close lines it no longer draws twice.

t: ONE SALE ON 5 SEP: CH5-KLC TAKES HALF A UNIT AT RM 75, COLLECTED AND PAID ON THE DAY
n: ONE ROW FOLDED ON HIS WORD, SALT, DATED 5 SEP 2026. CH5-KLC takes 0.5 unit for RM 75, RM 150 a unit, collected and paid in full on the day, so the row closes on arrival and leaves nothing outstanding. Row s134. Entered by the fold as the four rows of v489 were, after the phone entries did not arrive; the figure is his.

HIS SECOND COMPLETED ORDER AND HIS FIRST SINCE JULY. s024 of 17 Jul was 0.5 unit at RM 105; the 0.5 at RM 80 he agreed on 31 Jul was cancelled on 5 Aug. RM 150 a unit is RM 60 under the July rate and RM 23.69 over the 0.5-unit collected floor of RM 51.31. Costed at the shelf's RM 48, RM 24 against RM 75, RM 51 on the order at 68%: a small order carrying the RM 25 time charge comfortably, which is what the floor at this size is for.
THE SHELF GOES FROM 9.8 TO 9.3. The first movement off the 4 Sep count. Live credit is unchanged at RM 170: this row was paid on the day.

t: FOUR ROWS ON HIS WORD: CH5-OUG TAKES 12.5 BELOW THE FLOOR, THE SHELF IS COUNTED AT 9.8, AND CR3-DAM SETTLES BOTH ADVANCES
n: ENTERED BY THE FOLD ON HIS WORD, 05 SEP 2026, AFTER THE PHONE ENTRIES DID NOT ARRIVE. Twice in two days an entry recorded on the phone reached neither KV nor the drafter, and every figure here was dictated by him in the same conversation, so he chose to have the fold write them rather than queue them a third time. That choice has a cost and it is stated: no draft was made, so no drafter flag was raised, and the one row that would have carried one has its floor figure written into its own note instead. Each trail says on his word.

CH5-OUG TAKES 12.5 UNIT FOR RM 650, RM 52 A UNIT, COLLECTED AND PAID ON 4 SEP, RM 32.87 UNDER THE COLLECTED FLOOR. The desk's snapshot that morning put the floor for 12.5 unit at RM 682.87 collected and RM 692.87 delivered. Loaded cost is RM 52.63 a unit against RM 52.00 sold, so the order loses RM 0.63 a unit before the RM 25 timePerOrder charges for the work; at the shelf's RM 48 it shows RM 50 on the order at 7.7%, the thinnest salt margin this month. He took it with the figure in front of him. Beside the decision: CH5-OUG paid RM 600 for 12.5 unit on 20 Aug, so this is RM 50 more than his own last order at the size; he is the only customer buying 12.5 unit at wholesale, the other four such orders on the book running RM 750 to RM 1,300; and RM 650 is exactly SA5-BTR's live quote for 12.5 unit, so the lot goes out at what it costs to replace. Row s133.

THE SHELF IS COUNTED AT 9.8, AND THE COUNT IS ENTERED NET OF A SALE THE BOOK HAD ALREADY ROLLED. He counted 13.8 on 4 Sep, after CH5-OUG's 12.5 had gone and before CM4-MK's 4 did. v484 had already rolled CM4-MK's 4 off the shelf, and the fold sets the shelf to the counted figure rather than re-rolling what came after it, so 13.8 entered as counted would have stood 4 unit high and read as a surplus. The sale rolls first, 23 less 12.5 is 10.5, and the count then sets 9.8: a drift of 0.7, real shrinkage against the shelf as it stood, RM 36.84 at loaded cost, the first this book has booked since the 2 Sep count. COUNT_ON.salt moves to 4 Sep.

CR3-DAM PAID RM 160 ON 5 SEP AND BOTH HIS ADVANCES CLOSE. RM 80 on s116 of 27 Aug and RM 80 on s123 of 31 Aug, each a 1-unit advance with nothing paid; the units went out on their own dates and nothing moves on the shelf. Both rows read Completed. CR3-DAM comes off the receivable and out of the cap breach he had stood in since 31 Aug, 2 unit against a retail cap of 1, and s116 settles one day before it would have hit the 10-day term. Live credit falls from RM 330 to RM 170, CN6-WM's RM 110 and CM4-MK's RM 60; the next row to reach the term is CN6-WM's s124 on 9 Sep.

t: A DECLARED DEFAULT PROVISIONS IN FULL: CA4-DAM'S RM 260 IS WRITTEN OFF, AS SF6-KLC'S RM 750 WAS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 05 SEP 2026: CA4-DAM's outstanding is defaulted, with the same treatment as SF6-KLC, and he is not banned. Two rows carry it: s117, 1 unit for RM 100 handed over on 28 Aug and flagged defaulted on 2 Sep when he said the money would not come, and s128, 1.5 unit for RM 160 collected on 2 Sep, flagged today on his word through applyAmend so the row carries the trail a gate-folded Correction would have written. THE TREATMENT IS THE SUPPLIER'S, MIRRORED. supplierReceivable has said since 31 Jul that a write-off keeps the gross and zeroes the net: the provision stays charged, and the desk stops counting the money as expected cash. The sale side had no such rule at all.

THE FLAG WAS SET AND NOTHING READ IT. txStat ignored defaulted on a sale, so s117 stood as Open . Advance with the flag on it, the Ledger's Default filter could match nothing, and every net-of-ladder figure priced a debt he had written off at the ladder rate for its age: RM 160 two days old provisioned at 0%, counted at face. poStat has honoured the identical field on a lot since it was written. Two sides of one book, disagreeing about one word. txStat now reads Default after cancelled and after In-Kind; pay and deliv stay as computed, because unpaid and delivered are still true.

ONE READER, NINE SITES, AND THE SUPPLIER'S SEVEN LEFT ALONE. saleProvRate(s,days) in engine/position.mjs is the ladder for a live row and 1 for a declared default, and it is the only place the sale side reads that fact. The nine net-of-ladder readers of a sale's advance go through it: the walk's ar, the thirty-day cash in, the monthly provisioning, the ageing chart, the phone's ageing payload, the Order book's cash table, the forecast's cash-in leg, Today's chase action and the Order book's claim rows. The seven supplier readers keep calling provRate, because that side has its own record and its own rule. The sweep was by grep on provRate( over the desk region, and what is left is the wrapper and the supplier: it was not done by the twelve-name list the first design carried, which the alias outstandingOf=txAdvance had hidden twelve more readers behind.

WHAT MOVES, MEASURED ON THE BUILT DESK. Salt's receivable list still holds 6 rows and its gross is still RM 590.00, of which CA4-DAM's RM 260.00 stays on it: that is the record of what was traded and lost, the numerator of provision = arGross - ar, and what pxParty reads to penalise his next quote. Net of the ladder is RM 242.50: the RM 260 now counts for nothing. The IFRS statement's expected credit loss, which is arGross - ar, rises by the same amount and feeds opex, which is the loss landing where an accountant would put it. THE PRICE BOARD DOES NOT MOVE, at any size. Since v326 the ask is the ladder and engine/pricing.mjs never reads badDebt; badDebtPct reaches riskRates and a retired figure at the foot of the Price part, and nothing else. The first design claimed the loss would load the price, and the adversary that measured it false is why that sentence is not in this note.

PROVED RED BEFORE GREEN, ON THE REAL WALK. Three assertions failed against the unchanged engine, each for the reason the fix exists: a defaulted sale read Open . Advance, saleProvRate was undefined, and a two-row walk netted RM 235 where RM 75 was right. Four neighbours passed before and after, so the gate opened for one thing: the same row without the flag is still an advance, cancelled still wins, gross still keeps both rows, and a defaulted lot still reads Default. The v445 date regression had pinned s117 by rid as its victim; a defaulted row provisions in full whatever its date, so its four bad dates and the control would all have produced one ar and the differential would have passed while proving nothing. It picks a live, dated, unpaid advance now.

t: EVERY ROW ON THE LEDGER IS DATED, AND THE CHECK THAT SAYS SO CAN NOW FAIL
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 04 SEP 2026: no undated row may stand on the ledger. Three carried no date at all. s108 CN6-WM 1.5 unit RM185 is dated 22 Aug, the day v334 describes the order at RM123.33 a unit. s109 CS6-PER 6.25 unit RM350 is dated 20 Aug, which v381 states outright when it records that two orders went to him after the 30 Jul ban, s068 on 07 Aug and the cancelled s109 on 20 Aug. s119 CY2-NIL 2.5 unit RM230 is dated 28 Aug, which the row already carried as agreedOn and which v486 upheld the same day against a query putting it at 31 Aug. NO FIGURE MOVES. All three have nothing paid and nothing delivered, so revenue, cost, the shelf, every receivable and every party's standing are exactly what they were. What changes is that the desk, the Journal and a statement stop printing three rows with no date on them.

THE TRAIL IS WRITTEN BY applyAmend, NOT BY HAND, so each row carries the mod line and the amend entry a Correction folded through the gate would have produced: "corrected on 2026-09-04: date (unset) to ...". That matters because the three could not have been folded through the gate until the same day. All three were cancelled, and the fold refused every amendment against a cancelled row, so from the moment each was cancelled there was no route to date it. The narrowing that opened that road is the commit before this one, and it is what makes this fold possible rather than a hand edit standing in for one.

AND THE CHECK CI RUNS NOW FAILS ON AN UNDATED ROW RATHER THAN SORTING IT LAST. tools/sort-ledger.mjs has always put an undated row at the end, which kept the order stable and accommodated the row for ever: that is how three of them sat there, one since 24 Aug. The sort is unchanged, because it is still what holds the order steady mid-fold. What changed is --check, which is the thing ci.yml runs: it reports any row carrying no date and exits 1. Proved in both directions by spawning the real tool, not by importing a function: the book as it stands passes, and a copy of that same book with one date removed fails with exit 1 and names the row.

FOUR ASSERTIONS HAD BEEN USING THE FAULT AS THEIR FIXTURE, AND ALL FOUR ARE REBUILT. Dating the rows turned the suite red in four places, every one of them a test that only passed because the book was wrong. The v347 guard test pinned the real cancelled CS6-PER row and the literal key CS6-PER|undefined|350, so dating s109 moved the key and the fulfilment was then refused as "no row on the book matches" rather than by the cancelled guard: a broken guard would have read as a pass. It owns a synthetic target now, which is the v359 lesson arriving for the third time. The Ledger's date-descending test demanded blanks > 0, so it required a fault to exist; it asserts the ordering itself instead. The statement's undated-sort loop ran over an empty set and passed while proving nothing, the assertion that cannot fail, and now asserts the invariant directly. The extract in ledger/ledger.json was regenerated.

t: THE QUERY AGAINST s119'S DATE IS ANSWERED IN THE ROW, AND THE BOOK IS UPHELD
n: HIS CORRECTION, 04 SEP 2026: the 28 Aug order is paid and delivered, and the pending one now cancelled was placed on 31 Aug. v485 declined to rewrite the date on a recollection and folded the cancellation with the question left open, which was right at the time and is the wrong thing to leave in a ledger. The check is done and the book is upheld: the 31 Aug artefact is an amendment to s119, not a second order. It is a Fulfilment on s119 for RM 230 and 2.5 unit, queued from the phone at 19:23 on 31 Aug and dated 1 Sep, which v464 folded so that the order read paid and delivered, and which v467 withdrew two days later on his word that it was still pending. Both halves of the query therefore describe a state this row has already been through and left.

NO ROW IS MISSING, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. D1 holds three CY2-NIL drafts in the whole of its history, the original sale, the 31 Aug fulfilment and the 4 Sep cancellation, and no refused entry for the party at all, so nothing was queued and lost. The book holds four CY2-NIL rows, and v464's own note calls s119 the fourth: 11 Aug, 18 Aug, 26 Aug and this one. There is no fifth order to find.

THE ANSWER IS WRITTEN INTO THE ROW, NOT ONLY INTO THIS ENTRY. A question raised against a row belongs beside the row, because the next person to read s119 will read the ledger and not the changelog. v485's entry is left exactly as it was: the date really was unresolved when it was written, and rewriting a version entry to look wiser than it was would cost more than it saves.

t: AN ENTRY THE CLOUD NEVER TOOK IS NO LONGER CLEARED AS COMMITTED, AND CY2-NIL'S UNFULFILLED ORDER IS WITHDRAWN
n: THE v482 AUDIT'S CRITIC TRACED A LOST SALE, AND IT WAS THERE. The load clears a held entry once QUEUE_COMMITTED has passed it, on the reading that the watermark passing an entry means the fold has taken it. That is a fact about the LEDGER, not about this device. An entry recorded with no signal is held in localStorage, never reaches KV, is never drafted and never folded; when a fold elsewhere then carried the watermark past its stamp, the next load dropped it and said nothing. Proved red against the shipped filter before a line was changed: one sale of RM 360, one load, gone, with a control showing the same entry above the watermark surviving.

THE RULE NOW ASKS BOTH QUESTIONS. An entry goes only when the ledger has folded past it AND this device saw the server acknowledge it. qSentThrough is the newest stamp this device has had confirmed, and because qPayload() sends the WHOLE queue every time, one confirmed post covers every entry then held. qKeepOnLoad is a named function so the rule is run rather than grepped for, which is what v482 taught on the very poll that made this reachable.

THE MARK IS SEEDED FROM THE WATERMARK, NOT FROM NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE CARE IN IT. Defaulting to nothing-was-sent would retain entries the ledger already carries, and applyOverlay() folds a held entry into the figures, so the desk would have shown those sales TWICE: a wrong figure in place of a silent loss, which is no bargain. Seeding at the watermark keeps today's treatment of what is already folded and asks only what is recorded from now on to earn its clearance. The seed is WRITTEN on first use, because re-seeding from a watermark that had since moved would drop the very entry this protects.

RETAINING IT FOR ONE LOAD WAS NOT ENOUGH, AND ONLY DRIVING IT SHOWED THAT. The first fix kept the stranded entry, then qInit posted the held queue on the next open, the server took it, the mark advanced over it, and the load after that cleared it. Meanwhile the drafter skips everything at or below the watermark by design, so that post could never become a row: the sale was still lost, one load later and just as quietly. An entry that survives while the fold has already passed it is now flagged stuck, kept for ever, and named on screen, because only a person can settle it. Two further faults in the fix itself were caught the same way: q.at>null reads false rather than throwing, so the terser rule silently dropped the entry when the watermark was missing, and the notice counted only what had just become stuck, so it showed once and vanished while the entry sat there.

BOTH DELIVERED ROUTES ARE MARKED, SWEPT RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE NEXT VERSION. qDownload writes the file the daily run reads, which is the same guarantee the server route gives; unmarked, a download-route entry that WAS folded would be retained by the new rule and shown twice. The clipboard route is deliberately not marked, because copying is not delivery.

ONE ROW FOLDED WITH IT, AND ITS DATE IS LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE. A pending CY2-NIL order of 2.5 unit at RM 230, never delivered and never paid, is withdrawn: no cash and no stock move, and 2.5 unit of committed salt returns to the shelf. The row carries agreedOn 28 Aug, he states the pending order was placed on 31 Aug and that the 28 Aug order was delivered and paid, and the book holds neither a 31 Aug row nor a paid 28 Aug one. The cancellation is not in doubt, so it is folded; the date wants a Correction through the gate and is not rewritten here on a recollection.

t: ONE SALE ON 4 SEP: CM4-MK TAKES 4 UNIT AT THE SIZE IT ALWAYS PAYS AND LEAVES RM 60 OWING
n: One row folded. CM4-MK takes 4 unit of salt on 4 Sep at RM 360, RM 90/unit, delivered in full on the day against RM 300 paid. Costed on the shelf's own RM 48/unit, so RM 192 of cost and RM 168 on the order, 46.7%.

The rate flag reads low against the wrong comparison. The drafter measured RM 90/unit against CM4-MK's RM 110/unit median across seven orders and called it 18.2% under. That median is dominated by its 2 unit orders, which have gone out at RM 110/unit four times out of four. Both of this party's earlier 4 unit orders were struck at this grade, RM 360 on 10 Aug and RM 380 on 24 Aug, so RM 90/unit is the 10 Aug price repeated and not a discount. It clears the live floor for 4 unit, RM 245.52 delivered and RM 235.52 collected, by a wide margin.

The advance is real and it is a first. RM 60 of the RM 360 is unpaid with all 4 unit already delivered. Every one of CM4-MK's seven earlier orders settled in full on the day, so this is the first balance the party has carried and the first thing to chase on the next visit.

Not a replay. The row matches the 10 Aug sale in party, size and total and differs only in date. The 10 Aug row is fully paid and unamended; this is a fresh order, and the fold's replay guard passed on the date for that reason.

t: TWO ROWS ON 3 SEP: A 25 UNIT LOT FROM SA5-BTR LANDS AND CS6-BS TAKES 2
n: TWO ROWS FOLDED, BOTH SALT, BOTH DATED 3 SEP 2026. A lot in and a sale out: 25 unit from SA5-BTR for RM 1,200, and 2 unit to CS6-BS for RM 200. Both were queued from the phone at 09:50 KL on 4 Sep and approved a minute later, and the drafter raised no flag on either.

THE LOT HOLDS RM 48 A UNIT, SO THE COST BASIS DOES NOT MOVE. RM 1,200 for 25 unit is RM 50 under the RM 1,250 the 20 Aug live quote puts on this tier, and it is the second lot running at that rate after p019 of 31 Aug. The desk's own stockCostFor('salt') already returns RM 48 against p019, so the shelf cost is unchanged at RM 48 and no override was needed on the sale beside it. Paid in full and received in full on the day, so the lot closes on arrival.

THE SALE SITS RM 59.13 CLEAR OF THE FLOOR AND IS THE TAPER DOING ITS WORK. The desk's own ladder puts the floor for 2 unit delivered at RM 140.87, and this went out delivered, so that is the floor that applies. Costed at the shelf's RM 48 a unit that is RM 96 against RM 200, RM 104 on the order at 52%. CS6-BS has six salt rows before this one, five priced between RM 95 and RM 126.67 a unit and a free unit on 24 Aug, every one of them 1 to 1.5 unit. RM 100 a unit on 2 unit is his largest salt order to date at his lowest rate, which is what the ladder expects on the size rather than a concession.

THE SHELF GOES FROM 4 TO 27 AND THE 2 SEP COUNT STILL STANDS. Both movements fall after that count, so they roll the stated shelf rather than restate it and COUNT_ON is untouched. The lot was bought against a shelf of 4 unit, the lowest it has stood since the count, which is the reason to read a second RM 1,200 lot three days after the first as a restock and not a replay: the dates differ, the queue ids differ, and the fold's replay guard passed. Against the 27 the only standing commitment is still s119, 2.5 unit to CY2-NIL, pending and undated.

t: A QUEUED ENTRY NO LONGER BLOCKS THE RELOAD THAT WOULD CLEAR IT
n: HIS REPORT, 03 SEP 2026: after approving a row on the phone, the other tabs did not move. The approval itself was faultless, and the whole chain behind it ran: the row was staged, folded as v481, deployed and marked committed within minutes. What did not happen was the phone loading the build that carried it, so the Approve tab moved on while every ledger tab held the figures from before the fold.

THE FRESHNESS POLL WAS REFUSING TO RELOAD BECAUSE AN ENTRY WAS QUEUED, AND THAT REFUSAL WAS CIRCULAR. The ten-second tick reloads only when the desk is idle, and idle() counted any entry in the local queue as unsent work. In cloud mode that queue is emptied only by a LOAD whose QUEUE_COMMITTED has passed the entry. So recording an entry disabled the auto-reload until the very reload it was blocking, which is exactly the case the poll exists for: a fold lands, the build id moves, and the desk offers a chip nobody had been told to watch for.

NOTHING IS LOST BY RELOADING WITH A QUEUE, WHICH IS WHY THE CLAUSE COULD SIMPLY GO. saveQueue() writes localStorage before it posts anything, and the load reads it straight back, so a held entry survives a reload and the tick retries its post afterwards. The two guards that do protect something are untouched: a focused field and an open dialogue both still stand the reload down, because those are the only states a reload would actually throw away.

THE RULE IS NOW RUN RATHER THAN READ. The assertion calls the shipped idle() with a stubbed document instead of grepping for the deleted line: a queued entry reads idle, a focused field does not, an open dialogue does not, and a throw reads as not idle rather than as idle. Proved red against the old rule before it was trusted.

t: ONE SALE ON 3 SEP: CM6-PJ TAKES 3 UNIT COLLECTED AND PAYS ON THE DAY
n: ONE ROW FOLDED, SALT, DATED 3 SEP 2026. 3 unit collected by CM6-PJ for RM 270, RM 90 a unit, paid in full and taken in full on the day, so the row closes on arrival and leaves nothing outstanding. Queued from the phone at 00:50 KL on 3 Sep and approved at 14:50 the same day. The drafter raised no flag on it.

THE COST IS THE SHELF'S OWN, SO NO OVERRIDE WAS NEEDED. The draft carries RM 48 a unit, which is what the desk's own stockCostFor('salt') returns against p019, the 25 unit lot bought from SA5-BTR for RM 1,200 on 31 Aug and the latest on the book. That is RM 144 of cost against RM 270, RM 126 on the order at 46.7%.

THE RATE SITS WELL CLEAR OF THE FLOOR AND IS THE TAPER DOING ITS WORK. The desk's own ladder puts the floor for 3 unit at RM 183.80 collected and RM 193.80 delivered; RM 270 is RM 86.20 above the collected floor, which is the one that applies here. Against his own history, CM6-PJ has one prior row, s100 of 21 Aug, 1 unit at RM 100, itself restated from RM 120 with R3 credited. RM 90 a unit is below that rate on three times the size, which is what the ladder expects rather than a concession.

THE SHELF GOES FROM 7 TO 4 AND THE 2 SEP COUNT STILL STANDS. The entry was queued after the 12:05 watermark that batch carried, so these 3 unit come off the count of 10.5 rather than sitting inside it. Against 4 unit the only standing commitment is still s119, 2.5 unit to CY2-NIL, pending and undated.

t: TWO SALES ON 2 SEP: CM4-MK PAYS ON THE DAY, CA4-DAM TAKES A SECOND CREDIT
n: TWO ROWS FOLDED, BOTH SALT, BOTH DATED 2 SEP 2026. 1.5 unit collected by CA4-DAM for RM 160, and 2 unit delivered to CM4-MK for RM 220, paid in full on the day. Both were queued from the phone at 12:05 and approved at 12:07. Both are costed at RM 48 a unit, the shelf's own figure off p019, so neither draft was carrying a stale rate and no cost override was needed.

CA4-DAM'S ROW IS AN ADVANCE FOUR DAYS AFTER HIS DEFAULT, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING TO READ ON THIS VERSION. 1.5 unit went out with nothing paid. His 28 Aug row s117 still carries RM 100 handed over and unpaid, marked defaulted on his own word on 2 Sep, and the note on it reads that it was the first credit in thirteen orders and the last. This is the fourteenth order and the second credit. The drafter raised the advance flag and asked for the credit cap; it was approved two minutes later, so the decision was taken with the flag in front of him. The book now shows RM 260 out to that party, RM 100 of it defaulted and RM 160 of it fresh.

THE PRICES THEMSELVES ARE UNREMARKABLE. CA4-DAM at RM 106.67 a unit sits above his median of RM 100 and inside his own range, which tops out at RM 116.67 on 26 Jul, and clears the collected floor of RM 104.40 at that size. CM4-MK at RM 110 a unit is exactly what he has paid on each of his three previous two-unit orders and exactly his median, and clears the delivered floor of RM 140.87 on the order. Returns are RM 88 at 55.0% and RM 124 at 56.4%. The drafter flagged nothing on CM4-MK.
THE SHELF FALLS FROM 10.5 TO 7 UNIT. The one commitment standing against it is s119, 2.5 unit to CY2-NIL, still pending and undated. Nothing landed, so the cost basis stays at RM 48.

t: THE RETIRED PRICE LOCK NO LONGER BREAKS A RULE; A LOT THAT MOVES THE RATE IS A WATCH
n: HIS QUESTION, 02 SEP 2026: what is this rule that salt keeps on breaking. The v233 boundary Board unpriced compared the locked pricing snapshot against the latest lot and raised a breach whenever a newer lot had landed, with the advice to re-lock on the Pricing tab. v280 switched the lock off on his instruction and the board has priced live off the latest lot ever since, but the check kept reading the dead snapshot: salt's lock still names the 28 Jul lot, so every lot since 6 Aug read as a breach, and Today carried a red row for a retired policy pointing at a control the cloud desk does not have.

GATED ON THE LOCK, AND WHAT THE RULE WAS FOR SURVIVES AS A WATCH. With the lock on, the breach is exactly what it was. With it off, the desk raises a watch for the week after a lot lands that moves the rate, saying what moved: today, 25 unit at RM 48 landed 2 Sep, from RM 50. A purchase is the moment a price should move, and the row asks for the board to be read once rather than shouting until a snapshot nobody uses is rewritten. It prices nothing: the two rates are the lots' own.

PROVED RED FIRST. The v478 master run in the same harness raises the breach; this one raises the watch with the move in it. The suite gains three assertions, the watch's expectation computed from the book and today's date rather than from the desk, so on a week with no lot the section proves the absence instead. The queue was asked first: nothing pending, nothing approved and uncommitted.

t: THE 25-UNIT LOT WAS PURCHASED ON 31 AUGUST, AND THE COUNT'S CAVEAT CLOSES
n: HIS CORRECTION, IN CHAT, 02 SEP 2026: the 25 unit lot was purchased on 31 August. p019, SA5-BTR, 25 unit for RM1200, had been booked on 2 Sep from his dictation that morning. Its date moves to 31 Aug by a Correction drafted through the gate, approved on his word and folded here; the row keeps its receipt and payment on 2 Sep, because he stated the purchase date and nothing else, so the lot still lands on the shelf on the morning of the count. The drafter's flag is the one worth reading: money and stock had already moved against this row, so redating it moves when that counts as having happened, and here it moves the purchase into August's books and the receipt stays in September's.

THE COUNT'S CAVEAT CLOSES. v473 left open whether the lot was on the shelf when he counted 10.5 that morning. It was: bought two days before and received that morning, it had been stacked by the time the count was taken fifty seconds after the CF5-WM sale. So 10.5 is the shelf, the drift against the roll is a real 6.25 unit, and it books as shrinkage across every unit sold.

TWO REPAIRS TO THE LAPTOP ROAD, found by driving it. A draft staged from this machine carried no amends or amend_kind, so the fold read every laptop Correction as a nameless amendment and would have refused it; both inserts carry them now, as the Worker's does. And the INSERT went to wrangler on the command line, where Windows reads the | in an order key as a pipe and the staging failed with a shell error; writes go through a file now, which is safe because a write wants no rows back.

t: LEGIBILITY: A POINT UP ON EVERY FIGURE AND LABEL, A POINT AND MORE LEADING ON PROSE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026: consider easier legibility. v472 set the identity's type at the design system's sizes, which were drawn for a brand page read at leisure, and the desk is read for a figure at a stall. So every mono figure and label steps up half a point to a point: KPI labels 10 to 11, their figures 22 to 24, table heads 10 to 11, tables 12.5 to 13, the rail's tabs 10.5 to 11.5, the parts strip 11 to 11.5, buttons 10.5 to 11, chips and tags half a point each, the ledger's summary figures 17 to 18, and nothing on a control or a label below 10 on a desk or 11 on the phone. Prose steps up a point with more leading: the body 14 to 15 at 1.6, leads and descriptions 13 to 14, insights 13.5 to 14.5, notes 13 to 14, the journal 13.5 to 14.5, actions' reasons and observations 12.5 to 13.5.

TRACKING EASES AND RUNNING PROSE LIGHTENS. Mono caps at 0.14 to 0.22em read as a texture at a distance and as a puzzle up close; the longer labels drop to 0.08 to 0.14em, the eyebrow to 0.18em. Running prose, which the layer had set in mist light, moves one step lighter to #b4bcc2 through the desk's own --mut token, so a paragraph reads without leaning in while labels keep their mist.

THE ONE TABLE THAT MUST FIT IS HELD WHERE IT WAS MEASURED. v393 measured the board at three pixels inside a 325px card at 375. It keeps 12.5px on the phone while every other table goes to 13; measured again after this fold: the board's width against its card, the page never wider than 375, every rail tab on one line and 44 tall with the menu open. The queue was asked first: nothing pending.

t: THE v281 COLOUR RULES AND THE RAIL'S OLD ACTIVE TAB ARE RETIRED
n: THE THIRD RETIREMENT FOLD, AND THE LAST OF THE MATERIAL LAYERS. v281's colour rules go: the primary's gold glow and its hover, the active tab's cast, the ice glow on a meter's fill, the severity glow on an action's bar, the row hover, the accent focus ring with its colour-mix, and the fade colour on both scroll hints. With them, the base rail's active tab (the gradient fill, the dark count) and its hover, which the layer draws as glass with a brass hairline. What v281 owns and keeps is its motion: the section settle, the staggered children, the press transforms, the meters' fill-from-zero.

MEASURED: 34 shots against v475, all the same within the noise floor; the base layer's hover and focus states are not in a still render and were read instead. The queue was asked first: nothing pending, nothing newly approved.

WHAT IS LEFT, AND IS NOT A MATERIAL LAYER. The base layer still declares a colour inside most component rules (a tag's fill, a tier's glow, a badge's gradient), each overridden by the layer. They are the original desk, not a material pass, and retiring them is tidiness with a rising risk per rule; they are listed as a later fold rather than taken now.

t: THE v108 FROST AND THE v213 MATERIAL ARE RETIRED; THE LAYER OWNS THE MATERIAL
n: THE SECOND RETIREMENT FOLD, AND IT TAKES THE MATERIAL. The v108 frost on the panes, the rail's old gradient and blur, the frosted table backings, the translucent inputs and pills, the v109 radii v213 had already restated, the v111 heading bar and its gloss, the v213 token block, its material fill, its well and veil colours, the dropdown fills and the hover fills: every one of them a rule section 4 or 8 of design/desk.css re-declares in full. The base rail keeps its geometry (sticky, its own scrollbar) and loses its material.

TWO THINGS MOVED RATHER THAN WENT, because the layer had not carried them. The frost itself (24px blur, saturate 1.15, on the nine pane classes v108 frosted and no others) and the 10px blur on a sticky table head now live in the layer, with the two fallbacks for a renderer with no backdrop-filter and for prefers-reduced-transparency. A pane inside a pane stays flat by the v213 never-frost rule, which is structural and stays.

MEASURED, AND ONE ACCIDENT RETIRED ON PURPOSE. 32 of 34 shots against v474 read the same. The Ledger and Enter parts did not, and the cause was run down rather than waved through: v108 had frosted .note along with the panes and given it a pane's shadow and gloss, v213's never-frost list omitted .note, and v472 cancelled its background and border but not the shadow, so a note with no box was casting a 40px shadow and saturating what lay behind it. With that accident put back by hand the two parts read 0 pixels apart, so everything else is the same; with it gone, 43,000 pixels under the queue card's note and 19,000 on the ledger's move by up to twelve units, which is the shadow lifting. The layer now says so in as many words: a note casts no shadow and carries no frost. The queue was asked first: nothing pending, nothing newly approved.

t: THE PAGE-LEVEL COLOUR SYSTEM v472 REPLACED IS RETIRED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026: retire the older material layers, in smaller folds. This is the first, and it takes the page-level colour system alone: the twenty-three per-view accent rules, the root palette that named ice, gold, violet, green and crimson, the register palette and both of its body grounds, the three orb rules and the third orb itself, the diamond logo that left the markup at v472, and the two headline gradients. 5,231 bytes of rules the v472 layer had already overridden in full, and the ground now has one owner: section 2 of design/desk.css.

NOTHING VISIBLE MOVED, AND THAT IS MEASURED IN PIXELS. tools/renderdiff.mjs renders every part at 1280 and 375 with motion off, the stamp and the version hidden and the journal's version entries removed, and compares two renders shot for shot. It was proved red first: brass turned to red in one rule read as differing on all 34 shots, and two renders of the same build read identical on 32 with 3 pixels of chart antialiasing on two, which is the noise floor. This fold reads as the same on every shot against v473.
THE QUEUE WAS ASKED FIRST. Nothing pending; the three approved rows of the morning are the v473 fold, and the deploy marks them committed when it lands.

WHAT STAYS FOR THE NEXT FOLDS. The v108 frost and its gradients, the v213 material fills and fallbacks, the v281 motion and colour rules, and the colour declarations inside component rules that desk.css overrides one by one. Each is its own fold, each measured the same way.

t: CF5-WM JOINS THE ROSTER AND BUYS TWO, AND THE SALT SHELF IS COUNTED AT 10.5
n: THREE ROWS FROM THE PHONE, APPROVED ON THE DESK WITHIN A MINUTE OF EACH OTHER ON 02 SEP. CF5-WM is registered as a customer who buys direct; the name and the place are typed at the laptop and never travel. Then CF5-WM's first order: 2 unit of salt for RM230, RM115 a unit, paid and collected on the day, costed at RM48 from the shelf's latest lot (p019, SA5-BTR, landed the same morning). That is above the board's two-unit ask of RM100 a unit and clear of every floor, so the margin on the order is 58%.

THE COUNT WINS, AND IT IS 8.25 BELOW THE ROLL. He counted 10.5 unit of salt on hand on 02 Sep against 18.75 on the book, and approved the count with that gap in front of him. A count always wins: the stated shelf is 10.5 and COUNT_ON.salt moves to 02 Sep. The 2 unit to CF5-WM had already left the roll, so measured after the sale the drift is 6.25 unit, and it books as shrinkage across every unit sold. ONE THING TO SETTLE ON THE NEXT COUNT: the 25-unit lot p019 landed the same morning, so if the shelf was counted before it was stacked, the true figure is 35.5 and the drift runs the other way. The book carries what he approved; the note is here so the next count is read against it.

FOLDED ON HIS RULE OF 02 SEP 2026: a version bump asks about the queue first and folds what is approved. This fold is the ledger alone; the retirement of the older material layers follows it as its own version, measured against this book.

t: THE DESK IN THE SALT IDENTITY
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026: redesign the whole desk with the Salt design system. The identity of 29 Aug (obsidian ground, brass and copper light, glass once, figures in mono and sentences in the display face) is now the desk's own. It arrives as a LAST-WINS LAYER, as v213 and v281 did: not one class is renamed, not one figure moves, and every geometry rule the phone passes stands. Two blocks at the foot of the stylesheet, both generated and both proved by CI: DESIGN base is the design system's stylesheet vendored from Code/salt-ds, and DESIGN desk binds the desk's own vocabulary to its tokens. tools/designsync.mjs pulls, syncs and checks them, the way engine.mjs and booksync.mjs do.

ONE ACCENT. The seven view hues are retired: a view is known by its name and its figures. Brass leads, copper marks the exception, and three words carry meaning and nothing else does: verdigris for what is settled or owed to you, ember for what you owe, defaulted or breached, steel for what is pending. The two books keep a hue each, salt the pale one and oil the golden one, declared in the book as PRODUCTS.accent, which is where the extract read them.

EVERY COLOUR LITERAL IN THE DESK'S OWN CSS AND JS WAS MAPPED, NOT RESTYLED AROUND. 252 hex and 180 rgba values, from the ice, gold, violet, green and crimson families into the identity, with the generated ENGINE, BOOK and GEO blocks held out byte for byte. The charts therefore draw in brass, salt, verdigris, ember and steel without a second palette, and Chart.js is told once that figures are mono and hairlines are brass. The mapping table is in docs/DESIGN.md.

THE MARK. The crystal replaces the diamond glyph in the rail, the bar and the favicon, and the home-screen icons are the brand's own from salt-ds/brand. The rail is glass with a brass hairline; a tab is mono caps and the active one is glass, not a gradient. The one filled control is the brass-to-copper pill, kept for what books or produces; everything that navigates is a ghost.

NO WEB FONT, BY THE CSP. The desk loads nothing, so Fraunces and JetBrains Mono are asked for and Georgia and Consolas answer. The design system's font import moved out of its styles.css into fonts.css for exactly this, and the pull refuses a stylesheet that carries a remote import.

PROVED BY DRIVING IT. Rendered at 1280 and at 375 with the rail floated out of its button; no console error; every tab measures 44; the ledger's filters, the board, the order book, the map and Today all read in the new material. A new section proves the two blocks are their files, that no retired hex survives outside the generated blocks, that the crystal is in the rail and the books carry the identity's hues; its regexes were proved red against the v471 master before they were trusted.

t: THE LEDGER IS KEYED ENTRIES ONLY, AND THE PROSE IS IN THE JOURNAL
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026. Prose goes into a journal; the ledger should be key in, key in, key in, done. The note column, the captions on collapsed orders, the notes on trail steps and the correction strip all leave the sheet. A ledger line is now an E-number, a step, a date, a type, a product, a party, a quantity, a price, a total with its margin, a state and the update control. Eleven columns, and the two narrower tiers re-flow the same eleven.

FLAT. No card, no coloured rail, no pill: a hairline between orders, a dashed line before a closing line, and coloured text where a state, a type or a step kind was a pill. The update control is a text link. The sheet reads down a column the way a sheet does.

THE JOURNAL, BESIDE IT IN THE BOOK. A new part. Every note a person wrote on a row, every note on a step of its trail with its cross-references, and every correction strip with its claims read back, dated, newest first, each linked to its row by E-number and rid so a tap lands on the line. Below them, the version entries the folds wrote. A search narrows both lists. Nothing in the Journal is computed: it repeats what was written and comments on nothing.
ONE SOURCE FOR THE ORDER. The ledger and the journal mint E-numbers from the same ledgerAll(), so E12 in the journal is E12 on the sheet. The extract lists jrnF as desk state.

PROVED BY DRIVING IT. Nothing prose-shaped on the sheet; every noted row has an entry; newest first and undated last; every entry names rid and E-number; row notes, step notes and corrections all present; every version entry present; the link lands on the row; the search narrows to one E-number. The v451 correction-strip check reads the Journal now, and v461 finds a step through its card's party rather than its note. 1187 assertions across 92 sections.

t: CA4-DAM DEFAULTS ON THE 28 AUG UNIT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026. The 1 unit handed over to CA4-DAM on 28 Aug for RM100, nothing paid, is marked defaulted: the money will not come. It was his first credit in thirteen orders and the row's note said so. A Correction sets the flag; the row keeps its figures so the loss is visible where it happened. Drafted through the gate, approved on his word, folded from the staged batch.
WHAT MOVES. Owed to you falls from RM370 to RM270 across three rows (CR3-DAM twice, CN6-WM). The unit is out and stays out; nothing returns to the shelf.

t: v468 REVERSED: THE CZ4-MK RM20 PAYABLE STANDS AGAIN
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026, MINUTES AFTER v468. The withdrawal of the RM20 over-tender payable on CZ4-MK (s114) read his message wrongly and is reversed: the payable is back on the book as it stood at v467, since 26 Aug, and the row note is as it was. Nothing else in v468 touched the book.

t: THE CZ4-MK RM20 IS NOT A PAYABLE: IT WAS NEVER TENDERED
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026. The RM20 recorded on 26 Aug as an over-tender on CZ4-MK's oil order (s114) and moved to a customer payable on 28 Aug is withdrawn: the RM20 was never handed over, so there is nothing to refund and nothing to set off. RM130 was paid for RM130. The payable is removed from the book and the row's note says so; the 28 Aug correction of cash from 150 to 130 stands, because that is what was paid.
REFUNDS PAYABLE NOW STAND AT NIL. The one other record, CZ6-WM's RM80 refunded on 31 Jul, is history and untouched.

SF6-KLC'S LOT IS ALREADY WRITTEN OFF. p003 (12.5 unit, RM750, 8 Jul) has carried the default since it was recorded and the desk counts nothing open on it; a summary read to him on 2 Sep listed it among lots not received because it did not filter the write-off. No change to the book.

t: SEVEN DAYS DICTATED: A LOT LANDS, THE SHELF COMES BACK ABOVE ZERO, s119 IS PENDING AGAIN AND FOUR ROWS MOVE TO 31 AUG
n: DICTATED IN A CODE SESSION ON 02 SEP 2026 AND FOLDED ON HIS WORD. Nine entries went through the same drafter the phone uses, run against the master's own book because the mirror's reads are key-gated from the laptop, staged into D1 as pending, approved on his instruction and folded from the staged batch. Every cost is the RM50 shelf; every flag the drafter raised is in the row's note.

THE MISSING LOT. 25 unit from SA5-BTR for RM1200, RM48 a unit, paid and received on 2 Sep. This is the lot the v464 roll said was unrecorded when the stated shelf went below zero. The shelf goes 0.25 to 18.75: 6.5 unit out across five sales and this fulfilment, 25 in. The cost basis moves from RM50 to RM48, the newest lot, two ringgit under the 26 Aug lot and eight under the 18 Aug one.

s119 IS PENDING AGAIN, AND THE v464 FULFILMENT IS WITHDRAWN. CY2-NIL's 2.5 unit for RM230 has not moved and has not been paid; the v464 fold read his approval of the draft as the event, and he has said it is still a pending order. The row is put back exactly as it stood at v463: agreed 28 Aug, undated, nothing paid, nothing delivered. The 2.5 unit the v464 roll took off the shelf is put back in the same roll. The D1 draft stays approved and committed, as history of what was queued.

THREE SALES AND A FULFILMENT. CN6-WM, 1 unit for RM110 on 30 Aug, delivered ahead of payment, so an advance, and RM20 above the RM90 he usually pays. CE4-CHE, the 0.5 unit still owed from the 18 Aug order handed over on 30 Aug, which settles that order in full after twelve days. CI4-OKR, 3 unit for RM290 on 2 Sep, paid and collected. CE4-CHE again on 2 Sep, 2 unit for RM215, paid and collected, RM107.50 a unit against the RM92 he usually pays. He dictated the two CHE rows as CA5-CHE; there is no such code on the roster, CE4-CHE is the only party with a deferred balance to complete, so both are folded to CE4-CHE. If that reading is wrong, a Correction on the party moves them.

FOUR ROWS RE-DATED TO 31 AUG. s120 and s121 (CA7-JTR), s122 (CK4-SEN) and s123 (CR3-DAM) were entered as 1 Sep and happened on 31 Aug. Date, delivered-on and paid-on move together; no figure changes. The drafter flagged each, rightly, that redating a row with movement moves when the movement counts.

t: THE LEDGER NEVER SCROLLS SIDEWAYS: A NARROWER SCREEN RE-FLOWS THE SAME TWELVE CELLS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026, AN HOUR AFTER v465. No scrollable ledger to the right. v465 had made the table one line of thirteen columns and let a narrow screen scroll it sideways, which on a phone is a table with its right half out of sight. The scroller goes.

THREE WIDTHS, ONE TABLE. The one-line layout needs about 915px, and the desk's content column is 938px on a laptop, so it fits there and nowhere narrower. Below that the same twelve cells re-flow onto two lines: E, date, party, quantity, price, total and state on the first; step, type, product, the note and the update control on the second. Below 600px, on a phone, four lines: E, date, party and state; step, quantity and total; type, product, price and the control; then the note across the width. Twelve, not thirteen, on his instruction: the kind of a step (Fulfilment, Modification, Correction, Linked orders) sits in the step column beside Opened and Closed, not in a column of its own. The v307 phone stack, which hid the heading and boxed the figures with CSS labels, is retired: the heading means something at every width now. Each cell names its area, so a column still lines up down the whole table and the heading re-flows with the rows and still sits over them.
NOTHING IS DROPPED, FOLDED OR HIDDEN AT ANY WIDTH. A cell moves; it does not go. Sorting, the filters, the totals strip, the chart, the editor and the row control are unchanged.

PROVED IN A BROWSER AND IN THE SUITE. Measured at 375, 640 and 1300px: the wrap and the document each have no width to scroll. Five assertions keep the structure the layout depends on: no scroller, one container, every line and the heading carrying all twelve areas, two width tiers declared, no rule hiding the heading. 1174 assertions across 91 sections.

t: THE LEDGER IS A TABLE: FIRST TO LATEST, EVERY ROW, EVERY STEP, SORTED FROM ITS HEADINGS
n: HIS INSTRUCTION, 02 SEP 2026. Show the ledger from the first entry to the latest, sort it like a sheet on any column, make it a table, and fold or hide nothing. The three-day window and the "earlier orders" fold go: a folded row reads as a missing one, and this desk has been told so before. The disclosure that hid three or more interim steps goes with it. All 141 rows show, in book order.

THIRTEEN FIXED TRACKS FROM THE HEADING DOWN. E, step, date, type, product, party, kind, note, then quantity, price, total with margin, state, and the order's update control, which sat on a bar beneath every row and now sits on the row. An order line, a step line and the closing line are the same thirteen cells, a cell a line has no use for left empty in place, so the eye reads down a column. The rail and the wrapping left group are retired; on a narrow screen the table scrolls sideways rather than wrapping, because a wrapped table is not a table.

A HEADING SORTS. Once ascending, again descending, an arrow on the active one. Ten of the thirteen sort: E, date, type, product, party, quantity, price, total, margin and state. A blank key (an undated row, a pending or cancelled row's margin) sorts last in both directions, as a sheet treats an empty cell, and ties keep book order. The E-numbers are minted in book order and keep it whatever the sort, so a cross-reference still names the same entry.

WHAT STAYS. The search and the four filters, the totals strip, the day chart, the right-click and long-press editor, the update button on every live row, the correction strip, and his v447 model of a settled order as one Closed line carrying its figures.

PROVED BY DRIVING IT. Ten assertions on the live book through the desk itself: every row on screen, no fold or disclosure, thirteen headed columns, E1 first, Total ascending then descending read back off the book, Party by code, Date descending with the undated rows last, one arrow. 1168 assertions across 90 sections.

t: CY2-NIL'S PENDING 2.5 UNIT SETTLED IN FULL ON 1 SEP, AND THE STATED SHELF GOES BELOW ZERO
n: ONE FULFILMENT, FOLDED ON HIS INSTRUCTION. CY2-NIL's pending order of 2.5 unit for RM230, agreed on 28 Aug, was settled in full on 1 Sep: RM230 in cash and 2.5 unit moved. Queued from the phone on 31 Aug, drafted by the cloud drafter, approved on his word in a Code session on 2 Sep and folded in the same session. The row stops being pending, takes 1 Sep as its date, and leaves nothing outstanding.

THE FOURTH IDENTICAL ORDER FROM THE SAME PARTY. 11 Aug, 18 Aug, 26 Aug and now this one: every CY2-NIL order is 2.5 unit for RM230, RM92 a unit, paid and collected on the day it moves. Against the RM50 shelf cost the row carries it returns RM105 at 45.7%, well clear of every floor. Nothing about the price needs a decision; the party is a habit.

THE STATED SHELF GOES 0.25 TO -2.25, AND THAT IS THE THING TO READ. The v439 roll already said the book was 2.75 unit short of its own promises; this fold delivers 2.5 of those and the arithmetic goes below zero. Salt physically went out on 1 Sep, so the book is behind the shelf, not the other way round: either a lot has landed since the 24 Aug count that has not been entered, or the count itself was low. The desk will show the stockout it reads. What resolves it is a count, or the missing lot entered from the phone, and nothing in this fold invents either. The half unit still owed to CE4-CHE is untouched.

ONE ENTRY IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. The 30 Aug correction on CE4-CHE (delivered 5.25 to 5.75, handover collected) was rejected on the phone, so the row still shows 0.5 unit undelivered. If the rejection was a mis-tap, the same correction queued again and approved folds mechanically.

t: THE STATEMENT ROW CARRIED A FIELD NOTHING READ
n: FOLD 21 OF ROUND TEN, IN tools/make_statements.mjs, AND THE LAST OF THE LEFTOVERS. stmtRows minted a credit on every row, the negative of what was owed, and nothing in the tool read it: the overpayment it stood for is stmtRefunds' shape, which is what the document prints. A figure computed and never read is a figure a later reader trusts without anyone having checked it, so it goes.
WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING, BYTE FOR BYTE. All 37 live statements and the review sheet were rendered before and after the line went and compared as files: identical.
KEPT HONEST. One assertion that no row carries the field, red with the line restored. 1160 assertions across 89 sections.

t: A CANCELLED-ON DATE NEEDS A CANCELLATION, AND CANNOT PRECEDE THE ORDER
n: FOLD 20 OF ROUND TEN, IN engine/position.mjs. cancelledOn has been a correctable date since v363 and correctionFaults, the one gate every Correction passes through on the drafter, the fold and the desk, never read it. A Correction could stamp a cancelled-on date on a row that is not cancelled, revive a cancelled row and leave the date behind, or date the cancellation before the order was agreed. refundOnCancel dates the refund from it and the statement prints it.

TWO RULES. A cancelled-on date without the cancelled flag is refused, with the way out named: clear the date, or cancel the row with it. A cancellation dated before the order's own date is refused. Cancelling a clean row with its date passes, and so does reviving one when the date goes with the flag.
WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. The three rows carrying cancelledOn are cancelled and dated after their orders. The gate only reads what a correction would leave behind.

PROVED ON THE ENGINE AND THE MASTER'S COPY. Five cases through the module and the inlined engine. Three mutations, each with the engine re-synced, all red, including the one that reads the row before the correction instead of after it. 1159 assertions across 88 sections.

t: A LOT'S STEP ON THE LEDGER IS NAMED THE WAY THE WHITEBOARD TOOK IT
n: FOLD 19 OF ROUND TEN. v451 drew a lot's trail through the sale's renderer, and every step kept the sale's word, Fulfilment, where the pane that took it offers Payment and Receipt. Read off what moved: a step with units is a Receipt, with cash a Payment, with both, both; a sale's step still reads Fulfilment.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. The one lot with steps, p016, has both on its own agreed date, so the Ledger folds them into its head row and no lot step label renders. The next lot paid by deposit and balance would have read Fulfilment twice.

PROVED ON A FIXTURE. A lot with a deposit, a receipt four days on and the balance five days after that reads Receipt then Payment and never Fulfilment; a sale with a movement beside it still reads Fulfilment. Three mutations, every one red. 1154 assertions across 87 sections.

t: THE ROW SHAPE SAID A CANCELLED ORDER STILL OWED ITS WHOLE TOTAL AND ITS WHOLE QUANTITY
n: FOLD 18 OF ROUND TEN, IN engine/position.mjs. ledgerRow, the row shape the payload builds for every sale and lot, attached oweRM and oweUnits to a cancelled row beside a state that says canc: RM 90, 80, 120, 185 and 350, and 1, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 6.25 unit, on the five cancelled sales on the book, as money and goods still to be handed over. txPendRM and txPendUnits have said a cancelled order owes nothing since they were written, and txDeferUnits since v443.

A CANCELLED ROW OWES NOTHING, EITHER WAY. Both figures are zero on a cancelled row and so are not attached. Money the customer had paid on one is a refund, which is customerRefunds' shape since v444, not a negative here.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING ON SCREEN. The open list already filters canc through openable, so the drafter never read these; the full ledger list carried them into a payload whose only reader was retired at v387. The rule was wrong in the one place every row shape is minted, and that is reason enough.

PROVED ON THE LIVE ROWS AND A CONTROL. All five cancelled sales carry neither figure; the same synthetic row owes 200 and 2 uncancelled and nothing cancelled; the master's inlined engine says the same, so the sync is proved. Two mutations, each with the engine re-synced, both red. 1151 assertions across 86 sections.

t: THE ROW EDITOR MEASURES WHAT HAS MOVED WITH THE RULER ITS OWN GATE USES
n: FOLD 17 OF ROUND TEN, A TWIN. updOut, which tells the editor what is left to move on a sale, and ovSeed, which seeds the overlay's as-booked step, read txDeliv: delivered plus settled in kind. The cancellation gate beside them (v436), the whiteboard and the engine's own walk read txEffDeliv, which adds advanceUnits. Both now read txEffDeliv, and no caller of txDeliv is left in the desk outside its definition.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Nothing writes advanceUnits: the field is described in a comment and set nowhere, so the two rulers agree on every row that exists. That is exactly the condition under which a twin goes unnoticed until something does write it, and the day it does the editor would have offered to deliver a unit already advanced.

PROVED ON THE ONE ROW THAT DISAGREES. A synthetic sale carrying advanceUnits 1 and nothing delivered: updOut reads 1 moved and 1 left, the seed carries 1, and the two rulers read 1 and 0 to show the fixture is real. Two mutations, both red. 1147 assertions across 85 sections.

t: THE RECONCILIATION'S PAYMENT LIST IS A NARRATIVE BESIDE THE FIGURE, AND PRINTS ONLY WHEN IT SUMS TO IT
n: FOLD 16 OF ROUND TEN, IN tools/make_statements.mjs. Inside a reconciliation the statement lists the payments on the offset order by date, read off the amend trail. A Correction (v363) sets a row's cash directly and leaves the trail as it was written, so the dated list could add up to money the order never carried: s018 holds cash 710 after its audit with steps of 650 and 200 beside it, and a customer adding the list would reach 850.

THE ROW IS THE FIGURE. The dated list prints only when its steps sum to what the row says was paid; otherwise the row's own figure prints alone, which is what the sentence printed already when no step existed.
WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. The one live offset order, s009, carries a single step of RM 750 against cash of RM 750, so its statement is byte for byte what it was.

PROVED ON TWO BOOKS. The live one still prints 750.00 on 08 Jul 2026; a copy with s009 corrected to 700 beside the same step prints 700.00 and not the step. Two mutations, both red. 1144 assertions across 84 sections.

t: A CANCELLATION ON THE WHITEBOARD ASKED FOR A FIGURE NOTHING READS, AND PREVIEWED A PILL WHERE THE BOOK HOLDS A REFUND
n: FOLD 15 OF ROUND TEN. The amend pane's two fields were labelled Cash returned and Returned on a Cancellation. Nothing reads them: ovAmend, the fold's applyAmend and the drafter each mark the row and return, and since v444 what is owed back is what was paid, read off the row. A figure typed there was queued as a movement, qty and total on the entry and cash and kg in the payload, and then dropped, so RM 400 returned typed against RM 450 paid vanished without a word.

THE FIELDS ARE DISABLED AND SAY SO. Cash (not used), Units (not used), held at zero while the kind is Cancellation, re-enabled the moment it is not. The queued entry and its payload carry no figures on a cancellation, the way a Modification already carries none of a movement's, so a stale value in the field cannot travel.

THE PREVIEW SHOWS WHAT THE BOOK WILL HOLD. Refund due when anything was paid, Unpaid otherwise, Undelivered, Cancelled: the three axes txStat reads, where the bare Cancelled pill said only the last. The note names the figure: the RM 450 already paid becomes a refund payable back to the customer.
WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. Nothing on the book is a cancellation queued from this pane with a figure in the field; the fault was in what the pane invited, not in any row.

PROVED BY DRIVING THE PANE. An order paid ahead and a pending order on a copy of the book: labels, disabled state, preview text, and a record with RM 400 and 1 unit forced into the fields reaching the queue as nothing. Six mutations, every one red. 1141 assertions across 83 sections.

t: AN UNDATED ROW SAYS SO WHEREVER ITS DATE IS PRINTED, NOT ON THE ONE TABLE THAT WAS GUARDED
n: FOLD 14 OF ROUND TEN. The Order book's pending table has printed not dated for an undated row since it was built. The five tables beside it printed the raw field, which for an undated row is the word undefined under a heading that says Since. The finding named those five; the sweep of the class named eight more.

THE SWEEP WAS A CENSUS, NOT A GREP. Five undated fixtures, one per table, on a copy of the book, and every tab read for the word undefined. It reached the board's lock rule on Today and Overview (5 unit at RM 50 landed undefined), the sourcing table, the stock walk and lot list, a customer's last three orders, the replacement-rate line and its two notes, and the plans' evidence lines. Each now says not dated, the same guard the pending table has always carried.
WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. The one undated row is pending, on the one table that was guarded, and the census over the live book was clean before this fold.

PROVED BY THE CENSUS. The suite keeps it: every tab on the fixture book prints undefined nowhere, the Order book says not dated six times, the lock rule says it once. Seven mutations, one guard reverted each, every one red on the tab it reached. 1136 assertions across 82 sections.

t: THE RECONCILIATION READ A LEG'S SHORTFALL FROM THE FIELD THE SETTLEMENT HAD ALREADY FILLED, AND TABULATED ZEROS
n: FOLD 13 OF ROUND TEN, IN tools/make_statements.mjs. When salt is withheld from an order to clear earlier balances, the statement reconstructs the chain: each earlier order billed, paid in cash, and short. It read short as billed less cash. The fold credits an in-kind settlement INTO the leg's cash, as a Fulfilment step carrying ref to the order that settled it, so by statement time every settled leg read Short 0.00, Carried forward 0.00, 0.00 at 0.00 a unit is 2.06 unit; and the v192 no-leg guard did not fire, because the legs existed.

THE SHORTFALL IS WHAT THE CREDIT SAYS IT WAS. A leg carrying such steps reads its shortfall off them, and Paid in cash becomes billed less that, which is what the column names. A leg with no such step is still unpaid and reads billed less cash as before. Legs that carry no shortfall between them explain nothing, so the offset is told plainly through the no-leg branch rather than tabulated.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. The one row with settledKg has no legs and the one with legs has no settledKg, so the legged branch does not run on any live statement. It is the case v186 was written for.

PROVED THREE WAYS. The live CJ4-BJ rows with the 15 Jul order carrying its 2.0588 unit as settledKg: legs credited as the fold writes them read RM 50 and RM 90, carried forward RM 140 at RM 68 a unit, and the document prints it; legs left unpaid read the same through the old road; legs paid in cash go to the plain telling. Three mutations, every one red. 1132 assertions across 81 sections.

t: THE STATEMENT STATES A CANCELLED PAID ORDER'S MONEY: PAID COUNTS IT, THE FOOTER SAYS OWED TO YOU, THE REFUNDS TABLE SAYS WHY
n: FOLD 12 OF ROUND TEN, IN tools/make_statements.mjs ALONE. v444 books the refund on a cancelled paid order as a payable in customerRefunds, and the statement's own stmtRefunds reads that list, so the Refunds table already listed it. Everything around it still treated the row as if no money had moved: the totals dropped the cancelled row whole, so Paid was short by the RM 450 the customer had actually handed over; Balance read nil directly above a refund still owed to them; the Refunds table called it an overpayment, its one label being fixed text from the two live rows; and the review sheet flagged the account clear.

WHAT IT SAYS NOW. Paid is what they handed over, cancelled orders included, with the cancelled part named on its own line beneath it. The footer carries Owed to you for any refund not yet returned, beside Outstanding or Balance rather than netted into either, because the engine records them separately. The Refunds table says Cancelled order, money returned to you, read off the record's rid and note. The struck row says what was paid on it and points at the table. The review sheet flags such an account refund and shows the sum owed to them in the Owed column.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. No cancelled order on the book was paid for, and the two refund rows are overpayments and keep their label. The change is for the case v443 and v444 were written for.

PROVED ON THE DOCUMENT. An order paid RM 450 and cancelled before collection, with the refund record refundOnCancel writes, through makeStatements on a fixture book: Paid up by RM 450 against the live rows, the two footer lines, the table label, the struck row's pointer, the review flag, and a customer owed nothing carrying no Owed to you. Seven mutations, one per site, every one red. 1126 assertions across 80 sections.

t: A LINE PRINTS THE MEASURE ITS SUM USED: THE STOCK WALK'S RECEIVED ROW, THE LOT LIST AND THE HELD-OUT ORDER
n: THE SAME CLASS, THREE SITES. An itemised line printed a whole-row figure beside a sum that had netted it. The stock reconciliation's Received row and the lot list printed a lot's ORDERED quantity, where buyUnits, and so the ledger figure the walk closes to, sums what LANDED: a lot six of ten received would have walked in as ten, listed its four again under Still to arrive, and the lines would not have summed to the figure printed beneath them. The held-out line on Financials said an order carried RM 200 of revenue in its headline, then named it at RM 400, because the headline nets the pending tail and the name did not.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. No lot on the book is part received, and the one undated order is unpriced, so neither line renders differently. The change is for the next lot that lands in two deliveries and the next undated order half delivered.

EACH SITE NOW PRINTS THE RULER ITS SUM USED. The walk and the lot list print poRecvUnits at poRate; the held-out order is named by its delivered revenue, with what was ordered beside it when the two differ: RM 200 of RM 400 ordered.

PROVED ON BOTH PARTS. A lot six of ten received and an undated order half delivered, both fixtures through booksync into a scratch master: the Received row reads 6 unit, the lot list 6 in the basis and 4 still to arrive, the walk sums to its own On hand line, and the held-out line reads RM 200 in the headline and RM 200 of RM 400 ordered in the name. Three mutations, one per site, every one red. 1117 assertions across 79 sections.

t: THE FINANCIALS MONTH CHART DRAWS THE TABLE'S OWN FIGURES, AND NAMES THE YEAR WHEN THE MONTHS SPAN TWO
n: A SECOND ACCUMULATOR, BESIDE THE FIRST. The chart summed pricedSales itself, 190 lines from finRows, and the two disagreed in a way the book does not show today: a sale partly pending counted its whole total and its whole quantity in the bars, where the statement beneath nets the pending tail out of both revenue and cost. v423 held the undated row out of both and left this. The chart now reads finRows and draws revenue and revenue less cost from the rows the table prints, so there is one set of month figures on the part.

AND A YEAR ON THE LABEL. The labels were bare month names, so the January after this December would have drawn as a second Jan with nothing to say which. When the months span more than one year every label carries the two-digit year; within one year they stay as they are.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING. Every month's bars equal the table to the ringgit before and after, proved by a probe over the live book. The change is for the next order delivered in part across a month end, and for January.

PROVED WITH A RECORDING CHART. Two fixture sales, one half pending in August and one in the January after, rendered through booksync into a scratch master; the Financials part draws one block per product, so the stub keys by canvas and product, which is how the first reading came back as oil's two months. Every month's bars equal the table; August draws RM 200 short of what the old accumulator counted, the half not delivered; every label carries a year in the fixture and none does on the book. Four mutations, every one red. 1112 assertions across 78 sections.

t: THE LEDGER DRAWS A LOT'S TRAIL: ITS STEPS, ITS CORRECTION STRIP AND ITS SEARCH TEXT, AS IT HAS DRAWN A SALE'S SINCE v254
n: THE THIRD FOLD OF THREE. The card map read a row's steps and corrections behind a SELL gate, off a wrapper that carries a purchase under _buy and therefore has no amend and no mod, so no lot ever showed a trail, a correction strip or matched a search on its note. v449 made the seed read a lot with the lot's ruler and v450 made both engines write one; this fold reads it. The replay is arithmetic on total, qty and the steps' cash and kg, and poStat names the same states a sale's replay does, so a lot goes through it unchanged and its head reads Open, Deferred when the money went first.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE BOOK TODAY: NOTHING VISIBLE. p016, the one lot with a trail, was restated the day it was booked, so it folds to the one Completed line it already had. The change is for the next lot corrected or received in stages: its card will open and close on two lines dated by what moved, and a correction will sit in its own strip beneath, crimson if a claim does not read back.

PROVED ON THE CARDS. Two fixture lots rendered through booksync into a scratch master: one paid on the 10th and received on the 20th, opening Open, Deferred and closing Completed on the receipt's date; one corrected, carrying a quiet strip that reads Corrected 2026-08-30 with both claims read back. p016 read for regression, and the search proved on a lot's mod. Four mutations, each gate and each wrapper read, every one red. 1107 assertions across 77 sections.

t: A LOT KEEPS A TRAIL: THE FOLD AND THE DESK SEED AND STEP A LOT AS THEY DO A SALE, AND P016 IS BROUGHT UNDER THE CONTRACT
n: THE TRAIL A LOT NEVER HAD. A sale's amendments seed the trail with the row as booked and append a step before the figures move, and the Ledger replays those steps into a card. Both engines' BUY branches returned before either write, so a lot restated or fulfilled through the fold carried no trail at all. The one lot with a step, p016, had its Modification written by hand with no seed, and would have replayed as Pending on a lot paid and received in full. Nothing drew it, so nothing showed it; v449 made the seed read a lot with the lot's ruler, and this fold makes the seed and the step happen.

THE SAME WRITES, IN THE SAME ORDER, ON BOTH SIDES. In tools/fold.mjs and in the desk's ovAmend, the BUY Modification branch seeds and appends a Modification step before it restates the figures, and the movement branch seeds and appends the step before the Default, Cancellation and receipt handlers, exactly where the SELL tail does. The v420 differential now polices a lot's trail as it polices a sale's, because it compares the whole row.

P016 GETS ITS SEED. One step added at the head of its trail in ledger/book.json, the lot as booked: RM 2,200 and 50 unit on 20 Aug, the figures seedStep would have written. Its trail now sums to the row. ledger/ledger.json was regenerated with it, which the fold routine does and a hand edit had to remember to.
THE LEDGER STILL DRAWS NO LOT TRAIL. That is the next fold, on purpose: the data had to be right before it became visible, and the two are separately provable.

PROVED BY FOLDING. A first movement and a restatement on lots through the fold, the trail read back and summed against poCash and poRecvUnits; the same two amendments on two of the book's own lots through the desk, the desk's trail equal to the fold's byte for byte; p016 read off the file. Five mutations, each side's seed and step and p016's seed, every one red. 1102 assertions across 76 sections.

t: A LOT'S TRAIL OPENS WITH THE LOT AS BOOKED, READ WITH THE LOT'S RULER, ON THE FOLD AND ON THE DESK
n: THE TWIN OF v441 AND v446, IN THE SEED RATHER THAN THE STATUS. The first step of every trail, `as booked`, was written at six sites, three in tools/fold.mjs and three in the desk's ovAmend, and all six read the row with txPaid and txDeliv: cash, settledRM, deliveredQty and settledKg, the sale's fields. A lot has none of them. On p001, RM 800 paid in full and 12.5 unit received, both read zero, so the first Correction folded against any lot would have opened its trail with nothing paid and nothing received, and every replay after it would have summed from there.

WHY NOTHING ON THE BOOK SHOWS IT. A Fulfilment or a Modification on a lot returns before the seed, so a lot reaches it through a Correction alone, and no lot has been corrected yet. p016's Modification step was written by hand. The Ledger also draws no trail for a lot at all, which is the next fold, and is why this one had to land first: a trail nobody could see was about to become one everybody could.

ONE HELPER A SIDE. seedStep(row, dir) in the fold and ovSeed(row, dir) on the desk, each reading poCash and poRecvUnits for a lot and txPaid and txDeliv for a sale; the six lines are calls. A helper used three times on each side is the one abstraction this fold earns.

PROVED BY FOLDING ONE. A Correction on a paid, received lot on both engines, the seed read back: RM 800 and 12.5 unit, and a sale exactly as before. Five mutations, each side's money and units and a sale reading the lot's ruler, every one red. 1096 assertions across 75 sections.

t: THE ROW EDITOR OPENS ON THE SIX STATES AND ONE BUTTON; THE SHEET, ITS SAVE AND ITS REASONS SIT BEHIND ONE FOLD
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 02 SEP 2026: `WAY TOO COMPLICATED FOR NO REASON`. What a tap on a row opened was two forms stacked and three buttons: Queue the update under the chips, then the sheet's own Queue the correction, then a Cancel that sat one chip away from Cancel the order. Two of the three queued different things, the third closed the panel, and the word Cancel appeared twice meaning two things. Nothing on the panel said which was which.

WHAT IT IS NOW. The cross, the six states, the two amounts and the date, the sentence, and Queue the update. Below that, one fold, Change something else, shut, holding the sheet, its own Queue the correction and the reasons a refused save prints. The cross is the only way out; Escape and the glass behind the panel still close it. The chip reads Cancelled, a state beside Completed and Defaulted, and arms the same Cancellation the old chip did. A new order has no states to open on, so its sheet stays open with Queue the order and the cross. Nothing queued changed: the same entries reach the same drafter and the same tap at Approve.

THE CLASS, SWEPT. Cancel the lot went with Cancel the order; nothing else in the repo names the old fold or the second button. The state pills and the card rail stay, by his choice, until he has lived with the figures v447 draws.

PROVED ON THE PANEL, NOT THE SOURCE. Fifteen assertions over an order, a lot and a new order, read off the rendered dialog: which buttons sit outside the fold and which inside, the fold shut, the reasons beside the sheet, one dismiss control, the chip's word and what tapping it arms. Six mutations, every one red. 1093 assertions across 74 sections.
